Title: Ian McEwan with Alex Salmond
Subtitle: A Great British Writer Meets Scotland’s First Minister
Description:
According to Alex Salmond, his eclectic cultural interests range from Miss Marple to Star Trek and in this evening’s unmissable event the First Minister talks about life beyond politics with the most successful British literary novelist of the past 30 years. Ian McEwan also boasts a wide range of interests beyond fiction – not least among them film, music and science.

	If you didn't manage to get tickets to see Ian McEwan at the Book Festival he will also take part in a Q&A session following the screening of The Cement Garden on Thursday 23 August at 6pm at the at the Filmhouse in Lothian Road, Edinburgh. Tickets are available from the Filmhouse website or call their box office on 0131 228 2689.

Title: Occupied
Description: Amy took a year off which three years later she's still on, having occupied herself and her home with poetry, stories, songs and props. Now coming to a living room near you. Expect cardboard. No tents.
Venue accessibility: \nNo lift to second floor performance area.

Title: The Price of Everything
Description: A smart whistle-stop tour of bizarre facts and impassioned arguments about value. Splendidly insightful, occasionally misleading but always a joy to watch. And you get a free glass of milk. ‘The future of British theatre’ (Times).
Venue description: Northern Stage at St Stephen’s is a creative home for the most exciting and unusual theatre made in the Greater North of England. Original stories, new performances and spirited special events that will delight, provoke and entertain you.

Title: The Halton Quartet
Description: Comprising the collective talents within two of Scotland’s most innovative and captivating duos (Angus Lyon and Ruaridh Campbell, and Wingin’ It), The Halton Quartet make music which is both rich in tradition and boldly forward-looking.
Venue description: Brunton Theatre is just off the city bypass, 20 minutes journey from the city centre. Comfortable, raked auditorium with clear sightlines. Plenty of free parking and a bus stop outside the door. Please check www.bruntontheatre.co.uk for information on buses.
Venue accessibility:
29840
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space), improved access for visually impaired people, assistance dogs welcome, accessible parking.

Title: The Brothers Grimm Spectaculathon
Description: The Brothers Grimm fairy tales are turned on their heads in this fast-paced, rollicking ride as a troupe of actors attempt to combine all 209 stories. A wild comedy with audience participation and madcap fun.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: Seymour Mace: Squeg!
Description: Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Square! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Peg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Square Peg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! Squeg! ‘Relentless originality’ (Guardian). seymourmace.co.uk.
Artist: Seymour Mace / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Round the corner, our little sister club is in its thirteenth year. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Gemma Arrowsmith: Defender of Earth
Description: 'She is the greatest female comic actor of the 21st century' (Vic Reeves). 'Witty, geeky and engaging. You really couldn't ask for more.' **** (Chortle.co.uk). Sketches and characters from half of Mould and Arrowsmith. www.gemmaarrowsmith.com.
Venue description: Shanghai @ Le Monde, George Street is a brand new Free Fringe venue for 2012. Le Monde is open 8am- 3am and serves food till late. No street level disabled access available. Please contact venue for more information.
Venue accessibility:
49
\nAssistance dogs welcome, accessible WC

Title: Beyond the Fringe of Reason
Description: We present four special fringe events: Alt Med challenger Prof. Edzard Ernst, philosopher Prof. AC Grayling, the real Belle DeJour, Dr. Brooke Magnanti and magician Paul Zenon. For full event listings please visit: www.skepticsonthefringe.co.uk.
Venue description: The Jam House is a live music venue, conceived by Jools Holland. It offers live performances, fine food and has a vibrant atmosphere. A broad range of musical styles is available for all age groups. We are situated on Queen Street, and have a beautiful venue which includes our historical Chapel Bar.

Title: Frank Close
Subtitle: A RACE FOR THE HIGGS BOSON
Description: The race to identify the Higgs Boson has led to multi-billion dollar investment in the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. The return promises to be the revelation of how the universe came into being. Frank Close is Professor of Theoretical Physics at Oxford University and in The Infinity Puzzle he tells the astonishing story of three scientists – all good friends of Close – whose work has played out against a backdrop of high politics, and who stand to win a Nobel Prize. The event will be chaired by Professor Peter Higgs who first identified the concept of the Higgs Boson in the 1960s and this will be the first time that Higgs and Close have appeared together at a public event since the announcement of the recent breakthrough discovery at CERN.

Title: The Oxford Gargoyles - Jazz a Cappella!
Description: The beautifully black-tied Gargoyles return with an unmissable show, performing an eclectic mix of jazz, pop, soul and Disney! 'Stand-out a cappella group of the Fringe' *****  (Fringe Review). 'Charm personified' (Times). www.theoxfordgargoyles.co.uk.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Nick Cope: Family Songs and Music
Description: Nick sings about things that really matter to kids - monkeys, fluffballs, jumping in mud, howling wolves, drums and goodnight kisses. 'If only all music for under fives was made by indie-pop geniuses' (Schofield family).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Gordon Southern's A Brief History of History
Description: All history. One hour. With jokes. Lightning fast edu-tainment romp. Everything, ever in hardly any detail. Total sell-out Melbourne Comedy Festival 2012. 'Poetic, clever and joyfully freewheeling' **** (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Seann Walsh: Seann to be Wild
Description: Star of TV's Live at the Apollo, Stand Up For The Week and Argumental with an all-new hour of 'Sharp, creative observational comedy. See him now, before the stadium tour' (Sunday Times).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Jarlath Regan: The Audacity of Hope and the Inspirational Stupidity of Perseverance
Description: Free-wheeling, uplifting, jokes and stories about being silly in the face of adversity from the award-winning author and guy off the telly. ***** (Independent). 'Comedy genius' (Irish Times).
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
02459
\n
\nOn street parking for a blue badge holder, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC

Title: Jane Bom-Bane - Free
Description: Multi award-winning JB-B returns with her self-penned songs of 'charm and gentle wit' (Scotsman), a harmonium, and a mechanical hat or two. 'Utterly refreshing - unlike anything I've ever seen or heard before' (Dave Gorman). www.bom-banes.co.uk.
Artist: Jane Bom-Bane / Laughing Horse Free Fesival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier music venue, at the heart of town just off of the Royal Mile hosts free festival shows during the day, and live music in the evenings - with a wide offering of drinks available all day!

Title: I Never Saw Another Butterfly
Description: ABJ Theatre (Canada) tells the beautiful, heart-wrenching story of Raja Englanderova, a survivor of the Holocaust during WWII. Raja's journey through life - she lives memories of love, loss, life and most importantly, survival.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: Edinburgh
Description: A meditation on drama and place, on cities, on what we think of as home and on Edinburgh. Some jokes, some ritualistic carry-on, lots of ideas. 'A playwright of a quite fearless and magnificent originality' (Playwrights' Studio Scotland).
Artist: Theatre of the Impossible / RJ Thomson
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Paul Gilbody
Description: From pin-drop delicacy to infectious acoustic grooves that leave you smiling. Described as a dirty Jamiroquai / John Martyn cross-breed, this renowned singer/songwriter's quartet present songs of love and seafood from his debut album. www.paulgilbody.com.
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: Holly Webb
Description: The author of Lost in the Snow, the My Naughty Little Puppy series, Rose, Lily and many more comes to Edinburgh with all your favourite characters. Discover where Holly Webb gets the amazing ideas for her gentle, magical stories, which are so hugely successful. A great opportunity to meet Holly, hear about her latest books and see lots of super-cute pictures!

Title: Chapel Street
Description: Hilarious, heartbreaking, and compelling throughout, Chapel Street provides a crackling mix of poetry and profanity that takes on a deep resonance in Cameron’s Broken Britain. Winner - Old Vic New Voices Edinburgh Award.
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Bring Me the Head of Adam Riches
Description: The 2011 Foster's Edinburgh Comedy Award-winner returns for four nights only with his breath-taking hour of character comedy, anarchic stagecraft and fearless level of audience engagement.
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: BBC: London 2012 Olympics Closing Ceremony Screening
Description: Join BBC Comedy as we screen the closing ceremony of the London 2012 Olympic Games live with special Fringe guests. Keep up with the Olympic action on our big screen on site.
Venue address: Corner of Potterrow and Marshall Street,Edinburgh
Venue description: Experience the best of the BBC under one roof and a taster of all the delights of the Fringe. Join us at Venue 25 for BBC shows, big names, stand-up every night plus masterclasses from BBC Radio, TV and Online. Free events are ticketed via a random draw. To enter the draw please use the show website link: bbc.co.uk/tickets.

Title: Barra and Beyond: Songs of the Western Isles - Maggie MacInnes
Description: Songs from Maggie's family's treasured rich tradition. Renowned award-winning singer and clàrsach player in a relaxed, enormously enjoyable, intimate performance. ‘Nothing short of captivating’ (Hi-Arts Magazine). With Brian McAlpine (keyboards/accordion).
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Kamishibai Tales with Fergus McNicol
Description: Storyteller Fergus McNicol introduces the traditional Japanese Kamishibai bike, a bicycle with a small wooden stage, which is used to tell tales using different picture cards. The enchanting stories he tells come from around the world from Japan to Scotland and back again.

Title: Owen O'Neill: Struck By Lightning
Description: Owen O’Neill will tell you how he survived being struck by lightning, escaping with minor burns. The apples down his wellingtons were stewed, his school uniform destroyed. It shaped the rest of his life.
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
02459

\nOn street parking for a blue badge holder, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC

Title: Tom Watson
Subtitle: WHERE JOURNALISM WENT OFF THE RAILS
Description: The Labour MP Tom Watson has been on a mission for the past two years to uncover the truth about phone hacking. Watson's grilling of the founder of the News Corp empire in a Commons Select Committee was one of last year's major political talking points. In this keynote event he discusses Dial M for Murdoch, his new book about the scandal, with the leading BBC broadcaster James Naughtie.

Title: An Evening With Dementia
Description: An Evening With Dementia, Fringe sell-out, 2010. ***** ‘One of the most essential pieces of theatre to come out of the Fringe’ (BritishTheatreGuide.info). Poignant yet humorous - enlightens, inspires - a love letter to a well-lived life. www.aneveningwithdementia.co.uk.
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Smokey Joe's Cafe
Description: Mix cool and classy with a splash of sparkle and fizz. Shake, rattle and roll! Sit back and enjoy a musical cocktail of wonderful Leiber and Stoller songs (On Broadway, Jailhouse Rock, Stand By Me). Delicious! www.tempo.org.uk.
Venue description: The Edinburgh Academy is centrally located in the New Town, with ample off-street parking and an on-site cafe for festival patrons. The venue is centered on its amazing oval Hall, built in 1824 and designed by William Burn.

Title: Frontline
Description: A colourful piece bursting with energy and dance that goes behind the mask worn on the frontline. Exploring the strengths and strains of a soldier, you'll be taken on a journey of love, death and war.
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Awkward!
Description: Secrets and illicit relationships spill out when writer Greg and girlfriend Matilda arrive at their grotty second home, abetted by friends. Tempers flare, a disturbing truth is uncovered, and the course of the friends’ lives is revised forever.
Warnings: Strong Language, adult themes & strobe lighting Brief nudity, adult themes, strong language, strobe lighting
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Jeremy Vine
Subtitle: THIS IS THE OLD NEWS
Description: Jeremy Vine marks his quarter of a century at the BBC with It’s All News to Me. He takes a look back from the very first day when he arrived at his office (which just so happened to be 1987’s Black Monday) to being fired at by a sniper in Bosnia and dealing with the brickbats chucked at him in Westminster by the likes of Alastair Campbell and Peter Mandelson.

Title: The Raven Mysteries with Marcus Sedgwick
Description: Welcome to the goth-froth world of The Raven Mysteries, with Edgar the Raven and the hapless, hopeless, but ultimately harmless Otherhand family – a cross between the Addams family and the Munsters (you may need to Google the reference if you’re under forty!). Marcus Sedgwick brings us Diamonds and Doom, the latest in the series, and some dramatic fun as you meet this unusual, slightly spooky but always very funny family.

Title: Paterson Arran Ten at Ten
Description: A delicious morning reading from one of our Festival authors to set you up for the day. Check the screen in the Entrance Tent to see who’s reading each day.

Title: Riot! The Musical
Description: Summer 2011 - the London riots. Critically acclaimed About Turn present a powerful tale of youth culture gang violence told through music and physical theatre. The rock opera of 2012 not to be missed.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Opera Scenes
Description: Following sell-out shows, ESO returns with a daring performance of opera's best-loved arias and scenes. Opera newcomers and connoisseurs alike will enjoy this year's portrayal of operatic scenes. 'A wealth of outstanding young singing talent' (Scotsman). www.edinburghstudioopera.com.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: My Plaice / The Lake
Description: An escape. A fight for survival. A struggle for freedom. The life-cycle of fish and fowl is explored in a dance double-bill inspired by life under and above water, and by Swan Lake. www.lincolncompany.co.uk.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Can You Put This in the Bin for Me? - Free
Description: Three stand-ups: Michael Mooney (wandering ponderer) Anthony Ayton (himself but funnier) and Rue Barratt (tattoos in strange places). Will make you laugh so hard, you'll keep the flyer!
Artist: Bin for Me / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: CineFringe Film Festival
Description: CineFringe is the film festival of the Edinburgh Fringe. Join us for screenings of short films programmed especially for Fringe lovers. Visit CineFringe.com for full programme details. 'Who needs the EIFF when there's CineFringe?' (Edinburgh Evening News).
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Adrian Levy & Catherine Scott-Clark
Subtitle: TRUE STORY OF A KASHMIR KIDNAPPING
Description: In 1995 a group in Kashmir was kidnapped and held hostage by jihadis. They hid out in remote shepherds’ huts while western negotiators converged on Kashmir. In their stunning and explosive book, Adrian Levy and Catherine Scott-Clark unveil the tragic story of an episode which marked the beginning of modern terrorism. Today, they discuss their work as investigative journalists, and reveal the research behind their new book.

Title: NeWt play Jaws
Description: NeWt trio tribute Grammy composer John Williams in their unique fiery prog-jazz style. Expect movie-themes '...the real triumph of this extra-curricular exercise...they manage to honour the object of their homage...satisfy their urge to experiment.' (Herald).
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: THE 99 Unbound
Description: Introducing to the screen in crisp computer generated animation the super heroes of Naif Al-Mutawa’s comic strip ‘The 99’, this feature debut from British animator Dave Osborne brings together the first five heroes connected by their special relationship with the Noor stones; Gem stones imbued with the wisdom and knowledge of the lost civilization of Baghdad. Each represents one of the 99 attributes of Allah. An action pact international journey packed with intrigue, conflict and advocacy of unity amongst diversity.

Title: James Gleick
Subtitle: CREATURES OF THE INFORMATION
Description: Having previously penned Chaos and Genius, science and technology guru James Gleick pored over The Information for years. In it are portraits of Charles Babbage, Alan Turing and Samuel Morse as well as an analysis of how we came to be drenched in a world of tweets, blogs, signs and images. Information, argues Gleick, is ‘the blood and the fuel, the vital principle’ of the world. He talks to the Guardian’s Literary Editor, Claire Armitstead.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning events for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. Appearing today: Annie Dalton.

Title: Bound
Description: International collaboration, with Antwerpian New Wave direction and an unmistakably American script, based on the author's time riding freight trains. Two modern-day hobos help a teenage runaway, but when their boxcar door locks, they discover true freedom. www.noosfeer.org.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Comedy Gala 2012: In Aid of Waverley Care
Description: Edinburgh's biggest comedy event featuring an all-star cast, hosted by Seann Walsh and Josh Widdicombe. Previous years have included, Kevin Bridges and Sean Lock among others. Book early. Recorded for television. www.offthekerb.co.uk.
Venue description: A magnificent venue at the heart of the Fringe and International Festival, and one of Edinburgh's cultural hotspots year-round. The auditorium is a dramatic mix of Art Nouveau, Beaux Arts and Neo-Classicism, encompassing perfect acoustics within a parlour-like intimacy.

Title: Final Whistle with Dan Freedman
Description: After leading Scotland to near-victory in the World Cup, Jamie Johnson has landed the dream job: playing football for one of the best teams in the world, Barcelona. Dan Freedman is one of the UK’s leading football fiction writers and has worked at the top level of football, writing for the FA and the Premier League as well as attending two World Cups. Join him as he talks about the last book in his hugely popular Jamie Johnson series, Final Whistle.

Title: James Acaster - Prompt
Description: James Acaster returns to Edinburgh with a show full of comedy. 'Blisteringly funny and highly original' (List). Seen on Russell Howard's Good News, Show and Tell, Dave's One Night Stand and Live at The Comedy Store.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Abanico Flamenco
Description: Abanico, 'fan' in English, is symbolic of the way in which this show spreads out and transmits the varying emotions characterised by flamenco music/dance, bringing together the purest flamenco with unique interpretation. *** (Scotsman/Skinny). www.myspace.com/dondeduendes.
Venue description: Mood Nightclub is a large central venue offering fantastic drinks offers every day. We are open 10pm-3am Tuesday-Sunday. We have disabled access and facilities within the venue. With friendly staff and great customer service we provide a happy, fun atmosphere.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nWheekchair access, assistance dogs welcome, accessible WC

Title: Edinburgh Traditional Building Festival
Description: Celebrating Edinburgh's Traditional Buildings - Edinburgh's Traditional Building Forum provides a series of talks to raise awareness of the challenge of providing appropriate skills and materials for the upkeep of Edinburgh's World Heritage Site.
Artist: Various individuals involved in traditional building skills.
Venue address: Edinburgh World Heritage,5 Bakehouse Close,146 Canongate

Title: Puppet. Book of Splendor
Description: 2011 Herald Angel and Total Theatre Award winners, neTTheatre come back with a Tadeusz Kantor-inspired project. A vibrant world of effigies, golems and mannequins viewed through cabalism. Welcome to the Clinic of Dreams!
Warnings: Supported by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute www.culture.pl
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: George's Marvellous Medicine
Description: George lives a peaceful life on the farm owned by his parents. That is, until the arrival of Grandma. Can you help George to make a medicine marvellous enough to make even the meanest Grandma better?
Venue: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel
Venue description: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel offers two performance spaces ideal for intimate, experimental, and engaging theatre. We present a programme of theatrical performance, especially innovative works, original works, devised theatre, movement, puppetry, immersive theatre and music.

Title: The Trojan Women
Description: Evil against reason. Victory against justice. Vengeance against mercy. Carnage, blood and grief stretching back to ancient Troy. Fathers, husbands, brothers, children lost. The women who weep honour the dead and endure. A tragedy for our time.
Venue description: Just off the Lawnmarket our friendly venue is centrally placed on the terrace above Victoria Street . We provide a 65 seating rake and a black box theatre, our own box office and reception area. Our venue profits go to charity.

Title: Sally Magnusson & Norman Stone
Description: Join writer and broadcaster Sally Magnusson to hear all about her first children’s book, Horace and the Haggis Hunter. The book, illustrated by TV producer husband Norman Stone, is a tale of a refugee haggis running from an evil haggis-hunter and finding safety among the kind animals of Acre Valley. It’s a charming story of adventure, secrets and unforgettable characters.

Title: Dorothy Squires: Mrs Roger Moore
Description: She was among the biggest recording stars of the 1950s, but her marriage to the future 007 ended in disaster. Now Dorothy's songs and story live on, starring Al Pillay (Channel 4's The Comic Strip).
Artist: The Biggest Diva of Them All
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: One Man Lord of the Rings
Description: 100,000 characters. Nine companions. Three masterworks. One Man. Charles Ross recreates Tolkien's trilogy in just 3600 seconds of kinetic entertainment, armed with nothing more than a pair of elbow pads and his outrageous imagination.
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Doll
Description: Ethan is a married man. His wife, Monica, is a $600 doll. He decides to become plastic like her, and meets the enigmatic Doctor Whiteman, who agrees to help him. But the doctor is not all he seems.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Val McDermid & Sue Black
Subtitle: CRIME FICTION ON THE DISSECTION TABLE
Description: Television has thrust forensic science into popular culture and made it sexy. But as DNA developments revolutionize criminal cases, what is the reality of a crime scene? How do crime writers keep up without losing the plot? Val McDermid is joined by Professor Sue Black, director of the Centre for Anatomy and Human Identification (CAHID) at Dundee University and champion of the ‘Million for a Morgue’ campaign.

Title: Amused Moose Comedy Awards Final
Description: Vote alongside international comedy cognoscenti for breakthrough stars of tomorrow, who battle brilliantly for fame, fortune and shiny moose trophies in the prestigious finals of Amused Moose's Laugh Off and Laughter Awards 2012. www.amusedmoose.com/laughoff.
Venue description: Edinburgh's all-year-round multi-arts venue. We offer a gourmet selection of theatre, cabaret, live music, visual arts and clubbing. Our cafe adds delicious homemade food, free internet and great coffee to the mix. All brought to you by the friendliest staff in town.

Title: The Adding Machine
Description: When Mr. Zero, an allegorical character that represents what happens when you become another cog in the universal machine, is fired and replaced by an adding machine, he snaps and faces problems bigger than his nagging wife.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: NILE RODGERS
Description:
Le Freak, Everybody Dance, We are Family, Let’s Dance, Like a Virgin, The Reflex. All songs that define decades of our music history; all songs which Nile Rodgers played on or produced. Often described as one of the people who invented disco, to describe this man as a music legend is no exaggeration. His book Le Freak – An Upside Down Story of Family, Disco and Destiny is the story of his life, love and the music that defined it all. As part of his visit to Edinburgh, Nile Rodgers will do a very special solo show of songs and stories.

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Title: Two Dogs
Description: Two dog brothers, Lai Fu and Wang Cai, leave home seeking their dreams. Finding city life far from perfect and caught in increasingly absurd money making schemes, they discover that despite life’s hardships, we all must be brave.

Title: Unconditional

Subtitle: INTO AFRICA
Description: With an accompanying BBC TV series, The Lost Kingdoms of Africa will put Gus Casely-Hayford firmly on the map as he helps us understand a far more diverse, creative and culturally rich continent than the public image might suggest. Alastair Hazell’s The Last Slave Market tells the extraordinary story of John Kirk, the Scottish botanist who singlehandedly ended the slave trade in East Africa.

Title: China Miéville
Subtitle: GOING OFF THE RAILS
Description: China Miéville is often billed as a genre-busting science fiction writer but in truth he’s impossible to categorise. With Railsea, Miéville has imagined a post-industrial landscape of small islands, where the sea is not water but a mass of criss-crossing rails. The story takes a young islander across the railsea, and Miéville has created his most enticing and compelling novel to date. He discusses his work with another innovative and critically acclaimed novelist, Patrick Ness.

Title: The Edinburgh Writers' Conference 1962: The Legacy
Subtitle: Putting a Bomb Under Scottish Literature
Description:
The first Writers’ Conference, which took place in the McEwan Hall in August 1962, can be regarded as a seminal moment in Scotland’s literary renaissance. John Calder organised it with the assistance of Jim Haynes and today they discuss their memories of those five heady days. Eleanor Bell and Angela Bartie, heading up a Strathclyde University research project on the Conference, explain their attempts to disentangle the myths from the realities of the famous Edinburgh events.

	Visit the Edinburgh World Writers’ Conference website - www.edinburghworldwritersconference.org - to watch a live broadcast of the conference events and to join in the conversation online. Follow the conference twitter feed: #WorldWritersConf.

In this event Welsh discusses his work with another great Scottish writer, Doug Johnstone.

In his ambitious new book The Natural Explorer, he encourages us to increase our enjoyment of every journey we make, from the shortest of walks to the most epic of voyages.

Title: Henry Rollins
Description: New show from legendary Black Flag frontman, author, actor, award-winner and passionate stream-of-social-consciousness raconteur. Hard-hitting, side-splitting, always in your face. ‘Fabulous spoken-word ... audience were in tears of laughter.’ (Daily Record). ‘Compelling’ (List). ‘Sometimes Truth hurts’ (H.Rollins). Sold-out 2008/10/11. www.henryrollins.com.
Venue description: Edinburgh's leading live music venue offers classical, jazz, blues, pop, rock, world, folk and comedy in the intimate surroundings of a converted Georgian church. www.thequeenshall.net

Title: Jamie Demetriou's People Day (and Special Guests)
Description: Character comedy from the character comedian who dares to say what everybody's thinking/saying. And some lovely guests. ‘The absolute highlight in a show full of highlights’ ***** (Skinny). ***** (ThreeWeeks). ***** (FreshAir.org.uk). @mcmetriou.
Venue description: Dragonfly is a unique cocktail lounge experience. Throughout our multi award-winning interior of minimalistic clutter, colonial treats and retro fun lie a number of lounge retreats for decadent cocktail action. Come join us for free comedy throughout the festival.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: How the World Wags
Description: The best thing to come out of Croydon since rioting. How not to hack a celebrity's voicemail, the ultimate gathering of Scandinavian detectives, and many more... A plethora of sketches from three-time Empire 60s finalists.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Seussical
Description: Seussical - a family musical with dazzling costumes and exciting music. Dr. Seuss' best-loved characters are brought together in one magical adventure. Performed by the cast of our award-winning London production, Seussical is not to be missed. www.seussical2012.moonfruit.com.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: A Romance of Asian and Western Classical Voice
Description: East meets west in the powerful, lilting voice of versatile soprano Khor Ai Ming. In this folk-inspired programme, she combines western classical training and Asian life experience to bring you an intimate selection.
Venue description: the SpaceUK present another high calibre venue. This wonderfully-located space between Bristo Square and the Pleasance offers a high brow alternative to the traditional fringe venues. Ideal for Stand-Up, Chat, Music (bands), A Capella, Improv, Sketch and Cabaret.

Title: Scottish Comedian of the Year 2011 - Jamie Dalgleish
Description: ‘A deserving winner ... the assured Dalgleish charmed the crowd ... merciless' (Scotsman). 'Comic timing of Jack Milroy and Hector Nicol, with a big dollop of Kevin Bridges thrown in for good measure.' (Glaswegian).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Dennis O'Donnell
Subtitle: WARDING OFF SOME DARK MEMORIES
Description: In 2000 Dennis O’Donnell was approached to work as an orderly in the intensive psychiatric care unit of a large hospital in central Scotland. The Locked Ward sets out to reveal the true story of a life divided by fear and care, and by violence and compassion, recounting the stories of the patients, and those of the friends he made in the unit over seven years. Chaired by author John Burnside.

Title: Amused Moose Comedy Awards Showcases
Description: Grab your hot tickets to talent spot this year's stellar crop of industry approved breakthrough comedians, plus some discovered before who are now rather famous!  Every showcase is different, so keep coming back. www.amusedmoose.com/shows.
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Propaganda
Description: Propaganda is the UK's biggest indie night, attracting over 25,000 people a week to its 21 club nights across five countries!
Venue description:
The HMV Picture House is Edinburgh's best venue in which to experience live music and clubs. 
\nThe lovingly restored Caledonian cinema on Lothian Road - you may remember it as the Caley Palais - is perfect for performers and audience alike.

Title: Visual Aids
Description: Two comics duke it out using slides, props, videos and even words in a heroic battle to win comedy! ‘Completely bizarre - deadpan, yet totally off the wall ... a real highlight’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘Pick of the acts’ (Londonisfunny.com).
Artist: Ali Brice and David Bussell / PBH’s Free Fringe
Venue description: Rush Bar is one of Edinburgh's most popular student and backpacker bars. Open 7 days from 1pm until 3am throughout the festival, the bar also plays host to Beer Pong Sundays, Monday Live Sessions and Karaoke Tuesdays and an amazing party atmosphere not to be missed. 18+ only.

Title: How to Tour Your Show in the UK
Description: Develop your show after the Fringe with focus on touring in the UK. A panel of experts will discuss the benefits, complexities and logistics of touring theatre in the UK.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Chris Difford and Norman Lovett: It's All About Me!
Description: Squeeze lyricist and legend Chris Difford joins forces with Red Dwarf star and stand-up comedian Norman Lovett for an evening of great songs, tall tales and big laughs.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: This Comedy Mob Belongs to Lionel Richie
Description: Come and be part of a mass guerrilla comedy sketch - a comedy mob. Meet in Princes Street Gardens by the Scott Monument (the gothic spire) and await instructions at 2.30pm.
Venue description: The Scott Monument was built to commemorate Sir Walter Scott, one of Scotland's greatest novelists. The monument is 200ft high; climb 287 steps up the spiral internal staircase to four levels to see unrivalled views of Edinburgh's historic Old and New Towns.
Venue accessibility: \nNot accessible to wheelchair users. No accessible WC.

Title: Once On This Island
Description: This critically acclaimed company (ENDA winners 2008, 2009, 2010) present a vibrant and stunning musical set in the Caribbean Sea in a story of life, pain, love, grief, faith and hope echoing Romeo and Juliet.
Venue description: Inverleith Church Hall has been the setting for Forth Children's Theatre Productions for the past three decades and has hosted many colourful productions from the young, talented cast of this multi-award-winning company, now in their 34th year!

Title: Some Small Love Story
Description: Intimate and honest, two tales of passion and heartbreak woven together. Spellbinding music. Directed by Noreen Kershaw (Coronation Street, River City, Shameless). 'Deeply dynamic … packs real emotional punch' **** (WhatsOnStage.com). 'Beautiful' (Lyn Gardner, Guardian). #LittleFest. www.hartshornhook.com.
Artist: Hartshorn - Hook Productions #LittleFest at C nova
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Our Island
Description: Three characters are washed up on an island... Can they overcome their fears to work together and share their new home? With physical theatre, comedy and music, this is an international collaboration about international collaboration! www.kippertietheatre.com. www.itheatre.org.
Artist: Kipper Tie Theatre and I Theatre (Singapore) with C theatre
Venue address: St Columba's by the Castle,Johnston Terrace
Venue description: C's original offshoot with alfresco chillout barbecue-bar. C4kids - the top children's shows. Showstopping musicals. Shakespeare played backwards, forwards, any way at all. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Bhundu Boy Rise Kagona
Description: Driving Afrobeat rhythms from legendary Zimbabwean Bhundu Boys guitarist Rise Kagona’s Jit Jive band! Catch his ‘sunny, intricate, agile yet rock-steady guitar’ and ‘incantatory call-and-response vocals, shifting between mellow, expansive warmth and deeper gravitas’ (Scotsman).
Artist: Rise Kagona and the Jit Jive Band
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: The World Fringe Fair
Description: Meet Fringes from across the globe to find out how you can take part in their festivals and get your work seen in the UK and internationally. Browse their tables and meet the organisers in person.
Artist: Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society, World Fringe and World Festival Network
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Shell
Description: In a remote part of the Scottish Highlands, a father and daughter live and work at a small petrol station. They spend their days tending to domestic chores and to the needs of rare passing motorists. At night they are forced together by the cold and by their loneliness. An intense story of two people who struggle to keep their longings for freedom under control, set against a beautiful and remote landscape that reflects their isolation back at them.

Title: Masterclass with David Hewson
Subtitle: MAKING A KILLING
Description: It's not uncommon for a hit TV series to be based on a bestselling novel, but David Hewson is turning this formula on its head with a new novel based on BBC4’s The Killing. In this masterclass, the bestselling author offers a practical guide on how he deconstructed 20 hours of television into one novel, and how he drew unusual inspiration from an earlier project: rewriting Macbeth as an audiobook.

Title: Alpine Horn with Flange Krammer - Free
Description: Olympic skiing sensation and world class ladies’ man, Flange Krammer, brings his internationally renowned lecture on the importance of squat thrusts in ski training to Edinburgh. Character comedy.
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
Description: A punchy one-hour adaptation of Shakespeare's classic set in post-apocalyptic dystopia. This famous comedy rises reborn from the ashes like the radioactive flowers that make ‘man or woman madly dote upon next live creature it sees’.
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Old Saint Paul's Festival Masses
Description: Traditional Catholic Anglican liturgy in this historic church with its renowned choir and organ. Music includes Missa Bell’ Amfitrit’ altera (Lassus), Missa brevis (Raymond Monelle) and Messe solennelle (Vierne). Further details: www.osp.org.uk or venue leaflet.
Venue description: Historic Anglican church in the Catholic tradition. The 'hidden gem' of the Old Town, with numerous features of architectural and artistic interest, and Father Willis organ; descriptive leaflets available. Open daily 08:30-17:45 to visit, or for peace and stillness.

Title: No Pants Thursday: T'il Death Do Us Party
Description: NPT are a late-night Irish sketch group. The show contains little death, and less partying.'NPT are fantastic any day of the week and even if you are wearing pants.' ****(ThreeWeeks).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: All About the Craic
Description: Showcasing four of the brightest stand-up comedians Ireland has to offer! Including special guests every day. This free show has something for everyone so why not come along and see why Irish comedy at its best!
Artist: Close To The Bone Comedy Club
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items ... Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: Katianna Was Here
Description: Katianna Robinson - life changes in a way no one would wish, and yet her life begins to have a purpose and meaning that goes beyond herself, to friends and family alike.
Venue: Leith on the Fringe @ Out of the Blue Drill Hall
Venue description: A vibrant, multi-arts venue. A hub for aerial work, circus, dance and physical theatre. LOTF offers a range of workshops to compliment our program this year, to book, or for more information visit www.leithonthefringe.com. Cafe and licensed bar open Mon-Sun 10:00-22:00. LOTF will run for the first 2 weeks of the Fringe - 3rd - 19th August
Venue accessibility:
24789
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space), assistance dogs welcome. Some performances are: Signed, captioned.

Title: You Obviously Know What I'm Talking About
Description: Topsy-turvy-tale about those days when if anything can go wrong it will and inevitably at the worst possible moment. Welcome to a day in the life of Winfield Scott-Boring. Visually fantastical. Deeply poignant.
Artist: How It Ended Productions / Escalator East to Edinburgh
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Graduates Essentials: How to Launch Your Career
Description: From agents to auditions, marketing your skills to managing your finances, this session will give you essential advice to help your career take off in the right direction.
Artist: The Stage Events with Jennifer Resichel
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: The House of Shadows
Description: The Learned Man is obsessed with telling a story that is good and true and beautiful to gain entrance to the Cult of Beauty, but his Shadow breaks free and threatens to consume his humanity.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Paul McCaffrey: Pills'n'Thrills and Belly Laughs
Description: You can take the boy out of Glastonbury... Paul reunites his mates at a festival. What could possibly go wrong? 'Charisma and success written all over him' (Evening Standard).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Impro-Slam
Subtitle: PACKING A PUNCH WITH POETRY
Description: Created in partnership with Masters students for their Festival Events Tourism course at Edinburgh Napier University, Impro-Slam promises to be a night of the unexpected, pitting performance poets against each other to inspire, entertain and improvise before the audience and judges. Four poets, three rounds but there can only be one winner! Fast, furious and fun.

Title: Meet the Buttons Family with Vivian French & Sue Heap
Description: Writer Vivian French and author-illustrator Sue Heap introduce their new series of six picture books all about the Buttons family. Each tale looks at a different first experience for little people from first day at playschool to staying with grandparents for the first time. Vivian tells the stories as Sue draws all the characters. The perfect event for a first-time visit to the Book Festival!

Title: Writing Workshop
Subtitle: THE POWER AND THE STORY
Description: The first need for writing fiction is to understand where the nub of your tale lies. Then you can structure it. Award-winning novelist Jonathan Falla is teaching director of the St Andrews Creative Writing summer school, and has long experience of teasing out the beating heart of stories. This workshop is based on his book The Craft of Fiction.

Title: Absolutely Romantic
Description: Adrian Sims (piano) returns to Edinburgh to perform virtuoso favourites by Rachmaninov, Liszt, Strauss and Mendlessohn.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Laughing Horse Free Comedy Selection
Description: A selection of the best in new comedy at the Fringe, alongside some top headliners picked from Fringe shows, national competitions and around the world. And it's free! Three times a night! Line-ups - www.freefestival.co.uk.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Dance Interrogations
Description: Dance Interrogations is a real-time performance experience, bringing the audience into forensic range of the dancing body. Her surfaces animated by fable and fiasco, projected image and prophetic gibberish, an awkward adagio between things real and imagined.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Oliver Twisted with J D Sharpe
Description: J D Sharpe has written a clever, authentic reimagining of Dickens’ classic, Oliver Twist. In this pacy, horror make-over, Oliver is a powerful warlock and evil forces want to turn him to the dark side. There’s action and gore and J D never strays from the original plot or key characters. Come along and find out why she was inspired to adapt the story and why she’s a fan of Dickens. Keep your ticket as it entitles you to half price entry to The Edinburgh Dungeon; they provided the ghoulish props for this event (www.thedungeons.co.uk).

Title: Paul Chowdhry - What's Happening White People
Description: Star of C4's Stand Up for the Week returns with his new show. Strap yourself in for this hard-hitting, unique take on modern Britain. Good clean fun for all the family. No under 16s. www.offthekerb.co.uk.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Amusements
Description: Returning from their acclaimed sell-out show at Fringe 2011, Total Theatre Award nominees Sleepwalk Collective present their new work Amusements, an intensely sensorial and unsettlingly voyeuristic one-woman headphone-theatre spectacular, backroom carnival ride, lo-fi sci-fi pleasure machine. www.sleepwalkcollective.com.
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Alex T Smith
Description: When Alex T Smith was a little boy he wanted to be a chef, a rabbit or a children’s book illustrator. Guess which path he chose? Let Alex introduce you to Ella, the ladybird Cinderella from his brand new picture book. He shows you how to draw your very own Ella then you'll be let loose to decorate her in whatever style you choose! Perhaps you can create her some sparkly spectacles?

Title: Mega Mash-Ups with Nikalas Catlow & Tim Wesson
Description: Do you like to read bonkers stories with gorillas and robots, dinosaurs and Romans, mad scientists and aliens? And have you ever been tempted to doodle on a book but know you would get into big trouble? Well, come and meet Nikalas Catlow and Tim Wesson, creators of the Mega Mash-Up books. They give you a great adventure story, wacky illustrations and plenty of space for you to add your own ideas too. Perfect.

Title: Andrew Maxwell: That's the Spirit
Description: Maxwell returns after 2011’s Edinburgh Comedy Award nomination. You’ve seen him on Wall of Fame, Live At The Apollo and Celebrity Juice - now see him live. 'Fiercely funny and utterly invigorating' (Times).
Artist: Get Comedy by arrangement with United Agents
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579

Title: Sean Hughes - Life Becomes Noises
Description: Dealing with his dad's death the only way Sean can, this hilarious yet poignant tale looks at the lighter side of dying, how ridiculous life is and how quickly it can be taken away.
Artist: Bound and Gagged Comedy by Arrangement With Old Man Management
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Mark Watson: The Information
Description: Seen on numerous TV shows and fresh from a sell-out Australian tour, considers the internet's effect on humanity. Tells jokes in the process. Email markwatsonspreview2012@gmail.com for pre-show briefing. ** * * * (Chortle.com, Festmag.co.uk, List, Metro).
Artist: Phil McIntyre Entertainments by arrangement with Lisa Thomas Management

024579

Title: The Beast
Description: Award-winning Australian theatre maker Stuart Bowden, 'narrative ingenuity and boundless charm' **** (Metro), returns with a poignant and playful tale. The Beast will touch your heart and then tickle it (in a non life-threatening way).
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Antigone
Description: Atmospheric reworking of the Sophocles classic. In the air raid shelter in 1943 the nightly residents gather to hear the tale of Antigone, a self-willed little beast, who would defy Creon and will die for it. Tense, energetic tragedy.
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Rebus - Secret Edinburgh
Description: Examine best-selling crime writer Ian Rankin's Edinburgh and experience Scotland's mysterious history. Politics, corruption, power and murder in the real Rebus locations. Unusual Edinburgh stories and stunning Old Town views. Readings from the books included. See www.rebustours.com.
Venue description: The Royal Oak is Edinburgh's premiere traditional music and folksinging howff. Rub shoulders with the top names in folk music, join in or just sit and listen; sample a cask ale or a fine malt and enjoy the convivial atmosphere.

Title: Richard Wiseman: Psychobabble
Description: Six shows only! Best-selling author, psychologist and magician Richard Wiseman rummages around in your mind. Discover how to tell lies, read thoughts and transform a tea towel into a chicken. Several laughs. Some swearing. No powerpoint.
Venue description: At the heart of Canongate on the Royal Mile, the Canon's Gait is an historic, recently redecorated bar serving lunches, real ale and an extensive selection of malt whiskies. Comfortable seating and relaxed, friendly atmosphere to enjoy a drink between shows.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Geoff the Entertainer
Description: Geoff and his dog have been entertaining people on the streets for over 20 years. Now they bring their joyful show indoors for the first time. Celebrate Geoff’s incredible life with singing, dancing and chess. 'Geoff' (Chortle.co.uk).
Artist: Lee Fenwick / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue: The Stand Comedy Club III & IV
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue, Stand III is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand IV an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Life or Something Like It - Free
Description: Two for one. Keelan described as the female John Cooper Clarke by her mate Pauline. Mooney, political, satirical, singer/songwriter goes from feisty radical to Caprice in a fleece in 60 seconds.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Captain Taylor's Coffee House
Venue description: A stylish and relaxing licensed cafe, and a brand new Fringe venue offering a mixture of quality food and drink, and free shows throughout the day - all right in the heart of Edinburgh, just off of the Royal Mile.

Title: Rob Deering's Beat This
Description: 'Employing live music mash-ups, megamixes (not enough of them nowadays) and music trivia, the nimble-fingered Deering pits comedians and the audience against each other' (Comedy Central). New show and top-notch guests every night. Listings - twitter@DeeringRob
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Sean Borodale & William Letford
Subtitle: ACCESSIBLE AND INNOVATIVE LINES MEN
Description: Two of the hottest young poets on the circuit lock horns here. William Letford’s Bevel is an accessible and rich collection which succeeds in being both Scottish and universal. Sean Borodale’s debut is a daring portrait of life as an apiarist. Bee Journal chronicles the life of a hive, from its small nucleus on day one to the capture of a swarm two years later.

Title: Chris Cooper
Subtitle: CAN CHEATING PROSPER?
Description: Top biochemist Chris Cooper looks at the science behind drugs in sport with Run, Swim, Throw, Cheat. Using biochemistry, physiology and anatomy, he looks at what stops us running faster or jumping higher and explains why certain substances are used and whether they truly have an effect. Exploring the moral, political and ethical issues, Cooper addresses the big question: what constitutes cheating?

Title: Jim Smallman: Let's Be Friends
Description: Award-winning comedian Jim Smallman (BBC 5Live's Fighting Talk) has dedicated his life to work, losing friends along the way. Now he wants new ones, and he's looking at you. ***** (NewCurrent.com). 'Wonderfully gritty' (Guardian).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Belt Up Theatre's A Little Princess
Description: Frances Hodgson Burnett's classic novel. Princess to pauper: listen to Sara's tales, join her in play, relish in the magic and the tragic beauty of her story. 'Edinburgh Fringe royalty' (Time Out). www.beltuptheatre.com.
Artist: Belt Up Theatre and Jethro Compton Ltd
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Club Noir Burlesque - The Games
Description: World's biggest burlesque club - up to 2,000 people. Biggest cabaret event at the Fringe. Lavish, glamorous, risqué. Olympic-themed shows - international sexploits. ‘Top 10 cabaret nights’ (Travel Channel USA). 'UK's best burlesque nights' (Times). www.clubnoir.co.uk.
Venue description:
The HMV Picture House is Edinburgh's best venue in which to experience live music and clubs. 
\nThe lovingly restored Caledonian cinema on Lothian Road - you may remember it as the Caley Palais - is perfect for performers and audience alike.

Title: Paul Broda with Tam Dalyell
Subtitle: BOTH MY FATHERS WERE SPIES
Description: Professor Paul Broda grew up with a father, and then a stepfather, who both passed Allied secrets about atomic weapons to the Soviet Union in 1942. One of those men was Allan Nunn May, who was jailed and vilified. In this event Broda discusses with Tam Dalyell his view that they both believed the USSR could prevent the march of fascism. They may also, he argues, have helped avert nuclear war.

Title: Debate: Rethinking Islam
Subtitle: IS RADICAL ISLAM THE WORLD’S GREATEST THREAT?
Description: Tony Blair described radical Islam as ‘the world’s greatest threat’. Others argue that the widespread embracing of Islam has generally been thanks to its tolerance and its mission to deliver justice. The reality is more nuanced with recent history requiring us to re-evaluate our hopes and fears for the future. Mustafa Cerić, Grand Mufti of Bosnia and Herzegovina, academic Dilip Hiro and Egyptian author Parker Bilal (pen name Jamal Mahjoub) present perspectives from Europe and Afghanistan, Pakistan and India. Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Title: Dirty Thirties

Title: Free Photo Exhibition – Wildlife, Landscapes and Townscapes
Description: Returning to the Fringe with an exciting display of photographs of Scotland’s capital as well as landscapes and townscapes, and wildlife images. We look forward to welcoming you to this friendly exhibition.

Title: Denise Mina

In the latest affair, Gods And Beasts, DS Morrow investigates the senseless murder of an old man in a post office and proceeds to uncover blackmail, political chicanery and a bag of untraceable cash.

Title: Magical Mice with Tracey Corderoy
Description: Join picture book author Tracey Corderoy as she reads from her new book, Monty and Milli, a delightful tale of a big brother frustrated by his younger sister’s determination to do everything he does. There will be magic tricks, stories, pictures and exciting things to make and do.

Title: Kit and McConnel

Title: Amy Plum

Kate is sixteen and moves to Paris after her parents' death. She falls for Vincent, who she discovers is not the typical French teenager he appears. Love, mystery and horror combine in the city where dreams are sometimes the same as reality. Join Amy for talk of immortals, zombies and Paris.

Title: Thomas Nelstrop: Great(ish) Hits
Description: A barnstorming debut solo hour from a man who has quite literally been on television. This riotous one-man music festival is a euphoric mix of character comedy and songs. 'Hilarious' (Sun). 'Gleefully vicious' (NME).

Title: Dana Alexander: Breaking Through

Title: Give Me a Tune
Description: Chris Clark, on a journey through the great American songbook (Sinatra, Bennett, all your favourites) with captivating vocals, a classy piano trio and humorous anecdotes. Who said what and to whom? And what's a dummy lyric?
Venue description: A funky modern bar close to the Playhouse Theatre, just off famous Broughton Street down a lane. This popular and inviting bar also has a beer garden that hosts BBQs in the summer months, providing a buzzing atmosphere.

Title: Mugging Chickens

Title: Collision

Title: A C Grayling
Subtitle: THINKING ANEW: A MIND FOR THE 21ST CENTURY
Description: Since he published his 'secular bible', The Good Book, last year A C Grayling has been busy launching his own university. It's an audacious idea that has brought many plaudits as well as controversy. In this unmissable event Grayling outlines his views on the moral and philosophical beliefs underpinning a good university education, drawing on The Good Book to illustrate his ideas.

Title: The Silky Pair: Happy to Help (Plus Special Guests)
Description: Female duo sells sketches and songs in their comedy shop. 'Slick, sexy and stunningly original. Damn funny too.' (BBC Radio Scotland, Jeff Zycinski). 'Jokes are consistent winners and songs well-crafted little gems.' (EdinburghGuide.com).

Title: The  Boy With Tape On His Face - More Tape
Description: Brand new show! As seen on The Royal Variety Performance, BBC2’s Comedy Prom and BBC3’s Live at the Fringe. ‘Spectacular! Hysterically funny – fight for a ticket!’ ***** (TimeOut).

Title: The Unspeakable Act
Description: Adolescent anxiety inspires a “love that dare not speak its name” in Dan Sallitt’s frank and patient family drama. Jackie, a New York suburban teen, lives at home with her withdrawn, but loving, widow mother, her sister and her older brother, Matthew, with whom she just so happens to be properly, deeply in love. But Matthew’s about to bring round his first girlfriend, and will shortly be leaving for college…

Title: Michael Gerard Bauer
Description: Australian author Michael Gerard Bauer brings us his novel from down-under, Don’t Call Me Ishmael, a sensitive yet funny look at how one boy deals with being tormented by a school bully. How Ishmael copes, the friends he makes and the embarrassment, fear and the triumphs he experiences, combine to create a compelling story. Michael has created a truly authentic voice for Ishmael and his wry telling of the story shows a deep understanding of what it’s like to be a bully’s target.

Title: Anon(ymous)
Description: UK premiere of a modern retelling of Homer's Odyssey. With a goddess as his guide, a young refugee must use his instincts to survive a harsh journey to be reunited with his mother and his home. www.pepperdinedrama.com.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Seeking help from the people he once knew in Incheon, the writer gradually finds himself forced to confront the painful high-school incident that scarred his psyche and furnished the unacknowledged inspiration for his work. A hard-hitting debut feature from director Yang Jung-ho.

Title: When Alice (Cooper) Met (Prince) Harry
Description: Fifi was never meant to be the star, but today she is. A playful and touching physical comedy; an intelligent fusion of sincerity and humour with flavours of Amelie and BBC comedy. ‘Outstanding' (ArtsHub.com.au).

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: HUMAN RIGHTS IN RUSSIA
Description: Human rights defenders and independent journalists face threats, harassment and attacks in Russia. Freedom of assembly and expression also come under attack. Today’s Book Festival authors read extracts from works by persecuted writers such as Galina Starovoitova, an outspoken Russian MP who was assassinated in 1998, and journalist Anastasia Baburova, shot dead in 2009 by a contract killer in Moscow. Reading today: Tom Bullough, Cynthia Rogerson, Natasha Farrant and Richard Milward.

Description: Following his critically acclaimed 2011 sell-out tour, ’The Oscar Wilde of Comedy’, Dylan Moran returns to the Festival for two dates only. ‘In a class of its own’ (Independent). ‘Razor Sharp’ (Times).

Title: The Harmonettes Go Into Orbit

Title: Mozart: The Impresario
Description: Mozart's fast-paced comedy tracking the highs and lows of a struggling opera house. With a cast of rising operatic talent and a new, English libretto written by the Cambridge Footlights' president, this one-off collaboration cannot be missed.

It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. On today: Stories with Edinburgh For Under Fives.

Title: Leaves on the Line
Description: Ali Shahrukhi's hilarious take on the things we'd never dream could bring life to a grinding standstill ... but do! Learn to laugh at those problems that blindside us as we pumice our feet in the bath.
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, the Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11am-2am. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.

Code: In Person: Masterclass with Wang Bing
Title: In Person: Masterclass with Wang Bing
Description: From his first film, West of the Tracks (2003), to his latest work, Wang Bing has brought rigour and compassion to the archaeology of the physical and social changes China has undergone since the Cultural Revolution. Not only a pivotal figure in Chinese documentary filmmaking, Wang is an artist whose work with time and space marks him as one of the most significant filmmakers of our time. At this masterclass, co-sponsored with the Scottish Documentary Institute, Wang will share his insights. Be sure also to see Wang’s Fengming: A Chinese Memoir, The Ditch, and Coal Money, all screening at EIFF.

Title: Jeremy Strong
Description: You can’t beat a Jeremy Strong event to brighten your day and make you laugh. And this will be no exception. Join Jeremy and Streaker, the ‘Hundred-Mile an-Hour Dog’, as he goes for gold (that’s Streaker, not Jeremy) and hear about the new comic book adventure for Cartoon Kid and all his superhero friends.

Title: Sally Grindley
Description: Author of over 130 books, Sally Grindley offers a lively, interactive event all about International Rescue, her brand new series of adventure books written in collaboration with the Zoological Society of London, and featuring a family who travel around the globe to help save endangered animals. Sally has always been fascinated by animals and so jumped at the chance of writing an animal adventure series and if you too love animals, you’ll love this event.

Title: Eccentronic Presents: We Won't Rock You - Free
Description: Eccentronic (John Callaghan and Hypnotique) present their first ‘mainstream musical’ featuring eccentric, electronic, enthralling songs about time-wasting, socks and visiting Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch. Philip’s irreverent take on traditional tales is full of charming, funny and slightly smelly characters. Come and find out more.

Title: Normal
