Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: BBC: The Festival Cafe
Description: The cream of the talent from all the Edinburgh festivals join Janice Forsyth and Clare English. Prepare to be entertained by the sharpest minds and the top performers in town. Witty, sharp and frequently funny.
Venue address: Corner of Potterrow and Marshall Street,Edinburgh
Venue description: Experience the best of the BBC under one roof and a taster of all the delights of the Fringe. Join us at Venue 25 for BBC shows, big names, stand-up every night plus masterclasses from BBC Radio, TV and Online. Free events are ticketed via a random draw. To enter the draw please use the show website link: bbc.co.uk/tickets.

Title: The  Indescribable Phenomenon
Description: A bizarre and beautiful true story of one remarkable woman in a world of mad scientists, escapologists, fraudsters and thieves. This play incorporates magic and mind reading as life, death, belief and illusion entwine.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Kid-Thing
Description: The Zellner brothers bring their trademark deadpan humour to a poignant and disturbing tale of growing up wild. Somewhere in rural America, 10-year-old Annie lives with her divorced father, who is even more incompetent at parenting than he is at goat farming. Left to her own devices, Annie wanders the nearby town and woods, committing random acts of anarchic destructiveness, until she forms a relationship with a woman trapped in a well. “Bracingly original… a female trailer-trash 400 Blows”. (Jonathan Romney, Screen Daily)

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning events for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. On today: Stories with Edinburgh For Under Fives.

Title: Home for the Weekend
Description: “An elegant, economical and superbly acted mapping of psychological undercurrents and (not always explicit) family relations”. (Jonathan Romney, Screen Daily)

Title: Blues!
Description: 90 years of blues, 60 minutes to play it. From delta blues to Stevie Ray Vaughan, Blues! is a gig covering the history of the genre that is sure to get your mojo working. www.theblueswater.com. ***** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Silky: Nut Allegory
Description: Against 7,840 other comedians, some Olympics, weather, and entropy, you need something special in your bag. I found mine while showering. Here’s what happened next. ‘Very, very funny‘ (John Bishop). ‘Funny and clever’ (Tim Minchin). ‘Brilliant’ (Metro).
Warnings: 14+. Must be accompanied by an adult
Venue description: Round the corner, our little sister club is in its thirteenth year. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area.

Title: Rob James: Magicana
Description: A retro-modern magic show. Elegant sleight of hand, baffling magical apparatus and inexplicable illusions presented with humour and flair. 'Beautifully crafted show ... Wowed the audience.' (Magicseen Magazine). www.magicanashow.com.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Zimbabwe Sculptures
Description: Vhukutiwa Gallery returns for its 10th exhibition of sculpture, presenting a haunting range of work, all with a remarkable tactile quality evoking a world part natural, part spirit-oriented, from some of the finest sculptors in the world.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Singing a Different Song
Description: Two evenings with seasoned singer/songwriters who put their individual slant on songs that evoke aspects of our psychological, emotional and political lives. On the first night, expect to join in. On the second night, don't.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Talkfest Two 2012
Description: Lively and fascinating discussions, expertly chaired by Scotland’s leading playwrights. Dramatising Catastrophe - What goes into transferring dramatic live events to the stage? The Theatre of Technology - Is technology changing the way we create theatre?
Artist: Playwrights' Studio, Scotland, Made in Scotland, Traverse Theatre
Venue description: Scotland's new writing theatre 'is the festival's most prestigious home of serious drama' (New York Times) and a multiple Fringe First and Herald Angel award winner. 'The main hub of festival-focussed action during August' (List).

Title: Project Adorno's Record Collection
Description: Songs about 8-bit computer games, library stamps and Newsnight. Cross between Brel, Pet Shop Boys and Camberwick Green. Retro-futurist visionaries with stylophones in their hands and Charles Aznavour on their headphones. ‘Nerd heaven’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com). www.projectadorno.net.
Venue description: Shanghai @ Le Monde, George Street is a brand new Free Fringe venue for 2012. Le Monde is open 8am- 3am and serves food till late. No street level disabled access available. Please contact venue for more information.
Venue accessibility:
49
\nAssistance dogs welcome, accessible WC

Title: Adam Larter: Happy New Year - A Free Comedy Show
Description: An insane, musical, exploding, puppeting, dramatic comedy count-down to midnight with oddball stand-up Adam Larter. ‘The sheer volume of his daft ideas is stunning ... a very disorganised genius’ **** (Skinny, 2011).
Artist: Adam Larter / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Captain Taylor's Coffee House
Venue description: A stylish and relaxing licensed cafe, and a brand new Fringe venue offering a mixture of quality food and drink, and free shows throughout the day - all right in the heart of Edinburgh, just off of the Royal Mile.

Title: The  Gospel According to Mr Niz
Description: Guitarist and enthusiastic sinner Stuart Nisbet presents a radical reworking of 50's gospel quartet material with Nico Bruce on string bass – no sermons, no harmonies, no tambourines, but all the groove and soul.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Mermaids and Meanies with Moira Munro
Description: The best thing about stories is the characters. Kittens don't have to be cute, mermaids don't have to be wet and we all love meanies don’t we? Characters are fun to imagine and to draw. Writer and illustrator Moira Munro brings you the Finger of Doom and other weird and wonderful ways to create your own awesome characters.

Title: Fringe Festivals Around the World
Description: A once-a-year chance to meet and hear from Fringe directors from around the world. Join the discussion and get the global insights, hear why they're important and how they differ. A great networking opportunity.
Artist: World Festival Network and World Fringe
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: The Golden Cowpat
Description: Join naughty cow Betty and her farmer Hector on their magical adventure. With breathtaking storytelling and catchy folk music, Tucked In return following last year's five-star favourite, Tim and Light. 'Spellbinding' (Stage).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Minu1s
Description: A blend of captivating dance works that portray an infectious energy and an unfussy style. Diverse and innovative, drawing upon the performers’ individuality, physicality and raw vitality. 'JMUpstart have attitude, daring and promise' (ThreeWeeks). 'Entertaining and inspiring' (BroadwayBaby.com).
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: The Joke Circus - Free
Description: Round up, round up for free stand-up of the likes you've never seen! Be amazed by one-liners, witness incredible feats of storytelling and experience death-defying self-deprecation. (Disclaimer: Not a real circus in any way.)
Venue description:
Bannermans is one of Edinburgh's premier live music venues, located in the heart of the historic Old Town. With live music six nights a week, and a host of other events constantly on the go, it's proved a firm favourite with locals and tourists for many years now.
\nOpen 12pm till 1am every day, apart from Sunday when we open at 12.30pm.

Title: Anthropoetry
Description: BBC R4 Slam Champion Ben Mellor takes you on a stand-up poetry and music fuelled tour around the body, attempting to get the measure of modern life through anatomical analogy. With sounds, beats, beeps and whistles by Dan Steele.
Venue description: Finger's piano bar is an institution established in the early 80s. During the Free Fringe shows Finger's turns into one of the best cosmopolitan venues in Edinburgh. An experience not to be missed! Opening hours 2pm till 5am. No disabled access.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: The  Jumblies
Description: 'Far and few, far and few, are the lands where the Jumblies live.' A musical adventure into Lear's nonsensical world featuring the Owl, the Pussycat and their friends! A fun-filled voyage about friendship, home and growing up.
Venue description: the SpaceUK present another high calibre venue. This wonderfully-located space between Bristo Square and the Pleasance offers a high brow alternative to the traditional fringe venues. Ideal for Stand-Up, Chat, Music (bands), A Capella, Improv, Sketch and Cabaret.

Title: Miss Julie
Description: We are a small theatre company based on passion, spontaneity and ensemble work. We are a non-profitable company that produces five-star performances. So come and have all your senses excited on the ride of your life!
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Steve Barlow & Steve Skidmore
Description: Often referred to as The Two Steves, Steve Barlow and Steve Skidmore are prolific writers who have been entertaining audiences worldwide with their crazy double act for over two decades. They are back with Action Dogs, the coolest canines around! Join the magnificent mutts as they battle to save helpless humans from the evil schemes of their fiendish arch-enemy Katmanchew! A real doggie treat that will keep your nose wet and your tail wagging.

Title: Through the Looking Screen
Description: A brand new one-woman comedy opera by Anne Chmelewsky about a single girl's pursuit for love on social networks. Starring Clare Presland. 'Mesmerising, has an intensity that almost sears the flesh' (Times).
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Marcus Brigstocke: The Brig Society EXTRA SHOW
Description: No less than the total restructuring of every aspect of life in Britain organised through the medium of jokes. See this show and Win! a free hospital or school! Second prize: a major High Street bank.
Artist: Off The Kerb Productions in association with Corduroy Productions
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound presents the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces The Hall, Rainy and the Baillie.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nWheelchair accessible except for Baillie Room, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: The SomeNews Live Show - Free
Description: Would you shoot a burglar? Which of Jedward would you eat first in a celebrity version of the film Alive? Find out the answers at the SomeNews Live Show.  See www.somenews.co.uk.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Captain Taylor's Coffee House
Venue description: A stylish and relaxing licensed cafe, and a brand new Fringe venue offering a mixture of quality food and drink, and free shows throughout the day - all right in the heart of Edinburgh, just off of the Royal Mile.

Title: Faust/us
Description: The tragic history of Doctor Faustus, notorious magician and necromancer. World premier of innovative new solo version of the classic tale of a man who sold his soul. Fusing animation, mixed media, and physical theatre. Join us. www.dbs-productions.co.uk.
Warnings: Strobing Images partial nudity (multimedia projection not live), strobing images,
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: The Last Dragon Chronicles with Chris d'Lacey
Description: Chris d’Lacey tells you all about The Fire Ascending, the next exciting instalment in his breathtaking The Last Dragon Chronicles series. Get to know more about hero David Rain, his quest to save the tear of the last dragon and his thrilling endeavours to protect mankind and dragons from evil forces.

Title: Sir Charlie Stinky Socks with Kristina Stephenson
Description: It’s time for the honourable, feisty and courageous young hero, Sir Charlie Stinky Socks to return to Edinburgh and this time to discover the secret of the pitiful sobbing coming from the rumbling, grumbling castle. Join Kristina Stephenson for music and songs and one more of her now legendary, dramatic Book Festival appearances.

Code: Fukushima: Memories of the Lost Landscape
Title: Fukushima: Memories of the Lost Landscape
Description: Tokyo-based documentary filmmaker Yojyu Matsubayashi, anxious to document the tragedy of the tsunami in northeast Japan and the nuclear disaster at Fukushima, won the trust of the Tanakas, a middle-aged couple working to help people forced to evacuate their homes in the town of Minami-soma. Matsubayashi’s portrait of the Tanakas’ dedication and of the varying experiences and emotions of the evacuees creates a compelling image of loss and resilience.

Title: Jazz Bar Music
Description: Edinburgh's famous, multiple award-winning atmospheric music venue hosts all kinds of shows all day from 1pm, and stages its own fantastic programme of high-quality modern jazz, late-night funk/soul and electric bands, open to 5am! Programme: www.thejazzbar.co.uk.
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: The Aspidistras - Hi Noon!
Description: For two weeks only, catch semi-musical comedy duo The Aspidistras on their annual Edinburgh holiday/business trip. Crisps provided. **** 'Fantastically funny' (Big Issue Scotland). **** 'Delightful' (ThreeWeeks) 'Leaves you feeling doused in sunshine' (Stage).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Hot
Description: Winner 2011 and nominee 2012 Best Cabaret Adelaide Fringe. After sell-out seasons the Yorkshire diva in a unitard returns with a tale of self-love gone mad and really proper theatre. 'A new shining star' **** (Scotsman). @DamselSophie #LittleFest. www.damselsophie.com.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers - A Celebration in Song
Description: Pick Yourself Up, Slap That Bass and Let's Face the Music and Dance. Pam Lawson returns with her 2011 sell-out show. So Let Yourself Go. Tap dancing is optional!
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: 24h
Description: 24 hours, non-stop. 24 life stories suspended in time. To break free, to get away from what appears to be, and what has been named. Extending time, theatrical experiment, filled by sounds, live painted pictures, improvisation and words. www.culture.pl/edinburgh.
Warnings: One ticket entitles you to to one entry and to stay as long as you like. Supported by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute www.culture.pl
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Annie Dalton
Description: Join Annie Dalton, writer of the popular Angels Unlimited series, for her latest story. If you like cats (especially magic cats) and cakes, then Moonbeans and the Dream Cafe is the book for you. Annie has created the first in a series of charming and heart-warming tales of a little girl with a magic kitten trying to fit in when she moves to a new town. Chaired by Vivian French.

Title: A Betrayal of Penguins - Harmed and Dangerous
Description: Comedy's sweatiest trio return with their most white-knuckle, frenetic hour yet, as they (consensually) take you places you've never been before. 'The Perfect Sketch Show' ***** (ThreeWeeks). 'Unmissable' (List).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: The Story of the BBC in Scotland
Subtitle: MAKING BROADCAST HISTORY
Description: Since its establishment in 1922 the BBC has continually asserted itself as one of the great British institutions at home and abroad. David Pat Walker has written an in-depth analysis of the history of BBC Scotland from its creation in 1923 through to its 50th anniversary. Mike Shaw, who produced one of the 50th anniversary programmes and worked closely with Walker on the book, discusses the development of the BBC in Scotland with James Boyle.

Title: Gavin Esler
Subtitle: TOP MAN
Description: Gavin Esler is one of Britain’s leading journalists and interviewers and in Lessons from the Top, he reveals that through the stories they tell, the most successful leaders educate, persuade and bring about change. Esler explains how creating a leadership story can promote success whether you’re running for the United States presidency or applying for a place at university. Chaired by Jamie Jauncey.

Title: Birds on a Wire
Description: A family living in Dust Bowl days in Texas display unbelievable resilience to stay and save their family farm from the ravages of dust, drought, grasshoppers and death. From disaster comes redemption and forgiveness.
Artist: Hardin-Simmons University - International Collegiate Theatre Festival
Venue description: One of the festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross genre performance makes this central venue a must for all.  Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Leo
Description: Winner of the Carol Tambor Best of Edinburgh Award 2011 returns! 'Leo is an eye-teasing, grin-inducing, deeply impressive work of sustained absurdist magic' (Time Out New York). 'A gravity-defying spectacle' (New York Times). 'Absolutely brilliant!' (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: The Roxy, a beautifully converted former chapel, is the latest addition to Assembly's growing list of venues.  Built in 1809 and located just north-east of our George Square hub, the Roxy houses three performances spaces; the 400 seat former nave Roxy Central, the 168 seat Roxy Upstairs and our 60 seat studio Roxy Downstairs.  The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Late 'n' Live
Description: The first and the best of late night shows on the Fringe presents its 26th year of unadulterated comedy mayhem. Expect the unexpected and enjoy live music from our fabulous house bands. Now a BBC1 Scotland TV series!
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Trojan Women
Description: Revenge, war, murder and sex. An action-packed Greek tragedy reinvented. This tense and brutal story will leave you on the edge of your seat. Not to be missed.
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Maria, 1968
Description: Noah is a clichéd writer and knows it. His girlfriend breaks up with him, he begins to write. A comedy that transports the audience in a playful, cinematic way between Noah's life and his wayward imagination.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Robert Burns: A Life in Words and Song
Description: A celebration of Scotland's national poet. Writer/raconteur Allan Foster brings to life the immortal bard’s story, joined in Captain's Bar by folk legend Andy Chung or the delightful singer Elizabeth Merritt.
Artist: Robert Burns: A Life in Words and Song
Venue description: A historic small bar with literary connections. Atmospheric and known for its great folk music.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: The Etherington Brothers' Comic Making Workshop
Description: After their storming performance last year, Lorenzo and Robin Etherington return with a new comic-making workshop extravaganza based around their critically acclaimed book Baggage. You'll discover all the secrets you need to create your own adventures in words and pictures, plus you'll receive a free copy of the Etherington Brothers’ Go Nuts comic-making activity book!

Title: The Bob Blackman Appreciation Society Presents - Free
Description: Variety with the leading fans of Bob 'The Tray' Blackman - Sir Richard Swan and Johnny Sorrow, winner Malcolm Hardee Award for Comic Originality. ‘It's great fun’ (Kate Copstick, Scotsman).
Artist: Bob Blackman Appreciation Society / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Refurbished in 2011, The Meadow Bar offers two stylish bars with distinctive service and an extensive selection of beers, spirits, shooters, cocktails and drink offers. Also an internet cafe. Free performances of stand-up comedy run here from midday to 3am

Title: Black Box Shorts 3: Passing Through
Description: Six films from Canada, Austria, the Netherlands, and the USA that offer very different perspectives on bodily trajectories through new and uncertain territories. Aimlessly wandering, tentatively negotiating, confidently conquering and directly intervening, these intensely personal films are brought together through a curiosity for the outside world. Seen through the eyes of Marc Pelletier, Yang Hey Yeun, Albert Sackl, Fern Silva, Robert Todd and Anna Abrahams.

Title: Roland Rides The Rail's! (again) - Free
Description: Roland returns! ‘What a joy from Grangemouth's greatest export. Sometimes laugh-out-loud, sometimes bizarrely surreal, always entertaining. Don't go because it's free, go because it'll brighten your afternoon’. ‘Absolutely bonkers’ (Audience reviews, 2011). www.rolandridestherails.co.uk.
Warnings: May include mild but appropriate use of swearing and partial naturism
Artist: Gregarious Productions / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier music venue, at the heart of town just off of the Royal Mile hosts free festival shows during the day, and live music in the evenings - with a wide offering of drinks available all day!

Title: Censorship Today
Subtitle: SHOULD FREEDOM OF SPEECH EVER HAVE LIMITS?
Description:
Freedom of speech is not only under threat in undemocratic countries: the American Library Association received challenges to ban no fewer than 326 book titles in 2010, including And Tango Makes Three, which attracted complaints because its young penguin hero has two fathers. In this session, Carnegie Medal-winning writer of novels for adults and children, Patrick Ness, addresses the Conference about censorship and freedom of speech, chaired by Belgian-Nigerian author Chika Unigwe.

	Visit the Edinburgh World Writers’ Conference website - www.edinburghworldwritersconference.org - to watch a live broadcast of this and other conference events and to join in the conversation online. Follow the conference twitter feed: #WorldWritersConf.

	Supported by the Scottish Government's Edinburgh Festivals Expo Fund, Creative Scotland, the City of Edinburgh Council and Event Scotland.

Title: William Brodrick & James Runcie
Subtitle: A FORMER MONK AND AN ARCHBISHOP'S SON
Description: The authors featured here may share a religious background, but it is the quality of their writing that brings them together today. James Runcie discusses his new Grantchester Mysteries (to be screened as a BBC1 drama), while the former Augustinian monk William Brodrick talks about his newly-published The Day of the Lie. Both have written page-turning novels with moral dilemmas at their heart.

Title: Porphyria
Description: Every night Reginald Blake dreams of sex with his fantasy woman, a woman that is not his wife. One morning he awakes to find this fantasy come to life and eating breakfast in his kitchen.
Warnings: Violence and sexual content Violence and sexual content
Venue description: An award-winning extravaganza of the best performances from across the Fringe spectrum. The majestic Main House is packed with outstanding dance and physical theatre from around the world while the Cabaret Bar and Studio host thrilling drama, comedy and music.

Title: Amused Moose Laughter Awards Top Ten Semi-Final
Description: Vote alongside international talent scouts for 2012's Top Ten comedy shows, which outshone hundreds of other entries from undiscovered/unsigned performers, to select three finalists eager for fame and £5000. www.amusedmoose.com/laughoff.
Venue description: Edinburgh's all-year-round multi-arts venue. We offer a gourmet selection of theatre, cabaret, live music, visual arts and clubbing. Our cafe adds delicious homemade food, free internet and great coffee to the mix. All brought to you by the friendliest staff in town.

Title: Ian Black & Paul Mason
Subtitle: WHAT CAUSED THE 2011 REVOLUTIONS?
Description: Two books by influential journalists are among the first to look at the factors that caused a wave of protests across the world in 2011. BBC Newsnight Economics Editor Paul Mason discusses Why It's Kicking Off Everywhere, looking at the effect social media had on events, while the Guardian's Middle East Editor Ian Black talks about The Arab Spring – selected material from the Guardian's website during the momentous events. Chaired by Iain Macwhirter.

Title: They Came With Outer Script - Free
Description: Love a B-movie? So do we! Join seven talented improvisers and create a new B-movie based on your suggestions. The most unpredictable free show in Edinburgh! 'Steven Spielberg should take notes' (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: The Darkroom
Description: Don your bobble hat and come exploring in a world where memory is everything and it's about to be lost. A shed, an old man, piles of notes. This is the evidence, but what is the story? www.witness-theatre.co.uk.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Chris Corcoran and Elis James - The Committee Meeting
Description: Chris Corcoran (Radio Wales, Rhod Gilbert Show) and Elis James (BBC2, 8 Out of 10 Cats) bring the best of their 21st-century take on workingman's clubs to Edinburgh.
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Knee Deep
Description: Australia's hottest new circus company, created by the stars of 2009's C!RCA, present the gem of the Adelaide Fringe. Walking on eggs, flying from the sky and breathtaking physical magic. ‘The crowd was in awe’ (Adelaide Now).
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.

024579

Title: The School of Night
Description: Witness a Shakespearean masterpiece being created on the spot, based on audience suggestions. This daring group, founded by Ken Campbell and the Showstoppers, is 'one of the most eccentric, enjoyable shows on the Fringe' **** (BritishTheatreGuide.info).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Jane Rogers & Juli Zeh (*Juli Zeh has cancelled*)

Title: A National Literature?
Subtitle: Nationality and  identity in the novel today
Description:
Since the first Edinburgh Writers’ Conference in 1962, there has been a renaissance in Scottish literature, bringing the voices of Scottish people of different backgrounds into ground-breaking novels by writers such as James Kelman, Alasdair Gray, Janice Galloway and A L Kennedy among many others. Have there been similarly powerful developments in the ‘national literatures’ of other countries? In this session chaired by Ian Rankin, Irvine Welsh addresses the impact of national identity on the novel today.

In this event she discusses her book, Relish, and her recipe for survival in life and business, with BBC journalist Sue MacGregor.

Title: Steve Reich Late
Description: Steve Reich's Grammy award-winning Different Trains for string quartet and tape, plus another American classic, Barber's luscious String Quartet, of Adagio fame, performed by the Cavaleri Quartet. Includes a complimentary glass of wine beforehand. www.roslarts.org.uk.
Venue description: Edinburgh's most central venue, with stunning castle views, has an intimate chamber music room, plus gallery. Restaurant and bar with food. An oasis of calm in the heart of the festival hustle and bustle.

Description: Scottish artist Hatti Pattisson exhibits recent work inspired by Fife and the surrounding landscape. Pattison's work varies from loose, painterly land and seascapes to floral and abstract paintings. www.roslarts.org.uk.

Title: The Machine
Description: The Machine travels around the world planting all the trees, grass and flowers. This morning, it broke down! Two bumbling assistants have been left in charge and they need your help! 'Packed with visual invention' **** (Scotsman).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Chris Martin - Spot the Difference
Description: After a debut sell out show, Chris (as seen on Dave's One Night Stand) explains how to wind up squirrels and shows techniques to confuse a pervert. 'Destined for greatness' (Sunday Times). 'Hilarious' (Metro).
Artist: Phil McIntyre Entertainments by Arrangement with Lisa Thomas Management

Title: Alan Warner
Subtitle: RETURN TICKET TO OBAN
Description: Since he exploded onto the literary scene with Morvern Callar, Alan Warner's international success has been mirrored by the settings of his novels – most recently Spain, and Gatwick Airport. With his new book, The Deadman's Pedal, Warner returns to the Scottish Highlands. In his story of a West Coast port and its railway in the 1970s, Warner offers a vivid and moving portrait of life in small-town Scotland. Chaired by David Robinson.

Title: Kevin Shepherd: Thus Spoke Kev - Free
Description: Kevin recently discovered Nietzsche. Join him as he explains why he believes Nietzsche was actually a comedian stuck in a philosopher’s body and how Nietzsche's words and random Wikipedia aphorisms helped him rediscover himself.
Artist: Kevin Shepherd / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Captain Taylor's Coffee House
Venue description: A stylish and relaxing licensed cafe, and a brand new Fringe venue offering a mixture of quality food and drink, and free shows throughout the day - all right in the heart of Edinburgh, just off of the Royal Mile.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning events for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. Appearing today: Ryan Van Winkle.

Title: Danielle Ward - Speakeasy / Playdead
Description: Take a lucky dip with Danielle Ward's shows and you might get stand-up about politics, sex and Ryan Gosling or extremely silly tales of horror. See Pleasance.co.uk for details! ***** (List).
Artist: Mick Perrin for Just For Laughs Live
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Creative Writing Class
Subtitle: PRESENTING LIFE WRITING
Description: Dwelling on highly personal material to allow it to emerge as effective writing can stir strong emotions. But when it comes to explaining it to others – potential investors or your family – the difficulties increase. It can be hard to detach yourself sufficiently and your right to handle the material at all, when those close to you are involved, may be difficult to defend. This course examines the issues, offering ideas on how to separate yourself from the work to present more effectively. The class is led by author Alison Baverstock, Course Leader for MA Publishing at Kingston University. (Lunch & coffee included.)

Title: Debate: Rethinking Growth
Subtitle: ARE THERE ANY ALTERNATIVES TO MARKET FORCES?
Description: The idea that the market is the best means to regulate society has been the dominant ideology of British life for 30 years. But if the banking crisis has put paid to the idea that ‘the market knows best’, is the only alternative a return to widespread nationalisation and the domination of the state? Or are new forms of local governance possible? Margaret Thatcher’s former speechwriter Ferdinand Mount joins Jules Goddard, author of Uncommon Sense, Common Nonsense and Andri Snær Magnuson, Icelandic author of Dreamland: A Self-Help Manual for a Frightened Nation to take up the debate.

Title: Josh Widdicombe: The Further Adventures of...
Description: Hotly-anticipated follow up to last year's Foster's Newcomer nominated, Live at the Apollo and Stand Up for The Week. ‘One of the most hilarious and unforgettable hours I have had this year.' (Scotsman). www.offthekerb.co.uk.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: BBC: Crossing the Media
Description: BBC Radio Drama and the Traverse Theatre are major forces in developing new writing. Orla O’Loughlin, Artistic Director of the Traverse and David Ian Neville, Drama Producer lead a discussion on writing for theatre and radio.
Artist: BBC Radio Drama and The Traverse Theatre, Edinburgh
Venue address: Corner of Potterrow and Marshall Street,Edinburgh
Venue description: Experience the best of the BBC under one roof and a taster of all the delights of the Fringe. Join us at Venue 25 for BBC shows, big names, stand-up every night plus masterclasses from BBC Radio, TV and Online. Free events are ticketed via a random draw. To enter the draw please use the show website link: bbc.co.uk/tickets.

Title: The Trench
Description: Inspired by the story of a miner entombed in a tunnel during WW1. As the horror engulfs him, not everything in the darkness is what it seems when he discovers a strange world beneath the mud and death.
Artist: Les Enfants Terribles with Wales Millennium Centre, Luton Hat Factory
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: A Donkey and a Parrot
Description: An epic tale of escape and survival passed down in Sarah's family for over 300 years. One woman plays 16 characters. 'Jaw-dropping theatre ... captivating' ***** (Adelaide Magazine). 'Quirky, witty, and charismatic' **** (FringeReview.co.uk).
Venue description: Gilded Balloon at Third Door is an exciting new space, just moments from Teviot Row House. Bringing you the very best in theatre, comedy and magic, reflecting the diverse and innovative programming that the Gilded Balloon is world renowned for.

Title: Jessica Fostekew: Brave New Word
Description: Gag-suffused show about etymology, brave words, new words and brave new words. Not just for nerds. 'All about the jokes, winning delivery' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Sharp wit' (List). 'Tremendous charm' (Scotsman). 'Original, elegant and funny' (FringeReport.com). www.jessicafostekew.com.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: The Vocal Orchestra
Description: A spine-tingling hour of incredible musical entertainment celebrating everyone's favourite tunes using seven mouths, seven mics and no instruments. You'll be whooping, clapping and dancing all the way home. 'Effervescent, energetic, audience-grabbing' **** (Times).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Adelaide Fringe Info Session
Description: Artists from across the globe converge on Adelaide Fringe for this leading open access festival. Meet staff, venue operators and past performers, and find out how you can take part in Australia’s largest arts event. www.adelaidefringe.com.au.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Fauré Requiem by Candlelight
Description: There can be few more atmospheric settings in which to experience the serenity and soothing gentleness of Fauré's Requiem than by candlelight in the historic St Giles' Cathedral. Also features a new Paul Mealor piece.
Venue description: Founded in the 1120s, St Giles' was the church of John Knox during the Reformation and is renowned for its stained glass, Rieger organ and beautiful Thistle Chapel. Open daily. Free guided tours, concerts, Cathedral shop and restaurant. Donations welcome.
Venue accessibility:

Title: Listen! The River
Description: A tough-talking cat, a one-eyed dog, a reluctant fiancé, his sexy betrothed and a bible-toting mother flow through this story of love, loss and new beginnings. Solo show with New York's Wendy Peace. @turbo_cat. www.listentheriver.com.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Macbeth
Description: This is a creepy, often funny and fast-paced stylised version of the Scottish play with some macabre twists and a cast of highly talented and energetic young actors from the Edinburgh-based Little Shakespeare Theatre School. www.littleshakespearetheatreschool.co.uk.
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.

Title: Richard Thompson in Concert
Description: Critically acclaimed prolific songwriter (Ivor Novello Award winner), recipient of BBC's Lifetime Achievement Award and named one of Rolling Stone Magazine's Top 20 Guitarists of All Time for his acoustic and electric virtuosity.
Venue description: Edinburgh's leading live music venue offers classical, jazz, blues, pop, rock, world, folk and comedy in the intimate surroundings of a converted Georgian church. www.thequeenshall.net

Title: Leaving Limbo Landing
Description: Dancers and aerialists perform in air, water and on land in Caroline Bowditch's ambitious new outdoor production. Exploring 12 individual's stories of journey and settling, this is a must-see Fringe experience, and it’s free! www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com.

Title: Valery Ponomarev Quintet
Description: In from New York via Moscow, the famous Russian trumpeter toured and recorded with Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers for four years. Catch his fabulous, sparkling Clifford Brown trumpet style here, with a driving five-piece of top players.
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: Forgotten Heroes
Description: Emmett was never like other children - he always wanted to be a hero. His chance has come, but it's not all he hoped. See him come to grips with reality just as he is about to lose it...
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Deserving?
Description: Inspired by Artaud's Theatre of Cruelty and media coverage of rape. In an Amnesty International survey, one in four claimed a woman is partly to blame for being raped if she dresses provocatively, drinks too much or is flirtatious.
Warnings: Nudity and violent scenes Nudity and violent scenes
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: Rob Deb - the Dork Knight Triumphant - Free
Description: Free show. Rob Deb, Sci-Fi London host and regular convention specialist, returns to Edinburgh for an hour of comic book stand-up. Follow @RobDeb. Great comedy hour of power.
Warnings: ONLY FOR GEEKS ONLY FOR GEEKS
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items ... Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: Say Something
Description: h2dance/Escalator East to Edinburgh presents Say Something. An exhilarating mix of contemporary dance and live vocal/electronic score, putting audience and performers centre stage. This unique show explores group behaviour, conformism and freedom of expression. www.h2dance.com.
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: The Stand Late Show
Description: Late night Fringe comedy at its best. Eight superb showcases from Scotland’s favourite club. Five comics, two hours, late bar. Different sizzling selection nightly. ’Best value in town’ (Evening News). ‘They keep the laughs coming’ (Times).
Venue description: Edinburgh's year-round comedy club is housed in an intimate basement bar just off St Andrew Square. The atmosphere is relaxed and informal with comfortable cabaret-style seating (although some late night shows are not all seated).

Title: Bestiaire
Description: Curious, compelling and compassionate, Denis Côté’s contemplative portrait of animals in captivity is, put simply, a series of beautifully framed and composed tableaux of a variety of animals at Quebec’s Parc Safari; but it’s also a complex meditation on the relationship between man, beast and environment. Côté lets his often startling imagery speak for itself, giving us, the viewer, plenty time, and food, for thought.

Title: Kevin Tomlinson: Seven Ages!
Description: A comic look at the seven stages of life! A truly life-affirming show that will make you laugh until you cry! 'Tomlinson creates magical comedy theatre!' (Evening Standard). 'Wonderfully hilarious!' (Paramount Comedy Channel).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: BBC: Radio 2 New Comedy Award
Description: The most prestigious new comedy talent search in the UK. See the best acts battle it out for a place in the semi-finals. Hosted and judged by the hottest talent at the festival.
Venue address: Corner of Potterrow and Marshall Street,Edinburgh

To enter the draw please use the show website link: bbc.co.uk/tickets.

Description: Combining the titles of the two previous Edinburgh Comedy Awards winners, to create something considerably less successful. But still very funny. He's willing to stake £295.20 on it. @jcbeermat.

Description: From Brisbane, Australia, Out of Abingdon and their sublime jazz grooves travel 10,000 miles to make their much anticipated return to Edinburgh. Check out their very aptly titled debut CD, Journeys, and festival dates at www.outofabingdon.com.au now.
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. Title: Chris Priestley
Description: Mister Creecher is Chris Priestley’s Frankenstein novel. Exploring the relationship this classic monster has with a young boy called Billy, it is a wonderful read with a great twist in the tale. Chris’ novels, such as Uncle Montague’s Tales of Terror, are brilliantly original additions to a long tradition of horror stories by the likes of Edgar Allan Poe and Henry James. Come and talk spine-chillers, gothic and horror with an inventive master of the genre. Keep your ticket as it entitles you to half price entry to The Edinburgh Dungeon; they provided the ghoulish props for this event (www.thedungeons.co.uk).

Title: Genevieve Swallow is Sharing
Description: Genevieve needs a new roomie. Could it be you? Hilarious characters about house-sharing from Funny Women Finalist & Stage Awards Nominee. ***** (Whatsonstage) 'She has the audience hooting with glee.' (Scotsman)
Venue description: Shanghai @ Le Monde, George Street is a brand new Free Fringe venue for 2012. Le Monde is open 8am- 3am and serves food till late. No street level disabled access available. Please contact venue for more information.

49
\nAssistance dogs welcome, accessible WC

Title: Ward and Bartlett's Double Impact

Title: The  Oxford Revue - Prattle Royale
Description: The world-famous, critically-acclaimed Revue returns, providing a cheaper, considerably slower alternative to the 2012 Olympics. 'Brilliantly executed' **** (ThreeWeeks). 'An hour of comic genius' (Oxford Info). 'The best student sketch group by far' (TheNewCurrent.com).

Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: They're Gonna Crucify Me
Description: Political, pornographic, angry, offensive comedy with original satirical songs by the routinely banned innovator of Violent Comedy, all delivered with a spirited loving sermon. 'The bastard son of Bob Dylan, Bills Hicks and Eminem' (Mojo).

Title: Man on the Moon with Simon Bartram
Description: Simon Bartram is the talented author and illustrator behind Bob, the Man on the Moon and Dougal, the deep sea adventurer. If you are fascinated by the mysteries of the universe or the secrets of the deep, come and embark on exciting adventures with stories and pictures.

Title: Cathedral Lunchtime Concerts
Description: A former Times Critics' Choice. A whole month of free concerts with leading performers from some of the world's top conservatories and universities. Full details at www.cathedral.net.
Venue description: One of the world's great neo-gothic buildings, with its three distinctive spires and a tradition of daily choral services sung by the cathedral choir: a magnificent concert venue.  The Song School is covered by vibrant murals by Phoebe Anna Traquair.

Title: Heads Up
Description: The Fringe spirit distilled into 45 minutes of spanking new dance - a mixtastic line-up of brilliant ideas, freshly made work and random moments of pure madness or joy. You decide. The programme changes every day.

Venue: Dance Base - National Centre for Dance

Title: Activism Is Fun

Title: Peter Robinson
Subtitle: NEW DCI BANKS NOVEL LAUNCHED
Description: Yorkshire-born Peter Robinson is fast gaining a reputation as one of the finest crime writers in the country. Following the success of a four-part ITV series, his DCI Banks is joining Rebus as a premier league crime character. We are delighted to welcome Robinson to unveil his brand new Banks book, Watching the Dark, in which a murder in the Yorkshire Dales is linked to Estonia. In this eent he talks to bestselling Scottish crime-writer Lin Anderson.

Title: Firenado! The Sketch Show
Description: What is a Firenado? Find out the answer to this and other questions you had never imagined would be worth asking. Prepare yourselves for the hilarious onslaught of entertainment that is... Firenado! www.firenado.com/thesketchshow.
Artist: Firenado! The Sketch Show / PBH’s Free Fringe
Venue description: Ascend the stairs (quite a few!) to great space and atmospheric bar and stage. Worth it to be entertained in quirky venue.  Alcoholic drinks available.

Title: Back and to the Left in the Turkish Prison
Description: Two fools sent to prison for a crime they probably did commit, rehearse a sketch show in which one gets sent to prison, a different prison, confused? So are they.
Warnings: Some strong language and some adult themes
Venue address: 50 Blackfriars Street within Smart City Hostels,(entrances on Blackfriars Street and Cowgate),Edinburgh
Venue description: Located within the five-star Smart City Hostel, Bar 50 is a bar and restaurant offering free shows, drinks and tasty, locally-sourced pub grub in laid-back, modern and stylish surroundings – and a rooftop terrace.

Title: Zoë Strachan & Benjamin Wood
Subtitle: PAGE-TURNING FICTION FROM BRITAIN'S FUTURE STARS
Description: Two young authors have created very different, but equally page-turning stories of intrigue and coming into self-knowledge as a young adult. Acclaimed Scottish author Zoë Strachan has produced Ever Fallen In Love, her most compelling novel to date. She is joined by English novelist Benjamin Wood, whose debut The Bellwether Revivals was the subject of frenzied competition among editors keen to publish it.

Title: The  Dead Memory House
Description: Bea, Anne and Sylvia are your sisters, girlfriends, aunties, mothers and wives. They are your friends, and perhaps even your enemies. The Dead Memory House is a collision of their lives and your experiences.
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Martin Dockery: Wanderlust
Description: A man treks into Africa, demanding an epiphany. Any epiphany at all. Exhilarating, hilarious and true. Best of Fest: Vancouver, Edmonton, Winnipeg. Adelaide Critics’ Circle Award. ‘A tour de force’ (Orlando Sentinel). ‘Blisteringly funny’ (Toronto Eye Weekly).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Catherine the Great: An Enlightened Empress
Description: Explore magnificent collections of one of Russia's most successful rulers. This UK exclusive exhibition, presented in partnership with the State Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg, features hundreds of works collected and commissioned by the Empress.
Venue description: All our collections have tales to tell. The redeveloped Museum is fully open following a £50m transformation. Discover the wonders of life, the universe and everything in it – from science and art to nature and outer space.

Title: Metamorphosis: A Return to Presence
Description: A journey of change. By gaining keys of self-development, Ridade portrays some moments of her past and present lives as she faces her ego, alters it, and celebrates her strengths through live performance art.
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: The New Conway Dimension
Description: It's like if Michael has organized a space party and Conway has turned up with a variety of lizards and the lizards are mad djs. Best Newcomer Nominee 2011 Melbourne International Comedy Festival **** (List).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Luath Book Banter at Henderson's
Description: Debate, poetry, fiction and politics from Luath authors. Including the nation’s favourite Burns, John Cairney, David Purdie (who brings Ivanhoe back to the people), acclaimed new talent Catriona Child and much more... Details at www.luath.co.uk.
Venue: Henderson's Vegetarian Restaurant and Arts Venue
Venue description: Just minutes from Princes Street, Henderson's is Scotland's legendary vegetarian restaurant and arts venue, long a favourite with festival goers. We host a varied programme of theatrical and musical performances alongside art exhibitions and talks.

Title: I Heart The Accidentals
Description: Heart a cappella? Heart The Accidentals! Eight girls who are gutsy, feisty and know how to have a laugh. This national award-winning university a cappella group sings everything with infectious enthusiasm, expert musicality and attitude!
Venue description: Vibrant Cabaret bar located on the Royal Mile. A global feast of song, music, cabaret, comedy, dance and theatre. Free entry after midnight. Open til 3am daily See: www.thespaceuk.com for more info.

Title: Bruce Hammers' Bananapocalypse
Description: Mat Ewins presents a fun character/sketch show about actor Bruce Hammers and his 1982 blockbuster Bananapocalypse. Discover a movie star you never knew existed, but won't be able to forget. 'Never far from a solid punchline' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: International Animation
Description: This screening allows you to catch up with a selection of the best animation from around the globe, and sees a welcome return to Edinburgh of the work of Don Hertzfeldt, who was our guest in 2009. Animation derives its name from the Latin ‘anima’ – which describes the soul. The creation of that life essence through the illusion of animation is even more fascinating when the loss of that animating principle is explored, as happens in many of the films presented here.

Code: Film Festivals in the Digital Age
Title: Film Festivals in the Digital Age
Description: We live in a time when new digital technologies are transforming how film festivals are organised and experienced. Meanwhile, a new type of cosmopolitan cinephilia is evolving in response to changing models of film circulation. Join Dina Iordanova, editor of the new book Digital Disruptions: Cinema Moves On-line, and other distinguished experts as they explore the future of film festivals.

Title: Translation Duel: French
Subtitle: WHERE WORDS HAVE MANY MEANINGS
Description:
What happens to the essence of a story when it is translated from one language into another? Author Laurent Binet is joined by acclaimed translators, Adriana Hunter, and Frank Wynne, who will pit their linguistic skills against each other to prove that every translation is a creative work of merit in its own right. No knowledge of French is needed to enjoy this event. Hosted by writer, editor and translator Daniel Hahn.
	

	Please note: Laurent Binet is no longer able to appear in this event and it will go ahead with Adriana Hunter, Frank Wynne and Daniel Hahn.

Title: Say You Love Me
Description: You’re eavesdropping on fellow cafe goers, Jane and Lee, and overhear them reveal the tumultuous story of their lives. The tension, passion, laughter and intrigue you spy on ensures an entertaining and thoughtful theatre experience.
Venue description: Cafe and theatre with 170 seats.  Cafe open all day from 9am till late.  Well equipped theatre with a mixed arts programme running throughout the day and evening.

Title: Writing Workshop
Subtitle: SCIENCE AND LITERATURE: SEPARATED BY A COMMON LANGUAGE?
Description: Science is real and fiction is made up – so what do they have in common? They both rely on specific and detailed descriptions of the world around us. Description: Ever thought how lovely it would be to be a cat? To forget about school, bullies, parent problems and just spend all day fence-balancing and sniffing the air for the scent of sardines? Venue description: Experience the best of the BBC under one roof and a taster of all the delights of the Fringe. Title: Should Literature Be Political?
Subtitle: NOVELS AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP WITH CURRENT AFFAIRS
Description:
The 1962 Writers’ Conference organisers stated: ‘Many believe that the novelist has the duty to further by his writing the causes in which he believes. Others think that literature must be above the problems of the day.’ 50 years on, writers remain divided about the role political events should play in novels. Ahdaf Soueif, who witnessed last year’s revolutionary events in Cairo, addresses the conference in a session chaired by leading Turkish author Elif Shafak. This event will be filmed and broadcast live online at www.edinburghworldwritersconference.org.

	Please note: Due to the situation in Egypt, Ahdaf Soueif was to deliver her keynote address via a specially created film however we are delighted to announce that Ahdaf Soueif is now able to travel to Edinburgh to deliver her address in person and lead the ensuing discussion.
	

	Visit the Edinburgh World Writers’ Conference website - www.edinburghworldwritersconference.org - to watch a live broadcast of this and other conference events and to join in the conversation online. Follow the conference twitter feed: #WorldWritersConf.

Come and hear them talk about their work and influences.

Chaired by Sheena McDonald.

Title: Barnaby Rogerson (Cancelled)
Subtitle: AFRICA REVISITED
Description:
Dunfermline-born Barnaby Rogerson studied Medieval History at St Andrews and has now become a leading travel writer and publisher. Rogerson’s particular interest in North Africa has led to the publication of an impressive new history of the region which he discusses in today’s event. According to John Julius Norwich, ‘no-one interested in the Maghreb can afford to be without this book.’ Chaired by Stuart Kelly.

	Please note: Barnaby Rogerson is no longer able to appear and this event has beeen cancelled.

Title: Iszi Lawrence's Wotnot
Description: Nerdy, wordy and purdy. **** (ThreeWeeks). ‘She’s good. Really good’ (Oxford Mail). ‘In a bracket alongside Sarah Millican’ (Oxford Times). ‘Invites comparisons to Stewart Lee whilst being less of an acquired taste’ (SnipeLondon.com). www.iszi.com.

The stories are perfect for turning into rhymes, songs or pictures and – of course – for telling to your friends and family.

Description: Philip Ardagh and his beard, are on hand to disclose all about Eddie Dickens, son of Mr and Mrs Dickens, nephew of Mad Uncle Jack and Even-Madder Aunt Maud. His tales describe Victorian Britain, a time of runaway orphans, blotchy yellow skin and stuffed stoats called Malcolm. Whilst these ridiculous stories have no historical accuracy whatsoever they do, bizarrely, follow the life arc of another Mr Dickens we all know.

Title: Patterson and Ranganathan

Come and hear her talk about the series, the characters and her research, which has taken her from LA to Mexico City.

Title: Nicholas Parsons' Happy Hour
Description: Celebrating 12 year of this stage, screen and Fringe legend, Nicholas Parsons brings you his most flamboyant show ever! Parsons' sell-out comedy chatshow features a myriad of special guests. Not to be missed.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Fresh Faces at the Free Fringe
Description: Elise and Danny present year six of the show that brings five or more of the newest comedy acts daily. Some measure their careers in months, others a little longer. Comedy in small chunks.
Artist: Danny Worthington, Elise Harris and Others / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Located on Market Street (opposite Waverley Station) Belushis is your one stop venue for food, drinks, live entertainment and sport. With a great programme of live entertainment during the festival, great drinks offers and amazing food, Belushi's is the place to be.

Description: Mask exhibition with interactive performances. A unique journey of discovery into this traditional Italian craft led by Harlequin himself! Funny, historical, the forerunner of pantomime! Authentic leather masks by Renzo Antonello, Dario Fo's mask maker.

Title: The Ballad of Pondlife McGurk
Description: ‘A really touching family show’ (List). **** (Herald). Recently returned from Sydney Opera House, this is a coming-of-age tale about friendship, bullying and overcoming adversity.
Artist: Catherine Wheels in Association With Brunton Theatre, Musselburgh
Venue address: Sandeman House, off High Street,Trunk's Close,55 High Street
Venue description: Sandeman House is the home of the Scottish Book Trust. It offers a unique space and a delightful award-winning garden just off the Royal Mile. This year, the Scottish Book Trust will become an extension of the Traverse Theatre.

Title: Helen FitzGerald & Herman Koch
Subtitle: WHEN TOUGH DECISIONS ARE ON THE MENU
Description: With The Donor, Scotland-based Aussie Helen FitzGerald delivers yet another tense thriller in the vein of previous triumphs such as My Last Confession and Dead Lovely. Single dad Will has perfectly functioning kidneys but twin daughters both need a transplant. How far will he go? In Spain-based Dutchman Herman Koch’s The Dinner, a polite social occasion temporarily camouflages some dark emotions.

Title: NLS Donald Dewar Lecture
Subtitle: SCOTLAND AND BRITAIN IN 2025
Description: A keynote Book Festival event, the annual Donald Dewar lecture looks at the past, present and future of Scotland. This year’s event is delivered by former Prime Minister Gordon Brown, who knew Dewar well and who shared his passion for encouraging a confident Scotland to have a greater say in its own affairs through devolution. In today’s lecture Brown will paint a picture of Scotland and Britain as he hopes they will be experienced by a future generation. Introduced by BBC Scotland’s political editor, Brian Taylor.

Title: Why Do You Stand There in the Rain?
Description: New play by Scottish playwright Peter Arnott. In 1932, 25,000 First World War veterans occupy Washington DC to petition the government for promised relief. Hoover's relief? Bayonets, bullets, tanks and gas. www.pepperdinedrama.com.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Grabbers
Description: Featuring an endearing lead performance from Richard Coyle, (also to be seen in PUSHER, page ??), GRABBERS is an exciting, light-hearted “monster movie” that affectionately tips its hat to everything that ever fell from the sky, or crawled from the sea onto a cinema screen.

Title: I Am Son
Description: A dreamy mix of dance, music and words, this is a voyage through images of the contemporary Italian world. Flipping between irony, physical intensity and lightness, three performers wonder who we are and where we come from.
Venue: Dance Base - National Centre for Dance
Venue description: Centrally located in the Old Town, Dance Base is a beautiful and inspiring setting for dance. We present performances by the best British and international dance companies and also offer classes and workshops from breakdance to ballet - for all ages.

Title: Domestic Science
Description: Join Helen and Rob for a lunchtime hour of home-cooked science and comedy. They’ll be investigating cosmological conundrums, solving microscopic mysteries and trying to maintain their own domestic bliss. Fingers crossed then. New guests daily, see www.domesticsciencecomedy.com. @DomesticScience.
Artist: Helen Arney and Rob Wells / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: At the heart of Canongate on the Royal Mile, the Canon's Gait is an historic, recently redecorated bar serving lunches, real ale and an extensive selection of malt whiskies. Comfortable seating and relaxed, friendly atmosphere to enjoy a drink between shows.

4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: James Kelman with Liz Lochhead
Subtitle: ORDINARY PEOPLE, EXTRAORDINARY VOICES
Description: He has been described by Amit Chaudhuri as 'the greatest living British novelist' and by the Times as 'probably the most influential novelist of the post-war period.' Today James Kelman, winner of the 1994 Man Booker Prize, is joined by Scotland's Poet Laureate Liz Lochhead to discuss Kelman's latest novel: a tender and deeply affecting story of a Glasgow woman in London, Mo Said She Was Quirky.

Title: Born to be Mild
Description: Andrew Watts used to be single, and he used to tell jokes about being single. Now he isn't, and he doesn't. 'Stand-up laced with a cerebral cutting edge' **** (ThreeWeeks). As seen on ITV's Stand-Up Hero.
Venue description: A year round comedy space in Edinburgh's city centre.
Venue accessibility: \nThis venue is in a basement and as such is not accessible for wheelchair users.

Title: Pappy's: Last Show Ever!
Description: Brand new show! Sketches! Songs! Silliness! But is this really the end for 'the funniest sketch troupe on the Fringe'? (Scotsman). Edinburgh Award nominees, Chortle Award winners, Loaded LAFTA winners. 'Masterful comic invention' (Guardian).
Artist: Phil McIntyre Entertainments by arrangement with Lisa Thomas Management
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Oh! What a Lovely War
Description: A powerful reminder of the atrocities of World War One told through sketches, popular songs and images of the period. Satirical, funny and extremely moving. It will bring a tear to your eye.
Venue description: The Edinburgh Academy is centrally located in the New Town, with ample off-street parking and an on-site cafe for festival patrons. The venue is centered on its amazing oval Hall, built in 1824 and designed by William Burn.

Title: Flicker
Description: Electricity allergies, lonely hearts, frustrating IT problems, and the ultimate solution for severe arachnophobia - the feature debut of Oscar nominated short director Patrik Eklund is a beautifully absurd, occasionally touching web of comical stories, endearingly brought to life by a charming ensemble cast.

Title: Mind Reading for Breakfast
Description: Weaving magic and comedy with his life story, Rob explores his childhood love of supernatural mysteries, working in secure psychiatric wards, and Fringe shows. Told with sensitivity, humour and baffling psychological illusions. **** (Big Issue). www.psychicpsychologist.co.uk.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: David Melling
Description: Hugless Douglas is very excited about Rabbit's sleepover, but he collects so many friends along the way that soon it's a big squash in Rabbit's small burrow! How will they ever get to sleep? Join David Melling for this heart-warming third adventure for funny Douglas. There will be stories, pictures and the chance to meet Douglas himself!

Title: Catherine Wilkins' Stand-Up Workshop
Description: Catherine Wilkins’ debut novel, My Best Friend and Other Enemies, is a very funny look at the trials and traumas of adolescent life. It’s humorous because Catherine is also a successful and edgy stand-up comedian (but for older people!). With her knack for creating laughter, Catherine leads a workshop on how to be a comedian. If you fancy yourself funny or find that others do, come along to find out if you’ve got what it takes to get the world giggling.

Title: Sad Faces Remember It Differently
Description: Journey into the minds of BBC Radio's 'side-splittingly funny' (BroadwayBaby.com) Sad Faces! Witness the destruction of their friendship in one fateful day! Ascertain that they remember that day differently! Enjoy those gratuitous exclamation marks!
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Cats and Dogs with Maria Cairnie
Description: Writer and storyteller Maria Cairnie comes to the Book Festival with a highly interactive tale of canine tearaway Blitzy Boy Walker and his devoted feline friend, the beautiful white Persian cat named Sassica Spall. Maria combines her flair for energetic and engaging story-sharing with a back-drop of dance, musical theatre and creative spontaneity. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: The Two Worlds of Charlie F
Description: Performed by those it happened to, the play explores a soldier's view of service, injury and recovery. A darkly comic, authentic and uplifting tale of survival. ***** (Telegraph).

Title: Platero Y Yo by Juan Ramon Jimenez

Venue description: Festival Fringe productions in a small theatre 'beyond the treasure house of salamis, cheeses, balsamic vinegars and olive oils' (Sunday Times). 'If anything makes a London-based gourmet jealous of the Scots, it is Valvona & Crolla' (Financial Times).

Title: Greek Myths for Kids
Description: Soar above the clouds with Pegasus! Help battle the fearsome Minotaur! Breathtaking journey from the Gorgon's lair to the heights of Mount Olympus. Told using storytelling and puppetry. Family festival hit. ***** (Freshair.org.uk). ***** (ThreeWeeks). www.backhandtheatre.com.

Title: The Blanks' Big Break
Description: The Blanks (Ted’s Band from TV’s Scrubs) perform hilariously entertaining a cappella music and sketch comedy. An online phenomenon with over eight million YouTube views. For their Edinburgh debut expect skits, antics and talking toys. Book Early! www.theblankswebsite.com.

Title: Neal's Yard Remedies Chillout Zone

Title: Jennifer Carnovale - Scraping the Barrel - Free

The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Taylor Glenn - Reverse Psycomedy
Description: Ever feel like you're the craziest person in the room? That's not a good sign when you're a psychotherapist. Award-winning comic's frank, revealing and utterly hilarious journey from one delightfully insane profession to another.

Title: Charles Ferguson (Cancelled)
Subtitle: NIGHTMARE ON WALL STREET
Description:
Dubbed scarier than anything John Carpenter or Wes Craven have given the world of film, Charles Ferguson’s Inside Job was a searing Oscar-winning documentary about the financial meltdown of 2008. Narrated by Matt Damon, it pointed angry fingers at the systemic corruption in the financial services industry. Sue MacGregor chairs as part of her series entitled ‘A survival kit for the information age’.

	Please note: Charles Ferguson is no longer able to appear and this event is cancelled.

Title: Threads
Description: If you can’t remember who you are, how do you know what you are capable of? Michael wakes with no memory and blood on his hands. A girl is missing - he must retrace his steps to prove his innocence.
Warnings: scenes of a violent nature violence and strong language

Description: Scotland may have failed to reach the Euros, but the alcoholic soccer pundit returns from Poland with some outrageous musings on the beautiful game. 'Needle-sharp observations on the British psyche' (Guardian). 'Almost better than football' (Independent).

Title: The Two O'Clock Show
Description: A perfect appetiser for your day at the Fringe with three instalments of stand-up comedy from Anna Freyberg - 'impeccable comedy writing and bundles of charm' (ComedyKnights.co.uk), David Hannant - 'intelligent humour' (TheNewKid.co.uk), and Chris Boyd - 'Glorious' (Chortle.co.uk).
