New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Paul Foot - Kenny Larch Is Dead
Description: Deep within the sinking sands of the Perspex jungle of youth, in the forgotten nebula of nothingness, comes an objet du desir - a trombone fruit. Needless to say, it's another warm year. 'Masterful' (Scotsman).

Title: Looby Loo: No Strings Attached
Description: Looby and Andy were puppets. They were loved by so many children that they became 'real'. Today being 50+ is proving very difficult. Don't watch with mother! 'A roller-coaster of laughter and tears' (Portsmouth News).

Title: Roisin Conaty: Lifehunter

Title: The Comedy Manifesto
Description: The most popular live political panel show in Britain. Back at the Fringe for the fifth year. Hosted by Kate Smurthwaite with team captains David Mulholland and Rick Molland. ***** (Scotsgay). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). Free, arrive early.

Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am, as well as delicious cakes, freshly ground coffee and award-winning "best ice-cream in Scotland" 2011!

Title: Irish Shorts One
Description: Alba Leisure Group's 2012 offering - The Words Upon the Windowpane and Riders to the Sea. Two works of exquisite, thought-provoking beauty. Poetry, intellect and tragedy condensed into an hour. Absolutely mesmeric.

Title: Proof
Description: Evening News Drama Award winners 2011. David Auburn's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama. After nursing her late, genius, unstable mathematician father for years, Catherine grasps his legacy as her boyfriend and her sister doubt her sanity and her potential.

Title: 7 Days in Havana
Description: A week in the life of one of the most fascinating cities on earth, chronicled day by day by seven highly individual international directors. The seven stories add up to a complex mosaic of contemporary Havana in all its richness, filled with vivid characters and dramatic contrasts, capturing a moment of time in a city on the verge of a major historical transition.
Artist: Benicio Del Toro, Pablo Trapero, Julio Medem, Elia Suleiman, Gaspar Noé, Juan Carlos Tabío, Laurent Cantet

Title: Miss Julie
Description: ***** ‘One of the best pieces of theatre ... this year’s Fringe. Louise Seyffert’s feisty Miss Julie ... the perfect foil to arrogant servant Jean (Bart Vanlaere - outstanding)’ (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘Exceptional ... more palpable emotion than half the Fringe guide’ (ThreeWeeks). www.vagabondproductions.weebly.com.

Title: Lovely Molly
Description: Eduardo Sánchez, co-director of The Blair Witch Project, returns with a persuasive bid to reconquer his place in the forefront of filmic terror. Two newlyweds move into the wife’s long-uninhabited family home in the countryside. With her truck-driver husband away for days on the road, the wife is left alone to face escalating assaults from a mysterious force. Her predicament is not helped by the fact she’s an ex-junkie with father issues…

Title: Simply the Jest presents Middle Class Tripe
Description: Following a packed-out run at last year's Fringe, the 'exceptionally witty' (NewKid.co.uk) sketch troupe are back with a brand new show dissecting the habits, rituals and downright absurdities of middle class life.
Artist: Simply the Jest / PBH's Free Fringe

Title: Anthony Browne & Catherine Rayner
Description: Our Guest Selector Vivian French brings together two of her favourite illustrators to talk work, life and inspiration. Anthony Browne is the acclaimed author and illustrator of nearly forty books, each defined by his exquisitely surreal pictures and touching stories of often sensitive or lonely characters. Catherine Rayner’s beautiful, gentle tales depicting different animals have already garnered awards and she is fast becoming one of our leading picture book artists.

Title: Within This Dust
Description: ‘So beautiful I had tears pouring down my face’ **** (Scotsman). Three dance works interwoven with film and sound explore Richard Drew’s Falling Man photographs of 9/11. Return of Smallpetitklein’s 2011 Fringe sell-out. www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com.

Title: The Complete History of the BBC in 60 Minutes
Description: Terence and Ingrid present a concise history of the greatest public broadcasting institution known to man. And beyond. Nation Shall Speak Peace Unto Nation, and they will speak BBC unto you!

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION
Description: Each day we pay tribute to persecuted writers from around the world. Freedom of Expression is at the heart of any book festival but it is also necessary for citizens and communities to speak out against injustice, express their needs and hold their governments to account. Today’s event is chaired by Scottish PEN and authors taking part include: Joanna Nadin, Oliver Balch and Holly Webb.

Title: Nick Helm: This Means War!

Title: Dan Willis: A Comedian's Life
Description: Willis presents his brand new show, an hour of no-nonsense stand-up comedy based around the Willis working week; a comedian's attempt to perform his arse off 'PMAO'. 'Unpretentious, informal, belly-laughs-a-minute stand-up' **** (ThreeWeeks). **** (List).

Title: Revill's Selection - Free

Title: This Arthur's Seat Gala Belongs to Lionel Richie
Description: One of the most memorable shows in Edinburgh! Since 2007 Josie Long, Simon Munnery and Rich Fulcher have played this fun, friendly, spectacular, one of a kind gig. Don't miss it!

Title: Anthony McGowan

Now, children’s author Anthony McGowan has been commissioned by the Willard Price estate to write four new books, starring the children of the original characters. As night slowly falls, she tells her life story, which spans the history of the Cultural Revolution. Once idealistic young journalists, Fengming and her husband were denounced as counterrevolutionaries, separated, and thrust into labour camps. A moving testament to human endurance, an extraordinary piece of oral history and a landmark in recent documentary cinema. Filmmaker in attendance.

In his new book, The Price of Inequality, he argues that unless we can reverse a terrifying concentration of wealth among top earners, the prospects for Western economies are bleak.

Douglas Coupland’s recent review of Hari Kunzru’s novel Gods Without Men suggests Kunzru has spawned a new literary genre: Translit. It’s certainly a sparkling, multi-layered gem that confidently slides across boundaries. But then so too does US-based Yiyun Li’s superb book of short stories Gold Boy, Emerald Girl which is predominantly set in modern China. Whether or not they’re creating a new genre, here are two writers whose writing is a joy to behold.

Description: Now in its fifth year, the Edwin Morgan Poetry Competition has become one of the best respected poetry prizes in Britain. With a first prize of £5,000, it attracts more than 1,000 entries each year, and for 2012 it is judged by two award-winning Scottish poets, Gillian Ferguson and Don Paterson. In today’s event the judges reveal the names of 2012’s winning poets, and invite them to present their work. Chaired by David Kinloch.

Title: Doctor Who: Dark Horizon with Jenny Colgan & Steve Cole
Description: The new BBC Doctor Who book Dark Horizons, written by bestselling author Jenny Colgan, has our hero arriving on the Western Isles to play on the famous Lewis chess set. But not everything goes to plan… Join Jenny and sci-fi author Steve Cole, who has worked for the BBC on the merchandising for Doctor Who as well as producing a range of Doctor Who audio dramas for Big Finish Productions. They talk aliens, time-travel and explore the enduring appeal of the Doctor.

Title: Gordon Southern's A Brief History of History
Description: All history. One hour. With jokes. Lightning fast edu-tainment romp. Everything, ever in hardly any detail. Total sell-out Melbourne Comedy Festival 2012. 'Poetic, clever and joyfully freewheeling' ***** (chortle.co.uk)
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Ed Eales-White: Champions
Description: Writer/performer in sketch group Clever Peter (BBC Radio 4) presents a collection of characters in his debut one-man character sketch show. 'Suffering little in comparison to Peter Cook' (Scotsman). 'Have you thought about teaching?' (Ed's mum).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: The Explorers
Description: Jazz/rock for the 21st century. Tim Rose and Steve Richardson's eclectic compositions are inspired by bands such as Weather Report, Gentle Giant, Frank Zappa, Pat Metheny and The Brecker Brothers. Expect catchy grooves, colourful harmonies and dynamic solos.
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: 21A - Free
Description: Sex-deprived cat ladies, imperialist hobos, and jaded invisible friends. These are fewer than half the raucous characters who frequent the Minnesota bus line, 21A. Master storyteller Kevin Kling's play features the many subconscious states of Neal Beckman.
Warnings: Occasional Strong Language, gunshot sound effect
Venue description: At the heart of Edinburgh’s pink quarter, GHQ is a stylish bar and venue. Free shows running throughout the day, and a late-night bar and club in the evening. Shows 11am-10pm, club 10pm-5am 7 days.
Venue accessibility:
2
\nDisabled access Broughton St Lane.

Code: Sexual Chronicles of a French Family
Title: Sexual Chronicles of a French Family
Description: Sexual frankness of a very Gallic kind abounds in Jean-Marc Barr and Pascal Arnold’s wholly aptly-titled fifth joint directorial outing. Mum, Dad, Brother, adopted sister and Granddad are all at it – all but 15-year-old Romain, in fact, who fears there’s no end in sight for his virginity. But when he is caught in the act of filming himself in a bout of classroom onanism, a sudden new awareness and openness is triggered across the whole family…

Title: Music at Palmerston Place
Description: Free evening classical concerts in beautiful West End church, featuring chamber orchestra, choir, piano and organ. Full details and programmes available at www.palmerstonplacechurch.com/activities/music.
Venue description: Modelled on Saint-Sulpice in Paris, this splendid church dates from 1875 and is in the heart of the West End. A magnificent yet intimate internal space is ideal for music concerts, featuring a fine Wells-Kennedy organ built in 1992.

Title: Rambling in an Empty Room
Description: 2012 new project, Rambling in an Empty Room. Dreams are mysterious. They're real while they last, but an illusion once you wake. Website: www.facebook.com/TheKeyPhysicalTheatre.
Artist: Chien Tzu-Ting, Huang Ching-Yu / The Key Physical Theatre
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Monkey Bars
Description: Award-winning writer Chris Goode asked 38 to 10-year-olds to talk about their lives. In Monkey Bars, their worlds are spoken by adults - playing adults in adult situations. A revelatory verbatim show that's funny, touching and endlessly surprising.
Artist: Chris Goode & Company and the Unicorn Theatre
Venue description: Scotland's new writing theatre 'is the festival's most prestigious home of serious drama' (New York Times) and a multiple Fringe First and Herald Angel award winner. 'The main hub of festival-focussed action during August' (List).

Title: Janine di Giovanni & Ed Vulliamy
Subtitle: RECALLING ONE OF EUROPE’S DARKEST HOURS
Description: Bosnia is what links these two authors. Ed Vulliamy’s The War is Dead, Long Live the War marks the 20th anniversary of the worst carnage to blight Europe since the Third Reich while Janine di Giovanni’s Ghosts by Daylight paints a raw portrait of marriage in the aftermath of war. Bidisha chairs the event which may broaden out onto the need to rethink war reporting in the light of Marie Colvin’s death.

Title: Ian Shaw - A Bit of a Mouthful
Description: Award-winning singer-pianist and cheeky raconteur’s show overflows with tales of grumpy midlife woe, salacious witty memoir, heart-stopping songs and rude sing-alongs. Perfect end to a festival day! 'Superb' (Guardian).
Artist: Ian Shaw / The Stand Comedy Club / Lakin McCarthy
Venue: The Stand Comedy Club III & IV
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue, Stand III is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand IV an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Tim Key - Masterslut
Description: Key (Edinburgh Comedy Award winner, 2009) is doing poetry and getting sodden in the same manner as last year. 'Sublime, busy and evocative work from a man who keeps getting better and better' ***** (List).
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Rosie Nimmo
Description: ‘Like it a lot. Great voice’ (Ian Rankin). ‘Utterly enchanting...’ (BluesMatters.com). ‘Delicious collection of songs’ (Fatea-Magazine.co.uk). ‘Blue velvet of her voice...’ (Sunday Herald). ‘An exquisite disc’ (NetRhythms.co.uk). ‘Deeply moving’ (Piers Ford). ‘Hugely enjoyable’ (Iain Anderson, BBC). www.rosienimmo.com.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: A Guide to Second Date Sex
Description: Witness the rawest most hilarious portrayal of male and female attitudes, anxieties and agonisingly familiar sex tricks as Ryan and Laura meet for their second date. A true story based on your sex life.
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Summer Concert
Description: Edinburgh Incidental Orchestra’s pleased to present its fourth annual summer concert, comprising entirely of aspiring young musicians. Soloist - Siobhan Parker, conductor - Calum Zuckert. Ravel - Tombeau de Couperin, Vaughan Williams - Concerto for Oboe and Strings, Tchaikovsky - Symphony No 5.
Artist: Edinburgh Incidental Orchestra, Calum Zuckert, Siobhan Parker
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Sara Pascoe - The Musical!
Description: The tale of Sara who lived from the 1980s to 2012. Sara's life includes being on TV in Stand Up For the Week and Campus (C4), The Thick of It and Twenty Twelve (BBC).
Artist: Phil McIntyre Entertainments by arrangement with Dawn Sedgwick Management
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Niddry's Wynd Haunted Underground Tour
Description: Walk through Edinburgh's infamous haunted South Bridge Vaults. Explore the gloomy rooms where Edinburgh's poor once lived alongside the criminal underworld. Be afraid! Free whisky and shortbread at tour end (whisky over 18s only).
Venue description: Half way between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood palace on the Royal Mile is the Tron Kirk, the departure point for Auld Reekie's Tours in Edinburgh. Meet at the sign boards by the Tron Kirk and learn about the dark side of Edinburgh.

Title: Ned Beauman & Nick Harkaway
Subtitle: FICTION FOR WHEN YOU’RE FEELING SINISTER
Description: After his heavily acclaimed debut Boxer, Beetle, Ned Beauman recounts The Teleportation Accident. In this 1930s tale Egon Loeser seeks pleasure in Berlin’s experimental theatres, the absinthe bars of Paris and physics labs of LA. Nick Harkaway’s Angelmaker features Joe Spork who sidestepped his criminal ancestry to enjoy a quiet life repairing clockwork. But why is he receiving visits from sinister cultists and dastardly lawyers?

Title: Comedy Club 4 Kids
Description: Otter-ly fantastic! Now in its eighth year at the Edinburgh Fringe, we're back and better than ever. Cracking entertainment for everyone, we have the best comedians doing what they do best... but without the rude bits!
Venue description: Edinburgh's all-year-round multi-arts venue. We offer a gourmet selection of theatre, cabaret, live music, visual arts and clubbing. Our cafe adds delicious homemade food, free internet and great coffee to the mix. All brought to you by the friendliest staff in town.

Title: Ian Smith and Tom Toal
Description: Ian Smith (beardy award winner, BBC2's Popatron) and Tom Toal (the Double-T, runner-up, Loaded Laftas) are two of comedy's most exciting young acts. Here they present a hilarious hour of free stand-up. **** (Scotsman, ThreeWeeks).
Artist: Ian Smith and Tom Toal / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Open from 1pm until 5am every day. 450 capacity Whistlebinkies presents over 150 artists throughout the Festival. Features local and national Scottish talent, smaller touring artists alongside tribute and covers acts. Free comedy from 1pm, free live music from 9pm.

Title: Jarred Christmas: Let's Go MoFo
Description: Electric, arse-kicking comedy. Seen on 8 Out of 10 Cats, Buzzcocks, and Dave's One Night Stand. (He's the guy with sideburns and glasses.) 'One of the funniest men to pick up a microphone' (Time Out).
Artist: Mick Perrin for Just For Laughs Live
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Hairy Pretty Things
Description: You’ve heard of burlesque, but have you heard of bearlesque...? Hairy growler Dave the Bear and ‘close friend’ Mister Meredith present something naughty, seductive, ‘sultry and soulful, I could have listened to him all night’ (Scotsman).
Warnings: Partial Nudity (thong) but the venue is over 18s anyway. It was fine last time
Artist: Dave the Bear, Mister Meredith / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Finger's piano bar is an institution established in the early 80s. During the Free Fringe shows Finger's turns into one of the best cosmopolitan venues in Edinburgh. An experience not to be missed! Opening hours 2pm till 5am. No disabled access.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Dr Book
Description: Going to the doctor can be a ball and to prove it, here’s Dr Book. This is how it works: you tell us what you like, Dr Book takes a moment to think about it, then writes a prescription for some wonderful and inspiring new books for you to read. A simple medical procedure for all – from babies to teens (and parents), courtesy of Edinburgh City Libraries.

Title: Tony Ross
Description: Tony Ross has illustrated more than 800 books, working with some of the biggest names in children's publishing such as Roald Dahl, Jeanne Willis, Francesca Simon and David Walliams. Drawing inspiration from the Little Princess series and from the weird and wonderful stories whizzing around his head, Tony Ross gives you a lesson in creativity. This is a unique opportunity to be inspired by and ask questions of one of the most popular and successful illustrators around.

Title: Scotland’s Harp - A Celebration
Description: Hear haunting Gaelic and Scottish airs and sparkling dance tunes presented in an informal ceilidh atmosphere by Na Clàrsairean (the Scottish Harp Orchestra), Lothian Gaelic Choir and guests.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: On the Move With Escalator, Shifting Disability Debates on Access to the Festival
Description: A forum that puts issues surrounding the practice and presentation of artists with disabilities at the Edinburgh Festivals centre stage. An invited panel responds to the challenge.
Venue description: Fully functioning pop-up café where food meets live-art. The entire business will be presented as art, open to public scrutiny and served with a twist. Live art duo Hunt&Darton blend art with the everyday with guest appearances from your favourite artists.

Title: Charles Nicholl
Subtitle: TRACING A DIVERSE PATH
Description: In a stylish and eclectic essay collection, historian, biographer and travel writer Charles Nicholl pursues the fugitive traces of the past with skill and relish. The subjects of Traces Remain range from a murder-case in Renaissance Rome to the disappearance of Jim Thompson in 1960s Malaya, from Christopher Marlowe to Jack the Ripper, from Shakespeare to the last days of the poet-boxer Arthur Cravan.

Title: Rent-a-Cat
Description: “A film made for cat lovers that will no doubt win over the hearts of anyone who's ever felt a yearning for unconditional companionship”. (Patrick Gamble, Cine-Vue)

Title: Ghost and Torture Tour
Description: View up close our collection of torture instruments and hear all their gory details before entering the notoriously haunted South Bridge Vaults. Free whisky and shortbread at tour end. Whisky over 18s only.
Warnings: No suitable for those with a 'Nervous Disposition' walking involved
Venue description: Half way between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood palace on the Royal Mile is the Tron Kirk, the departure point for Auld Reekie's Tours in Edinburgh. Meet at the sign boards by the Tron Kirk and learn about the dark side of Edinburgh.

Title: Absolute Improv!
Description: Scottish group create witty improvised sketches based on your suggestions. Come shout zany ideas, or bring unique items and see them transformed into fabulous scenes! Fringe 2011 smash hit returns! 'Had me laughing uncontrollably' **** (EdinburghSpotlight.com). www.tbcimprov.co.uk.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Youth on The Fringe
Description: NorthernXposure aka The Irn Cru, joined By Psychostyles BBoy Crew and G-Code Plus Special Guests.Join us for the best in local Scottish talent! Be prepared for showstopping live performances from all age groups, special guests, break-dance and spectacular surprises headlined by BAFTA Nominated NorthernXposure's SweeTs. Sponsored by Doveteam Casting & Creative Agency and Enigmatic Production & Promotion.
Venue: Leith on the Fringe @ Out of the Blue Drill Hall
Venue description: A vibrant, multi-arts venue. A hub for aerial work, circus, dance and physical theatre. LOTF offers a range of workshops to compliment our program this year, to book, or for more information visit www.leithonthefringe.com. Cafe and licensed bar open Mon-Sun 10:00-22:00. LOTF will run for the first 2 weeks of the Fringe - 3rd - 19th August
Venue accessibility:
24789
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space), assistance dogs welcome. Some performances are: Signed, captioned.

Title: Beth Cross
Description: Make a book with a difference with storyteller Beth Cross, with pockets to store drawings or puppets of favourite stories and characters. This fully interactive family event offers the perfect way for you to help your child trace their journey through books and to truly engage with reading. Beth is an accomplished performer on both sides of the Atlantic and her infectious enthusiasm makes her a firm favourite with young audiences. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: Wet Paint: A Magic Variety Show - Free
Description: Featuring spectacular new illusions, variety acts, comedy and live music, last year’s sell-out success is back! You might travel sideways in time, see the psychic bearded lady, or quiz a clairvoyant automaton.
Venue description: 100 seater venue in the basement of Le Monde Hotel just a stone's throw from the Assembly Rooms with a modern atmosphere to it.

Title: Newland
Description: A professional cast premiere an electrifying new musical, where treachery and love prevail during the Californian Gold Rush. An original, contemporary and jazz-infused score underpins drama, comedy and colourful characters in an era both vibrant and deadly.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Shadow Dancer
Description: thriller from Oscar-winning director James Marsh (Man on Wire, Project Nim) boasts outstanding central performances from Clive Owen and Andrea Riseborough as the main protagonists caught in a complex web of political intrigue, set against a deeply insightful depiction of pre- peace-process Belfast.

Title: Kazahana
Description: Print courtesy of Be Wild.

Title: Lord Nelson Presents...
Description: A repressed Englishman, a bitter Irishman and a delusional organist. Back from sea, Nelson presents a rum cocktail of talent currently sweeping the comedy streets of London (literally). These rising stars offer stand-up, music and character comedy.
Venue description: At the heart of Edinburgh’s pink quarter, GHQ is a stylish bar and venue. Free shows running throughout the day, and a late-night bar and club in the evening. Shows 11am-10pm, club 10pm-5am 7 days.

2
\nDisabled access Broughton St Lane.

Title: The Canterville Ghost
Description: Bringing Oscar Wilde's farcical tale to the stage, come and see what happens when the Otis family move into Canterville Chase, haunted by a ghost that none of them believe exists. Will he succeed in scaring them?
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Mark Restuccia: How to Succeed at Internet Dating
Description: Mark's a world-expert internet dater. Now he's sharing his secrets with you. They might prove too powerful to guarantee an actual relationship but they'll certainly up your click-thru rate. 'Corking lines' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: Gilded Balloon at Third Door is an exciting new space, just moments from Teviot Row House. Bringing you the very best in theatre, comedy and magic, reflecting the diverse and innovative programming that the Gilded Balloon is world renowned for.

Title: Dream Plays (Scenes From a Play I'll Never Write)
Description: Dive into the dream world of leading UK playwrights in a series of specially commissioned staged readings. Curated by Orla O'Loughlin and David Greig. Ticket includes coffee and a breakfast roll.
Venue description: Scotland's new writing theatre 'is the festival's most prestigious home of serious drama' (New York Times) and a multiple Fringe First and Herald Angel award winner. 'The main hub of festival-focussed action during August' (List).

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning events for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. Appearing today: Andy Stanton.

Title: Jack and Nikki: Killing Machines
Description: Jack Heal (Chortle Student Comedian 2008) and Nikki Blemings (a girl) request the pleasure of your company at their business seminar on contract killing. Bring cash for this once in a lifetime opportunity. Goggles optional.
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.
Venue accessibility: \nNo access for wheelchair users - venue up flight of stairs.

Title: Return to Ribblestrop with Andy Mulligan
Description: Imagine a boarding school in an old mansion with ghosts, monks, animals, noisy boys and odd teachers. If this is your kind of place then join Andy Mulligan as he describes his Guardian Fiction Prize-winning novel Return to Ribblestrop, a tale with a great adventure at its core but also packed with wonderful, warm and funny characters. This is one school that would certainly challenge an HMI Inspector.

Title: JSAC Presents: A Lot of Seoul
Description: A Lot of Seoul showcases five dance companies from Seoul, South Korea. Dance styling that features hip hop and modern contemporary dance, with a blend of traditional Korean movement.
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Ben Okri
Subtitle: THE SHORT STORY AS PLAY
Description: Man Booker prize-winning novelist Ben Okri’s 2009 short story The Comic Destiny has been turned into a play by Lazzi theatre company and it receives its premiere during this year’s Fringe, at the Scottish Storytelling Centre. Joining Ben Okri on stage at the Book Festival are actors Charlotte Jarvis and Robert Williamson, who will present a short extract from the performance. The play’s director David Johnstone will also join them to discuss why Okri’s story lends itself so well to a theatre adaptation.

Title: Mr Braithwaite Has a New Boy
Description: Adoption, inheritance, a raunchy rent boy and one stressed-out pussy... With everyone after a slice of the pie, someone's bound to get it in the end. From creators of Butt Boy and Tigger. www.outcast.org.au.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: The Famous Club Spiegel
Description: Where were we last night...? Convivial craic, slick suits, fine spirits, lipstick and leather lounges. Subversive acts, famous cats, great hats and who was tickling the 88s? Just a dream? No… The Famous is back!
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult
Venue description: The Famous Spiegeltent. The original, beloved, iconic festival venue returns to the faithful! The grandest dame of all is back in town, out of the gardens and onto George Street: sexy, funny, dangerous – a living legend!
Venue accessibility:
2459
\nWheelchair access, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC.

Title: Bernard the Ferret (Happy to be Himself!)
Description: This funny and magical storytelling with puppets, launches a new book by playwright Eve Stebbing. Performances are followed by a workshop. See www.spinofftheatre.co.uk for more information.

Title: Breabach
Description: Nominated simultaneously in the BBC Radio 2 and Scottish Traditional Music awards as Best Group, Breabach’s originality on double bagpipes, fiddle, vocals and bass have earned them an international reputation as one of Scotland’s foremost acts.
Warnings: under 16's must be accompanied by an adult
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.

02459

Title: The Bongo Club Cabaret (and NYE Club)
Description: The original and best cabaret returns for its 14th year. Expect to be tantalised, shocked, entertained and mocked by some of the best hand-picked Fringe acts. ***** (Scotsman). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). **** (Fest).
Warnings: nudity, adult themes, strong language, strobe lighting, controversial material
Artist: The Bongo Club and The Kitten Has Claws
Venue description: Edinburgh's all-year-round multi-arts venue. We offer a gourmet selection of theatre, cabaret, live music, visual arts and clubbing. Our cafe adds delicious homemade food, free internet and great coffee to the mix. All brought to you by the friendliest staff in town.

Title: Making Life Taste Funnier
Description: Get a taste of how funny life can be with north-east comedians Graham Oakes and Sean Turner. Their second year at the Fringe, they bring you stand-up comedy ranging from observational to surreal. www.makinglifetastefunnier.co.uk.
Artist: Graham Oakes and Sean Turner / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Paterson Arran Ten at Ten
Description: A delicious morning reading from one of our Festival authors to set you up for the day. Check the screen in the Entrance Tent to see who’s reading each day.

Title: Bitesize Chekhov
Description: Three short plays (The Proposal, The Bear and Swan Song) performed by three actors inside an hour. Music, farce and physical theatre performed in a unique style. 'What a range of emotion inside this breast!' (Chekhov, Swan Song).
Venue description: 40 metres from the centre of Princes Street, just up from the National Gallery, this beautiful venue has a reputation for quality ***** and **** sell-outs! Outstanding, international companies: interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, classics, cutting-edge plays, dance, quirky comedy and musicals...

Title: Mick Miller and Jimmy Cricket
Description: Two comedy legends together. One night only. With nearly 70 years experience between them, they are showing today’s comics how it’s done. TV credits include The Royal Variety, IDEAL, Comedy Rocks, Comic Relief and more…
Artist: Lee Martin for Gag Reflex Management
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Harpsichords at St Cecilia's 2
Description: Gerard McDonald and John Kitchen contrast works by virtuoso Italian oboists Sammartini, Besozzi and their countrymen with bravura keyboard works by Scarlatti and Marcello, featuring the 1769 Kirckman harpsichord. ‘Acclaimed period instrument group’ (Guardian).
Warnings: The show requires a quietly attentive audience.  Not suitable for extremely young children.
Artist: Arborea Musica: Masters of the Hautboy
Venue address: Corner of Niddry Street and Cowgate,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cecilia's is the oldest purpose-built concert hall in Scotland, dating from 1763, and is one of Edinburgh's best kept secrets.  An historic and interesting space, it is ideal for acoustic music performances. The Russell and Mirrey Collections of Early Keyboard Instruments are housed in two adjacent galleries.

Title: Underground History Tour
Description: Discover the colourful, violent history that makes Edinburgh's Old Town's infamous underground city a huge worldwide attraction, for visitors to experience the slum conditions and the stories that brings to life both bygone characters and events.
Venue description: Half way between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood palace on the Royal Mile is the Tron Kirk, the departure point for Auld Reekie's Tours in Edinburgh. Meet at the sign boards by the Tron Kirk and learn about the dark side of Edinburgh.

Title: Markus Birdman – Love, Life and Death
Description: This son of a preacher man ponders, where’s God when you actually need him? 'A soul bearing joy. Such weighty material, handled with the utmost respect. Beautifully captivating, genuinely charming, hilarious’ **** (Skinny). www.markusbirdman.com.
Artist: Markus Birdman / The Stand Comedy Club

Title: Fringe Guide to Running a Venue
Description: Managing a venue at the Fringe can be a rewarding experience, but is also a mammoth undertaking. This discussion will guide you through the A-Z of venue operation before, during and after the festival.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Call Me!
Description: Come rejoice with us at the ridiculousness of love! Gorge on therapist Sandy’s speciality tartlets as you witness cringe-worthy tales of dating woe and relationship calamities. ‘Hugely funny’ (BritishTheatreGuide.info). ‘Perfection’ (ManchesterSalon.org). ‘Hilarious’ (WhatsOnStage.com).

Title: Sh!t Theatre Present: Sh!t Theatre's JSA (Job Seekers Anonymous)

Come and meet favourite characters, see how Lydia draws her bold and vibrant pictures and have the opportunity to join in with songs, stories and more.

His weekly satirical cartoons are pitch-perfect, balancing the humour of caricaturing high-profile figures with incisive political comment. In this special masterclass, he reveals his techniques and inspiration.

Their food supply dwindles to nothing, as a woman comes searching for her husband, one of the labourers. Cinematography by Lu Sheng, whose directorial debut, Here, There, is also screening at EIFF.

Description: Situated on the historic Royal Mile, open from 9am - 3am every day. Presenting free comedy from 1pm and live music from 9:30pm including acoustic rock, indie, blues and folk. Food served until 9pm. www.royalmiletavern.com.
Venue description: Open from 9am at the heart of the Festival on the Royal Mile, free comedy shows starting from 10am every day and free live music from 9:30pm to 3am every night. Food is served all day with outside seating available.

\nAccessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Hannibal Buress: Still Saying Stuff
Description: Brand new, razor sharp stand-up from 2011 Foster's Newcomer nominee, star of The Secret Policeman's Ball and 30 Rock writer, Hannibal Buress. ‘A must-see’ **** (Scotsman). ‘Worth getting excited about’ **** (Guardian).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Christopher Brookmyre
Subtitle: DEVILISH DOINGS AT THE SHARP END
Description: Delving into the dark nooks of the Glasgow underworld is no walk in the park. Thankfully, ballsy PI Jasmine Sharp is well up to the task, but even she has to gasp as a new case uncovers decades of sex, drugs, ritualism and murder. With his characteristic humour and eloquence, Brookmyre steers his abundance of fans towards his latest tale, When The Devil Drives.

Title: Beatle Mal's Legendary Band
Description: He was the shadow that appeared behind the act you've known for all these years. Beatles roadie and friend Mal Evans remembers, with a pinch of Pepper! Late-night entertainment with original music.
Venue description: Paradise Green's purpose-built venue in the vaulted basements of Augustine United Church hosts an exciting programme of theatre and comedy for all tastes, from classics to new and experimental work. Soak up the true spirit of the Fringe.

Title: Shlomo: Ministry of Mouth
Description: After last year’s sell-out debut, World Loopstation Champion and internationally acclaimed beatboxer Shlomo returns with his latest solo show, taking vocal music to new heights in a dazzling combination of intricately crafted beats, loops and basslines.
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Ceilidhs in Lauriston Hall
Description: With caller Ken Gourlay and ceilidh bands HLI / MacAlba / Scott Leslie / Willie Fraser and piper. All dances walked through and called. Hall has air conditioning! Soft drinks £1, alcohol £3. www.edinburghceilidhs.co.uk.
Warnings: No stilettos / high heel shoes please
Venue description: Lauriston Halls (both modernised) are situated between the Grassmarket and Tollcross, 10 minutes walk from Princes St. The Large Hall has air-conditioning which makes it ideal for dancing. It is a regular ceilidh venue, popular with locals and visitors.

Title: Blackwell's Writers at the Fringe
Description: Blackwell's Bookshop presents an evening filled with the best of Scotland's literary scene. Get ready to experience everything from Scottish poetry to cutting-edge drama, from folk music to contemporary fiction.
Venue description: Edinburgh's oldest bookshop, with over 150,000 titles spread over three floors of converted Georgian townhouses.

Title: An Audience With the Duke of Windsor - Bob Kingdom
Description: Who was the real Edward, Duke of Windsor and who 'chaperoned' Wallis in New York? Bob Kingdom's explosive and revealing new play explores one man's choice between love and money.
Artist: Richard Jordan Productions Ltd in association with Assembly
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound presents the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces The Hall, Rainy and the Baillie.

\nWheelchair accessible except for Baillie Room, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Rumpelstiltskin's Grimm Tales
Description: Join the magically mischievous Rumpelstiltskin and rambunctious Little Red-Cap on the ever enchanting trail of the Golden Goose as this award-winning company weave the magic of the Grimm Tales. Fringe sell-out 2006, 2007, 2009, 2011. **** (EdFestMag.co.uk).
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: P.E.M. Acting Workshop
Description: The P.E.M. is an innovative acting method that offers most effective triggers to access authentic emotions. With its pure physical approach the scientifically evaluated P.E.M. provides performers with a reliable, direct and guidable access to emotion.

Title: Alan Gibbons & Ally Kennen
Description: A chance to meet two leading writers for young adults. Alan Gibbons’ latest novel, An Act of Love, is a frank, highly-charged story about war and its impact on two friends. Ally Kennen introduces Bullet Boys, a gripping, thought-provoking story filled with twists, turns, guns and danger. Together, they share their research methods, what inspires them and how they develop their characters to create authentic, heartfelt novels.

Title: Itch: A Scratch Event
Description: Festival comedians perform their latest batch of brand new scripts - rehearsed and unrehearsed. Funny, moving... and sometimes entirely unpredictable! Itch performers include Hattie Hayridge, Fred Macaulay, Jo Caulfield, Jack Whitehall, Phil Nichol and Clovis van Darkhelm.
Artist: Comedians Theatre Company / Pleasance Theatre Trust
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: What Comes Next?
Description: Acclaimed author Keith Gray has edited an anthology of stories by leading writers looking at where we go when we die, entitled Next. Each short story examines the idea in different ways. Kate Harrison’s trilogy Soul Beach is about a girl whose sister is murdered and trapped in a kind of limbo website for young people but can communicate with a chosen loved one through the site. Join Keith, Kate and Iona Heath, President of the Royal College of General Practitioners and author of Matters of Life and Death, to explore the idea of afterlife, why some cultures and individuals believe there is such a thing and why death is such fertile territory for writers.

Title: Big Sean, Mikey and Me
Description: Join Big Sean Connery, Hibs Boys, sadomasochistic Irish girls, American randoms, London metrosexual weirdos and wee radge Edinburgh wideos on this dark comedy journey with a heart. ‘A slice of true Edinburgh class’ (Irvine Welsh).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Trevor Browne - I Think ... I Am
Description: Trevor Browne - the greatest folk-rock singer of all time takes a break from international fame to go on a spiritual journey of self-discovery. 'Brilliantly funny and perfect ... hilarious.' ***** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Plenty More Fish (But I Don't Have a Fish Fetish)
Description: Would you date a dictator? Would more people study mathematics if they knew Pythagoras was a hottie? Irish Girls, big questions, big answers. www.facebook.com/accidentandemergencycomedy. ‘So funny ... cured my constipation’ (Graffiti).
Artist: Accident and Emergency / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue accessibility: \n

Title: Moishe's Bagel
Description: Genre-defying original acoustic music from one of Scotland's most admired bands. A cutting-edge, triple distilled brew of eastern European dance music, Middle Eastern rhythms and virtuoso performances. ‘Exhilarating ... breathtakingly intricate, with the momentum of an express train’ (Herald). www.moishesbagel.com.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Mary Contini
Subtitle: SIZZLING STORIES FROM THE QUEEN OF CULINARY EDINBURGH
Description: Valvona & Crolla owner Mary Contini's previous books took the form of letters to her daughters. As well as being touching memoirs, they just happened to be excellent cookery books. Now, Contini takes on the great Italian sausage, and she joins us today in an entertaining and wide-ranging event which begins with the amazing history and surprising versatility of this delicious everyday favourite.

Title: Ladies Live Longer: Ladylike
Description: Shortlisted for Laughing Horse New Act Comp 2012, Funny Women Variety Winners 2011. You'll love them - however they're likely to offend the person sitting next to you! Warning: this comedy includes female, musical and sketch. www.ladieslivelonger.com.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Malones Live Music
Description: In the heart of Edinburgh's Old Town, Malones presents seven days of live music absolutely free. Showcasing artists from across the musical spectrum with over 150 acts featuring local and national talent. For full listings visit www.malonesedinburgh.com.
Artist: Malone's Irish Bar / PBH's Free Fringe

Title: Jigsy
Description: Jigsy is a jobbing comic. Over thirty years, he's worked with them all - and he’ll tell you the stories to prove it. Starring Les Dennis, this blisteringly funny play reflects on the success Jigsy might have had. www.jigsylive.co.uk.
Warnings: 14+ must be accompanied by an adult
Artist: Jigsy Productions Ltd / The Assembly Rooms
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.

Title: Tania Edwards - Killer Instinct
Description: A Faustian epic of middle-class proportions from 'hilarious' (ThreeWeeks) stand-up Tania Edwards as she examines just how far we should go to get ahead. 'Born to perform' (Times). 'Very talented' (Time Out). 'Urban sharpster' (Stage).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Hell's Bells by Lynne Truss
Description: A DVD of an obscure British costume drama is planned. The creative talents assemble to record a commentary. Warning: contains intense bitterness and mild irreverence towards hats.
Artist: Pleasance Theatre Trust, Lynne Truss, Simon Scullion
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Laurent Binet & María Dueñas
Subtitle: FROM HISTORY TO HISTORICAL FICTION
Description: Meet two spectacularly talented authors whose debut novels have caused a sensation in Europe, and which now look set to do the same in Britain. Both take place against the backdrop of real events: Laurent Binet’s HHhH is the Prix Goncourt-winning story of Heinrich Himmler and the plot against Reinhard Heydrich. Meanwhile María Dueñas’ multi-million-copy bestseller The Seamstress is set in Morocco and Franco-era Spain. Chaired by Stuart Kelly.

Title: Cadillac
Description: The performance is a lottery show, similar to Wheel of Fortune. The rules are simple - everyone who buys a ticket and takes part in the lottery has a chance to win the Cadillac. Is this a fair game?
Warnings: Supported by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute www.culture.pl
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Roy Hattersley
Subtitle: IN PRAISE OF IDEOLOGICAL POLITICS
Description: When Tony Blair swept to power, conceptions of 'left' and 'right' seemed destined be replaced by a centrist politics that transcended ideology. Since then, political ideas have taken second place to a technocratic approach to government in Britain. But in this explosive lecture by Roy Hattersley, he argues that ideology is the lifeblood of democratic politics and we should embrace it passionately again.

Title: Morgan & West: Clockwork Miracles
Description: Enter the workshop of Victorian magical duo Morgan and West. Delve deep into the conjuring clutter and discover a multitude of magical marvels hidden within. Sell out show 2009 - 2011. 'Simply spiffing!' ***** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Cadenza at the Fringe
Description: Mozart Solemn Vespers and Haydn Little Organ Mass, performed by one of Scotland's most exciting and versatile choirs. Conductor Jenny Sumerling with Wilma MacDougall, Beth Mackay, Andrew Nunn and Brian McBride (soloists) and Morley Whitehead (organ).
Venue description: Over the past 18 years, Greyfriars Kirk has become an acclaimed city centre venue with a relaxed atmosphere and magnificent acoustics. The Kirk is open every day throughout the festival. Perfect venue for choral and orchestral performances.

Title: Professional Ballet and Contemporary Classes
Description: Daily ballet and contemporary classes with inspirational teachers, suitable for dancers with extensive technical training. For daily teacher listings see www.dancebase.co.uk.
Artist: Dance Base, National Centre for Dance
Venue: Dance Base - National Centre for Dance
Venue description: Centrally located in the Old Town, Dance Base is a beautiful and inspiring setting for dance. We present performances by the best British and international dance companies and also offer classes and workshops from breakdance to ballet - for all ages.

Title: Irish Shorts Two
Description: Celebrating the great Dublin-born Sean O'Casey's flamboyance and versatility with two of his one-act plays. While immediately fun, they sustain the impression of bigness of mind which is inseparable from his tragi-comic vision of life.
Venue description: These secluded gardens, overlooking the stillness of Duddingston Loch, made famous by the painting 'The Skating Minister', lie under the shadow of Arthur's Seat and the ancient Duddingston Kirk. 'The most beautiful venue in Edinburgh' (Scotsman). Bus service No 42.

Title: Wake Up and Sing!
Description: Wake Up and Sing! This is a full audience participation event! Have fun, be surprised, be moved! Free the voice you were born with. Internationally acclaimed voice-meister Edwin Coppard takes you on an amazing journey. Free!
Venue description: The Pear Tree offers a large outdoor courtyard and stage for free daily performances of shows and music all day during the Fringe, plus regular barbecues - and is also right next door to the Counting House Free Festival venue.

Title: Philip Ardagh & Axel Scheffler
Description: Come and meet The Grunts, a slightly disgusting and very unusual family. The ridiculously tall and beardy author Philip Ardagh introduces his new stories while illustrator Axel Scheffler demonstrates how he came up with what they all look like. This event is guaranteed to be icky, entertaining and, as Philip would say, ‘FUN just doesn’t express it.’

Title: Karen Campbell & Stef Penney
Subtitle: WHY DON’T THEY WANT TO FIND ROSE JANKO?
Description:
The novels of Edinburgh-born Stef Penney have now been translated into 30 languages, with new legions of global fans drawn in by The Invisible Ones. It has been seven years since Rose Janko went missing without a huge amount of fuss. Now her father has hired PI Ray Lovell to uncover the truth, but his task is hampered by the very people he thought he was helping.

	Please note: In this event Stef Penney will now be joined by Karen Campbell. Former police officer turned writer, Campbell has won awards for her gripping and utterly realistic portrayals of police force investigation.

Title: Joseph Delaney
Description: Join Joseph Delaney to discover what happens in the tenth installment of the hugely popular Wardstone Chronicles. Time is running out for Thomas Ward as his final battle with the fiend draws near. Come and hear all about the series, where Joseph got his ideas for this supernatural tale and the importance of the tutor-student relationship which is at the heart of each adventure.

Title: Dream or Not?
Description: Visual Virus present a storytelling performance of sexuality within adult relationships. A fun, flirty and highly-charged play delivered by male and female sign language users who cleverly show both perspectives of this adult theme.
Warnings: Adult content. Performed fully in BSL
Venue description: The Scottish Storytelling Centre is the world's first purpose-built centre for storytelling, right on the Royal Mile. The award-winning Netherbow Theatre and Storytelling Court spaces host live storytelling, literature, theatre, children's and visual arts events. A warm welcome for families. Book online for tickets.

Title: Debate: Rethinking Europe
Subtitle: DO WE NEED A EUROPEAN COMMUNITY ANY MORE?
Description: Storm clouds have been gathering over Europe for some time. Yet in the past the European community came together to improve trade, and to avert war, famine and disease. Do the factors which made Europe so important after the war still matter today, or would it be better to cut its losses and break apart? David Ellwood, author of The Shock of America: Europe and the Challenge of the Century, Matthias Politycki, German author of Next World Novella and José Rodrigues dos Santos, bestselling Portuguese novelist and news commentator, fire up the debate.

Title: Watch It!
Description: A multi-media dance odyssey fusing hip hop, contemporary dance, theatre, interactive film and animation about one man's love/hate relationship with his TV. ‘Essential viewing ... not only for lovers of dance but for theatre enthusiasts. ***** (Skinny). www.r-2-m.net.
Venue description: An award-winning extravaganza of the best performances from across the Fringe spectrum. The majestic Main House is packed with outstanding dance and physical theatre from around the world while the Cabaret Bar and Studio host thrilling drama, comedy and music.

Title: Adolf
Description: ‘Terrifying, searing, transfixing... It is quite impossible to be anything other than totally absorbed by Utton's performance. Adolf reaffirms the need and worth of political theatre.’ (Scotsman). One of the most exciting solo shows of the past decade.
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.

Title: The Eighth Day
Description: What's it like to lose everything? Hero to zero overnight. Everything gone, Sam has only the family dog. Yet she stands between him and a warm bed! Darkly comic, deeply moving, laugh-out-loud funny.
Venue description: Venue 13 promotes new writing. Run by the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama in collaboration with the California Institute of the Arts, the 2012 season will feature the best new theatre from Wales and the United States.

Title: Get Plugged In!
Subtitle: KICK-START YOUR WRITING CAREER
Description: Emerging writers, look here! Are you looking for fresh ideas and smart solutions on how to plug into the vibrant literary community in our city of literature? Join us to tap into the buzz on zines, ebooks, Twitter and performance opportunities. Be inspired by folk who have come up with grassroots, independent, cross-artform and non-traditional ways of getting their work heard and read. Part of the Edinburgh City of Literature New Writing Programme.

Title: The  Great Big Comedy Picnic - Free
Description: For the 10th year, the picnic returns for more teatime titters. Critics' Choice 2006 and 2007. **** (ThreeWeeks). A stand-up selection box of comedy quiche and sausage rolls in the aisles.
Artist: Ian Fox in Association With the Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: Colm Tóibín
Subtitle: NEW WAYS TO KILL YOUR MOTHER
Description: A writer absolutely at the height of his powers, Colm Tóibín is known for his stunning novels such as Brooklyn and The Master. He is also an avid reader and a perceptive literary critic. In this event Tóibín delves into his breathtakingly entertaining new book of essays about writers and their families, in conversation with the Orange Prize-longlisted novelist Tessa Hadley.

Title: Bashabi Fraser
Subtitle: WHERE SCOTLAND AND INDIA MEET
Description: Trained as an Indian dancer and choreographer, Bashabi Fraser is now a highly-respected poet and author in Scotland. She joins us with two new books: Ragas and Reels is a book of poems on the New Scots, with photographs from Herman Roderigues, while Scots Beneath the Banyan Tree recounts stories from Bengal. Includes music and poetry recited 'in the voices of the Tay and the Ganga'.

Title: Robin's Ukulele Extravaganza
Description: Be whisked away to a world of ukulele fun with Robin and friends. Learn your first chords and play along to classics such as Stand By Me, Yellow Submarine and maybe even something by Jessie J!
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Heroes of Alternative Fringe
Description: Pick of the Fringe. Genuine Alternative comedy legends alongside the most exciting Fringe freaks. Raw, exciting stand-up, variety, bizarre... Master of Chaos Bob Slayer hosts Phil Kay, Greatest-Show-on-Legs, Miss Behave etc. 'The real Fringe' (Metro). www.heroesof.com/fringe.
Warnings: This is The Greatest Show On The Fringe so Bring your Friends! This is The Greatest Show On The Fringe (It is important they know this!)
Venue description: Genuine Comedy Legends, alongside the most exciting non-conformists of today. Centrally located. Shows all day. Nightclub until 5am. An alternative to expensive tickets. Recreating the spirit of adventure that existed before Alternative went Mainstream. No Rules, No Limits, No refunds!

Title: Reshape While Damp
Description: Surreal, truthful and topical. Comedy to make you laugh, smile and think. With original songs. Jewish stories. And a lemon. 'Comic timing here is sublime' (FringeReview.co.uk, 2011). 'Articulate, dry sense of humour' (Leicester Comedy Festival). www.reshapewhiledamp.com.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Captain Taylor's Coffee House
Venue description: A stylish and relaxing licensed cafe, and a brand new Fringe venue offering a mixture of quality food and drink, and free shows throughout the day - all right in the heart of Edinburgh, just off of the Royal Mile.

Title: Steal Away with Alyxandra Harvey
Description: Canadian writer Alyxandra Harvey is a poet, novelist and a Mr Darcy devotee. She’s also one of the leading supernatural writers working today. Her novels such as The Drake Chronicles and Briar Rose contain everything from vampires to zombies. Her new novel, Stolen Away, explores the mythology of the faery folk. But we’re not talking sweet creatures at the bottom of the garden – these are dark Lords which will do anything to get what they want.

Code: Film Restoration in the Digital Age
Title: Film Restoration in the Digital Age
Description: This panel event will explain the process undertaken to restore classic films including LAWRENCE OF ARABIA, which we unveil this year in a brand new digital print.  Panellists include Grover Crisp, Senior Vice President of Film Restoration and Digital Mastering for Sony Pictures Entertainment, and multi-Oscar-winning editor, (and widow of the late Michael Powell) Thelma Schoonmaker. The panel will be chaired by Nick Varley, Managing Director of Park Circus, the leading international distributor of classic and repertory cinema.

Title: Ruth Rendell
Subtitle: CHILLING TALES FROM THE QUEEN OF CRIME
Description: Made a Life Peer in 1997 for her contribution to British literature, Ruth Rendell has been described by Ian Rankin as ‘probably the greatest living crime writer in the world.’ We are thrilled to welcome her back to discuss her latest novel, The Saint Zita Society. It’s a chilling story of an oddball gardener who begins to behave very oddly indeed.

Title: Japanese TerminatoL
Description: Japanese TerminatoL is a hilarious show featuring parody movie trailers, audience interactive orchestras, and Japanese Don Quixote slapstick. ‘The rare performance where the comedian can say anything and have the audience rolling in the aisles’ **** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Located right on the Royal Mile, The White Horse has been reborn in the last two years as a stylish bar, cafe and bistro right in the centre of Edinburgh. With great value lunches, followed by free shows from late afternoon until the end of the nght

Title: Bach for Solo Violin
Description: Acclaimed Hungarian violinist Tamas Fejes performs a selection of sonatas and partitas by J. S. Bach, written for unaccompanied violin, including the mighty Chaconne.
Venue description: Built in 1688, this beautifully light and spacious kirk serves both the Palace of Holyroodhouse and Edinburgh Castle. Experience its wonderful 'cathedral' acoustic at a concert, or join us for worship on Sundays at 10.00am or 11:15am.

Title: Alexander McCall Smith
Subtitle: MEET ONE OF THE WORLD'S MOST POPULAR AUTHORS
Description: Join us for a wonderful journey into the colourful world of Alexander McCall Smith, bestselling author of The No 1 Ladies' Detective Agency and 44 Scotland Street. In a joyful, rambunctious hour, McCall Smith introduces a cast of his loveable characters including Precious Ramotswe, Bertie and his mother Irene, and Edinburgh's own amateur sleuth, Isabel Dalhousie. Surprises await!

Title: Africa Calling!
Description: Traditional Zimbabwean dance, music, rhythm and song - greetings reaffirming friendship and warmth of community. Following sell-out shows in 2011, Grassroots brings a vibrant fusion of irresistible movement and beautiful melodies to invigorate the spirit. www.grassrootstheatre.com.
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Monski Mouse's Baby Disco Dance Hall
Description: Retro-fabulous DJ Hostess, Monski Mouse, unleashes high energy smiling in this disco for under fives. Bop along to lashings of swing, pop, soul and more! Adelaide Fringe sell-out, 2012!
Warnings: No more than 2 children per adult. All children must be accompanied by an adult, and no adults can buy tickets without bringing a child. Children under 6 months can enter free with a paying adult. Parents are encouraged not to bring children older <5

Title: Landing the Role
Description: This workshop explores the keys to landing the role in auditions. Taught by a professional actor who has worked in theatre, TV and film in NY and LA, see what it really takes to land the role!
Artist: New York Conservatory for Dramatic Arts
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Liam and Owen - A Cracking One Off Show!
Description: Liam and Owen do stand-up.
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: A smart bar, located right in the centre of the Grassmarket with a large open bar space, free shows upstairs and a secluded beer garden and terrace - with food and drink available all day a great place to hang out during the Fringe. 18+

Title: Postcards from the Zoo
Description: A charming and unclassifiable work. Instead of a linear narrative, one-named director Edwin uses a gently drifting series of images and episodes to follow the life of a young girl who is abandoned by her father to be brought up in a sprawling zoo in Jakarta. The second half of the film takes a different course as our heroine is lured outside her animal paradise into the more perilous world of humans.

Title: Elephant Man
Description: Benoit Hattet - Two Johnnies Live Upstairs ****(Scotsman) - returns as Joseph C Merrick, the world’s biggest monster. Meet the creature and his nurse. Joseph is impatient to see you. But he’s a sensitive man so control your emotions…
Artist: Compagnie du Fomenteur / Benoit Hattet, Isabelle Bouvrain
Venue description: Just minutes from Princes Street, the Institut français offers an intimate theatre space, presenting a fantastic programme of theatre and children’s shows. The Bistro offers a cosy French atmosphere to enjoy some food and drinks throughout the day.
