Code: Tim and Eric’s Billion Dollar Movie
Title: Tim and Eric’s Billion Dollar Movie
Description: Having gained a dedicated following with Tim & Eric’s Awesome Show Great Job!, US comedians Tim Heidecker and Eric Wareheim break out from the confines of online sketches and small DVD releases to bring their unique style of humour to  the glorious big screen. Long established collaborators Zach Galifianakis, Will Ferrell, John C Reilly and Jeff Goldblum star alongside the titular heroes in this brilliantly absurd and delightfully dark tale of greed, friendship and shrim.

Title: Leave It on the Track
Description: Hellcats. Meet the brilliantly named players (Curly Suicide, Miss Amerikill, Rocky Casbah...), get a lesson in the rules (despite appearances, there ARE rules), and witness the thrills and (eye-wateringly painful) spills of derby at its best.

Title: Ron Butlin
Subtitle: EDINBURGH MAKAR GETS COLLECTED
Description: Irvine Welsh described Ron Butlin’s The Sound of My Voice as one of the top novels to make its way onto the bookshelves in 80s Britain. As Edinburgh Makar, this fine gentleman has done readings, had poems printed in the papers about the trams, conducted interviews and made speeches. The Magicians of Edinburgh is his collection of poems written during that period as the capital’s Laureate.

Title: The Fastest Train to Anywhere
Description: A story about dislocation, adventures and where the winds might take us. This train can take you many places, but can never take you home. The man is lost, here, with you. @FlanCol #LittleFest. www.theflanagancollective.co.uk.
Artist: The Flanagan Collective #LittleFest at C nova
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Peter Pan on Dinosaur Island
Description: Defeat the T-rex with Peter and real swords! Bombard Captain Hook with dinosaur droppings! Professional interactive theatre: kids come onstage throughout! 2011 Fringe sell-out! ‘Exactly what every show for kids should be like’ ***** (ThreeWeeks). www.spotlites.co.uk.
Warnings: Adults must be accompanied by a child! Adults must be accompanied by a child!
Venue description: 40 metres from the centre of Princes Street, just up from the National Gallery, this beautiful venue has a reputation for quality ***** and **** sell-outs! Outstanding, international companies: interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, classics, cutting-edge plays, dance, quirky comedy and musicals...

Title: The Late Show
Description: Underbelly's very own late-night stand-up show, now in its 11th year, is moving to Bristo Square. Previous acts include McIntyre, Bailey, Noble, Howard, Byrne (both), O'Briain, Flight of the Conchords and many more. Full line-ups at www.underbelly.co.uk.
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Karma Comedian - Stella Graham - Free
Description: British comedian Stella Graham unravels hilarious tales of good and bad karma with side-splitting one liners you'll quote to friends. ‘Terrifically funny’ (TVNZ.co.nz). If you attend, good things will come your way. www.freefestival.co.uk, www.stellagraham.com.
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items ... Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: The Musicians
Description: The Ridley Road School Orchestra are at the European Festival of Youth, hours away from playing their most important performance. There is only one problem, their instruments seem to be missing! For anyone who has ever played air-trombone.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: For the Love of Willie
Description: This adaptation of Agnes Owens' novel tells the tragic and touching story of Peggy, an ordinary girl in extraordinary times. One day delivering newspapers, the next, her life spiralling out of control. www.theatredreams.co.uk.
Venue description: Just off the Lawnmarket our friendly venue is centrally placed on the terrace above Victoria Street . We provide a 65 seating rake and a black box theatre, our own box office and reception area. Our venue profits go to charity.

Title: Eat $h*t: How Our Waste Can Save the World
Description: Step aside Al Gore, the environment has a new champion! The PURU - his honest potty humour tackles the global sanitation crisis. He's changing the world, one flush at a time! www.thePOOPproject.org.
Artist: The POOP Project with WTE Theatre (New York)
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Well Behaved Women Rarely Make History
Description: Marilyn Monroe famously said 'well behaved women rarely make history'. Join us on a rollercoaster ride through the lives of this Hollywood legend and some ladies who subscribed to her theory. www.spannerintheworks.org.
Artist: Spanner in the Works Theatre Company
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Deadly Medley
Description: Don't miss Deadly Medley, a gleeful 45 minute romp through four of Shakespeare's great tragedies. Living the Bard's immortal words, ‘Never excuse, for when the players are all dead, there needs none to be blamed.’
Venue description: Pilrig St Paul's church is a spectacular Victorian gothic church and halls with a 100 seat studio theatre and a 400 seat sanctuary auditorium, all within an easy stroll or quick bus ride from Princes Street.

Title: Undercovered
Description: Explore the story of undercover cop Mark Kennedy through a montage of gripping physicality. Questioning identity misrepresentation, Undercovered merges visual media, dynamic movement and non-fiction to create a thought-provoking and captivating piece.
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Young Samurai with Chris Bradford
Description: The Ring of Fire is the final thrilling adventure in the hugely successful Young Samurai series. Join Chris Bradford for the exclusive launch of his last book and to learn what it takes to become a samurai. Witness Chris’ authentic samurai sword display and discover the mystic secrets of the deadly ninja in this all-kicking, all-punching event.

Title: Victoria Campbell's Viking Gold
Description: When Victoria Campbell was asked to describe her debut novel Viking Gold in five words she chose ‘historical, teen, action, adventure, quest’. All that’s left to add is it is a thrilling, heroic story of a young Viking boy who survives an attack on his village, forcing him on a journey across the seas and far from the people and the lands he knows and loves. Come and hear about Victoria’s own journey from great story to published book.

Title: Dido and Aeneas: Love and Betrayal
Description: An exciting new take on Purcell's classic opera. It recounts the story of Dido and her love for the Trojan warrior, Aeneas. With evil at work, despair and destruction are not far away...
Venue description: Just off the Lawnmarket our friendly venue is centrally placed on the terrace above Victoria Street . We provide a 65 seating rake and a black box theatre, our own box office and reception area. Our venue profits go to charity.

Title: Jon McGregor (Cancelled)
Subtitle: UNSETTLING STORIES UNDER HUGE OPEN SKIES
Description:
Jon McGregor's last novel, Even the Dogs, confirmed him as one of Britain's most talented fiction writers. He returns to discuss his new book of short stories, This Isn't the Sort of Thing That Happens to Someone Like You. There’s a strong sense of impending apocalypse in his stories, but many are playful and surprisingly funny. In what has been dubbed 'the year of the short story', this is one of 2012's literary highlights.

	Please note: Jon McGregor is no longer able to attend the Book Festival and this event has been cancelled.

Title: Lari Don
Description: Come and join Lari Don for the launch of the fourth book in her First Aid for Fairies series, Maze Running and Other Magical Missions. These books have proved incredibly popular – Lari’s use of the rugged Scottish landscape combined with mythical centaurs, selkies and dragons have gripped the imaginations of young readers. Lari reveals her inspiration and gives a taste of the latest exciting adventure.

Title: Paul T Eyres: T.Eyres of a Clown / Laughing Horse Pick of the Fringe - Free
Description: Come and see this brilliant free comedy show in which Paul tries to find out who he really is, and indeed who we all are!
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: Back to School's Disco
Description: Dance the night away at this rollickingly retro School Disco! Alongside a gloriously cheesy pop soundtrack, there'll be prize giving, prom king and queen election and a potent punch. DJs to be announced. www.backtoschooledinburgh.com.
Venue description: Braidwood Centre is 5 minutes behind the Pleasance Courtyard and from the Royal Mile. With full disability access and licensed bar. Meet at the Pleasance Courtyard Information Booth 10 minutes before the show to be whisked away.

Title: Fragment
Description: A light-hearted, athletic and quirky exploration of what pulls us apart and brings us together. Through graceful modern dance punctuated by energetic partnering, Fragment will be a feast for your senses with original live sultry jazz and folk music.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Cathedral Wilde Plays Liszt
Description: International concert and recording artist David Wilde returns to St Mary’s in a programme of music by Franz Liszt on the Cathedral Steinway. CD signing afterwards.
Venue description: One of the world's great neo-gothic buildings, with its three distinctive spires and a tradition of daily choral services sung by the cathedral choir: a magnificent concert venue.  The Song School is covered by vibrant murals by Phoebe Anna Traquair.

Title: Chansons Françaises
Description: Zahida will sing Piaf, Brel and many others. A beautiful hour of chansons francaises! You will not regret having attended the show as it closes with the all time classic, Non, Je Ne Regrette Rien!
Venue description: A daily selection of Free shows, comedy, theatre and cabaret, running as part of the Free Festival, with performances running all day from midday until midnight in this friendly venue, offering a wide range of drinks and food

Title: Skye
Description: When a child was left alone by her mother, the world erupted. Based on a true story, this new play explores the life of one mother who finds herself judged by those who have their own questions to answer.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Half of Next Year's Show - Free
Description: If you'll love next year's show you'd like this. It is the same but less. With me, Laughing Horse New Act Of The Year 2011, going strong in 2012 but stock rapidly depreciating...
Artist: Adam Belbin / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Debate: Rethinking Iran
Subtitle: IS IRAN WILLING TO GO TO WAR WITH ISRAEL?
Description: Apocalyptic predictions of lengthy and disastrous war between Israel and Iran in 2012 are growing in frequency. What is driving this sabre-rattling, and why does President Ahmadinejad persist in arguing that ‘the Zionist state will disappear’? Is there a grain of truth in George W Bush’s much-ridiculed claim that Iran is a member of an ‘Axis of Evil’? The Economist’s former Iran correspondent Christopher de Bellaigue is joined by Israeli historian Ilan Pappé in this discussion.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: HUMAN RIGHTS AND THE ENVIRONMENT
Description: A company’s operations can be deadly for communities. Damaging agriculture and fisheries destroys livelihoods and food sources, and the contamination of drinking water exposes communities to serious health risks. Our daily series of events today features extracts from works written by and about those whose human rights have been violated. Reading today: Joanna Bourke, Tristan Gooley and Nikita Lalwani.

Title: Unstable Fables
Description: Get ready for this totally wacky, outrageously hilarious venture into the world of improvised fables! With the audience changing the course of the plot at every turn, this is sure to be a rocky ride into the unknown!
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Armada
Description: A new musical's untold love story of the Spanish Armada. Dr John Dee, Elizabeth I and Sir Francis Drake foil the invasion aided by an angel. 'Great fun ... immediately engaging ... comic and musical timing is brilliant' (York Press).
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Gentlemen Bears
Description: Chortle finalist Nicholas Cooke, Laurie Rowan and Keiron Nicholson talk science, conspiracies and childhood dreams. A spin-off of the acclaimed cult comedy night. 'Completely original ... hilarious and disturbing in equal measure' **** (Latest 7). 'A lyrical wit' (Chortle.co.uk).
Artist: Nicholson, Cooke and Rowan / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description:
The Hudson Hotel is ideally located at the west end of Princes Street. With an extensive wine and cocktail list, live music on Friday and Saturday nights from 9pm, and Bacaro nightclub hosting free comedy from 1:30pm until 10pm daily. Open from 8am. Food served throughout the day until 10pm Sunday to Thursday and 9pm Friday and Saturday.

Title: Danny Wallace
Subtitle: TAYSIDE JESTER WITH MOVIE-FRIENDLY DEBUT
Description: In his non-fiction work, he’s tried to start a new country and helped a comedy friend find as many of his namesakes as possible. Now Dundee-born Danny Wallace brings us his debut fiction, Charlotte Street, in which a man becomes obsessed with the images inside a discarded disposable camera. Does that sound filmic? It should do, as Working Title has already optioned the movie rights.

Title: Art Assemblage - Cities and Other Topics
Description: A fascinating tribute to cities and related topics seen through the eyes of a Scottish photographer and a French painter, both world-travellers. Affordable art for sale.
Venue description: Leith Library is a 1930s Art Deco building. It is easily accessible by public transport (Lothian Buses). It is a short walk from/to Ocean Terminal and the Royal Yacht Britannia.

Title: Gerbrand Bakker & Linden MacIntyre
Subtitle: INTERNATIONAL STORIES OF MYSTERY
Description: Linden MacIntyre’s Why Men Lie offers a moving and complex conclusion to the Cape Breton trilogy featuring Effie, an independent, middle-aged woman working as a tenured professor of Celtic Studies. In Gerbrand Bakker’s The Detour, a Dutch woman rents a remote farm in rural Wales. She has fled from an unbearable situation in Amsterdam, but events at the farm become increasingly curious.

Title: Recent Tragic Events
Description: September 12th 2001 - Andrew meets Waverley for a blind date. What has pervaded New York a day before slowly creeps into their private space. Touching the absurd, the play discusses freedom and determination in a traumatised society.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: The Best Of Scottish Comedy
Description: Fifteenth side-splitting year. Quality showcase with Caledonia’s finest. Old favourites and rising stars. Four great comics for twelve quid. Changes nightly. ‘Great value in a relaxed environment’ (Scotsman). ‘Best in the country’ (Evening News). www.thestand.co.uk.
Venue description: Edinburgh's year-round comedy club is housed in an intimate basement bar just off St Andrew Square. The atmosphere is relaxed and informal with comfortable cabaret-style seating (although some late night shows are not all seated).

Title: A  Good Catholic Boy
Description: Good boy gone wrong! Find out how Canadian stand-up comedian Massimo went from good Catholic boy to whiskey drinking hardcore comedian. ‘A big loud Italian with a disarming soft side’ (Hour Magazine).
Venue description: A daily selection of Free shows, comedy, theatre and cabaret, running as part of the Free Festival, with performances running all day from midday until midnight in this friendly venue, offering a wide range of drinks and food

Title: Ronnie and the Other World
Description: Ronnie has woken up in the real world, a world without sing-a-longs or candy trees. Is he cut from the right cloth to save Happydale or will he be just a puppet all his life?
Venue description: Just off the Lawnmarket our friendly venue is centrally placed on the terrace above Victoria Street . We provide a 65 seating rake and a black box theatre, our own box office and reception area. Our venue profits go to charity.

Title: Gearoid Farrelly: Turbulence
Description: Gearoid makes his Edinburgh debut with Turbulence, a stand-up show about life's little bumps and major stresses. Turbulent events covered include break-ups, career-choices, childhood addiction to Kinder Surprise eggs, school reunions and sibling rivalry. Fasten your seatbelt!
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Lost Voice Guy and Jeff Lantern - Not Afraid of Tablets
Description: MC’d by Patrick Monahan. Lost Voice Guy is disabled but not silent. Jeff Lantern is a mentalist. A conspiracy factist who is going to save the world (again). www.jefflantern.com.
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink. With a section of free Fringe shows in the downstairs room throughout the day.

Title: Airy Delights
Description: A varying and colourful programme for different sized groups including the charming piano sextet by Thuille. After last year’s phenomenal success featuring Gulda’s cello concerto SCWE are at St Mark's Castle Terrace a second time. Details on website.
Venue description: The artSpace programme of music and drama, in our acoustically excellent auditorium within St Mark's Unitarian Church, is performed by virtuosos, both well-known and newcomers. The church welcomes you at 11:00 Sundays for Church Service including a short recital.

Title: Married With Snails
Description: It's an absurd life! A hilarious look at Miranda and Bernie’s eccentric marriage where structure, travel and snails are extremely important. But will the next adventure in Paris run smoothly? Absurdly funny and gloriously unique.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Dylan Evans & Margaret Heffernan
Subtitle: WHY SOME PEOPLE RISK EVERYTHING
Description: There is a special kind of intelligence for dealing with risk which doesn’t correlate with IQ, and is found in disparate groups such as weather forecasters and hedge fund managers. Dylan Evans’ Risk Intelligence shows the importance of probability and speculation. Margaret Heffernan’s Wilful Blindness takes the case of Enron as the starting point for an analysis of why we are so prone to ignoring the problems in front of us.

Title: The Complex: Oedipus
Description: It's the 2504th performance of Oedipus Rex and Chorus 6 wants to call it quits. But the tragic hero isn’t ready to let go. If you thought you knew Oedipus, think again. 'Indisputably excellent' (Varsity, Cambridge).
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Jon Gray & Jamie Keenan
Subtitle: JUDGING A BOOK BY ITS COVER
Description: Paper books are battling for survival against the rise of the ebook but new technology is opening up the creative potential of book design. Book jacket designers Jon Gray and Jamie Keenan have developed ‘Twenty Immutable Theories of Cover Design’ which explain how great design sells books and how our connection to a book goes beyond the words inside.

Title: The Andi Neate Band
Description: Quirky, well-travelled singer/songwriter returns home to perform songs from her beautifully crafted sixth album Flying Full Circle. Touching humour, solitude, love and loss. A wonderfully natural talent shining through. 'Pick of the Fringe' (Praguefringe.com).
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: Lucinda Dickens Hawksley
Subtitle: THE DEFINITIVE GUIDE TO CHARLES DICKENS
Description: To mark the 200th anniversary of the birth of Charles Dickens, we welcome his great-great-great granddaughter, Lucinda Dickens Hawksley, to discuss her beautiful illustrated guide to the man and his works. Featuring previously unpublished family photographs and proofs showing Dickens' own editing marks, this is a unique perspective on a much-loved writer.

Title: Chinese Music Traditional and New
Description: Enjoy the sounds of traditional Chinese instruments played by this Scottish-based group, featuring Fong Liu's entrancing voice, and including Hooi Ling Eng's percussion and zheng, Eddie McGuire's bamboo flute and Xian Shan's classical accordion.
Venue description: Built in 1688, this beautifully light and spacious kirk serves both the Palace of Holyroodhouse and Edinburgh Castle. Experience its wonderful 'cathedral' acoustic at a concert, or join us for worship on Sundays at 10.00am or 11:15am.

Title: Luke Benson - Backseat Hero
Description: Two-time Comedian of the Year nominee's much anticipated debut show. Ever been stalked? The Geordie Giant brings you a joke-filled hour about petty acts of heroism 'He looks the part, he's got the talent' (Sunday Times).

Title: Writing Workshop
Subtitle: PLACES, WORLDS AND WORDS
Description: This workshop is about engaging with the outdoors and the elements, and developing the writing skills for observing and evoking a vivid sense of place. Linda Cracknell is a writer of prose and radio drama. Her books include Life Drawing and The Searching Glance and she is editor of A Wilder Vein, a non-fiction anthology on the wild places of Britain and Ireland.

Title: Debate: Rethinking Sport
Subtitle: HAS PROFESSIONALISM RUINED OUR NATIONAL GAMES?
Description: Greed, debt, cheating and the cult of the overpaid celebrity: these are just some of the downsides of professional sport as we know it today. Is it time for a radical rethink of the way football, professional cycling and other sports are funded? Former BBC Sports Editor Mihir Bose leads this discussion with cycling journalist Richard Moore, Leeann Dempster, Chief Executive of Motherwell Football Cluband Ruth Wishart, who takes the chair.

Title: The Future of the Novel
Subtitle: WILL THE NOVEL REMAIN WRITERS' FAVOURITE NARRATIVE FORM?
Description:
Has the dominant literary form of the 19th and 20th centuries grown stale? Is it no longer the best means of delivering stories in the 21st century? Or does the classic literary novel remain the form best placed to deliver innovative, memorable writing? Drawing on discussions about censorship, style, politics and identity, this session, bringing Edinburgh’s 2012 Conference to a close, offers an address by multi award-winning author China Mieville, with renowned author Janne Teller in the moderator’s chair.

	Please note: The keynote address for this event was originally to be given by Aharon Appelfeld, who is no longer able to attend. Instead China Mieville will deliver the keynote and lead the discussion afterwards.

	Visit the Edinburgh World Writers’ Conference website - www.edinburghworldwritersconference.org - to watch a live broadcast of this and other conference events and to join in the conversation online. Follow the conference twitter feed: #WorldWritersConf.

	Supported by the Scottish Government's Edinburgh Festivals Expo Fund, Creative Scotland, the City of Edinburgh Council and Event Scotland.

Title: Crypted
Description: Interactive tragedy based on the life of Alan Turing, the Bletchley Park codebreaker chemically castrated by the government. Part of Negative Capability's double-bill by RSC prizewinner Freddy Syborn, co-writer of forthcoming BBC3 sitcom, Bad Education. 'A triumph' (Scotsman). www.freddysyborn.com.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Casablanca: The Gin Joint Cut
Description: A lovingly disrespectful homage to one of the classic films of all time. Casablanca has some of the most iconic scenes and best lines ever written, so why not play it again?
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: THE ARAB SPRING
Description: 2011 was a year without precedent for the Middle East and North Africa. Amnesty International stands in solidarity with peaceful protesters in demands for human rights and political reform. Our daily series today features extracts from works about the uprisings in Egypt, Tunisia, Libya, Bahrain, Yemen and Syria. Reading today: Elaine Proctor, Jon Gower, Kate Rawles and Selina O’Grady.

Title: Yoga for Performers
Description: A relaxing physical programme, aiming to equip the performer with a routine that can be used for stress-relief and energy-focusing in the crucial moments before stepping on stage. Run by professional actress and yoga teacher. www.theatrotranscendental.com.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Stu and Garry in The Lunchtime Show
Description: ThreeWeeks Editor's Choice Award 2010. ‘Their improvisation set goes down a storm’ (Scotsman). ‘Achingly funny’ (Evening News). ‘Anarchic, quick-witted improv at its fast-paced best’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘Pure, inspired genius’ (Skinny).
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult

Title: Hamlet! the Musical
Description: Shakespeare becomes funny, accessible and memorable in this fresh musical take on the doomed Danish prince. With young cast and live band, it's Hamlet like you've never seen it before - shorter, funnier and with show tunes!

Title: A Funny Thing Happened On the Way to the Forum

Title: Guinea Pigs

This will be a fascinating event for Tolkien fans both young and old.

Title: After the Rainfall

Title: And Still Rarely Rong

Title: Victorian Edinburgh with Frances Jarvie & Gordon Jarvie
Description: Come and explore Victorian Edinburgh from the crowded tenements to the Lord Provost’s office. Using the true story of Greyfriars Bobby, Frances and Gordon take you on a fascinating tour that includes the opportunity to handle artefacts from the National Museum of Scotland’s collection. Afterwards, you can head off to be an urban explorer and see all you’ve learned about.

Title: Excuse Me, I’m Trying to Please You
Description: Let Fiona, the ultimate people-pleaser take you to audience pleasure level 10. Inspired by the late, great Joyce Grenfell, ‘A fantastic, one woman, monologue-performing, spoof song-singing masterpiece. Pure pleasure' ***** (LargeManchester.com).

Title: Me and Mr C

Title: Rime
Description: A circus, theatre and dance show based on Samuel Taylor Coleridge's epic poem The Rime of the Ancient Mariner. ‘effortless precision… intriguingly explored’ – This Is Cabaret. Associate artists: Roundhouse and Jacksons Lane; co-commissioned by the National Theatre.

Subtitle: SHARP THORNE

His DI Thorne series began haunting readers in 2001 and with sales continuing upwards, it was only a matter of time before David Morrissey brought Thorne to life on the small screen in a Sky One series. Now, hear about the latest Thorne thriller and a new book, Rush of Blood.

Title: The Curious Scrapbook of Josephine Bean

Cathy Brett and Keren David write witty, charming tales with sassy lead characters. Cathy’s latest novel, Verity Fibbs, combines great illustrations with a story of fashion, gaming and mystery. She has written non-fiction books about cowboys, sharks and pirates, but now writes successful novels for young adults. Description: Music by Chopin and other romantic composers performed by international award-winning musicians including cellist Jun Sasaki, pianists Omri Epstein, Ashley Fripp and James Sherlock. Different artists and programmes each concert. Tea/coffee and shortbread included afterwards. www.roslarts.org.uk.
Venue description: Edinburgh's most central venue, with stunning castle views, has an intimate chamber music room, plus gallery. Restaurant and bar with food. An oasis of calm in the heart of the festival hustle and bustle.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Set List: Stand-Up Without a Net
Description: Whose Line? type challenge for stand-ups. Comedy stars get a never before seen 'set list' of topics as they walk onstage to create spontaneous stand-up! ***** 'The must see show of the festival!' (Scotsman).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Jeremy Paxman
Subtitle: WHAT RULING THE WORLD DID TO THE BRITISH
Description: 'The British Empire had begun with a series of pounces. Then it marched. Next it swaggered. Finally, after wandering aimlessly for a while, it slunk away.' Jeremy Paxman's engaging and insightful written history of the Empire is a powerful accompaniment to his wide-ranging TV series. Join him for his fascinating account of how he got to grips with this epic project. Chaired by Allan Little.

Title: A Little Night Music
Description: Pianist Alasdair Cameron returns with a kaleidoscope of nocturnal pieces by Debussy, Grieg, Granados, Chopin and Beethoven. Favourites will include Clair de Lune, Nocturnes, Moonlight Sonata etc. 'A masterpiece' (EdinburghGuide.com).
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Totally Tom
Description: After a total sell-out last year, the Foster's Edinburgh Newcomer Award nominees 2011 return with a brand new sketch show. ‘Refreshingly original’ ***** (Telegraph). ‘Warped, clever, funny and well acted’ **** (Times).
Artist: The  Mason Sisters @ PBJ in Association with Underbelly Productions
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Attempts on Her Life - Free
Description: U.W.E Drama Society presents Attempts on Her Life by Martin Crimp. We pursue the illusive Anne as we explore scenes depicting her life. Join us on the Attempt on Her Life, to discover who Anne is?
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Paul Dabek - Nothing Up My Sleeve!
Description: Award-winning magician Paul Dabek returns to the Fringe with his high energy one-man show. An eclectic mix of sleight of hand, illusion and quick fire comedy from a critically acclaimed international performer.
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.
Venue accessibility: \nNo access for wheelchair users - venue up flight of stairs.

Title: Putting it Together
Description: See them here, now, first! Each evening two top graduates from the Musical Theatre course at The Dance School of Scotland perform powerful, personal cabarets featuring classic and contemporary musical theatre and drama repertoire. www.thedanceschoolofscotland.org.uk.
Artist: Dance School of Scotland / Trinity College London
Venue description: Paradise Green's purpose-built venue in the vaulted basements of Augustine United Church hosts an exciting programme of theatre and comedy for all tastes, from classics to new and experimental work. Soak up the true spirit of the Fringe.

Title: Andrew Feinstein
Subtitle: DANGEROUS TRUTHS ABOUT THE ARMS TRADE
Description: The global arms trade is worth about $60 billion, much of it taking the form of shady weapons deals struck in offshore havens and out-of-town hotels. Andrew Feinstein's explosive new book pulls back the curtain on the trade, exposing a corrupt network of activities which links formal government deals and the illicit arms trade of the 'shadow world'.

Title: Don’t Expect Too Much
Description: As Nicholas Ray’s partner, Susan Ray lived with We Can’t Go Home Again  from the inception of that massive project through the director’s lengthy attempts to finish it. In Don’t Expect Too Much, she provides the ideal introduction to the ambitions, accomplishments and contradictions of the film. Capturing the memories of those who participated in the production as Ray’s students, Don’t Expect Too Much also incorporates rare film and audio documentation of Ray teaching at Harpur College in the 1970s.

Title: Sweeney Todd
Description: Stephen Sondheim's epic musical thriller. Dark and comic, wonderfully macabre and gruesome story of betrayal, love and bloody revenge. www.lincolncompany.co.uk.
Venue address: St Columba's by the Castle,Johnston Terrace
Venue description: C's original offshoot with alfresco chillout barbecue-bar. C4kids - the top children's shows. Showstopping musicals. Shakespeare played backwards, forwards, any way at all. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: CappellaJuice: Beyond the Wardrobe
Description: Musical sketch show highlighting the side-splitting situations that surround our clothing choices. This is a revue of physical, comic and harmonic delight for all. Complete with stunning a cappella medleys of popular hits. www.fiatofacile.co.uk.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Nights at the Circus
Description: ***** 'People to watch' (FringeReview.co.uk). Fourth Monkey return to the Fringe with a new adaptation of Angela Carter's mesmerising novel. Fevvers is a circus aerialist with wings, but is she a fraud or the real thing?
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Clare Beaton
Description: Clare Beaton’s rhyming board books contain beautifully crafted illustrations made from stitching colourful felt. Come and hear her tell the stories and then join in with crafty fun to create your very own touchy feely pictures. No stitching required, just a bit of imaginative sticking! Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: Being a Physical Actor / Clown at Cirque du Soleil
Description: Come meet talent scout Marc-André Roy to learn more about life at Cirque du Soleil from a physical actor and clown’s perspective. An insight from the audition process to on-stage experience.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Girimunho
Description: A film about embracing life with no fear of death. After the passing of her husband, an octogenarian widow is far from done with living and proves to be a source of inspiration for her blood relatives and extended family as she relishes the day-to-day.  Almost documentary in feel as non-professional actors portray versions of themselves in improvised scenes, this slice of existence in rural Brazil can’t help but be charming and life-affirming.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning events for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. On today: Storytime with Peter Rabbit

Title: Town: a Spirited Story
Description: Fact, fiction and the supernatural become ever harder to distinguish, through your stained and blurred window. Based on the Gothic stories Berenice and Ligeia by Edgar Allan Poe. Explore the worst fears imaginable! A truly chilling experience.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Patrick Ness
Description: The multi-award-winning author Patrick Ness is one of our leading writers for young adults. His Chaos Walking trilogy is en route to the silver screen and his latest novel, A Monster Calls, has been shortlisted for both the Carnegie and the Kate Greenaway Medals. An incredibly versatile writer, moving with ease from fantasy to family drama, Patrick has a lightness of touch that goes deep – his novels are not easily forgotten. Chaired by Keith Gray.

Title: Jackson Voorhaar's One True Love(s) - Free
Description: Jackson brings his self-deprecating style to his loves (beer, metal, sex) and loathes (babies, yoga, Australia). ‘The b*st*rd offspring of Eddie Izzard and Noel Fielding’ (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Paterson Arran Ten at Ten
Description: A delicious morning reading from one of our Festival authors to set you up for the day. Check the screen in the Entrance Tent to see who’s reading each day.

Title: Joyce Carol Oates
Subtitle: RISING OUT OF THE MUD
Description: The celebrated US novelist Joyce Carol Oates joins us to discuss her new novel Mudwoman, the intensely powerful story of a young Ivy League academic whose enormous success conceals personal traumas, including her mother’s attempt to submerge her as a toddler. Each year Oates' name is high on the list of people tipped for a Nobel Prize: this remarkable novel may well tip the balance.

Title: No Pressure to Be Funny
Description: The topical comedy panel show presented by LBC’s James O’Brien takes a no-holds-barred look at the news. Previous guests include Alexei Sayle, Mark Thomas and Andi Osho. www.amnesty.org.uk/edfest.
Venue description: Venue150 @ EICC just gets better and better! This year, take in some big names, world-class comedy, internationally renowned dance and jaw-dropping acts from across the globe. All in the capital's comfiest venue! www.venue150.com

Title: Mozart Requiem
Description: Scotland's most exciting chamber choir Coroedina return to the Fringe with a performance of Mozart's legendary Requiem in the beautiful setting of Greyfriars Kirk, accompanied by chamber orchestra. Programme also includes a performance of the Solemn Vespers.
Venue description: Over the past 18 years, Greyfriars Kirk has become an acclaimed city centre venue with a relaxed atmosphere and magnificent acoustics. The Kirk is open every day throughout the festival. Perfect venue for choral and orchestral performances.

Title: Alex Yellowlees Hot Club Jazz Quartet
Description: This modern day Grappelli, on violin, with virtuoso guitarists Ged Brockie and Mike Nisbet, and double bassist Kenny Ellis, perform intoxicating Hot Club jazz. Laced with Latin rhythms and Celtic gypsy flair! Outstanding! www.alexyellowleesband.com.
Artist: Alex Yellowlees Hot Club Jazz Quartet
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Sheeps - Dancing with Lisa
Description: Skits and sketches. 'Something quite different and very exciting indeed' (Independent). 'A winning combination' (Guardian). 'One of the strongest new acts around' (Times). 'One of the most exciting sketch acts to emerge in years' (TimeOut). www.sheepscomedy.com.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Bridget Christie: War Donkey
Description: How did Hitler choose soups in restaurants? What are Tory feminists? Why no Spielberg donkey blockbuster? Bridget Christie knows. ‘Avant-garde comedian of prodigious talent’ (Guardian). ‘Beautiful insanity’ (Sunday Times). ‘Excellent’ (Telegraph).
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
02459
\n
\nOn street parking for a blue badge holder, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC

Title: S D Crockett & Caroline Green
Description: Dystopia is the new Vampire! S D Crockett and Caroline Green have each created fascinating and unnerving stories set at a point in the future. Sophie’s world in After the Snow, is a collapsed society in which her young protagonist is trying to find a life beyond the ruins. In Cracks, Caroline’s central character Cal discovers he’s been in a deliberately induced coma for most of his life and his reality is an illusion. Find out more from the authors and speculate on the dark visions of what our future may hold.

Title: Phil Buckley - Simple Things - Free
Description: Award-nominated comedian Phil Buckley is 31, engaged, owns a house and has a good career, but he still wonders what happened. ‘Top class’ (Time Out). ‘All round funny’ (List). www.philbuckleycomedy.com.
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.

Title: North Sea Gas: In Concert
Description: Back again with more great Scottish songs, tunes, wit and banter. North Sea Gas are a highly entertaining band who appeal to all age groups thus giving their shows a wonderful atmosphere. www.northseagas.co.uk.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Will Brooker
Subtitle: WILL THE REAL CAPED CRUSADER PLEASE STAND UP?
Description: With the next Batman movie stealing the summer blockbuster thunder, cultural commentator Will Brooker shines a light onto the cultivation of the Dark Knight’s 21st century mythology. Offering a rigorous yet accessible account of the complex relationship between the Batman films and their audiences, Brooker explores themes of authorship and adaptation in an age of rampant media convergence.

Title: Kirsty Gunn & Elliot Perlman
Subtitle: STORIES TO MAKE SENSE OF OUR HISTORY
Description: In The Big Music, Kirsty Gunn has created an epic literary novel that weaves a story of Scottish history through the eyes of John Sutherland, a folk musician struggling to complete a composition that will define his life. Meanwhile, leading Australian writer Elliot Perlman's The Street Sweeper interleaves the devastating stories of two men in a remarkable novel that ranges from New York to Warsaw and Auschwitz.

Title: Anthony Cartwright & Richard Milward
Subtitle: ACCEPTABLE IN THE 80S
Description: The 1980s are under the spotlight again in two wild novels from rising British authors. In Anthony Cartwright’s slightly controversial How I Killed Margaret Thatcher, a Midlands lad sees his hopes being torn asunder under the new Tory government and decides to take drastic action. Meanwhile Richard Milward consolidates the reputation he first carved out with Apples, writing about one girl’s redemption (or damnation) in Kimberly’s Capital Punishment.

Title: Devvo Dole Queue Hero is Free
Description: Been on E4, C4, BBC3, massive on YouTube, massive in Yorkshire. Job quitters guide to becoming a Dole Queue Hero. Make millions. Bring yer drugs, buses are gay. 'Vilest man in UK' (Sun). www.devvo.tv.
Venue description: Genuine Comedy Legends, alongside the most exciting non-conformists of today. Centrally located. Shows all day. Nightclub until 5am. An alternative to expensive tickets. Recreating the spirit of adventure that existed before Alternative went Mainstream. No Rules, No Limits, No refunds!

Title: Paul Kelly
Description: One of the world's finest singer/songwriters, Australian Paul Kelly has recorded 18 studio albums in an influential career spanning over 30 years. 'There is no evening long enough to cover the best of Kelly' (Rolling Stone).
Venue description: Edinburgh's leading live music venue offers classical, jazz, blues, pop, rock, world, folk and comedy in the intimate surroundings of a converted Georgian church. www.thequeenshall.net

Title: Rock and Pop on the Fringe
Description: Hear music from Trinity’s groundbreaking new rock and pop exams and songbooks performed live by talented aspiring musicians. This fantastic concert will include songs from the classics to recent releases. Free goodie bags! www.trinityrock.com.
Venue description: Edinburgh's oldest bookshop, with over 150,000 titles spread over three floors of converted Georgian townhouses.

Title: Seven Secrets of the Working Actor
Description: This workshop answers the biggest questions in the business, discussing the balance between art and biz, handling the ups and downs of everyday living as an actor. Designed for the professional.
Artist: New York Conservatory for Dramatic Arts
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Rocky Horror Night!
Description: Rocky Horror Night! It’s astounding … time is fleeting… Join Dr Frank N Furter and the gang once again to celebrate our 10th year of Rocky Horror madness at Frankenstein’s Pub! Don't dream it, be there!
Venue description: Frankenstein Pub is a multi-level themed bar serving up a monster experience in eating, drinking and entertainment seven days a week! Dine with us from 12:00 or party with the live DJ 'til 03:00! Beware of the monster ... it's alive!
Venue accessibility: Restricted access, staff more than happy to help.

Title: Gareth Morinan Presents the Saturday Debates (1+2)
Description: At last! Comedians debating serious topics. Gareth chairs proceedings, and will be awarding points for both wit and sensibility. Line-up includes, Kate Smurthwaite, Nick Sun, Ian Smith, Nish Kumar and Joe Wells!
Venue description: This family-run restaurant on South Bridge hosts free comedy in the basement from 1pm until midnight every day of the Fringe. Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am, as well as delicious cakes, freshly ground coffee and award-winning "best ice-cream in Scotland" 2011!

Title: Dirty Blood
Description: ‘So Joe - if I bashed your head in, Mum could have your heart. She could take your kidneys, liver, pancreas, even your bones. But alive today, she can't have your blood.' New Writing. Scottish Playwright. www.dirtybloodplay.co.uk.
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Creative Writing Class
Subtitle: VISUAL STORYTELLING
Description:
Cate James explores the idea of visual storytelling, focusing on how an illustration can carry as much of the story as words. Cate's illustrations are full of humour and in this event she also shares ideas about visual jokes. Emphasis will be on character design, and translating words into pictures for publication. Cate James has a BA (Hons) Printmaking and an MDes Illustration from Edinburgh College of Art. She uses a wide range of media in a process combining Photoshop with traditional printmaking and painting. In 2011 she was the illustration department's Artist in Residence at Edinburgh College of Art, where she still teaches. She illustrates the delightfully quirky 'Lollipop & Grandpa' picture book series, written by Penelope Harper and published by Phoenix Yard, as well as producing work for Frances Lincoln Books, Quercus and Paper Tiger. This in-depth class will allow you to develop your writing and illustrative skills. (Lunch & coffee included.)

	Please note: Cathy Brett was originally due to lead this Creative Writing Class but is no longer able to appear and Cate James will lead the class instead.

Title: Pommery Champagne Tutored Tasting
Description: n/a
Venue address: The Signet Library, Parliament Square, Edinburgh

Title: Daughters of Lot
Description: A sexy and silly retelling of an ancient story, until the performers do a trick that requires more than flexibility. Arousing and agitating in biblical proportions, this is not your daddy’s burlesque club ... or maybe it is.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: The Not Quite Quartet
Description: Take a musical maestro, blend with spontaneous comedy, inject wit and intelligence and you get The Not Quite Quartet, a duo of unforgettable, unforgivable talent! 'Brilliant' (GetComedy.com). 'The Laughs - and awe - just kept coming!’ **** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Dare I Say It?
Description: Prohibited Jargon give a new flavour to verbatim theatre. Through words of others, a female cast tackle the taboo yet remarkably relatable topic: First Times. If you leave without thinking ‘that’s me!’ - you’re in denial.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: 1000 Years of Scotland's Dark Past
Description: Exciting, scary and fun... Delve into Scotland’s bloody history. Experience live actors, dark history, thrilling rides and special effects. For an extra special Fringe experience visit between 6pm and 7pm. Are you brave enough?
Warnings: May not be suitable for children aged 8 and under, and for persons of a nervous disposition
Venue description: 100 years of Edinburgh's darkest and most gory history, 11 actor led shows and two scary rides make the Edinburgh Dungeon an educationally chilling experience and a great day out for the whole family.
Venue accessibility:
29
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible.

Title: Magic Carpet Stories
Description: The National Museum of Scotland’s Magic Carpet will be flying in to Charlotte Square Gardens to introduce little ones to fantastic stories, songs and activities. Come and be transported to exciting places and meet a host of characters. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: Raymond Mearns - Rock'n'Roll Comedian - The Therapy Sessions
Description: Supporting Pete Doherty on Tour in 2011 was a blast, though everything we do in life has consequences. Some of these are hilarious, some not so!
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: A smart bar, located right in the centre of the Grassmarket with a large open bar space, free shows upstairs and a secluded beer garden and terrace - with food and drink available all day a great place to hang out during the Fringe. 18+

Title: Perle
Description: With one performer and his television, Perle is a live comic book about dealing with loss, told through a bold mixture of illustration and performance. Verity Bargate winner, Arches Brick winner, two-time Total Theatre nominees. 'Terrific new talent' (Guardian).
Venue description: The Roxy, a beautifully converted former chapel, is the latest addition to Assembly's growing list of venues.  Built in 1809 and located just north-east of our George Square hub, the Roxy houses three performances spaces; the 400 seat former nave Roxy Central, the 168 seat Roxy Upstairs and our 60 seat studio Roxy Downstairs.  The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Will Marsh's Ruination
Description: Britain has broken down and it needs a jump start. Will Marsh has discovered the real causes and salvation comes with shocks. This debut show delivers inventive ways to recover a ruined nation.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Enter the Woods
Description: If you go down to the woods today ... what might you find? A physical and musical experience focusing on the darker side of stories and real life happenings. Enter if you dare! **** (ThreeWeeks, 2010).
Venue description: One of the festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross genre performance makes this central venue a must for all.  Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Mr Millennium: Issue No.1
Description: The world is in need of a new breed of superhero. Mr Millennium is not it. But if you want to know what it’s really like to be a superhero, find out in this musical cabaret.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Borrowed Time
Description: Kevin, an inept young would-be criminal, needs money fast to pay back the local crime lord, a sword-wielding sociopath. Breaking into the home of an eccentric recluse seems to Kevin a likely plan, until the enraged old man unexpectedly shows up with a gun. The strange bond that forms between these two misfits becomes the premise of this unusual comedy-drama produced through Microwave, Film London’s micro-budget feature-film fund in partnership with BBC Films.

Title: Shaun Tan
Subtitle: DISPLACEMENT AND BELONGING
Description: Shaun Tan offers a fascinating journey through his work as author, artist and film-maker, explaining how his early career developed. In 2011 Shaun received the prestigious Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award in Sweden for his body of work and won an Oscar for his short film The Lost Thing. This is a rare opportunity to hear from an inspiring and uniquely talented master in his field.

Title: Twelfth Night
Description: An introduction to Shakespeare. Fools in love, cross-dressing and skiffle music… at the seaside! ‘The precision, nuance and comic brio was remarkable’ (John Retallack, Associate Director, Bristol Old Vic). A healthy dose of old-fashioned nonsense for all ages.
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Kaya's Born Under The Star Of Change
Description: Best-selling writer, multi-platinum song-writer Kaya, the globally renowned dream interpreter, brings his music to the Fringe.  Kaya premiers his album, Born Under The Star Of Change, at AMC @ St. Bride's. www.kayadreams.com/en/news/musicnews
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Once Upon A Time...
Description: ...but what time was that? Update your favourite tales and send the characters on a trip through time as we show you the story of the Three Little Tudor Pigs or Cinderella in the 80s.
Venue description: Paradise Green's purpose-built venue in the vaulted basements of Augustine United Church hosts an exciting programme of theatre and comedy for all tastes, from classics to new and experimental work. Soak up the true spirit of the Fringe.

Title: Terror Tour
Description: Explore one of the scariest places in the world. Visit Edinburgh's 1700s legendary underground haunted vaults, witchcraft temple and medieval torture exhibition, ending in Banshee Labyrinth, Scotland's most haunted pub. Be afraid, be very afraid!
Warnings: no suitable for those with a nervous disposition walking involved
Venue description: Half way between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood palace on the Royal Mile is the Tron Kirk, the departure point for Auld Reekie's Tours in Edinburgh. Meet at the sign boards by the Tron Kirk and learn about the dark side of Edinburgh.

Title: Robyn Young
Subtitle: THE STORY OF ROBERT THE BRUCE
Description: One of Britain's fastest-rising historical novelists has embarked on an epic trilogy that tells the story of Robert the Bruce. Robyn Young’s meticulously researched books are set against the backdrop of the violent Anglo-Scottish wars and marry historical detail with some imaginative characterisation and a fizzing plot. In this event she launches the second book in the series.

Title: Jack Barry and Patrick Turpin: Your New Mild Friends
Description: Jack Barry and Patrick Turpin mount the tired old horse that is stand-up comedy. They're riding bareback, so you'd be silly to miss it. 'Instantly likeable ... surreal and hilarious' **** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Ascend the stairs (quite a few!) to great space and atmospheric bar and stage. Worth it to be entertained in quirky venue.  Alcoholic drinks available.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Cucu-rucu-cu in the French Alps
Description: Snow, ski and a little Julio Iglesias. Tales of Marie's different jobs over five seasons in the beautiful French Alps. Five seasons? She must be a good skier? Well.
Artist: Marie Connolly / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: Okinawa! Okinawa! Okinawa!
Description: Okinawa, the most southern point of Japan, was once an independent country. A story of the Okinawa people who love to sing, dance and rejoice in life. Okinawa, an island of love, song and dance!
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Russell Swallow and the Wolf
Description: A powerful trio of picked guitar, soaring violin, dynamic piano and layered vocal harmonies. 'An acoustic evangelist ... clearly a man with poetry in his soul' (Tom Robinson, 6 Music). 'Simply beautiful' (London's Globe Theatre). www.russellswallowandthewolf.co.uk.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Cressida Cowell
Description: This is a great year to be meeting Viking Hiccup, hero of Cressida Cowell’s How to Train Your Dragon series of novels. For Hiccup was born on the 29th of February and since this is a leap year, it’s a Hiccup birthday year! Cressida introduces her latest adventure, How to Steal a Dragon’s Sword, and talks about all your favourite characters, stories and, of course, dragons!

Title: The Lady Boys of Bangkok - Carnival Queens Tour
Description: Pulsating with latin beats of fiesta, infused with chart-topping sounds. Add laughter, surprises and you have the unforgettable party that is the lady boys, returning with their new show Carnival Queens.
Warnings: Strobe lighting Adult themes, strobe lighting
Venue description: Spectacular state of the art Big Top, seating 700 cabaret-style. Complimented by a foyer and 'chill out' areas complete with licensed bars. The most stunning alternative venue at the Fringe.

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: THE BIG TIME SENSUALITY SHOW
Description:
Glasgow-based lit night Words Per Minute (described by both Radio 4’s Front Row and GQ Magazine as one of the best literary salons in the UK) is back at Unbound, and ready to get you hot under the collar. This year, they’re all about sensuality, and have brought together a collection of writers and musicians who know how to make you feel... something. The line-up includes Booker-nominated author Sarah Hall, Jenni Fagan (one of this year’s Waterstone's 11), Scottish Writer of the Year Alan Bissett, and the gorgeous young Scottish band Two Wings. As ever, nobody gets longer than ten minutes...

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Title: The Quadrantines
Description: Three up and coming comedians each sat on different chairs of the stand-up comedy spectrum, ranging from the adorably innocent David Murphy to the borderline psychotic Daniel Nicholas via the charmingly intense Jack Campbell. For free!
Artist: Jack Campbell, David Murphy, Dan Nicholas / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Opium Alternative Bar and Nightclub is Edinburgh's longest running dedicated Rock venue. Open 7 days a week until 5am, Opium offers the very best in Alternative Entertainment. From Rockaoke to Live Bands ... look no further ... and get ready to ROCK!

14

Title: Mark Grist - Rogue Teacher
Description: Mark Grist - Rogue Teacher. Millions watched an ex-English teacher defeat a teenage grime artist in a rap-battle. But it's a lot more complicated than that. Warning - Mark's journey contains poetry. 'Internet sensation' (Sun).
Artist: Mark Grist / Escalator East to Edinburgh
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Metamorphoses: Fables from Ovid
Description: Twisted, funny and not for the faint-hearted. Six myths from Ovid's Metamorphoses retold in a Victorian girls' dormitory. ‘Simplistically clever and slick storytelling’ **** (RemoteGoat.co.uk). ‘Entertaining’ 7/10 (Bristol Evening Post). www.hecatetheatre.co.uk.

New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Caimh McDonnell: The Art of Conversation
Description: Join Caimh (Bafta nominee, writer on Sarah Millican Television Programme) on a whistle-stop tour of his own social ineptitudes. If small talk is your kryptonite, then this is the show for you! 'Outstanding' (Telegraph).
Warnings: 'ID REQUIRED. If you look under 25, you will be asked for Proof of ID
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Tron
Venue description:
A close up room, perfect for comedy. Intimate, laid back, uptight. Low ceiling, up close, underground. Perfect!
