Title: Oliver Dean and His Fantastic Ego! Live
Description: There was Abraham, Jesus and then Mohammed... Now there is Oliver Dean. Well at least in his head. One of the hottest young talents of stand-up has arrived! A must-see.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Alexander McCall Smith
Subtitle: MEET ONE OF THE WORLD'S MOST POPULAR AUTHORS
Description: Join us for a journey into the colourful world of Alexander McCall Smith, bestselling author of The No 1 Ladies' Detective Agency and 44 Scotland Street. In a joyful, rambunctious hour, McCall Smith introduces a cast of his loveable characters including Precious Ramotswe, Bertie and his mother Irene, and Edinburgh's own amateur sleuth, Isabel Dalhousie. Surprises await!

Title: Lian Hearn
Description: Australian author Lian Hearn joins us to discuss her brilliant fantasy series Tales of the Otori. Beginning with Across the Nightingale Floor, the books transport the reader to a world very much like feudal, Samurai Japan but with elements of magic and mystery. With beautifully drawn characters and incredibly evocative descriptions of the land, the stories are full of battles, betrayals, adventure and love.

Title: Maziar Bahari & François Bizot
Subtitle: COMING FACE TO FACE WITH YOUR CAPTOR
Description: In 1971, François Bizot was kept prisoner for three months in the Cambodian jungle, accused of being a CIA spy. Eventually freed, it took Bizot decades to realise he owed his life to one of Pol Pot’s most infamous henchmen. Facing the Torturer tells this extraordinary tale. In Then They Came for Me, Maziar Bahari writes about the three months he spent in Iran’s most notorious prison while trying to cover the 2009 presidential election. Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Title: Harpsichords at St Cecilia's 1
Description: Critically acclaimed John Kitchen plays Couperin, Rameau, Forqueray and Duphly on the world-famous 1769 Taskin harpsichord, celebrating the launch of his new Delphian recording. ‘Kitchen's recordings have drawn universal praise’ (Early Music Review). www.stceciliasfriends.org.uk.
Warnings: The show requires a quietly attentive audience. Not suitable for extremely young children.
Venue address: Corner of Niddry Street and Cowgate,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cecilia's is the oldest purpose-built concert hall in Scotland, dating from 1763, and is one of Edinburgh's best kept secrets.  An historic and interesting space, it is ideal for acoustic music performances. The Russell and Mirrey Collections of Early Keyboard Instruments are housed in two adjacent galleries.
Venue accessibility:
023459
\nAccessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.
\nPlease notify the Hall on 0131 650 2805.

Title: Magic Carpet Stories
Description: The National Museum of Scotland’s Magic Carpet will be flying in to Charlotte Square Gardens to introduce little ones to fantastic stories, songs and activities. Come and be transported to exciting places and meet a host of characters. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: The  Election: A Silent Comedy
Description: Charting the final hours of a hopeless campaign, The Election mixes the unpredictability of election night with slapstick hilarity. This is politics with an edge – a silly edge. ‘Too good to miss’(ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Bedlam Theatre plays host to an eclectic mix of theatre, dance and comedy at the heart of the Fringe. Enjoy the unique atmosphere of our famous cafe and discover some of the most innovative shows the festival has to offer.

Title: The Showhawk Duo
Description: Showhawk are a furious instrumental acoustic blend of a classical connoisseur with a rock specialist, entertaining you with an eclectic selection. Spanning a wide stylistic spectrum - 70s pop hits to operatic overtures - they truly defy classification.
Venue description: Vibrant Cabaret bar located on the Royal Mile. A global feast of song, music, cabaret, comedy, dance and theatre. Free entry after midnight. Open til 3am daily See: www.thespaceuk.com for more info.

Code: Three Decades of Philippine Short Films
Title: Three Decades of Philippine Short Films
Description: From 1982 to 2012, this programme of shorts from one of the most volatile and exciting filmmaking nations in the world runs the gamut of sensibilities and styles, while charting cinematic transformations that are still under way.

Title: Pretty When I'm Drunk
Description: Pretty When I’m Drunk. *****, says Leeds Student Newspaper. 'The funniest play to be shown at Stage@Leeds for a long time ... The eclectic mix of characters is what makes this a brilliant production’ (LeedsStudent.org).
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: C venues vibrant vivacious variety
Description: Comedy! Music! Cabaret! A festival feast of live performance. Bands, bars, stars. Art, activities, workshops. Film, theatre, dance. Fantastic free events. Eclectic electric entertainment. The ultimate Edinburgh experience, all day, everyday, at C venues. www.CtheFestival.com.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Paul Dennis's Inappropriate Bits - Free
Description: 'Fantastic material ... slick delivery' (creative-cows.com). **** (ThreeWeeks, 2011). An often gritty and bizarre hour of stand-up covering disease, sex, profanity and other dinner party favourites. http://comedyox.tumblr.com.
Artist: Paul Dennis / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Tokyo Trilogy
Description: Comic adaptation of three of Haruki Murakami's short stories. Six actors explore modern Japan, coming to terms with the traditional and the new. Featuring encounters with Wagner, 30 burgers and an assortment of lethal weapons.
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Sandy Brechin and Ewan Wilkinson
Description: Reflective songs, driving tune sets and caustic wit. Accordionist Sandy and singer/guitarist Ewan return to the Acoustic Music Centre to play tracks from their much anticipated new album, Hard Times Come and Go. www.brechin-all-records.com.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Bec Hill is More Afraid of You Than You Are of Her!
Description: YouTube star and one of Time Out's Top 5 Funniest Comedians on Twitter, Bec is back with a brand new show about her biggest fear: you. ***** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: My Elevator Days
Description: Elderly gentleman seeks companion for conversation. Previous confidents: his Mother, Kafka (a dog), Grace Kelly (the greatly-missed), Enok (an elevator), Diana (sex-worker turned dog-walker). Hobbies: gate-crashing funerals. Says: ‘It’s nice if someone remembers you once existed.’
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: The Jocks and Geordies
Description: The finest Geordie and Scottish comedians come together for a fantastic hour of stand-up comedy. Presented by Newcastle's Dan Willis and 'Uber-Jock' Obie. The finest comedy for free! 'Unpretentious, informal, belly-laughs-a-minute stand-up' ****(ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Refurbished in 2011, The Meadow Bar offers two stylish bars with distinctive service and an extensive selection of beers, spirits, shooters, cocktails and drink offers. Also an internet cafe. Free performances of stand-up comedy run here from midday to 3am

Code: Science Fiction Filmmaking Challenge (16-25 year olds)
Title: Science Fiction Filmmaking Challenge (16-25 year olds)
Description: Inspired by Prometheus or Monsters? Think you could create your own Sci-Fi Short in two days? We are launching a 52-hour film challenge (in partnership with First Light) open to all aged 16-25 years old, and our guests at this event will inspire and inform you on how to make your own Sci-Fi film in just two days. Work with friends, family, classmates or new friends, stick to the rules, submit it by 4pm, Monday 25th and come along to see the very best films on 1st July. Register to participate at edfilmfest.org.uk/learning and find a team to work with at education@cmi-scotland.co.uk

Title: Alice Oswald
Subtitle: DEATH WAS ALREADY WALKING TO MEET THEM
Description: Alice Oswald re-imagines the world of Homer’s Iliad in her heartbreaking new book-length oral poem Memorial and here she performs the piece in its entirety. Oswald explains that her modern translation treats the Iliad as ‘an attempt – in the aftermath of the Trojan War – to remember people’s names and lives without the use of writing.’ This is a poem that speaks of the human tragedy of all wars.

Title: Dirty Paki Lingerie
Description: Sex, religion, and politics collide as six Pakistani-American Muslim females air their dirty lingerie... 'Breaks down stereotypes of Muslim women in America' (Wall Street Journal).
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound presents the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces The Hall, Rainy and the Baillie.

Warnings: Non-sexual nudity The Disgust Decalogue no.1

Description: 'Brilliantly written, laugh-out-loud funny and intelligent comedy' (Frost Magazine). Ancient gods, modern foibles and the nature of infinity collide to create an hour of the slightly sinister and the very silly.

Title: Windmill Theatre (AUSTRALIA) Grug
Description:
Ted Prior’s hugely popular character is brought to life for this magical stage production for our very young theatre lovers!

Grug began his life as the top of a Burrawang tree that fell to the ground. Resembling a small, striped haystack with feet and a nose, Grug is fascinated by the world around him and solves everyday problems creatively and without fuss.

When dancing instructions are too difficult to understand, he invents his own dance and calls it ‘The Grug’. When snails eat his cabbages, Grug plants more cabbages so there will be enough for both him and the snails. 

‘Windmill has again created a show in which children can wonderfully discover the magic and the fun and play in theatre.’ Australian Stage
Venue description: Scotland's new writing theatre, is the festival's most prestigious home of serious drama' (New York Times) and a multiple Fringe First and Herald Angel award winner. The legendary Traverse Bar Cafe offers high quality food and drink 09:00 'til late.

Title: Be Fruitful and Multiply
Description: A struggle between two leaders from opposite sides of town. This debut work offers a whimsical take on life's big questions. Pacy dialogue and powerful underlying themes of trust and control, love and collaboration. www.1945productions.com.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Description: Yet more hilarious world-class stand-up from star of Live at Apollo, Royal Variety Performance and Michael McIntyre's Comedy Roadshow. ‘Classic nonsense … Stand-up comedy at its best.’ (Scotsman). ‘Masterclass in delivery’ (Chortle.co.uk). ‘Inspired’ (Independent). ‘Awesome!’ (List). www.jimeoin.com.
Venue description: Venue150 @ EICC just gets better and better! This year, take in some big names, world-class comedy, internationally renowned dance and jaw-dropping acts from across the globe. All in the capital's comfiest venue! www.venue150.com

Title: Nice People Have Ruined My Life
Description: Two quite different, brilliant stand-ups ponder life’s complexities. Sweet and tender hooligan Asli Akbay and this charming man Simon Lilley are feisty, laidback and offbeat. You’re human and you need to be loved. www.nicepeoplehaveruinedmylife.com.

Artist: Camera Obscura and World of Illusions
Venue: Camera Obscura and World of Illusions

Title: Afghan Days Babylon Nights
Description: Stunning Theatre of War: courage, loss, comradeship, humour, resilience of the human spirit.  'I was moved many times.' Scilla Elworthy. Nobel Peace Nominee. 'Spare, shocking, beautiful' Anne Brown, Director of Voices War for Combat Stress.
Warnings: some recorded sounds of gunfire and explosions

Title: Matt Price: Fugly.
Description: True stories about why you should never judge someone just by their appearance. A show that celebrates differences between people and that features an ill-advised finale with a skateboard and a skipping rope. 'Superb' (Chortle.co.uk). Free.
Venue accessibility: \n

Title: Ian Rankin
Subtitle: DESERT ISLAND REBUS
Description: It’s 25 years since Knots and Crosses introduced us to John Rebus – and changed the face of crime writing in the process. To celebrate, Ian Rankin shares some of his favourite Rebus moments from the 17 novels featuring this flawed and deliciously puzzling character. A journey across Edinburgh’s topography as much as it is a voyage through Ian Rankin’s mind, this literary Desert Island Discs promises to be a highlight of the Festival.

Title: Leslie Hunter: A Life in Colour
Description: One of the most influential Scottish artists of the 20th-century. This new major exhibition comprises more than 70 works from collections throughout the UK. A bold and vibrant display from an artistic master.

Title: The Comedian's Comedian Live with Stuart Goldsmith

Title: How to Climb Mount Everest

Title: Word:Play

Title: Alistair Darling
Subtitle: BRINGING BRITAIN BACK FROM THE BRINK
Description: As Chancellor of the Exchequer in 2008, Alistair Darling held his nerve as the British banking system came within two hours of collapsing. Now in opposition, the Edinburgh-based MP remains a much-respected voice on the economy. In this unmissable event he talks with James Naughtie about the Coalition, Scottish devolution, and life at the pinnacle of British politics.

SWIMMING AND FLYING:
A TALK BY MARK HADDON

Celebrated author, artist and dramatist Mark Haddon presents a one-man talk about great white sharks, cosmology, creative writing, engine fires and ice hockey. Haddon’s career includes fifteen books for children, two poetry collections, several adult novels and two BAFTAs. His bestselling novel, The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time, won seventeen literary prizes, including the Whitbread Award. His latest novel The Red House is a wonderfully insightful novel about family, estrangement, secrets, loss and the persistent echoes of the past.

Gattu is an orphan, being raised as an apprentice, but he can’t concentrate on his work because he’s obsessed with kite-flying, and in particular with defeating the mysterious Kali, whose black kite rules the skies. To keep his supply of kites, Gattu is prepared to steal, lie – and even go to school, if absolutely necessary…

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: WORKERS' RIGHTS ARE HUMAN RIGHTS
Description:
Trade unionists are at the forefront of the struggle for human rights around the world. They are ordinary men and women who have to deal with harassment, political killings, ‘disappearances’, arbitrary detention, torture, exile and murder. Extracts from works that highlight trade union activity in Zimbabwe, Colombia and Iran are the focus of today’s event. Reading today: Ron Butlin, Kathryn Erskine, Emylia Hall and Jane Rogers.

	*Kathryn Erskine has cancelled

Title: Sally Gardner & Celia Rees
Description: Sally Gardner and Celia Rees are novelists who never shy away from the challenging aspects of life. Their latest books deal with loss, damage, cruelty and, ultimately, healing. Sally’s novel, The Double Shadow, is a complex tale set across different times and realities whilst This Is Not Forgiveness by Celia deals with the effects of war on a family at the most intimate level. If you thirst for books which are gripping, disturbing and emotionally engaging then these are the writers for you.

Title: Marat / Sade
Description: The Marquis de Sade is using the inmates of Charenton Asylum to put on a play. The play? A recreation of the bloody turmoil and eventual murder of Jean Paul Marat during the French Revolution that he helped instigate.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Description: The desert is the devil’s microwave. Eggs fry on rocks. Time toasts like cheap bread. You can’t even hide in your shadow. A demonic feast from creators of Larry, ‘amazing’ ***** (Fest) and Farrago, ‘sheer beauty’ **** (Scotsman).

Title: Riding Zorro
Description: This documentary recounts the life of “El Zorro”, a legendary untamable horse of the pampas. The filmmaker uses testimonies from those who tried to ride the horse and those who witnessed the attempts, together with archival footage in various formats. Through the creative treatment of these materials, the filmmaker generates both a strong narrative momentum and a deep empathy with the proud horse.

Title: Alexandra Harris & John Mullan
Subtitle: WHAT MADE JANE AUSTEN AND VIRGINIA WOOLF GREAT?
Description: Virginia Woolf wrote admiringly that Jane Austen had written ‘without hate, without bitterness, without fear, without preaching.’ In this event the ideas and work of these two giants of British fiction are compared and contrasted. Alexandra Harris’ previous book Romantic Moderns won the Guardian First Book Award, while John Mullan is a literary critic whose book What Matters in Jane Austen? has just been released. They talk to author and literary critic Lesley McDowell.

Title: The Proposal
Description: As Pete prepares to propose to Julia, he expects today to be the happiest of his life. However flatmate Freddy has other ideas. A twisted love story - raw, funny and absolute carnage. 'Frighteningly accomplished’ **** (Scotsman, for Territory).

Award-winning writer, playwright and journalist Caroline Dunford looks at the opportunities open to modern writers, encouraging you to discover how you can spread your wings into new areas of writing.

Taking as their watchword “the customer is king”, the idealistic boss of Chang Eh Sauna and his hard-working employees seek to transform their enterprise into a modern “entertainment kingdom”. Director Zou Peng, aided by master cinematographer Yu Lik-wai, offers a stylised and dreamlike take on the artificial universe of the brothel, together with sharp ironies about the mindset of the entrepreneurs of the new China.

Title: Prodigious

We are telling stories, sharing songs, and carousing late into the night with Unbound. The lyrical genius of Irish writers is well known with song and story living tangled lives in their literature. This night celebrates these feisty bedfellows, bringing together authors and special guests. Join Pat Kinevane and Julie Feeney, Kevin Barry and Maeve Higgins, Keith Ridgway and Jaime Nanci, to share inspiration, soundtracks, stories and songs. All are the perfect excuse for just one more for the road.

Here he presents a new history of the Israeli state, and the way in which the ideology of Zionism influenced its universities and media. Pappé, who now lives in England, was described by John Pilger as 'Israel's bravest, most principled historian.' Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Little did she know that a story would ensue of romance, insanity, fantasy and the boundaries of privacy in a society clinging to rigid ideas about marriage and sexuality.

Bellos' past achievements include the English re-translations (from French) of the Albanian genius Ismail Kadare. In this event the genial Scotsman discusses his masterful new book on the art of translation, Is That A Fish In Your Ear? with another of our Festival authors, Jennie Erdal.

Claire Kilroy’s Devil I Know is her much-anticipated follow-up to All Names Have Been Changed, and it takes the form of the testimony of a man who realises he's trapped in a world of greed and hubris. Our relationship with music is a complex, emotionally-charged beast and Coleman explores that connection via psalms, symphonies and love songs.

Roman Krznaric and Oliver Burkeman, in two very different books, offer intriguing alternatives. Krznaric's The Wonderbox presents a variety of historical approaches to living better, while Burkeman’s The Antidote interviews an unusual group of people that believe it’s our constant effort to be happy that is making us miserable and that there is an alternative path to happiness.

Title: The Gift of Dyslexia
Description: It is time to stop classifying dyslexia as a disability argues Vivian French; we need to start appreciating that different brain-wiring and neurobiological patterns allow people to process information in unique ways. Although dyslexia may cause difficulties with reading and writing, people with it prefer thinking in narrative form, often making them natural storytellers and actors. An ability to visualize 3D structures also means many are gifted artists. Vivian leads the discussion with Dr John Rack, Head of Research, Development and Policy at Dyslexia Action and actor, playwright and songwriter Matthew McVarish.

Subtitle: MAGIC WORDS
Description:
Edinburgh-based Illicit Ink make their Unbound debut with Magic Words, combining spoken word, storytelling and stage magic. Established in 2011, the group has been hosting regular themed nights across the city inviting writers to present prose on particular topics focusing on the dark, the weird and the witty. Gavin Inglis of Underword and Writers’ Bloc fame will compère the evening and Ariadne Cass-Maran, one of Illicit Ink’s founding members and the director of Graphic Scotland will perform pieces with other visiting authors from the Festival.

Title: Using Fiction to Teach Human Rights
Description: From early years onwards, picture books and novels can be powerful tools for educating children about human rights. Fiction can develop empathy, tolerance and understanding, often engaging readers at a deep emotional level. The Guardian Children’s Book Editor, Julia Eccleshare, joins leading children’s authors Sara Grant and Debi Gliori, secondary school Principal Teacher of English, Isobel Reid and teacher and educational advisor Carol Wood, to discuss and offer insight into how picture books and young fiction can be used in the primary classroom to explore human rights issues.

Title: Antony Beevor
Subtitle: A MAJOR NEW HISTORY OF THE SECOND WORLD WAR

Join him to hear about his masterwork. Chaired by Magnus Linklater.

Subtitle: WHY WE GAVE OUR HOME TO THE NATION
Description: In April 1946, Tam Dalyell's parents handed over their property to the National Trust for Scotland, as long as their son could continue to live there. The Dalyells are among countless families that have donated their homes to the nation over the past century. In A Noble Thing, historian Merlin Waterson explores what motivates them, and in this event he is joined by one of his subjects.

Now, the husband and wife team join us to launch Tuesday's Gone, the second in a new series of crime thrillers featuring a new heroine – a psychotherapist named Frieda Klein. Chaired by the Guardian’s Literary Editor, Claire Armitstead.

Title: Debate: Rethinking Russia
Subtitle: IS VLADIMIR PUTIN AN UNMITIGATED DISASTER FOR RUSSIA?
Description: With his strong-man PR imagery and shady KGB past, Vladimir Putin has been mocked, both internationally and increasingly within his own country, as a despot and a thief, ruling over a corrupt mafia state. But does the common Western characterisation of Russia hide a more complex reality? Russia remains one of the world’s more potent economies and its political influence is widespread. Might Putin’s reign yet turn out to be the best Russia could hope for? Russian experts Masha Gessen and MEP Struan Stevenson roll up their sleeves. Chaired by Allan Little.

It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. Appearing today: Alyxandra Harvey.

Title: We Got Rhythm

Title: Pankaj Mishra (Cancelled)
Subtitle: HOW THE WEST WAS LOST
Description:
We commonly think of the Victorian era as an age of progress and enlightenment. But in this eye-opening new book, the respected Indian author and essayist Pankaj Mishra shows that Asians experienced that same period as a catastrophe. Poets and radicals across Asia, he argues, began to formulate radical responses to Western ideas which laid the foundations for everything from the Chinese Communist Party to Al Qaeda. The event will be chaired by Anita Sethi.

	Please note: Pankaj Mishra is no longer able to attend and this event has been cancelled.

Title: PianoDivalicious!
Description: The PianoDiva is back! Enjoying worldwide sell-out seasons, Amy Abler returns with her signature Beethoven burlesque. With new music, more feathers, and the fastest fingers of the Fringe, she’ll tickle your fancy with saucy tales and astonishing virtuosity. **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Description: Crime writer Val McDermid’s first children’s book is a bold and colourful mix of the fantastical and the ordinary. Granny is a pirate whose exciting daytime adventures always get her home in time to tell her tales. It’s lovely to have a grandparent as a hero and pirate Granny is certainly that. Val tells you all about Granny including exactly what she can do with the skilful wielding of her handbag. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Description: Fraser MacLean is a veteran of the animation industry having worked with the likes of Warner Bros and Disney Animation Studios. Code: Lu Kemp and Oliver Emanuel in association with macrobert (SCOTLAND) Titus
Title: Lu Kemp and Oliver Emanuel in association with macrobert (SCOTLAND) Titus
Description:
The story of a 10 year-old boy on the edge - literally on the roof of his school - confronted by a situation that seems hopeless. He can either give up or fight.

Do you want to know why I’m called Titus?
It’s a funny story.
My dad thinks I’m always making stuff up.
Just tell the truth, Titus.
Just tell the truth.
The truth is much easier to remember than a lie.
But Dad the truth is so boring.
A drama about telling big lies and small truths.
About pigs that fall in love.
About crows that talk.
About running away and finding yourself.

A touching story of a 10 year-old boy that deals with issues such as love, loneliness, adolescence and death but told with gentle humour and sensitivity.

Titus, originally written by Belgian writer Jan Sobrie, was awarded the Dutch-German Author Prize in 2007 and is considered one of Europe’s most successful plays for young people.

The screening will be followed by a panel discussion about the deadly culture of gang, gun, knife and criminality which is endemic in all our inner cities.

Title: Debate: Rethinking the Union (Part 1)
Subtitle: WOULD CULTURE LOSE ITS SHINE IN AN INDEPENDENT SCOTLAND?
Description: Scotland’s resurgence as a confident 21st century nation has, without any doubt, been driven by its cultural success stories. Could it continue to thrive if Scotland breaks its bonds with Britain? This debate is not about funding – culture has been a devolved issue since 1997 – but about the country’s ability to succeed internationally, and to retain the international diversity so vital to cultural production here. Join our panel consisting of Labour MP and former UK Minister for Culture, David Lammy, Falkirk-based author, Alan Bissett and Linda Colley, Professor of History at Princeton University. Chaired by Libby Brooks, Acting Comment Editor of the Guardian.

Description: A dramatic portrayal chronicling the emotional meltdown of a singer during a dress rehearsal of a concert recital. Breathless will provoke, challenge and tease, so jump aboard the rollercoaster life that is pure Ferdi.
Venue description: Vibrant Cabaret bar located on the Royal Mile. A global feast of song, music, cabaret, comedy, dance and theatre. Free entry after midnight. Open til 3am daily See: www.thespaceuk.com for more info.

Title: Dusty Limits: Post-Mortem - Free
Description: Life. Death. Sex. Drugs. Love. But mostly singing. Cabaret legend Dusty Limits celebrates mortality. 'Astonishing, with incredible power and subtlety' **** (FringeGuru.com). 'Simply the best at what he does' **** (EdinburghSpotlight.com). 'The trailblazer' (TimeOut).
Warnings: This show contains strong language, sex and drug references. Adult themes, strong language, sex and drug references
Artist: Dusty Limits / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.

Title: Those People My Parents
Description: One man, eight characters. Chris Matragos presents, Those People My Parents. Get ready for an absolutely hilarious ride filled with an ex-criminal, a drug dealing student president and a few parents.
Venue description: Managed by theSpaceUK, this intimate space hosts an array of new and established theatre. Located seconds from the Royal Mile with bar and cafe facilities. For show information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: All the Things I Never Said
Description: As strangers wait on a train platform, talk turns to the passengers’ pasts and the words they wished they had said. Should those words be spoken or are some things better left unsaid?
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: The Comedy Reserve
Description: Catch four of the hottest new acts on the comedy circuit - Matt Rees, Suzy Bennett, John Kearns and Chris Turner - in the eighth year of Pleasance's Comedy Reserve, supported by the Charlie Hartill Special Reserve.
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: McLaren Animation 1
Description: Join us in celebrating the best British animation this year. All the films are in competition for the coveted McLaren Award, named in honour of Stirling’s Norman McLaren, a genius of film who dazzled the world with his innovative experiments in animation and synthetic sound for over half a century. In this selection, our films explore identity, neuroses and existential problems, many of them inherent in the trick of animated characters.  Forget Family Guy, this is adult animation.

Title: The Shambles
Description: The Shambles create never-before-seen scenes based entirely on audience suggestions. Without you, we are nothing. Come join our energetic and eclectic cast for a completely unique, unrepeatable show. Fringe favourite! www.dead-duck.co.uk.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Forever Loved
Description: There are an estimated six million documented and one million undocumented migrant Philippine workers scattered throughout 200 countries all over the world. Every day, some 4,000 more join their ranks. Weaving recollections and letters from various migrant workers around the story of a Philippine man searching for his missing wife in a Middle Eastern city, Christopher Gozum creates an intimate, evocative and hypnotic mixture of documentary, poetry and fiction.

Title: Stephen McGinty & Daniel Pick
Subtitle: TRYING TO FATHOM THE NAZI MIND
Description: Nazis continue to have a mesmeric hold over historians. Stephen McGinty’s Camp Z recalls the visit of Rudolph Hess to the UK in 1941 to broker a peace deal, but which turned into a psychological battle between a desperate government and an unhinged member of Hitler’s inner circle. Daniel Pick’s The Pursuit Of The Nazi Mind tells the extraordinary story of how psychoanalysis was used in the war against Germany.

Title: An Audience With Tomás Ford - Free
Description: Smashing together dance music with cabaret, Australian showman Tomás Ford plays with audiences, guiding them from confusion to crowd-surfing delight. ‘A man who can make changing his shoes into an awe-inspiring sight (Xpress).
Artist: Tomás Ford / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items ... Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: Tam Dalyell
Subtitle: THE FALKLANDS WAR: TRUTH AND LIES
Description: Margaret Thatcher's war with Argentina transformed her standing in the polls and would change British politics for a generation. Labour MP Tam Dalyell was a vehement critic of Thatcher, describing her command to sink the General Belgrano as nothing less than a war crime. 30 years on, the Falklands is a political hot potato again. Dalyell discusses the events with the Professor of Peace Studies at Bradford University, Paul Rogers. Chaired by Allan Little.

Title: The Jhiva of Nietzsche
Description: Combining live action and multimedia, the performance traces the life of philosopher Frederic Nietzsche through the eyes of his Jhiva (soul). Reason and intuition collide in an in-body divide between mind (digital character) and soul. www.theatrotranscendental.com.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: ETHNIC PERSECUTION AND DISCRIMINATION
Description: All around the world, people have been and are persecuted and discriminated against for who they are – in Rwanda, South Sudan, Bosnia and even here in Scotland. Our daily series today features works by writers from Gypsy, Roma and other Traveller communities who are marginalised because of their culture and way of life. Reading today: Gillian Slovo, Patrick Gale and Monique Roffey.

Title: Sam Fisher and Friends - Free
Description: Sam Fisher is a female comedian who can find humour in the strangest of places, she has invited friends Sean Thorpe and Mike Farmer who can share the lighter side of life!
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Steve Gribbin: Viva Gribbostania!
Description: Steve Gribbin in Viva Gribbostania! Satirical songbird Steve Gribbin takes a leaf out of Alex Salmond's book and declares unilateral independence. A scathing look at the trappings of nationhood: flags, anthems, currency and even Eurovision.
Artist: Steve Gribbin / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue: The Stand Comedy Club III & IV
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue, Stand III is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand IV an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Doug Segal: How to Read Minds and Influence People
Description: 'Imagine if Derren Brown was funny' (Evening Standard). Last year's sell-out hit returns! Learn to read minds and more. **** (Edinburgh Evening News) ***** (What'sOnStage.com). **** (Skinny).
Artist: Mick Perrin for Just For Laughs Live
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Guardian Children's Fiction Prize Event (Cancelled)
Description:
This fiction prize has now been running for 45 years and has recognised many leading children’s authors including Leon Garfield, Nina Bawden, Anita Desai and Ted Hughes. The longlist is announced each June, the shorlist in September and the winner in October. So come along to meet and hear from a selection of those in the running for this year’s award and think about who you would like to be the ultimate winner.

Please note: this event has been cancelled.

Title: James and the Giant Peach
Description: Richard R George's stage adaptation of Roald Dahl's classic fantasy. Join orphan James Henry Trotter as he escapes from his cruel aunts and crosses the Atlantic in a giant peach full of cantankerous insects.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Last Supper
Description: Revolves around the character of Joseph, who explores his ability to resist temptation as he battles a stranger’s dark influence. Intriguing, gripping and will have you questioning your own inner strength. Join Joseph for his final meal.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Seeing Double: Vision
Description: Julio Buenaventura, supposed theatrical visionary extraordinaire, and his dysfunctional cast rehearse for the show of the decade, unaware that their actions are being transmitted to the production team next door. Sister show to Seeing Double: Figures.
Warnings: Contains nudity, strobe lighting, sexual references
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Harriet Walter
Subtitle: AGEING WITH PRIDE
Description: Dame Harriet Walter’s glittering career as an actor on stage and screen has seen film credits including Atonement and Sense and Sensibility. Now, she has embarked on an ambitious photography project to celebrate the beauty of older women. She discusses the images she has chosen for her self-published book, and reflects on women's experiences of ageing in a world that only seems to celebrate youth.

Title: Eric Hutton: Every Other Show in the Fringe Sucks - Free
Description: This show may also suck. ‘My favourite up and coming comedian is Eric Hutton. He's like a mix between Daniel Kitson and H.G. Nelson. Brilliant!’ (Sam Simmons).
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.

Title: White Rabbit Red Rabbit
Description: Born on Azar 19th, 1360 in Tehran. That’s Tehran, December 10th, 1981 in Christian years. Imagine being 29 and forbidden to leave your country. Nassim Soleimanpour dissects the whole experience in an original play from Iran.
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Paterson Arran Ten at Ten
Description: A delicious morning reading from one of our Festival authors to set you up for the day. Check the screen in the Entrance Tent to see who’s reading each day.

Title: Kelly Kellner
Description: Kellner returns to AMC as a soloist promoting her new charity album Little Bird. The show will include new material, originals and covers, inspired by artists such as Amy Macdonald, Jewel, Sarah McLachlan and Joni Mitchell. www.kellykellner.moonfruit.com. www.facebook.com/kellymkellner.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Young Dudes
Description: An atmospheric mix of lo-fi science-fiction, glam-inspired rock music and Zeitgeist-immersed comedy-drama, set in Taipei. With newscasts announcing that the end of the world is imminent, two slackers – a rock musician and a carpentry teacher – decide it’s time to take action. They’re joined by a young Russian woman, with whom they launch a virtual Noah’s Ark on the web. The site becomes so successful that the trio’s activities come to the attention of space aliens.

Title: Shakespeare Didn't Write This
Description: ‘Shakespeare Didn't Write This.’ Meet a group of incompetent lack-wits embarking on a Fringe journey, recreating Shakespeare. Can the mismatched team overcome their artistic differences, coming together to beat the bard at his game?
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Michelle de Swarte
Description: ‘Bisexual, biracial and bilingual cos am from Brixton...’ A daring breath of fresh air to the female comic circuit; this hilarious woman will shock you with her frank honesty on everything from lesbian sex to Parisian catwalks.
Artist: Michelle de Swarte / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Located on Market Street (opposite Waverley Station) Belushis is your one stop venue for food, drinks, live entertainment and sport. With a great programme of live entertainment during the festival, great drinks offers and amazing food, Belushi's is the place to be.
Venue accessibility:
2349
\nShows are held in our big bar which has ramp access, there are two steps to the stage area but the stage can be viewed from anywhere in the bar. The disabled toilet is on the 1st floor but this can be accessed by lift.

Title: Interruption
Description: Devised from documentary research into memories and Norman MacCaig's poem, Interruption to a Journey. Combines naturalism with physical theatre and music to create a haunting and beautiful tale, where memories come to life. www.interruption2012.co.uk.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Christian Reilly: This Is Not A Love Song
Description: Perrier/Chortle winner. Come, feel the noise. Not necessarily in that order. 'Seriously cool, seriously funny' (Richard Herring). 'If you're a fan of Bill Bailey/Rich Hall, you're a Reilly fan already' (Guardian).
Venue description: Open from 1pm until 5am every day. 450 capacity Whistlebinkies presents over 150 artists throughout the Festival. Features local and national Scottish talent, smaller touring artists alongside tribute and covers acts. Free comedy from 1pm, free live music from 9pm.

Title: Neal Stephenson
Subtitle: REMARKABLE OUTPUT AND DIVERSITY
Description: In Neal Stephenson’s book of essays, Some Remarks, he blends such diverse topics as technology, economics, history, science, pop culture and philosophy, pondering a wealth of subjects, from movies and politics to video games and geekdom. In his latest novel, Reamde, he delivers a high-intensity, action-packed adventure thriller in which an entrepreneur gets caught in the crossfire of his own online war game. Chaired by author Christopher Brookmyre.

Title: Chris Riddell
Description: Join our Illustrator in Residence, Chris Riddell as he talks about his beautifully illustrated series of tales about a little girl called Ottoline and his mad romp through all things outer space in Alienography. Come and find out how one man can write such different books and get an insight into how he creates his incredible art.

Title: Fat Kitten vs. the World
Description: Make-a-Wish Theatresports Cup 2011 winners Fat Kitten Improv take on guest groups in a furious improv comedy smackdown to the death. Actual death not guaranteed. Sold-out 2010, 2011.
Artist: Fat Kitten Improv / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.
Venue accessibility: \nNo access for wheelchair users - venue up flight of stairs.

Title: Afternoon Delight
Description: A sample show of different acts from within Just the Tonic venues, and maybe some guests. Spend an hour in the company of five to eight performers and see if you want to go to their full shows. Good idea!
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Rubberbandits
Description: Ten million YouTube hit sensation with the riotous Horse Outside, these Irish chart-topping, Chortle Award-winning bag-heads make their Fringe debut with the funniest, filthiest comedy gig in Fringe memory. ‘Funny, groovy, a little bit scary’ (Hotpress).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Lisa Scott Sings Blues and Jazz
Description: From Billie Holiday to Frank Sinatra, Lisa sings with passion, humour, ease and sophistication. Her mature, moody voice is complemented by a professional three-piece live band - piano, bass and drums.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Roger McGough As Far As I Know - 50th Year at the Fringe
Description: Hilarious and surreal, he is a poet of many voices. Menace and melancholy there may be, but with plenty of McGough's characteristic wit and wordplay too.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: The Jungle Book
Description: A delightful adaptation of the Kipling classic. Mowgli is brought up to be a wolf but when he learns he is a human, does he remain part of the wolf pack or return to his roots?
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: Joe Lycett: Some Lycett Hot
Description: Highly anticipated debut from 'One of the strongest emerging comedy talents we've seen in a long time' (TimeOut). BBC New Comedy Award finalist 2011, Chortle Best Newcomer 2010. 'Entertainingly mischievous ... intensely charming.' (Guardian).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Best of the Fest Variety
Description: Hosted by the sensational Miss Behave, join us in the Teatro Spiegeltent as the finest performers from across the Fringe come together to showcase their weird and wonderful talents for your delight.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: James Carter
Description: Join acclaimed poet James Carter as he performs from his new collection of poems, Hey, Little Bug! This is a perfect introduction for very young children to the delights of poetry. James writes with great humour, tenderness and fun and his lively event offers plenty of opportunities for all to join in.

Title: Alternative Sex Education
Description: Queer. Feminist. Burlesque? Tales of terrible teachers, songs about sub-standard shags, and plenty of alternate perspectives. It's easy as ABC (Asexuality, BDSM, and Consent). 'If only Lashings could land themselves on the national curriculum' **** (Scotsgay). www.lashings.org.
Venue description: Edinburgh's all-year-round multi-arts venue. We offer a gourmet selection of theatre, cabaret, live music, visual arts and clubbing. Our cafe adds delicious homemade food, free internet and great coffee to the mix. All brought to you by the friendliest staff in town.

Title: Afternoon tea with Adrian Plass
Description: Adrian Plass - author and poet - has two million books in print, which have been an inspiration and source of laughter encouragement throughout the world. Recent bestsellers are Seriously Funny and Bacon Sandwiches and Salvation.
Venue description: Easily accessible by bus or by parking on Bruntsfield Place, this is our second year in the Fringe. On the ground floor the church has traditional fixed pew seating facing the stage, with some restricted view seats.
Venue accessibility:
0289
\nOn street parking for a blue badge holder, accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space).

Title: Rainbow
Description: Funny, dark, uplifting - the new play from Royal Court Young Writer Emily Jenkins embraces the brutality of the mundane. Martin, Tom and Russ make life-changing decisions that, unknowingly, have a devastating effect on the lives of each other.
Warnings: Violent scenes and strong language Violent scenes and strong language
Artist: Sell a Door Theatre Company and Boxed Cat Theatre
Venue description: An award-winning extravaganza of the best performances from across the Fringe spectrum. The majestic Main House is packed with outstanding dance and physical theatre from around the world while the Cabaret Bar and Studio host thrilling drama, comedy and music.

Title: Craig Hill - Jock's Trap!
Description: Indulge yourself in a deliciously wicked evening of gloriously camp no-holds-barred comedy and pure, unadulterated fun. 'Funny as hell' (Scotland on Sunday). 'Wickedly subversive... Funny, charming and charismatic' (Metro). 'Absolutely hilarious' (Evening News). Sell-out 2002-2011! www.mrcraighill.com.
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Well Done You - Free
Description: Ruth Bratt and Lucy Trodd deviate from Showstoppers to present their debut character sketch show. ‘Deliciously dark and very funny’ (Rob Brydon). ‘Blissfully comic’ (WhatsOnStage.com). ‘Clever comic mind’ (Independent). ‘A wonderfully silly show’ (Londonist.com).
Artist: Trodd en Bratt / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: The Most Dangerous Toy
Description: Nietzsche is 37, ailing, almost blind, and about to prophecy the superman. Lou is 21, independent, fiercely intelligent, and about to become his undoing. 'You go to women? Don’t forget the whip.' Incipit tragoedia...
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Sophie Ramsay
Description: Fresh from recording her new album and touring the Hebrides, critically acclaimed Scottish singer/songwriter Sophie Ramsay performs contemporary and traditional folk songs with guitar and piano and maybe guests. ’Beautiful person, beautiful songs, beautiful show’ **** (Scotsman).
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: Film Fringe Tour
Description: A touring compilation of film screenings showcasing up-and-coming filmmakers from around the world, and presenting their films to international audiences. Stopping at Fringe festivals in Hollywood, Edinburgh and Philadelphia. Specific film schedule at: www.filmfringetour.com.
Venue: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel
Venue description: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel offers two performance spaces ideal for intimate, experimental, and engaging theatre. We present a programme of theatrical performance, especially innovative works, original works, devised theatre, movement, puppetry, immersive theatre and music.

Title: Jo Caulfield - Thinking Bad Thoughts
Description: Award-winning comedian asks: Why are drunken girlfriends so much fun? Who watches hotel pornography? What constitutes an airtight alibi? Is friendliness overrated? 'Feisty, funny and wonderfully bitchy' (Observer). 'Stand-up comedy at its best' (Scotsman).
Warnings: 16+ must be accompanied by an adult
Artist: Jo Caulfield / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Edinburgh's year-round comedy club is housed in an intimate basement bar just off St Andrew Square. The atmosphere is relaxed and informal with comfortable cabaret-style seating (although some late night shows are not all seated).

Title: Meet the Media
Description: An event unlike any other, this is a chance to meet media representatives and promote your show. Strictly two representatives from each show and bring hard copies of news releases, flyers etc. Be prepared to queue!
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Dennis Locorriere Whatever's Burning Now - CANCELLED
Description: Dennis Locorriere lead singer and founder member of Dr Hook with 30 Platinum albums and composer/songwriter covered by Bob Dylan, Willie Nelson, Waylon Jennings and Jerry Lee Lewis performing his music and poetry and exhibiting his art
Venue description: The Jam House is a live music venue, conceived by Jools Holland. It offers live performances, fine food and has a vibrant atmosphere. A broad range of musical styles is available for all age groups. We are situated on Queen Street, and have a beautiful venue which includes our historical Chapel Bar.

Title: Pappy's Flatshare Slamdown
Description: The hilarious and anarchic award-winning panel game podcast (2012 Loaded Lafta Funniest Podcast) hosted by Pappy's with great comedian guests. 'Like Basil Brush meets the Young Ones' (Evening Standard). For info and to hear past podcasts, www.comedy.co.uk/pfs-dtrt.
Warnings: Show will be recorded for release as an edited audio podcast at a later date
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: In the Pink - Fantastic Female a Cappella!
Description: Oxford's singing sensations return for an astounding eighth year with their blend of harmonious arrangements and entertaining choreography, all polished with their signature charm! www.inthepinkacappella.co.uk.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Perfectly Bananas
Description: The Prop Man, Wes Zaharuk, combines routines with power tools, bananas and film noir. ‘Twin Peaks meets Cirque du Soleil’ (Toronto Sun). ‘Tommy Cooper on acid. A rip-roaring jump into the surreal’ (Channel4.com).
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: Tokyo Drifter
Description: Singer-songwriter-guitarist Kenta Maeno wanders alone at night around Tokyo, singing his songs before indifferent passers-by. Deliberately lo-tech, Tokyo Drifter is at once a conceptual concert film, an allegory of the solitude of the artist, and a document of the visual experience of Tokyo shortly after the March 11, 2011, disaster, when efforts to reduce power consumption resulted in a drastic toning-down of the usual brightly lit spectacle of Tokyo at night.

Title: Hitler Alone
Description: ‘An act of bravery’ **** (Scotsman). The show attempts to penetrate the heart and mind of this ‘maniac of ferocious genius’ (Churchill) who charms and repels as he contemplates his life in an imagined soliloquy before suicide.
Venue description:
We are a language centre and offer year-round conversational courses in all languages as well as translation services and au pair programmes. 
\nWe also have our own theatre group (once a week) and ongoing art exhibitions.
\n
\nWe look forward to welcoming you.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Scottish Sinfonia Play Haydn and Shostakovich
Description: Haydn Symphony No 102 in Bb, Haydn Trumpet Concerto in Eb, Iain Mundy, Shostakovich Symphony No 10 in E minor. Conductor Neil Mantle. Hear Sinfonia live in concert, there is no substitute!
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Festival Folk at the Oak
Description: Edinburgh’s famous hub for folk music presents 35 nights of acoustic folk and traditional music, featuring a different singer, musician or group every night, including some of the most well-known names in Scottish folk. www.royal-oak-folk.com.
Venue description: The Royal Oak is Edinburgh's premiere traditional music and folksinging howff. Rub shoulders with the top names in folk music, join in or just sit and listen; sample a cask ale or a fine malt and enjoy the convivial atmosphere.

Title: Ben Marcus & Colson Whitehead
Subtitle: UNSPEAKABLE HORROR WITH SATIRICAL TALES
Description: Humans are fighting back against a zombie outbreak in Colson Whitehead’s Zone One with ordinary guy Mark Spitz part of an armed unit patrolling the New York streets. As we dip into Spitz’s past life, he wonders whether a doomsday scenario is about to unfold. Ben Marcus’ innovative The Flame Alphabet zooms in on a virus which originates in the speech of children and kills their parents.

Title: 3 Days Off Jesus - Free
Description: Born on 22nd December, David Burke is only three days off Jesus. Join this non-drinking Irishman for a cup of tea and a night of comedy/stories about childhood in old Ireland, religion and women. www.freefestival.co.uk.

In G Willow Wilson’s Alif The Unseen, we journey to an unnamed Middle Eastern security state where a young hacker has just discovered an ancient book which may unleash a new level of information technology, and he’s extremely keen to get hold of it. Ken MacLeod’s Intrusion is another of his disturbing dystopia novels in which a future state commits atrocities with the best of intentions.

Title: Maggie Craig
Subtitle: GLASGOW’S HISTORY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE
Description: When The Clyde Ran Red is Maggie Craig’s lively social and political history of Glasgow through the First World War, roaring 20s, harsh 30s and the Clydebank Blitz. It celebrates the determination, achievements and sheer lust for life of the people of Clydeside, showing why so many of them fought for the right to work, the dignity of labour and a fairer society for all.

Title: Percurso - Course

Title: Tony Banks & Ian Gardiner
Subtitle: TWO ACCOUNTS OF A 1982 WAR
Description: With the 30th anniversary of the Falklands conflict firmly on people’s minds, this event marries two different aspects. Ian Gardiner’s The Yompers is the first account to be written by a company commander who fought in the war. Tony Banks suffered years of debilitating stress after playing a part in close-quarters combat, finding relief only when he met his former enemies.

Subtitle: GOOD PEOPLE AND THEIR IMPERFECTIONS
Description: The new novel by Patrick Gale is a moving and thought-provoking meditation on what makes ordinary people 'good' or not. Ambitious and complex in its structure, it tells the story of ordinary people in a Cornish village and their relationships. Gale is joined in this event by debut novelist Elanor Dymott, whose Every Contact Leaves a Trace is a stunning, intense literary thriller.

Title: Morag Joss & Monique Roffey
Subtitle: AFTER DISASTER STRIKES

One survivor starts her life over but keeping her secret is harder than she hoped. It’s a flood which changes lives in Monique Roffey’s Archipelago, with Gavin Weald unwisely bringing his family back to their Caribbean home.

Title: Ben Verth: Alsatian and Chips

Title: Gillian Slovo
Subtitle: HOW A HISTORICAL CALAMITY CAN ECHO DOWN THE AGES
Description: From the author of Red Dust comes the 1880s-set An Honourable Man. In a besieged Khartoum, General Gordon stands on the roof of his fortress, vowing to fight to the death. In this novel, the trickle-down effect of Empire influenced folly is felt by many, all the way down to a laudanum addicted woman in Victorian London. Slovo talks to the Guardian’s Literary Editor, Claire Armitstead.

Title: Ben Beattie & Geoffrey Beattie
Subtitle: RUNNING INTO FATHER-SON ISSUES
Description: Geoffrey Beattie is a successful academic and TV presenter with a passion for running, but his hectic schedule almost destroyed his relationship with his son Ben. Fortunately it was running that brought the two men back together and they join us today to share an emotional journey into the highs and lows of family relationships and the unique pleasures of running.

Title: Sex, Lyres and Audiotape

Struggling in their new country to earn money for their families back home, the women face social marginalisation and the imminent expiration of their work permits.
Artist: Nicole N Horanyi, Heidi Kim Andersen

He covers how to approach a text and the skills required to guide you through the process, and analyses the relationship between author, translator and text. Heim has translated contemporary and classical fiction and drama from Czech, Dutch, French, German, Hungarian, Italian, Romanian and Russian. He recently published new translations of Chekhov’s plays and is now working on his first translation from Chinese. This class is for everyone, offering insight into translating a range of languages into English. (Lunch & coffee included.)

	Please note: Michael Henry Heim is no longer able to appear in this event. Instead it will go ahead with Ros Schwartz.

	Ros has translated over 60 works of Francophone literature, notably Saint-Exupéry’s The Little Prince. Winner of the 2008 International Dagger award for her co-translation of Dominique Manotti’s Lorraine Connection, she was made a Chevalier dans l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres in 2009 for her services to French literature. She is currently translating Lebanese writer Dominique Eddé, whose first novel to be translated into English, Kite, has just been published.

Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Aaaaaaaaaaaaarghh! It’s the Malcolm Hardee Comedy Awards Show with Miss Behave - and It’s Free!
Description: Outrageously bizarre free two hour show including Fringe Alternative Comedy Awards, hosted by Olivier award-winning La Clique's, 'fabulous courtesan of comedy' (Times). Details - www.malcolmhardee.com/award.

Title: The Loves I Haven't Known
Description: 'No, love's a b*tch', I said, 'love, not you'. But the damage was done... Uproarious tales of romantic misadventure from the creators of Tony! The Blair Musical. 'Genius' **** (Scotsman). 'Spot-on' **** (Evening Standard). www.bushmccluskey.co.uk.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Just the Tonic Comedy Club's Midnight Show
Description: Consistently boasting the most interesting line ups in the country' (Times). The best acts from the Fringe come and muck about and make you laugh at midnight. It's only a tenner!
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Barbershopera: The Three Musketeers
Description: Barbershopera are back! This time with swords, reinventing the classic adventure story with fresh four-part harmonies. Musical Theatre Matters award winners three years running (2008-2010). 'A feast of frenetic ridiculousness and superb singing’ *** ** (Scotsman).

Title: We Love Comedy
Description: We Love Comedy comes back to Edinburgh. A different showcase of the very best stand-up every day and entry is free! You can donate what you think it's worth at the end! We love comedy. Do you?
Warnings: Adult Themes. Children must be with parents.
Artist: Jools Constant / Sean Brightman Ltd / PBH's Free Fringe

Title: Simon Mayo
Description: You may know Simon Mayo as an award-winning broadcaster; he currently presents the hugely popular BBC Radio 2 Book Club on his Drivetime show. He has been listened to by millions who rely on his insightful film reviews and music choices but now he’s turned his talents to writing. His first book for young readers is entitled, and stars, Itch, an accident prone, science obsessed 14 year old. Itch has a slightly explosive hobby – he collects chemicals but when he discovers a previously unknown element, he attracts the attentions of some unpleasant sorts…

Title: Don Paterson
Subtitle: 'SAY THIS TO THE QUICK STREAM: I AM'
Description: The publication of his Selected Poems, drawing on 20 years of Don Paterson's work, gives us an opportunity to reflect on the writing to of a genuinely great Scottish poet. Since his debut Nil Nil won the Forward Prize for Best First Collection in 1993, Paterson has built a body of work of a consistently breathtaking standard. Today he reads some of his all-time favourites.

Title: Ian Fox - Shutter Monkey (The Comedy Show With Pictures) - Free
Description: Forget typewriters. What would happen if you give an infinite number of monkeys a camera each? 'A wonderfully entertaining hour' **** (Comedy.co.uk). 'Funny, fascinating and engaging' (Copstick, Scotsman).
Artist: Ian Fox in Association With the Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: Derek Ryan: Time Lord - Free
Description: Irish comedian Derek Ryan reveals how much time is needed before humiliation becomes funny, why the Irish are always late and the secret to time travel. Time flies. We’re going to crash and die. Meet the pilot.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Captain Taylor's Coffee House
Venue description: A stylish and relaxing licensed cafe, and a brand new Fringe venue offering a mixture of quality food and drink, and free shows throughout the day - all right in the heart of Edinburgh, just off of the Royal Mile.

Title: Michael Morpurgo
Description: It’s been a crazy couple of years for Michael Morpurgo, following the success on stage and screen of his acclaimed novel War Horse. Come and hear Michael talk about his life, his work, Oscars and Spielberg. He also discusses Private Peaceful, the latest of his novels to be adapted and the process involved. Afterwards, you have the chance to receive a specially designed bookplate as Michael will not be available to sign individual books.

Title: Catriona Knox - Hellcat
Description: Critically acclaimed, red-blooded and acutely well-observed character comedy. 'Hilariously executed with commitment, verve and a cracking script' **** (Chortle.co.uk). **** (FestMag.co.uk). 'Near ridiculously pitch perfect' **** (TheNewCurrent.com). 'Deliciously entertaining' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). www.catrionaknox.com.
Artist: Mick Perrin for Just For Laughs Live
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Rosie Thorn and The Patsy Cornish Saga
Description: With the assistance of Mr Gardener, the accordion playing man servant, Rosie Thorn's darkly irreverent and hilarious tale marking the demise of Miss Patsy Cornish comes to life with music and song.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Huggers - Free Festival Family Fun
Description: More great comedy and cabaret for all the family to enjoy on the top deck of a bus at this delightful and fun afternoon show. 'Great fun, go and see it' (Kate Copstick, Scotsman).
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Des Clarke: Final Destination
Description: Scotland's star of stand-up and the Capital Breakfast Show takes us on a wild journey of enlightenment and jokes. Will we ever reach our Final Destination? Chortle Award Winner. **** (Metro). **** (Chortle.co.uk). **** (List).
Artist: Bound and Gagged by arrangement with Debi Allen Associates

Title: On the Edge
Description: Frank deals with the coastal erosion of his cliff top home and his disintegrating lifestyle in a Prospero like way, uniting his family and accepting his destiny in one last, brave, magical act. www.theatreontheedge.co.uk.
Venue: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel
Venue description: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel offers two performance spaces ideal for intimate, experimental, and engaging theatre. We present a programme of theatrical performance, especially innovative works, original works, devised theatre, movement, puppetry, immersive theatre and music.

Title: Sell Yourself: Self-Marketing for Actors
Description: Spotlight's PR manager Emma Dyson and social media manager Gary Andrews will be offering essential career advice for actors. Topics include networking, CVs, showreels, headshots, online presence and how to approach agents and casting directors.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Short Films 2: Dream Machine
Description: These films are united in a shared engagement with a process of creative salvage and the incantation of magical elements. Drawing upon vintage film formats, found film and a keen aesthetic imagination, they boast dark tales of sacrificial offerings, alchemists, mystical Scottish folklore and a stunning twist upon the classic vampire archetype.

Title: FNT Live presents... The Jingling Lane Family Singers
Description: FNT = Friday Night Therapy = Belfast's newest sketch comedy sensation, showcasing new stand-up comics, new writers and new directors. Don't miss their first appearance at the Edinburgh Fringe.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: The Heart and History of The Dandy
Description: Join Mr Gum writer and comic book fan Andy Stanton as he introduces Morris Heggie, former editor of The Dandy and author of The Art and History of The Dandy, and Gordon Tait, an illustrator on the Dandy and the Beano. Explore all the brilliant characters, discover where the ideas came from and find out who inspired the character Beryl the Peril. A rare opportunity for fans of all ages to get a glimpse into the minds of the creators of the iconic comics.

Title: Not the Adventures of Moleman
Description: 'They've created something like comedy jazz, I might have been watching something that goes onto greatness' (SnipeLondon.com). Come see if you agree as Not the Adventures of Moleman do some entertainment for you.
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink. With a section of free Fringe shows in the downstairs room throughout the day.

Title: Jimmie MacGregor - A Gathering of Songs, Stories and Famous Folk
Description: Half of Jimmie MacGregor and Robin Hall, they toured the world, appeared weekly on the Tonight Show and hosted the White Heather Club. Jimmie’s stories with humour, songs and images.
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult

Title: Departure Lounge
Description: Four teenagers, one delayed plane, a holiday they'll never forget. A high-energy comedy musical, commended by the Scottish Daily Mail Edinburgh Festival Fringe Drama Award 2012. **** 'Hugely entertaining' (Liverpool Echo). **** 'Wonderfully funny, heartbreaking, euphoric' (LSMedia). www.insteptheatre.co.uk.

Title: A Scottish Journey and Beyond
Description: Singer Coreen Scott performs with Laverock. Beautiful musical arrangements of Celtic ballads, favourite Scottish folk songs and the haunting French melodies of Edith Piaf.  'Beautiful renditions of traditional and modern songs' (Scotsman). www.coreenscott.co.uk.
Venue description: The Festival of Spirituality and Peace has a breath-taking array of activities taking places from drama to drumming and conversations to art exhibitions. A non-profit organisation it aims to engage its audience with the original ethos of the Edinburgh Festival.

Artist: Hunt & Darton / Escalator East to Edinburgh
Venue description: Fully functioning pop-up café where food meets live-art. The entire business will be presented as art, open to public scrutiny and served with a twist. Live art duo Hunt&Darton blend art with the everyday with guest appearances from your favourite artists.

Title: John Scott - Totally Fed Up
Description: In 2010 the government issued a questionnaire to measure how happy we were. I mean … really? F*ck right off! ‘A stand out, stand-up … hilarious’ (RipItUp.com, Adelaide 2012). ‘Nothing missed the mark … superb' (List).

Artist: Off The Kerb Productions by arrangement with Lisa Richards Agency
