Title: Pornography

Description: Is this your first time? Edinburgh can be daunting for new participants, so come and meet Fringe Society staff who can support your experience. Also, find out about all the services provided at Fringe Central.

Description: “As no other filmmaker, Lav Diaz is involved with the suffering of the people of the Philippines, with its history of colonialism, corruption and poverty. A philosophical drama about the psychological effects of injustice and arbitrariness” (Gertjan Zuilhof, programmer, International Film Festival Rotterdam).

Title: Matías Néspolo & Chibundu Onuzo
Subtitle: COMMUNITIES IN STRIFE
Description: Matías Néspolo’s 7 Ways to Kill a Cat is a debut novel that takes us into the slums of Buenos Aires telling the story of two boys on the cusp of adulthood who have no choice but to join the gangs that rule their community. Chibundu Onuzo’s The Spider King’s Daughter is the story of two star-crossed lovers in Lagos which rapidly takes on darker tones.

Title: Company
Description: Bobby is turning 35 - time to settle down? His girlfriends and friends think so. But for a New York bachelor can there ever be too much Company? 'Deserves more stars than I can hand out' (BroadwayBaby.com). ***** (Scotsman). www.companyatthefringe.com.
Artist: One Academy Productions (Royal Conservatoire of Scotland)
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Carmen Funebre
Description: Charity performance. Fringe First Award-winning. ‘An unforgettable dramatisation of war’ (Observer). ‘Terrifying and highly recommended’ (Guardian). ‘A contemporary performance created with theatrical skill and sensitivity of an open nerve, a poetic piece devoid of euphemism’ (Espectador).
Warnings: Outdoor show, all standing, charity performance
Venue description: The distinguished and historic surroundings of the University of Edinburgh's 200-year-old college are transformed into 'consistently one of Edinburgh's most exciting venues' (Scotsman). Anything and everything goes with spectacular outdoor shows in this gracious and original space.

Title: Lawrence of Arabia
Description: To mark the 50th anniversary of this masterpiece, Sony Pictures Entertainment presents this new digital restoration.  During the First World War, a British officer succeeds in uniting the Arab tribes and goes to war against the occupying Turkish army. Grand in every sense, this example of an established director at his height aims for greatness and achieves it. Restored by Sony Pictures Colourworks and distributed by Park Circus.

Title: Thin Ice
Description: Daniel’s frozen solid in an Arctic hut. Richard and Laura arrive too late to rescue him. As the body thaws, deadly secrets surface. Wartime thriller, love story from Total Theatre nominees (Reykjavik).  ‘Beautifully simple and effective’ (EdinburghGuide.com). www.shams.org.uk.

Venue: Laughing Horse @ Edinburgh City Football Club

Title: Tissue
Description: Astonishing physical theatre that packs genuine emotional punch. Ensemble performance at its very best. ‘If they come up again next year – and I sincerely hope they do – then make every effort to see them’ (FringeReview.co.uk, 2011).

Title: She Married Her Boss
Description: An efficient secretary tries to bring some working-class common sense to running her boss’s household but meets resistance from his family. Played for naturalistic satire rather than belly laughs, this is an interesting set of variations on some of La Cava’s favourite themes.

Title: Sarfraz Manzoor: The Boss Rules
Description: Bruce Springsteen's songs contain the secrets of life, love and happiness. The Guardian journalist tackles race, religion and rock’n’roll, and how ‘the Boss’ saved his life - and why he can change yours. www.sarfrazmanzoor.co.uk.

Title: Will Self
Subtitle: A VERY MODERN CONDITION
Description: Since he burst onto the literary scene with The Quantity Theory of Insanity, Will Self has established himself as one of Britain’s most adventurous writers. Here, he discusses his ambitious new novel Umbrella with literary critic Stuart Kelly. Extravagant and wildly imaginative, it tells the story of a munitions worker who has fallen into a coma. Is her disease a microcosm of the technological revolutions of the twentieth century?

Title: Kevin Dewsbury: In...Sane - Free
Description: An autobiographical stand-up show about a nervous breakdown and a journey towards recovery. He's alright now, probably. 'A funny story that's worth telling. A cleverly-structured tale, amazing, redemptive and powerful' (FringeGuru.com). www.freefestival.co.uk @ComedyKevioni.

Title: The Value of the Environment
Subtitle: REPOSITIONING THE CLIMATE DEBATE
Description: With the economic crisis still threatening Europe, the impetus to solve the problems of climate change has diminished. But climate justice and access to precious resources have direct economic and social implications. How do we re-engage the public, politicians and the media to reposition the environment as an immediate concern? Join the debate, led by Gavin Esler as chair, and with poet Ruth Padel, Simon Pepper, the founding director of WWF Scotland and Alistair McIntosh, writer, lecturer, social activist and campaigning academic working in the field of human ecology.

Title: Secrets and Lies with Lil Chase & Chris Higgins
Description: Both Lil Chase and Chris Higgins write books about the challenges life can throw at us. In Secrets, Lies and Locker 62, Lil explores the issue of bullying and how far you should go to be popular – especially when you know everybody’s deepest secrets. Chris’ latest novel, He’s After Me, explores falling deeply, truly and intensely in love for the first time, but is the object of affection all he seems? Come and find out more and discover why secrets make such compelling stories.

Title: Cancer Time
Description: A dark comedy following two work colleagues at a south Wales call centre. Initially strangers, they get to know each other during their fag breaks, where they bond through witty conversation until interrupted by a very real tragedy.
Venue description: Venue 13 promotes new writing. Run by the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama in collaboration with the California Institute of the Arts, the 2012 season will feature the best new theatre from Wales and the United States.

Title: The Letter of Last Resort and Good With People

Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am, as well as delicious cakes, freshly ground coffee and award-winning "best ice-cream in Scotland" 2011!

Title: The Cagebirds
Description: Six birds locked in a cage, each trapped in their own world with their own problems. The Wild One tries to shake them out of their stupor to stand up against the tyrannical Mistress... David Campton's absurdist classic.

Title: Jacqueline Wilson
Description: In 1902, E Nesbit published Five Children and It which has never been out of print. Now, Jacqueline Wilson has revisited the original and created Four Children and It. Set in the modern day and following Rosalind and Robbie, their half-sister Maudie and step-sister Smash, the foursome discover the mythical sand-fairy, or Psammead, in a big sandpit in Surrey's Oxshott Woods! Come and hear more about her take on this much-loved story.

Title: Mackenzie Crook (Cancelled)
Description:
Actor and comedian Mackenzie Crook is best known for his roles as Gareth in The Office or Ragetti in Pirates of the Caribbean. But he started out wanting to be a cartoonist and graphic artist and he’s used this skill superbly in his first book for children The Windvale Sprites. Meet Mackenzie for talk about his tale of Asa, who discovers a tiny, winged creature at the bottom of the garden and watch as he draws some of the characters and scenes from this atmospheric, fantastical adventure.

	Please note: Mackenzie Crook is no longer able to appear and this event has been cancelled.

Title: John Banville (Cancelled)
Subtitle: HISTORY THAT HAUNTS THE FUTURE
Description:
‘Everywhere we look, we are looking into the past’ says one character in John Banville’s deeply moving and entertaining new book, Ancient Light. The 2005 Man Booker winner’s latest novel features an elderly actor reminiscing about a teenage affair he had in the 1950s with his best friend’s mother, while also coming to terms with the suicide of his adult daughter. Banville talks to the Guardian’s Online Books Editor, Sarah Crown.

	Please note: John Banville is no longer able to make it to Edinburgh and this event has been cancelled.

Title: Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust Book Awards
Subtitle: SCOTTISH BOOK OF THE YEAR
Description: At this keynote Book Festival event, BBC Radio 4 presenter Dame Jenni Murray unveils the winner of the prestigious Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust Book of the Year. The recipient of the £30,000 first prize is drawn from four remarkable Scottish writers already selected as finalists and voted for by the public. Join us to find out whether it's Ali Smith (fiction), Janice Galloway (non-fiction), Angus Peter Campbell (poetry) or Simon Stephenson (first book) who will take the top prize.

Title: The Pilgrim's Progress
Description: The Pilgrim's Progress adapted for stage by David Robinson and Richard Hasnip. Set in the Industrial Revolution, this is a modern adaptation of John Bunyan's classic novel. Follow Christian's challenges on his path to the Heavenly City.
Venue description: Modelled on Saint-Sulpice in Paris, this splendid church dates from 1875 and is in the heart of the West End. A magnificent yet intimate internal space is ideal for music concerts, featuring a fine Wells-Kennedy organ built in 1992.

Title: Message in a Bottle – David Bottomley’s Tribute to Radio 4’s Desert Island Discs
Description: David Bottomley’s affectionate homage to a national radio treasure. Unplugged and live at the piano. A nostalgic, nautical dip into his desert island discs. Come and launch your own message in a bottle.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Creative Writing Class
Subtitle: THE LOST ART OF CORRESPONDENCE
Description: Book artist Rachel Hazell introduces you to the art and pleasure of paper-words. Create your own unique book using letters, envelopes and stamps, inspired by fabulous mail art and artists’ books, examples of which will be available to view and handle during the event to inspire your work. Hone your creative skills in a series of exercises to generate words, practice calligraphy and learn binding, with a beautiful book the end result. Rachel Hazell is a book artist who believes that everyone has a book inside them. Her mission for 2012 is to teach a different class in twelve different places, then turn it into a book. Join her on the journey. (Lunch & coffee included.)

Title: Hardcore Pawn With Mick, Lewis and Shaun
Description: Exploring aspects of living with a disability whilst applying universal themes that apply to both performers and audience members alike with an exciting mixture of music, comedy, dance and more!
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Description: Come for 55 minutes of sketches with various characters. Watch them slip, trip and tumble in a fast-paced foray into timeless comedy with three short men in a world too big for them.

Title: Austen George

Title: Nina Conti: Dolly Mixtures
Description: Groundbreaking ventriloquist Nina Conti and her new entourage mediate on love, life and the edge of existence in a show that refuses to go as rehearsed. 'Uproariously hilarious' (Scotsman). 'A formidable talent' (Observer).
Artist: Mick Perrin for Just For Laughs Live

Title: Stay at Home Dad - Free
Description: Hazard! Stay at home Dad! Ex white-van man takes on the responsibility of two baby girls. An uplifting show about failing, joy, untidiness and perspective. Tales of ineptitude and buffoonery on a gargantuan scale.

Title: Self-Criticism
Description: Bohemian Rhapsody as background music. Two women waiting, two women stuck. Two personalities that cannot stand each other, living in the same body. Ego and super-ego battling to the end. Who will survive? Two women, one life. Self-Criticism.

Title: Who's Dorian Gray?
Description: Ed, Dom and Rich have lived with each other for three years, but when control, power and betrayal take hold, their lives start to unravel before them and they pursue a path that only leads to destruction.

Title: The Wolves Descend
Description: A darkly-comic modern opera satirising today’s obsession with the supernatural. A village becomes a tourist destination for lovers of the macabre. Losing its lure, staff of a guesthouse take extreme measures to keep their blood money flowing...
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Stage School Star with Lyn Gardner
Description: Lyn Gardner is the theatre critic for The Guardian as well as the writer of the Olivia novels about a young girl at stage school. Join Lyn as she introduces Olivia’s latest adventure, Olivia’s Enchanted Summer, which sees the young heroine arrive in Edinburgh to spend August enjoying the Fringe. If you like the idea of one day being on the stage or just love a good story about friendship, families, finding yourself and theatre then this is for you.

Title: Sven Lindqvist
Subtitle: CAN ART BE THE ANSWER TO  LIFE?
Description: Sven Lindqvist is one of Sweden’s greatest living authors. Over the past 30 years he has published more than 40 books. His insightful travelogues have brought him huge acclaim, and now, for the first time, his classic of modern literature The Myth of Wu Tao-Tzu is published in English. Lindqvist shares his work – a book that has never been out of print since it was first published in Sweden in 1967.

Title: Mark Billingham & Christopher Brookmyre
Subtitle: UNIQUE MEETING OF A CRIME-WRITING DUO
Description: Two of the country’s top-selling contemporary crime writers hook up for an unmissable hour. It’s always a delight when authors come together to celebrate the capricious spirit of creativity, and to show their profound respect for everyone who plays a part in their journey through the world of literature. But by half past nine at night we think you are ready for the dark side. Mark Billingham and Paisley boy Christopher Brookmyre are both laconic wits and here present a show where readings from their latest novels and the weighty discussion of genre are jettisoned completely in favour of cheap laughs and dirty stories. They will lift the lid on the real world of being a writer. The angry letters from readers. The backstage shenanigans. The banter and the bampots. Expect strong language, plenty of laughs and at least one extremely disturbing story about a chicken.

Title: Thomas Hardie Presents: Where's Thomas, Hardie?
Description: ‘Talented and versatile sketch duo’ **** (RemoteGoat.co.uk), Thomas Hardie, are back with a show full of mystery and suspense for Hardie, and a joyous rollercoaster of characters and sketches for the audience!
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.

Chaired by Ewan Morrison.

Tom Benn’s crime novel The Doll Princess is set in mid-90s Manchester, with the body of an Egyptian heiress discovered in the basement of a block of flats.

Title: Still Home
Description: Still Home explores the breakdown of a relationship in a contemporary home. In our globalised age where ‘moving forward’ is the only way to exist, what happens when we find ourselves standing still?
Venue: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel
Venue description: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel offers two performance spaces ideal for intimate, experimental, and engaging theatre. We present a programme of theatrical performance, especially innovative works, original works, devised theatre, movement, puppetry, immersive theatre and music.

Title: Danceforms' 60th International Choreographers' Showcase
Description: Award-winning US and international choreographers present a high-energy blend of avant-garde works. Dancers enjoy the beauty of Susana B Williams's brilliant choreography with superb musical composition by Gabrielle Roth and the Mirrors. www.danceformsproductions.com.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: MAHMOUD DARWISH
Description: Imprisoned for his political activism and for publically reading his poetry, and exiled for 26 years for trying to connect the people of Israel and Palestine, Mahmoud Darwish, regarded by many as Palestine’s national poet, used powerful words to defend Human Rights. Today’s Book Festival authors read extracts from his works. Reading today: Ruth Padel, Jenni Fagan, Lydia Cacho and Jonathan Meres.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: AUNG SAN SUU KYI
Description: Political opposition leader, Nobel Peace laureate and now MP, Aung San Suu Kyi spent much of the past two decades under house arrest. She has come to symbolise the struggle of Burma’s people to be free of widespread and systematic abuses. Our daily series today features extracts from her writings, such as Freedom from Fear. Reading today: Maziar Bahari, Chibundu Onuzo and Joan Bakewell.

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: THE FABLE OF THE HUNGRY ICELANDER
Description:
Iceland: sagas & myths, geysers & volcanic ash, big jumpers & impressively long names, and that frozen food company. The stereotypes are many and probably very irritating for the people that live there, but in recent years Iceland has continually produced a remarkable range of new literary voices creating an exciting contemporary literary scene. This has been capped with Reykjavik, the city of the ‘jólabokaflód’, becoming UNESCO City of Literature in 2011. Sjón is an award-winning poet, musician, novelist and now Book Festival regular. Join him as he hosts a very special event with some of Iceland’s finest writers and musicians including Auður Ava Ólafsdóttir and Kristín Ómarsdóttir.

	Presented in partnership with The Icelandic Literature Fund.

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Title: Kin
Description: ***** ‘A powerful meditation on the shifting dynamics that seep into relationships between middle-aged children and elderly parents' (Herald). Punctuated by Rutherford's live commentary alongside performances-to-camera from members of Forced Entertainment, Quarantine, Reckless Sleepers and Alison Peebles. www.donnarutherford.org. www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com.
Venue description: An intimate 74 seat studio space created for the month of August within the UK’s largest working theatre - the Edinburgh Playhouse, part of the Ambassador Theatre Group.

Title: A Streetcar Named Desire
Description: Tennessee Williams' classic drama presents haunting portrayals of the tempestuous relationships between aristocratic Blanche Dubois, her sister Stella and Stella's brutish husband, Stanley Kowlaski. Award-winning young actors offer bold performances of this mature, challenging play.
Venue description: Pilrig St Paul's church is a spectacular Victorian gothic church and halls with a 100 seat studio theatre and a 400 seat sanctuary auditorium, all within an easy stroll or quick bus ride from Princes Street.

Title: The Brockas in Film-Concert

For their first Edinburgh performance, The Brockas will perform along with the projection of Manuel Conde and Lou Salvador’s Genghis Khan, a 1950 Philippine film that screened at the Edinburgh International Film Festival in 1952 (“For the most part it consists of a battle scene of unparalleled, original ferocity and violence” – New Statesman & Nation).

Title: Debate: Rethinking the Union (Part 3)
Subtitle: THE UNION OR INDEPENDENCE: THE EMOTIONAL ARGUMENTS
Description: Much of the debate around Scottish independence has focused on oil revenues, the Barnett Formula and on the question of whether we’d be better or worse off if Scotland goes it alone. This debate looks beyond the question of economics, to ask whether this country should remain united or separate from Britain, regardless of the bottom line. Even if an independent Scotland were poorer, would there be good reasons for cutting the ties with Westminster? And conversely, can the Unionists articulate a clear argument – from the heart – for keeping the status quo? Join the debate with Stephen Tierney, author of Constitutional Referendums, former MSP and SNP frontbencher Andrew Wilson and Joyce McMillan from The Scotsman.

'Flawless, dynamic, utterly captivating, life- affirming' ***** (Edinburgh Evening News). 'Hilarious... engaging... Ashanti delivers' (New York Times Critics’ Pick).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Lucy Porter - People Person
Description: The Fringe favourite, Radio 4 regular and TV panel show luminary returns with her all-new stand-up show. 'Great gags and superbly worked material' (Edinburgh Evening News). 'Charmingly twisted, articulate and witty' (Sunday Times). Book early.
Warnings: 16+ must be accompanied by an adult
Artist: Lucy Porter / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Edinburgh's year-round comedy club is housed in an intimate basement bar just off St Andrew Square. The atmosphere is relaxed and informal with comfortable cabaret-style seating (although some late night shows are not all seated).

Title: Romeo and Juliet
Description: Welcome to Verona High where Sister Lawrence teaches botany, Tybalt (Queen of Cats) carries a Stanley knife, Nurse wears four-inch stilettos and the inter-house rivalry is really out of hand. **** (ThreeWeeks, for Trojan Women).
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.

Title: Marcus Brigstocke: The Brig Society
Description: No less than the total restructuring of every aspect of life in Britain organised through the medium of jokes. See this show and Win! a free hospital or school! Second prize: a major High Street bank.
Artist: Off The Kerb Productions in association with Corduroy Productions
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound presents the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces The Hall, Rainy and the Baillie.

Title: Kevin Tomlinson: Crazy Little Thing Called Love!
Description: A comic look at love. In all its many forms! Romantic. Platonic. The love of a hobby, pet, money or God. You name it, this show explores it! 'Hilarious, heartwarming comedy!' (Evening Standard).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Lysistrata - The Sex Strike
Description: Lysistrata - The Sex Strike. 'Witty, unpretentious fun. You'll come out with an appreciation of Braindead's genius’ ***** (FringeGuru.com). Fast, silly and profound. A contemporary cross-gender battle-of-the-sexes twist on Aristophanes' irreverent all-male original.
Venue description: One of the festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross genre performance makes this central venue a must for all.  Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Either Way
Description: Writer/ Director Hafsteinn Gunnar Sigurðsson has created a carefully paced comedy of opposites – between stillness and slapstick, activity and inertia and silence broken by thumping electro.

Title: Bourgeois & Maurice - Sugartits
Description: An unrivalled mix of social commentary, musical comedy and fashion so high you'll wonder what you've taken, from award-winning cabaret duo Bourgeois & Maurice. 'Talented to within an inch of their lives' **** (TimeOut).
Artist: Soho Theatre By Arrangement With Tim Whitehead
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Reel Perspectives
Description: An intimate, engaging journey through contemporary dance and film. Reel Perspectives combines two contrasting new works, exposing audiences to abstract, emotive movement to create an intense dance-theatre experience.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Spank!
Description: Back again! Sexy hosts, awesome comedians, controlled anarchy and booze. 'This is what the festival should be about' (List). 'Comedy and legendary party night ... get down there right away!' (Time Out). ‘Best Wild Night Out’ (Scotland on Sunday).
Artist: James Wren, Leon Fleury / Corrie McGuire for Objective Talent Management
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Bordello Blues
Description: Isobel, a French prostitute, falls for her client in a tale of bittersweet, unrequited love. A glamorous and tragic world featuring fetish burlesque and the songs of Edith Piaf, Nina Simone and Hollywood screen legend Marlene Dietrich.
Venue description: Vibrant Cabaret bar located on the Royal Mile. A global feast of song, music, cabaret, comedy, dance and theatre. Free entry after midnight. Open til 3am daily See: www.thespaceuk.com for more info.

Title: Bernard the Ferret (Happy to be Himself!)
Description: This funny and magical storytelling with puppets, launches a new book by playwright Eve Stebbing. Performances are followed by a workshop. See www.spinofftheatre.co.uk for more information.
Venue description: Central Library is a beautiful Victorian building in the heart of the Old Town and Edinburgh World Heritage site. We welcome around a million people a year to use its extensive resources and facilities or just to enjoy the space. www.edinburgh.gov.uk/libraries
Venue accessibility: \n

Title: Mary - A Musical Play
Description: Laugh and cry as the tragic life of Mary Queen of Scots is sympathetically portrayed in this innovative and original production. Experience a talented young cast igniting interest in one of Scotland's most enigmatic monarchs.
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Andy and Mike's... Tick Tock Time Machine
Description: Andy Day (CBeebies' Andy's Wild Adventures), stars alongside comedy partner, Mike James, and a time machine! 'If I could go back in time and watch it all over again I would' (Justin Fletcher).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: BBC: The Radio 2 Arts Show
Description: Live from Edinburgh, The Radio 2 Arts Show captures all the excitement from Europe's most significant cultural event, Edinburgh's Festival Fringe, with guests from the world of comedy, theatre, dance, literature and music.
Venue address: Corner of Potterrow and Marshall Street,Edinburgh
Venue description: Experience the best of the BBC under one roof and a taster of all the delights of the Fringe. Join us at Venue 25 for BBC shows, big names, stand-up every night plus masterclasses from BBC Radio, TV and Online. Free events are ticketed via a random draw. To enter the draw please use the show website link: bbc.co.uk/tickets.

Title: Go to the Devil and Shake Yourself
Description: The shocking history of the medieval papacy. Fourteen centuries of scandal chronicled in a series of experimental folk/pop songs by London-based Sheffielder Joe Murphy, AKA Sergeant Buzfuz. www.sergeantbuzfuz.com.
Venue description:
Ryan's is situated in the heart of Edinburgh's chic west-end and comprises of three departments: Main Bar, Coffee Shop and Cellar Restaurant. 
\nRyan’s hidden gem is bursting with character and this is where the comedy acts will be on. As well as the main area where the performances take place the restaurant features seven private alcoves for dining. The venue boasts a piano bar and live Jazz every Sunday night.

Title: Dragon
Description: A supremely imaginative blending of A History of Violence, TV’s Sherlock and Chang Cheh’s 1967 classic One-Armed Swordsman, Wu Xia is a visually ravishing, compelling and (rare in the genre) thoughtful kung fu actioner, with Hong Kong superstar Donnie Yen taking on both acting and choreographic responsibilities. In 1917 southwestern China, an investigation into the killing of two robbers by a seemingly mild-mannered paper-maker, leads forensic detective Xu (Takeshi Kaneshiro) inexorably towards the infamous 72 Demons gang…

Title: Gate #5
Description: Habre presents a bigger picture: of Lebanon itself and how the country has changed from the 1960s to the present day.

Title: The Sidcup Family Portrait
Description: The Sidcup Family unearth their lineage in this debut show. Physical comedy, improvisation, puppetry and live music engulf the audience in this show. Guaranteed to tickle some of your ribs almost all of the time.
Venue description: 40 metres from the centre of Princes Street, just up from the National Gallery, this beautiful venue has a reputation for quality ***** and **** sell-outs! Outstanding, international companies: interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, classics, cutting-edge plays, dance, quirky comedy and musicals...

Title: Playing Fate
Description: A couple on the verge of break up and a journey into their past. A humorous and touching new play. ‘A thoughtful exploration of fate and the future’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘Special moments’ (Jeremy Kingston, Times).
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Scotch Broth
Description: An entertaining mixture of Scottish family songs at the Fringe for the first time. Come and join the best sing-along in Edinburgh! Scotch Broth is funny and engaging and gets everyone joining in. Not to be missed!
Venue description: Paradise Green's purpose-built venue in the vaulted basements of Augustine United Church hosts an exciting programme of theatre and comedy for all tastes, from classics to new and experimental work. Soak up the true spirit of the Fringe.

Title: Sparks - CANCELLED
Description: Quirky fairytale, somewhere between Rapunzel and The Adventures of Alvin Sputnik. Features live music. The show is ideal for children of all ages and fans of Tim Burton - a story about love, loss and clockwork. 'Simply brilliant' (DurhamOne.co.uk).
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Macbeth on Inchcolm Island
Description: Meet us at Summerhall at 6.30pm and journey with us by coach and or meet us at Hawes Pier, South Queensferry for the boat to the stunning island of Inchcolm, Firth of Forth, for Macbeth.
Warnings: No disabled access, unsuitable for the elderly and infirm. Walking is involved; please dress appropriately as some of teh production will take place outside.
Artist: Mermaids, Hands in the Air & Demarco European Art Foundation
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Uninvited
Description: A stranger’s in your house, whistling. He’s drinking tea, he's got his eyes on the egg whisk ... and the wallpaper’s talking. Then there’s her, and her Madeira cake - experience Fat Git's absurd comedy of pedants, whistlers and apathetic furniture.
Venue description: Bedlam Theatre plays host to an eclectic mix of theatre, dance and comedy at the heart of the Fringe. Enjoy the unique atmosphere of our famous cafe and discover some of the most innovative shows the festival has to offer.

Title: Duplica
Description: A stunning and stylish performance that plays with the harmonies between light, body and shadow. A mysterious mute dialogue emerges between the body and its image. Bianchi’s lonely body is monstrously reflected, perpetually seeking something other than the self.
Venue: Dance Base - National Centre for Dance
Venue description: Centrally located in the Old Town, Dance Base is a beautiful and inspiring setting for dance. We present performances by the best British and international dance companies and also offer classes and workshops from breakdance to ballet - for all ages.

Title: Pete Johansson - Utopian Crack Pipe
Description: Edinburgh Comedy Award nominee Johansson is back in Edinburgh this year to chronicle his self addiction of trying to make the world what he thinks is a better place. Book early! 'Supremely entertaining' (Independent).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Toots and the Maytals
Description: Toots and the Maytals, originally called simply The Maytals, are considered legends of ska and reggae music. Their sound is a unique, original combination of gospel, ska, soul, reggae and rock.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier Live music & Club venue now into it’s 15 year.

Title: The Big Bite-Size Breakfast Show
Description: Three brilliant breakfast feasts of playlets. New international/UK writers. Coffee, croissant and strawberries. ‘One of the most important shows you'll see at the Fringe’ ***** (Daily Record, FringeReview.co.uk, WhatsOnStage.com, Carol Tambor - shortlist, Sky Arts).
Warnings: Some occasional strong language and sexual references
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Jon Richardson - Funny Magnet
Description: The 8 Out Of Ten Cats team captain is back at the Edinburgh festvial to end his 2012 tour with a limited run of just four shows.
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound presents the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces The Hall, Rainy and the Baillie.

Title: Hamlet and Other Theatrical Nightmares
Description: Theatre, why do we do it? Fame? Glory? Certainly not for money! Furthermore, why are we fixated on that theatrical nightmare, Hamlet? Hopkins Drama explores this obsession through the comedies of Durang, Stoppard and Haenel.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: I'm High On Life: What Are You On?
Description: 'My upbringing was wonderful, but might not make sense to you...' Trauma, addiction, love! Fringe World 2012 Best Local Comedy award-winner. 'A rising talent ... one to keep watching' (Sunday Times, Australia).
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Paterson Arran Ten at Ten
Description: A delicious morning reading from one of our Festival authors to set you up for the day. Check the screen in the Entrance Tent to see who’s reading each day.

Title: Ian Livingstone
Description: Ian Livingstone celebrates Fighting Fantasy game books. Ian has been in the interactive games industry for over twenty five years, is the co-founder of Games Workshop, launched Dungeons & Dragons in Europe and wrote the first Fighting Fantasy with Steve Jackson thirty years ago! Just ask your dad, he’s bound to have a couple of dusty copies in the loft. This promises to be a thrilling interactive event to celebrate the 30th anniversary of the series and Ian’s new gamebook, Blood of the Zombies. Whether you know the books or are new to the concept, we guarantee you’ll be hooked.

Title: One Mile Away
Description: A compelling tale of courage and determination with a smooth hip-hop soundtrack. Dylan and Shabba, members of rival Birmingham gangs, attempt to broker a peace agreement after being introduced by filmmaker Penny Woolcock, who had directed Dylan in the drama 1 Day (also screening). After the screening on 24 June, there will be a Q&A with Penny Woolcock, producer James Purnell and the young men in the documentary, followed by a special live performance at the Traverse Theatre, with Zimbo, YT, JB and surprise guests.

Title: Aberdeen vs. Glasgow vs. The World II - Free
Description: We're bigger, better, and more insane than ever! Through the entire festival we will bring you stand-up comedians, ventriloquists, character acts, games, fun and general mayhem. **** (ThreeWeeks).
Artist: FGC Comedy / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, the Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11am-2am. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.

Title: The Ugly Duckling
Description: Kipper Tie Theatre are back with the musical tale of an unhappy duckling who turns into a beautiful swan. Lashings of catchy tunes, magical storytelling and a heap of farmyard fun. It's a quacking good time! www.kippertietheatre.com.
Artist: Kipper Tie Theatre with C theatre
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Rick Shapiro: Rebirth
Description: Crash. Boom. Silence. Following an amnesia causing accident, the American comedy legend returns - revitalized, regenerated and reborn – with his jazz-styled lyricism and more ‘of the most inventive filth you've ever heard’ (London Evening Standard).
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: One Track Minds - Free
Description: We are the 'meat in our heads'. The human animal may not be divine, but that does not make it any less marvellous or comical. Robert and Andrew each do a 20-25 minute set.
Artist: Robert Coyle and Andrew Gilmore / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue accessibility: \n

Title: Flamenco Flow Global
Description: Fringe favourite Ricardo Garcia's music has travelled to four continents in recent years, demonstrating the art of Flamenco music, rhythm and dance. Just returned from Ethiopia, creating and performing a collaboration sponsored by the Spanish Embassy. www.flamencoflow.com.
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: WitTank
Description: Like a battering ram to the funny-bone, stars of BBC3’s Live at The Electric rocket back to the Fringe with a lavish parade of inventive characters and sketch magnificence. ‘Hilarious’ (Independent). ***** (List). ***** (Comedy.co.uk). www.wittank.com.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Passion, Pints and Potatoes - An Irish Guide to Life
Description: Two Irish country bumpkins from the land of priests and potatoes talk life, love and everything between. Jokes while standing, sung words and fun moments.
Venue description: Edinburgh's only late night Irish pub situated just off the Grassmarket in Edinburgh's historic old town. Open daily from 3pm-5am (Festival hours). Closest bus routes are 2, 23, 27, 41, 45. Any queries contact us on 0131 2252002
Venue accessibility:

\nAccessible WC, assistance dogs welcome. Wheelchair accessible.

Title: The Creative and Commercial Worth of Children's Theatre
Description: Do people think children's work of a lesser quality than work for adults? Is it more difficult to get reviewed? What is the motivation to make children's work?
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Lavinia Greenlaw & Marie Howe
Subtitle: BEING AND NOTHINGNESS
Description: Alongside her exquisite poetry, Lavinia Greenlaw has written opera libretti, radio dramas and essays on art. Now she brings her interest in perception, thought and experience to an absorbing and enigmatic new collection of poems, The Casual Perfect. She is joined today by the celebrated American writer Marie Howe, whose poems can be breathtaking and heartbreaking in equal measure. This is a rare opportunity to hear this astonishingly perceptive writer reading her work.

Title: Boy In a Dress
Description: Transdrogynous fallen Catholic, council estate queen and former catwalk model La JohnJoseph's raucously political and accidentally profound retrospectacle combines autobiography, vaudeville, song, striptease and postmodern philosophy in an exhilarating collage exploring gender, class, religion and identity.
Warnings: Under 18's must be accompanied by an adult contains a small amount of nudity
Artist: Critical Mass / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue: The Stand Comedy Club III & IV
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue, Stand III is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand IV an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.

4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: BBC: Alex Horne Presents The Horne Section
Description: Fringe favourites The Horne Section present a one-off Edinburgh special after their first series on Radio 4. Comedian Alex Horne marshals his talented band in a joyous, life-affirming combination of music and comedy.
Venue address: Corner of Potterrow and Marshall Street,Edinburgh
Venue description: Experience the best of the BBC under one roof and a taster of all the delights of the Fringe. Join us at Venue 25 for BBC shows, big names, stand-up every night plus masterclasses from BBC Radio, TV and Online. Free events are ticketed via a random draw. To enter the draw please use the show website link: bbc.co.uk/tickets.

Title: A Man Or a Muppet?
Description: The latest Academy award-winning movie song since the Oscar's 1934 inception. Four singers and a pianist explore the eclectic collection of the songwriters’ art that have won the Academy's coveted gold statuette - at the (Edinburgh) Academy!
Venue description: The Edinburgh Academy is centrally located in the New Town, with ample off-street parking and an on-site cafe for festival patrons. The venue is centered on its amazing oval Hall, built in 1824 and designed by William Burn.

Title: Bach: Magnificat and Handel: Coronation Anthems
Description: Bach’s thrilling Magnificat and Handel’s ever-glorious Coronation Anthems with the spine-tingling Zadok the Priest for the Diamond Jubilee year. Edinburgh’s sparkling baroque ensemble continues to thrill audiences with music by our favourite composers.
Venue description: Built in 1688, this beautifully light and spacious kirk serves both the Palace of Holyroodhouse and Edinburgh Castle. Experience its wonderful 'cathedral' acoustic at a concert, or join us for worship on Sundays at 10.00am or 11:15am.

Title: Pattie Brewster's Friendship Venture (For Some Friends)
Description: Hi guys! Just a normal girl (not creepy!) called… Pattie! It’s 2012 these days, so I’m trying to make friends, because at the moment I mainly know cats. Anyway, enough about cats! www.pattiebrewster.co.uk
Venue description: Two comfortable and spacious performance spaces set in Scotland's most haunted pub.

Title: Eddie Naessens: The Thing Is This...
Description: Please, please, please, don't make me pander! ‘Talented, sexy, and funny’ **** (Scotsman). ‘Thoroughly enjoyable’ (Stage). ‘A brave comedian who finds comedy material in places most would be afraid to look’ (Irish Independent).
Venue description: This family-run restaurant on South Bridge hosts free comedy in the basement from 1pm until midnight every day of the Fringe. Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am, as well as delicious cakes, freshly ground coffee and award-winning "best ice-cream in Scotland" 2011!

Title: Tony Black & Gordon Ferris
Subtitle: RISING STARS OF CRIME
Description: The immense ebook success of The Hanging Shed has put Gordon Ferris firmly in the minds of the crime fiction fraternity. His next tale with former soldier Douglas Brodie is Bitter Water in which a tarring and feathering triggers a trail of violence. Tony Black’s central figure is Rob Brennan and in Murder Mile the DI wonders whether an Edinburgh Ripper is on the loose.

Title: Stewart Lee - Carpet Remnant World
Description: What can a sexless middle aged married man, whose life now consists mainly of watching Scooby Doo cartoons with a four year old boy, possibly find to write comedy about? 'Superlative' ***** (Metro). www.stewartlee.co.uk.
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult.
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
02459
\n
\nOn street parking for a blue badge holder, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC

Title: Clooney, Cowell, Pitt and Me: Amusing Encounters with the A-List
Description: A rollicking one-man show, direct from LA and New York, where leading showbiz reporter Sandro Monetti reveals what Hollywood stars are really like. ‘The perfect storyteller’ (Daily Express).
Venue description: 40 metres from the centre of Princes Street, just up from the National Gallery, this beautiful venue has a reputation for quality ***** and **** sell-outs! Outstanding, international companies: interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, classics, cutting-edge plays, dance, quirky comedy and musicals...

Title: Meg Rosoff
Description: In the beginning there was Bob and then he made the heavens and the earth… Meg Rosoff’s latest novel There Is No Dog features a typical lazy, self-obsessed, sex-crazed teenage boy. Unfortunately, this teenage boy is also God! Meg’s books such as How I Live Now and The Bride’s Farewell are complex, intriguing, challenging and utterly compelling. Come and hear her discuss ideas, characters and what happens when you leave an adolescent boy in charge of the universe.

Title: Now.Here
Description: Now.Here. Hobbyhorse. Mist. Breath. Flesh. Sun. Two riders, journey. Hoof and heel. 17 days. 200 miles. Wales to London. Collecting stories from those met. Stories from nowhere seeking Now.Here. Seeking life. A beguiling and provocative theatre performance. www.drawntostars.co.uk. @DrawnStars.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: The Day the Sky Turned Black
Description: Multi award-winning drama returns. Inspired by interviews with survivors of Australia’s Black Saturday Bushfires. Stories of courage, humour amidst adversity and hope. Winner: People’s Choice (Sydney Fringe), Solo Performance (Fringe NYC). ‘Enthralling’ (NY Times).
Artist: Best of Sydney Fringe / Ali Kennedy Scott / Direction-Adrian Barnes
Venue description: The Roxy, a beautifully converted former chapel, is the latest addition to Assembly's growing list of venues.  Built in 1809 and located just north-east of our George Square hub, the Roxy houses three performances spaces; the 400 seat former nave Roxy Central, the 168 seat Roxy Upstairs and our 60 seat studio Roxy Downstairs.  The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Dirty Pretty Money
Description: An enchanting piece of new theatre that explores our special relationship with money and the associated power that comes with it. 'For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil' (Timothy, 6:10).
Warnings: Strong Language and References of a Sexual Nature
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Howard Jacobson
Subtitle: CALLING TIME ON THE NOVEL?
Description: Winner of the Man Booker in 2010 for The Finkler Question, Howard Jacobson is sure to rattle some cages with Zoo Time. Arguing that literature may be on its last knees thanks to that pesky internet, Jacobson introduces us to novelist Guy Ableman whose publisher and agent are no longer around. While the novel might be dying, Ableman’s desire to squeeze out one more great book is not.

Title: Compagnie Arcosm (FRANCE) Traverse
Description:
Exhilarating dance, phenomenal choreography and live music, Arcosm is back! 
 
From the company which brought Echoa to the Imaginate Festival in 2009, comes Traverse - they enjoyed it here so much they named their show after their venue!

Alone on stage, in the privacy of his cramped home, a man is apparently very busy and preoccupied by a series of actions necessary for his daily routine, actions that are repeated with precision, day after day.

Yet, from time to time he becomes pensive and dreamy and allows himself a little break... to escape into his secret world, where small grains of his dreams begin to clog up the well-oiled machine of his routine life.
                                                                    "a magnificent spectacle" Le Trident
Venue description: Scotland's new writing theatre, is the festival's most prestigious home of serious drama' (New York Times) and a multiple Fringe First and Herald Angel award winner. The legendary Traverse Bar Cafe offers high quality food and drink 09:00 'til late.

Title: Peter Buckley Hill and Some Comedians XVI

Title: Little Jazz Bird
Description: Jazz vocalist Victoria Bennett has a singular talent for interpretation and a whimsical approach to melody. Tender ballads and sultry swingers (Gershwin/Porter), delivered with shades of Billie Holiday and Blossom Dearie, backed by top trio. www.littlejazzbird.co.uk.

Title: Billy The Mime
Description: ‘Politically incorrect! Uncomfortably funny! Twisted! Chilling!' (New York Times). 'A one-man variety show depicting the most taboo and controversial stories of our culture. It absolutely should not be missed!' (NewYorkTheater.com). Not for children or the easily offended.
Warnings: Not for the easily offended Not suitable for under 16s
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Mark Haddon
Subtitle: RED HOT AND BLUE
Description: The Red House was one of the most anticipated novels of 2012, and it has certainly lived up to that billing. Mark Haddon’s latest revolves around a newly remarried hospital consultant, who attempts to build bridges with his estranged sister. The author of The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time talks to the Guardian’s Literary Editor, Claire Armitstead about how he constructed his new novel using 8 distinct voices.

Title: Fitkin Late
Description: Four pianists, two pianos. New Zealand's Estrella Quartet perform Fitkin's Untitled 11 and Sciosophy, plus virtuoso works written for them by David Hamilton and Gareth Farr. Prepare to be amazed and beguiled. Includes complimentary glass of wine.

Title: Stand-Up at the Jekyll & Hyde - Free
Description: Looking for an afternoon selection of fresh and exciting stand-ups? Look no further. Get to sample a broad range of styles in a classic, no frills stand-up format. www.tomorrowsstanduptoday.co.uk.
Warnings: May contain adult themes, strong language
Artist: Multiple Performers / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items ... Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: Lach: Up the Anti!
Description: Lach's to Antifolk what Kerouac was to Beat. Brilliant songs and comedy! 'NYC's living legend' (TimeOut). ***** (Herald). 'Dangerously fun!' (Uncut). 'Splendid! Best of its kind!' (Mojo). 'Face-ache funny, beat-punk-unplugged joy!' (Guardian). 'Manhattan institution!' (NY Times).

Title: So You Want to Be an Actor
Description: Spotlight’s PR manager Emma Dyson will provide you with practical help on how to realise your dream and become an actor. Looking at choosing a drama school, understanding the industry, and approaching auditions.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Disability Equality Training
Description: Practical training sessions for you to look at how you can better respond to the needs of disabled customers, as well as looking at some of the wider social issues.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Tranquility, Serenity, Calm
Description: A charming, loopy and fast-paced comedy about Peter-Joe, an anarchist trying to rescue an idealistic civil servant, Francis, from the bomb he planted the night before. Inconveniently, Francis is too busy designing Utopia to be rescued.
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: I Heart Peterborough
Description: Joel Horwood turns from Walberswick crabs to Peterborough trannies. A desperate bloke with a chaotic backstory, wig and killer heels staggers through his car crash of a cabaret act. Not for the faint-hearted! www.easternangles.co.uk.
Artist: Eastern Angles /  Escalator East to Edinburgh

Title: Mod Girl
Description: Mod Girl is a reflective melodrama about the brief relationship between a child prostitute and a handsome widower. Two discarded souls seize a fleeting chance for happiness. In the end, nothing in life has to be so carnal.
Warnings: Adult themes, strong language, partial nudity
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Phoebe Traquair Song School Murals
Description: Painted in 1888-1892, Traquair's acclaimed murals, restored in 1998, illustrate the canticle Benedicite Omnia Opera. Showing the Pre-Raphaelite influence, they are a moving expression of faith. Tours meet at the Cathedral entrance (Palmerston Place).
Venue description: One of the world's great neo-gothic buildings, with its three distinctive spires and a tradition of daily choral services sung by the cathedral choir: a magnificent concert venue.  The Song School is covered by vibrant murals by Phoebe Anna Traquair.

Title: Tommy Talks
Description: Sun comedy columnist Tommy Holgate's multimedia bash with stand-up, improv, music and dance. 'Clever and funny' (Al Murray). 'I find his questions genuinely invigorating' (Rob Brydon). 'I wish every interviewer was like this' (Jason Byrne).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Writing Workshop
Subtitle: The Art of Adaptation
Description: The dramatisation of Montmorency, Eleanor Updale's classic tale of double identity, is the prime time attraction at the Fringe’s C venue on Chambers Street this year. Director Chris Snow and his co-writer Matthew Hopkinson (who plays both lead roles) join Updale to reveal the inside story of the transformation, and to discuss the reshaping of favourite books for the stage.

Title: Letter to the Man (from the Boy)
Description: Depraved comedy duo for every bad decision you've ever made. Including onstage DJ, dance numbers and talking penises, Guilt & Shame return with one unmissable late-night party. ‘Brilliant’ (Gay Times). **** (FringeBiscuit.blogspot.com).
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Robertson’s Crusoe
Description: A Hitman and others theorise on loneliness and Big Bang Theory, with precise physicality and bold atmospheric imagery. Classic novel meets movie Collateral, plus The Sky at Night, and Little Britain! From creator of five-star sell-out Space Oddity.
Venue description: An award-winning extravaganza of the best performances from across the Fringe spectrum. The majestic Main House is packed with outstanding dance and physical theatre from around the world while the Cabaret Bar and Studio host thrilling drama, comedy and music.

Title: Juliet Meyers: Raised By Fridge Magnets
Description: Like her favourite flour, Juliet is self-raised, but is she equipped for life’s dramas? ‘Devilish’ (Scotsman). ‘A laugh-out-loud show that resonates’ **** (Chortle.co.uk). ‘Smart and very funny’ (Sarah Millican).Twitter: @julietmeyers.
Warnings: 14+. Must be accompanied by an adult

Venue description: Round the corner, our little sister club is in its thirteenth year. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area.

Title: Mark Easton
Subtitle: THE BREED ON THE END OF THE LEAD
Description: Defining Britishness 'is like painting the wind' says the BBC News home editor, Mark Easton. With the rise in people wanting to be described as Scottish or English rather than British, the Glasgow-bred journalist's new book is a witty and razor sharp analysis of the nation we have become today. Join this proud Scot to discuss dogs, fish and chips and much more. Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Title: The Rat Pack - Live
Description: West End producers Hartshorn and Hook swing back into Edinburgh with their celebrated Rat Pack. Expect sharp suits and smooth vocals as Frank, Sammy and Dean hit the stage with their 12-piece jazz orchestra. **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Dick Gaughan Solo
Description: The only performer to hold the honours - a Lifetime Achievement award from BBC Radio 2 Folk Awards, and induction into the Scots Traditional Music Hall of Fame. Gaughan returns for his annual hometown solo Fringe appearance. www.stoneyport.co.uk.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Rites and Regulations
Description: A girl grapples with strange Taoist funeral rituals, whilst an insomniac office worker battles bureaucracy to bury Grandfather's oversized coffin. An evocative, sensorial, theatrical experience exploring space, funeral bureaucracy and banalities of life in everyday Singapore.
Venue description: An award-winning extravaganza of the best performances from across the Fringe spectrum. The majestic Main House is packed with outstanding dance and physical theatre from around the world while the Cabaret Bar and Studio host thrilling drama, comedy and music.

Title: Journos
Description: This ode to the great British newspaper introduces you to the jovial journos behind the headlines at the Daily Parade newspaper offices. A colourful yet chaotic depiction of a small-town newsroom punctuated with moments of real significance.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: The Magnets: Homegrown
Description: Festival favourites premiere 'best of British' show. 'A cappella maestros' (Telegraph). '...sonic phenomenon you have to hear to believe' (Guardian). 'Singing straight from the gods' (Evening News). 'Guaranteed to put a smile on your face' (Herald).

Title: Eddie Pepitone's Bloodbath
Description: Eddie Pepitone is an Apocalyptic-American master of the dark art of stand-up. Hailed as Don Rickles meets Eckhart Tolle, the Bitter Buddha switches onstage between social rage and self-doubt. 'Directly descended from Bill Hicks' (AV Club).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Tron

Title: Godspell
Description: No sugar stick musical this - a second coming in the midst of the London riots. In a world of torment, dissatisfaction and unrest, even in this chaos there is a ray of humanity and hope.

Title: David O'Doherty: Seize the David O'Doherty
Description: Winner, 2008 Edinburgh Comedy Award. Life is a marathon, not a sprint. But it is a sort of marathon that you really have to sprint. ‘A national treasure’ (Irish Times).

Title: The Drowsy Chaperone

Title: Dispatch
Description: Forget slapping a label on Dispatch. You're welcome to give it a shot - people have - calling them at times a heartfelt acoustic trio, a wailing rock band, a devil-may-care funk act, but the band defies epithets at every turn.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier Live music & Club venue now into it’s 15 year.

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: SIMONE FELICE & T M WOLF
Description:
A special collaboration of literature and music. Simone Felice appeared in the first Unbound in 2010; since then his reputation as a solo artist has continued to grow. Once of The Felice Brothers and The Duke & the King, his last, eponymously titled, album received huge critical acclaim. In addition, 2011 saw the publication of his debut novel, Black Jesus, the story of a young American soldier trying to find meaning on his return from the Iraq War. TM Wolf has published his debut novel Sound; built on musical notation and modeled after hip-hop beats, it is an innovative first novel set on the New Jersey Shore telling the story of a young man who returns to his hometown only to find that home is not what he remembers it to be.

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Title: The Sorries
Description: Inspired by a love of the Corries, the kilted duo return with selections from the Scottish songbook. www.thesorries.co.uk. 'Lovely hour's entertainment ... heart-warming ... genuinely funny' (FringeReport.com). 'Anyone would struggle not to have a good time ... authentically Scottish, 4/5 (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Just off the Lawnmarket our friendly venue is centrally placed on the terrace above Victoria Street . We provide a 65 seating rake and a black box theatre, our own box office and reception area. Our venue profits go to charity.

Title: Neil Forsyth
Subtitle: BOB SERVANT IS BACK
Description: At last year's Book Festival, Broughty Ferry's fictional hero Bob Servant was brought to life by Greg McHugh (aka Gary Tank Commander) in a sell-out performance. Since then, filming has begun to turn Neil Forsyth's comedy creation into a BBC TV series and there’s a new book. In tonight's event, leading Scottish actors perform scenes from the book, and Forsyth talks about his life as a writer.

Title: Soaring Leap: Eric Whitacre
Description: Scotland's most exciting chamber choir Coroedina present an exciting programme of the music of sublime contemporary American composer Eric Whitacre. An a capella performance in the rich acoustic of Edinburgh’s St Giles' Cathedral.
Venue description: Founded in the 1120s, St Giles' was the church of John Knox during the Reformation and is renowned for its stained glass, Rieger organ and beautiful Thistle Chapel. Open daily. Free guided tours, concerts, Cathedral shop and restaurant. Donations welcome.

Title: Eoin Colfer
Description: A new Artemis Fowl is a much-anticipated event but when it’s the last ever… Eoin Colfer introduces his final thrilling instalment, Artemis Fowl and the Last Guardian, featuring a magical portal, fairies and rampaging dead soldiers. Thankfully, Eoin has stated that he will keep writing until people stop reading or he runs out of ideas. As neither is likely, the final Artemis adventure doesn’t spell the end for his fans, there will be plenty more from Eoin Colfer to look forward to in the future!

Title: Platero Y Yo
Description: Platero Y Yo, an adaptation of a Juan Ramon Jimenez book, is an allegoric journey through life through the eyes of Platero and his master that explores the possibilities of movement, voice and stagecraft.

Title: Giacinto Palmieri: Pagliaccio
Description: Giacinto Palmieri came to Edinburgh, felt the pains of unrequited love, but had to make people laugh ... like in the opera Pagliacci! Jokes on Berlusconi are available upon request. ‘Giacinto has charm as Tuscany has wine’ (Scotsman).
Artist: Giacinto Palmieri / Laughing Horse Free Festival

Title: Fable of the Fish
Description: A heartfelt portrait of a disintegrating marriage, a sweeping view of shanty-town life in the Philippines, but Adolfo Alix Jnr’s film will surely be remembered as “that film about a woman who gives birth to a fish.” Astonishingly, Alix treats his absurd central conceit with complete seriousness, which doesn’t prevent some humour inevitably manifesting, but the prevailing tone is tragic and deeply sympathetic.

Title: Captain Ferguson's School for Balloon Warfare
Description: Enlist with the Captain! WWI changed everything and Thomas Ferguson got carried away by it. Find out what it takes to spy on the Kaiser at 1,500 metres. Sound crazy? It is.

The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Music of Two Nations
Description: Eddie McGuire and Dong Yi give a presentation with bamboo flutes, classical flutes and Chinese zheng (zither) of music of two nations in comparative perspective. Part of the Glamour of Jasmine Chinese Arts Festival.

Title: Dr Book
Description: Going to the doctor can be a ball and to prove it, here’s Dr Book. This is how it works: you tell us what you like, Dr Book takes a moment to think about it, then writes a prescription for some wonderful and inspiring new books for you to read. A simple medical procedure for all – from babies to teens (and parents), courtesy of Edinburgh City Libraries.

Title: Laughing Horse Free Comedy Selection
Description: A selection of the best in new comedy at the Fringe, alongside some top headliners picked from Fringe shows, national competitions and around the world. And it's free! Three times a night! Line-ups - www.freefestival.co.uk.

Title: Lingua Frank - CANCELLED
Description: In an Edinburgh language school a Scottish fanatic paints nude pictures of Alex Salmond. Meanwhile English teacher Lingua Frank is tackling love, language, lies and spies. This comedy explores culture clashes and questions national identities and Scottish independence.
Warnings: Some adult themes, bad language and some suggestive art work.

Title: Nothing But The Poem
Subtitle: Poetry of War
Description: Reignite your love of poetry with an in-depth approach to reading with our friends from the Scottish Poetry Library. War and conflict have produced some of the most powerful and emotive poetry. In this discussion, explore further why poetry resonates in such times. No background knowledge is required and poems will be provided. Today’s event is led by Lilias Fraser.

Title: Foodies Festival
Description: Foodies Festival moves to Inverleith Park this year, opposite the Botanical Gardens, bringing you the best in fine food and drink. Sample tasty treats from artisan producers and watch Michelin-starred chefs cook live. A fabulous, fun day out.

Title: Josh Richards: Keith Looks Back in Anger - Free
Description: Ever watched a man-sized ginger koala scream about making napalm, playing ukulele? Meet Keith the Anger Management Koala. ‘Keith gave me chlamydia, but his double-koala-willy was worth it’ (Innocent Bystander). www.themightyginge.com.

Title: Be My Baby
Description: Follow the fortunes of Mary, 19 and pregnant. Sent to a mother and baby home, she has to cope with the shame of her pregnancy and the dawning realisation she must give up her baby for adoption.

Title: The Pajama Men's Improv Show
Description: The Pajama Men do a completely improvised set in their street clothes. Seeing them raw and unscripted like this is like seeing a snow leopard mate with an eagle.

Join Margaret Ryan as she introduces Roodica and a cast of her other book characters. There will be stories, activities and lots of fun.

Title: Metropolitan Cathedral Latin Choral Vespers
Description: The traditional evening service, with plainsong and choral polyphony, exquisite renaissance and baroque settings, as well as a rare full liturgical performance of Dupré's Vêpres de la Vierge (11th August). Full music lists: www.stmaryscathedral.co.uk.

Title: Blues and Burlesque
Description: ***** ‘Clever, funny, charming, friendly, elegant, sexy ... an outstanding evening delivered with charm, wit and polish’ (RemoteGoat.co.uk). 'Funny and enigmatic' (Daily Mirror). Rare chance to see this dangerously fun-packed West-End cabaret show in Edinburgh.

Title: Opinions Are Free
Description: A completely different show every night. Three random topics discussed, let the speakeasy begin. Amazing shows in 2010. Previous shows included kidnapping, marriage break-up, Angry Birds live. All genuine and hilarious, anything could happen! Also free!
Artist: Jay Sodagar A & J Productions Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)

Paul Cookson is poet in residence at the National Football Museum and his latest book, Give Us a Goal, is a collection of funny and honest poems about football – playing it, supporting it, living it, breathing it. Beware! Low Flying Rabbits by Roger Stevens also has football inspired verse along with poems about everything from rabbits to friends, sunshine to love. And with Stonemouth, he is firmly on his finest and funniest comedy-drama behaviour as he explores one Stewart Gilmour’s return to his north-east home town to attend a funeral after 5 years in exile. Not everyone is happy he’s back though and he spends a long weekend trying to keep one step ahead of local gangsters.

Description: A five-star dance festival-within-a-festival! Enticing, groundbreaking, exhilarating dance performed by awe-inspiring companies from the USA. From rapid-fire tap to innovative, multi-media choreography. Be moved! Bite-sized festival format. ‘Perfect for the Fringe lover!’ (ThreeWeeks). www.bookingdance.com.
Artist: Seven Dance Companies from the USA
Venue description: Venue150 @ EICC just gets better and better! This year, take in some big names, world-class comedy, internationally renowned dance and jaw-dropping acts from across the globe. All in the capital's comfiest venue! www.venue150.com

Title: Alex Scarrow & Simon Scarrow
Description: Be whisked away on a whirlwind tour of ancient Rome with Alex and Simon Scarrow. Alex’s Gates of Rome is the fifth book in his hugely popular time travel adventure series TimeRiders, in which his heroes grapple with an alternative timeline. Meanwhile, brother Simon’s second book in his Gladiator series, Street Fighter, follows young Marcus, sold into slavery and forced to become a Gladiator. Come and experience the sights, smells, blood and violence of ancient Rome.

Title: One Thousand Points of Light
Description: Dutch artist Melvin Moti has been invited by National Museums Scotland to make new work in response to the National Collection. Part of the Year of Creative Scotland and Edinburgh Art Festival.
Venue description: All our collections have tales to tell. The redeveloped Museum is fully open following a £50m transformation. Discover the wonders of life, the universe and everything in it – from science and art to nature and outer space.

Title: Thomas Heatherwick
Subtitle: THE SHAPE OF 21ST CENTURY BRITAIN
Description: From his 'dandelion clock' UK pavilion at Shanghai Expo to a bold new shape for double-decker buses, Thomas Heatherwick's creations have established him as British design's boldest superstar. Yet Heatherwick is no stranger to controversy. He joins us to unveil a new book and explain how he fights for the life of his shapely designs, in conversation with the director of the Victoria and Albert Museum, Martin Roth.

Title: Keira Daley: LadyNerd
Description: Indulge your inner (or not-so-inner) nerd with this award-winning hit - a rollicking, fact-packed cabaret tribute to some of history's greatest minds, from Marie Curie to that woman who invented Liquid Paper.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
