Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Tetsuo II: Body Hammer
Description: The first sequel to Tsukamoto’s Tetsuo, The Iron Man, this film is considered by many fans to be superior to the original. Reinterpreting the premise of the first film within a more straightforward action-thriller context, Tsukamoto here depicts a conspiracy of a gang of cyborgs. Their target is a seemingly ordinary salaryman who, in reality, is himself a fusion of man and metal. Newly restored from the original negative by the director himself, who will be in attendance at EIFF.

Title: Simon Munnery's La Concepta
Description: All the rigmarole of haute cuisine without the shame of eating. An exclusive non-dining restaurant experience. Chortle Innovation Award winner. 'The fringiest Fringe experience of 2011' (Guardian). Seen on BBC2's The Culture Show. 'Delicious' **** (Independent).
Venue description: Whitespace is a central venue at the top of Leith Walk with many restaurants and bars close by. An intimate space with good acoustics that stays cool in hot weather with good ventilation and good access from the street.
Venue accessibility: \n

Title: Roald Dahl Funny Prize Event
Description: ‘Laughter is the sun that drives winter from the human face.’ So said Victor Hugo (and he should know). Come and bask in the warm glow of 2011 Funny Prize winner, Liz Pichon for The Brilliant World of Tom Gates and shortlisted author, Rose Impey for The Get Rich Quick Club as they discuss all things humorous, amusing and how comedy is the hardest thing to write. Order will be kept by the irrepressible Philip Ardagh, previous winner and judge (although not the same year as that would have been wrong).

Title: PassionFlower
Description: Seductive songs of the New Torch delivered with a 'voice to fry green tomatoes' (Western Australian). From Radiohead to Waits and Piaf to original Sanderson, they explore the dark and the light of love. **** (ThreeWeeks). www.beccsanderson.com.
Venue description: Edinburgh's all-year-round multi-arts venue. We offer a gourmet selection of theatre, cabaret, live music, visual arts and clubbing. Our cafe adds delicious homemade food, free internet and great coffee to the mix. All brought to you by the friendliest staff in town.

Title: Mary Coughlan
Description: One of Ireland’s most distinctive voices since overnight success in 1984. Singing songs of joy, sadness, mischief and melancholy. Songs by Billie Holiday, Bessie Smith and Peggy Lee, her voice effortlessly straddling jazz, blues, chanson and pop. www.marycoughlanmusic.com.
Venue description: Edinburgh's leading live music venue offers classical, jazz, blues, pop, rock, world, folk and comedy in the intimate surroundings of a converted Georgian church. www.thequeenshall.net

Title: Assembly Gala Press Launch
Description: Join us as we celebrate our 32nd year and rocket into another season of the Fringe's best shows. The gala launch lets you take a sneak peek at the selection of shows from our 2012 programme.

Title: Benny Boot Def-Con 4
Description: Considered to be one of the best joke writers of his generation Boot delivers the perfect combination of one-liners, observations and non sequitur statements. 'Brilliant gags' (Guardian). ‘Charming, disarming and proper f*cking funny’ (Tim Minchin).

Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Christopher de Bellaigue
Subtitle: IRAN, OIL AND A VERY BRITISH COUP
Description: A timely book by the Economist's former Iran correspondent Christopher de Bellaigue looks at a key event in Iran's recent history. In 1953, after the Iranian Prime Minister nationalised the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company, Britain and the USA engineered a coup to protect British imperial power. In the process, an enlightened government was replaced by a dictatorial Shah. De Bellaigue is an Iran scholar who offers a fascinating new perspective.

Code: Sodankylä Forever: The Century of Cinema
Title: Sodankylä Forever: The Century of Cinema
Description: The Midnight Sun Film Festival in Sodankylä, Finland, is a mecca for film lovers, famous for festival director Peter von Bagh’s in-depth and free-flowing interviews with visiting master directors. From the hundreds of hours of video recordings, von Bagh has made four feature-length documentaries that add up to a passionate and personal history of cinema. The first part, The Century of Cinema, focusses on World War II in relation to filmmaking. Screening with A Day at Karl Marx’s Grave (Peter von Bagh/Finland/1983/16 min). See www.filmhousecinema.com for details.

Title: Aaron Twitchen's Quarter Life Crisis
Description: Ever felt crazier than Mel Gibson in a synagogue? You may have had a Quarter Life Crisis! More than just interactive stand-up, help Aaron tackle his issues and diagnose yours.

Title: Bookbug
Description: Sing along with traditional nursery songs and action rhymes. The event is hosted by Edinburgh City Libraries and is part of the Scottish Book Trust’s Early Years programme.

Title: Helen Dunmore
Description: When the worlds of Air and Mer meet, the consequences can be terrible. Orange prize-winning author Helen Dunmore explains all, as she talks about Stormswept the next book in her hugely popular Ingo series. Set on the Cornish coast, the books beautifully evoke the wildness, mystery and mythology of the area.

Title: Masha Gessen
Subtitle: BURSTING PUTIN'S BUBBLE
Description: It took less than a decade for Vladimir Putin to rise from KGB apparatchik to master of the Kremlin. Now Masha Gessen, who emigrated at 14, is back in Moscow and has produced a brave book suggesting that Putin is a crook – guilty of promoting a petty, pilfering and poisonous regime. She talks to James Meek, who reported for the Guardian from the USSR in the 1990s.

Title: End of the World Show 2012
Description: How will the end of the world affect you? Is it nigh? Which religion gives you the best and most convenient experience? Join nice Mr Death for this engaging and insightful comedy exposition. www.endoftheworldshow.com.

Description: Who did it? Where were they? What was the murder weapon? Back at the Fringe following a sell-out run last year, this is an original musical based on the popular board game.

Title: Metropolitan Cathedral Organ Concerts
Description: The Cathedral's organ has nearly 4000 pipes, up to 32 feet long. See and hear it in two solo concerts, plus trumpet and organ on 18th August. Full programmes at www.stmaryscathedral.co.uk.
Artist: Duncan Ferguson / Michael Harris / Calum Robertson and Tom Poulson
Venue description: St Mary's is ideally placed in the city centre, with its stunning new pipe organ, concerts Mon-Sat and the traditional service of Choral Vespers during the Fringe. The neighbouring Cafe Camino is the perfect place for refreshment and relaxation.

Title: Laughing Horse Free Pick of the Fringe

Title: Dear Dan Brown...

Title: Mike Sheer in Undergod - Free
Description: Afternoon stand-up comedy from Mike Sheer. Jokes and rants about death, God, genitals etc. with an experienced, beloved compère and act from Toronto. ‘Has the crowd in stitches’ **** (Adelaide Advertiser). www.mikesheer.com.
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.

Title: Steven Davidson: Gamesmaster
Description: Stand-up comedy and gameshow clash like two drunken tigers, with joyous laughter and prizes on offer that have cost more than a pound. 'Uproarious laughter and applause' (Edinburgh Evening News). 'Utter absurdity provokes many laughs' (EdinburghGuide.com).

Artist: AKHE - Russian Engineering Theatre / Russian Season 2012

The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Photographing the Dead
Description: A city in ruins. A man in mourning. A woman, waiting for a train. A haunting and evocative journey through memory, recalling the chance encounter that will forever change a life.

Title: William Fotheringham
Subtitle: A CYCLING LEGEND EXAMINED
Description: Eddy Merckx is to cycling what Ali (or Tyson) was to boxing and Pelé (or Messi) is to football: quite simply, the best there has ever been. Throughout his professional career the Belgian amassed an astonishing 445 victories which puts Lance Armstrong’s tally of less than 100 into perspective. Sports journalist William Fotheringham talks to the Guardian’s Literary Editor, Claire Armitstead about a story which covers horrific injury, a doping controversy and tragedy.

Title: BBC: Loose Ends
Description: Clive Anderson ties up the Loose Ends with cool music, lots of comedy and, of course, scintillating conversation. Recorded for BBC Radio 4.
Venue address: Corner of Potterrow and Marshall Street,Edinburgh
Venue description: Experience the best of the BBC under one roof and a taster of all the delights of the Fringe. Join us at Venue 25 for BBC shows, big names, stand-up every night plus masterclasses from BBC Radio, TV and Online. Free events are ticketed via a random draw. To enter the draw please use the show website link: bbc.co.uk/tickets.

Title: Ceilidh Club @ The HMV Picture House
Description: Modern Scottish ceilidh dancing with the very best ceilidh bands. Open to everyone to come and get involved in 21st century Scottish culture at its best, fiddles, accordions, drums, dancers and more.
Venue description:
The HMV Picture House is Edinburgh's best venue in which to experience live music and clubs. 
\nThe lovingly restored Caledonian cinema on Lothian Road - you may remember it as the Caley Palais - is perfect for performers and audience alike.

Title: All the King's Men present...
Description: Voice Festival UK 2012 champions, All the King's Men, present an evening of stunning singing with the very best of the collegiate a cappella scene. Don't miss this regal performance fit for a king! www.all-the-kings-men.com/fringe2012.

Title: D'You Hear About Todd?
Description: A talk on modern death: the etiquette of how did it happen? The death-o-meter reading - tragic or just sad? Last wishes, pimping your own funeral, silent tributes, public outpourings, juicy obituaries, and Todd. 'Brilliant' (Scotsman).
Artist: Will Pickvance and Jonny Hartley / PBH's Free Fringe

Title: Learning to Pray in Front of the Television
Description: The hilarious true story of one man’s journey from comedian to priest, while somehow not losing his sense of humour along the way.

Description:

Susan Sontag said: ‘if China has one possibility of a Nobel laureate, it is Can Xue’, and the avant-garde novelist joins us with Hungarian novelist László Krasznahorkai and Daniel Medin, editor of the Quarterly Conversation, who has written a book on the influence the Prague-born author had on Coetzee, Roth and Sebald.

Code: Andy Manley, Rob Evans and macrobert (SCOTLAND)
Title: Andy Manley, Rob Evans and macrobert (SCOTLAND)
Description:
A fast-paced, funny and emotional tale which looks at the difficulties of growing up.

It's hard to tell when your life will change. 
Hard to spot that moment, that day where you wake up normal, but end up falling far from everything you've ever known. Spinning into nothingness. Today is that day.

Mikey is 10. A sunny boy. He lives alone with his mum. Mikey's mum has a secret. It is not well kept. Everyone knows it. Everyone except for Mikey.

Addie is a good girl. She doesn't tell lies. Her father makes sure of that. Addie tells the truth. It's what you have to do. Isn't it?

Mikey and Addie is a visual piece of storytelling that asks how do you work out who you are when everything around you is changing.                                         Supported through the Scottish Governement's Edinburgh Festivals Expo Fund.                                               Mikey and Addie is commissioned by the London 2012 Festival.

Description: 'Specialising in classic soul with a very "now" attitude...' (Tonedeaf.com.au). Taking cues from the likes of James and Aretha and New York’s bangin’ modern soul scene, this nine-piece band take audiences from the depths of heartache to overwhelming joy.
Venue description: The Famous Spiegeltent. The original, beloved, iconic festival venue returns to the faithful! The grandest dame of all is back in town, out of the gardens and onto George Street: sexy, funny, dangerous – a living legend!
Venue accessibility:
2459
\nWheelchair access, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC.

Title: Mitchell Symons
Description: Amaze your friends, fascinate your family and frighten your granny with another collection of wise and wacky words of advice from the slightly disturbing mind of Mitchell Symons. Come and hear all about Don’t Wipe Your Bum with a Hedgehog (sound advice) and learn why you can't trust a dog to watch your food or why not to buy shampoo when real poo is free (don’t say you weren’t warned).

Title: Speak Easy with Kristen and Kurt
Description: Avalon Television and BBC Three present a work-in-progress chat show hosted by Kristen Schaal (Flight of the Conchords / 30 Rock) and Kurt Braunohler  in conversation special guests. Music by The Horne Section.
Artist: Kristen Schaal, Kurt Braunoler, Horne Section
Venue description: The Jam House is a live music venue, conceived by Jools Holland. It offers live performances, fine food and has a vibrant atmosphere. A broad range of musical styles is available for all age groups. We are situated on Queen Street, and have a beautiful venue which includes our historical Chapel Bar.

Title: Careers in Arts Journalism
Description: Theatre journalist Mark Shenton hosts this session on making a career out of writing about the theatre for print, online and broadcast media. Join us for an insight in how to build your career as an Arts journalist.
Artist: The Stage Events with Mark Shenton
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: CeilidhKids at the Fringe - Free
Description: Scottish dancing for all the family. Very simple child-friendly dances to traditional Scottish music. Hugely popular with local families, now it's your turn. Bring Mum or Dad along to partner you!
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.

Title: The Browning Version
Description: HOGHEAD are an innovative theatre company who bring a fresh and dynamic approach to Rattigan's classic text through bold directorial interpretation. Watch as Andrew Crocker-Harris attempts a final stand against those who would see him humiliated.
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Elsa Jean McTaggart
Description: ‘A beautiful voice and highly accomplished fiddling ... lovely show’ ***** (One4Review.wordpress.com, 2011). 'A mean fiddler, all round folk musician with a voice to match her looks, McTaggart gives a sweet and upbeat autobiographical set' **** (ThreeWeeks, 2011). www.mctaggart.info.
Venue description: Vibrant Cabaret bar located on the Royal Mile. A global feast of song, music, cabaret, comedy, dance and theatre. Free entry after midnight. Open til 3am daily See: www.thespaceuk.com for more info.

Title: Harry Baker: Proper Pop-up Purple Paper People
Description: Current UK Poetry Slam Champion is back with poems, puns and pole-dancing, German raps and gangsta maths, even representing his country in the Poetry World Cup. 'Fringe at its best' ***** (WhatsOnStage.com, 2011).
Venue description: The Royal Oak is Edinburgh's premiere traditional music and folksinging howff. Rub shoulders with the top names in folk music, join in or just sit and listen; sample a cask ale or a fine malt and enjoy the convivial atmosphere.

Title: Paul Ricketts - Ironic Infinity
Description: Funny isn't enough? Okay, try this hilarious stand-up show instead. 'Material is smart as well as funny. I don't think that even Simon Munnery has toyed with the concept of Ironic Infinity' (Scotsman).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Martin Palmer & Jean Sprackland
Subtitle: REVEALING THE SECRETS OF THE LAND
Description: Jean Sprackland’s Strands is the lyrical account of a year on one beach turning up a mermaid’s purse, lugworms, sea potatoes, messages in bottles and beached whales. Martin Palmer’s Sacred Land is an informative and enlightening travelogue revealing clues to the spiritual significance of the sites and features he visits. At the end of this event you’ll see your surroundings in a brand new light.

Title: The Silencer - David Calvitto
Description: Be careful who you fall in love with. Be more careful who falls in love with you. Acclaimed director Michael Sexton (Public Theater, NYTW) directs Fringe First winner Calvitto in a twisted, darkly comic, boy-loses-girl tale.
Artist: Leo Lauer, Richard Jordan Productions and Broken Watch Theatre Company
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Caroline McCracken-Flesher
Subtitle: BUT AN' BEN WI' BURKE AND HARE
Description: The story of the notorious Edinburgh murderers Burke and Hare two centuries ago has provided fodder for literature and theatre ever since. Caroline McCracken-Flesher's captivating study asks why the case has continued to resonate with writers from Walter Scott (who refused publicly to comment on the scandal) and Robert Louis Stevenson, to Alasdair Gray and Ian Rankin today.

Title: Nuclear Nation
Description: After the 11 March 2011 tsunami and nuclear disaster, residents of Futaba, a town in Fukushima Prefecture, are relocated to an abandoned high school in a suburb of Tokyo, 150 miles south. With  a clear and compassionate eye, filmmaker Atsushi Funahashi follows the displaced people as they struggle to adapt to their new environment. Among the vivid personalities who emerge are the town mayor, a Moses without a Promised Land; and a farmer who would rather defy the government than abandon his cows to certain starvation.

Title: 5-Step Guide to Being German 2.0 - Free
Description: Funnier than ever, the German comedian's hit show returns after its world tour. Hilariously honest. You will laugh. If you want. Zis is not an order. ***** ‘Genius’ (EdinburghGuide.com). ***** ‘Hysterical’ (BroadwayBaby.com).
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.

Title: Best of Scottish Comedian of the Year
Description: Multi award-winning Scottish comedy. A selection of Scotland's best. 'Hilarious' Alan Anderson (Chortle.co.uk) introduces previous SCOTY? winners and finalists. 'Genuinely prestigious affair... with a genuine sense of occasion' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Major talent' (Skinny).
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Permits and Prejudice
Description: Street performers contend with a growing number of restrictions. Coping with regional rules, regulatory systems, permits and public prejudice, from bad weather to bad attitudes - this dialogue explores positive ways forward in an increasingly privatised urban environment.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: It's Grimm Up North
Description: Unique ... a Fringe first ... animated comedy. Once upon a time there were only stand-ups and sketch shows... but now we present cartoon humour and parody, inspired by fairytales and films. You’ll laugh happily ever after.
Venue description: the SpaceUK present another high calibre venue. This wonderfully-located space between Bristo Square and the Pleasance offers a high brow alternative to the traditional fringe venues. Ideal for Stand-Up, Chat, Music (bands), A Capella, Improv, Sketch and Cabaret.

Title: How Much is Your Iron? and Dansen
Description: Brecht's lost play. It's Europe, 1936. Dansen and Svenson enjoy a respectable life selling their pigs and iron, trading with the neighbours. As friends get murdered one by one, they wonder who will be next...
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Google / Complex
Description: Phil Cooper can't get to grips with Google, and Geraint Evans has a complex. Two up-and-coming stand-ups team up to bring an hour of quality surrealist, self-deprecating comedy. 'Fun, and very funny' (Evening Post).
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: The Six O'Clock News
Description: Whatever the headlines on 7th August, Daniel Bye and team will digest and respond to the big issues of the day in an urgently topical, one-off performance. They promise they do not have a time machine.
Warnings: Potential strong language and adult themes
Venue description: Northern Stage at St Stephen’s is a creative home for the most exciting and unusual theatre made in the Greater North of England. Original stories, new performances and spirited special events that will delight, provoke and entertain you.

Title: Parker Bilal & Zoë Ferraris *Zoë Ferraris has cancelled*
Subtitle: CRIME NOVELS SET IN CAIRO AND JEDDAH
Description:
The 2011 revolution in Egypt is placed in fascinating context by Parker Bilal's brilliant fictional detective story The Golden Scales, in which a reluctant cop is asked to explore an unusual kidnapping. Meanwhile Zöe Ferraris' novel Kingdom of Strangers is set in Saudi Arabia, where an inspector on the hunt for a serial killer gets embroiled in an abduction much closer to home. Please note: Zoë Ferraris will no longer appear in this event and it will go ahead with Parker Bilal.

	Please note: Zoe Ferraris is no longer able to appear in this event and it will go ahead with Parker Bilal.

Title: Swordy-Well
Description: Compassionate abattoir Swordy-Well’s proprietor and philosopher Joseph Orty struggles wretchedly to maintain the balance between mankind and cowkind. But when a superpower hypermarket offers his employees a chance to triple their cattle kills the pat hits the fan. www.humblecrumbletheatre.com.
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: John McCarthy
Subtitle: HOW CAN WE LIVE WITHOUT A PLACE OF SAFETY?
Description: After the Israeli Declaration of Independence in 1948, 700,000 Palestinians fled to other countries. But some dared to remain in Israel. In his new book, You Can't Hide the Sun, journalist John McCarthy recounts his meetings with Palestinians who still think of Israel as their home. McCarthy, who himself lived under threat as a hostage in Lebanon, reveals the continuing tragedy of this lesser-known facet of the Palestinian struggle.

Title: Ross Collins
Description: Ross Collins is a successful illustrator of his own stories as well as the illustrator for the work of other leading authors. Join him as he talks about his latest picture books including When I Woke Up I Was a Hippopotamus and Doodleday. There will be stories, drawing and lots of guaranteed fun.

Title: Skerryvore
Description: STMA Live Act of the Year 2011 Skerryvore bring their unique sound to the Fringe. Their 2012 performances will showcase their progression from their traditional roots to the eclectic sounds of their recently released World of Chances album.
Venue description: Edinburgh's leading live music venue offers classical, jazz, blues, pop, rock, world, folk and comedy in the intimate surroundings of a converted Georgian church. www.thequeenshall.net

Title: The Society of Ethical Cat Burglars
Description: Three respectable professionals decide to spice up their evenings with a spot of breaking and entering and get more than they bargained for. Thought-provoking comedy from Edinburgh-based Foolproof Theatre. www.foolproofcreativearts.com.
Venue description: Managed by theSpaceUK, this intimate space hosts an array of new and established theatre. Located seconds from the Royal Mile with bar and cafe facilities. For show information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Michael Legge: What a Shame
Description: Can you imagine being caught by your mum with your trousers down kissing a statue of Kim Jong Il made out of ladies’ underwear you stole from Poundland? Then come to this show. Thanks. www.facebook.com/michael.legge.
Warnings: 14+. Must be accompanied by an adult
Artist: Michael Legge / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Round the corner, our little sister club is in its thirteenth year. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Celestial Banquet
Description: This Cumbrian chamber choir has been thrilling audiences with its rich sound, committed performances and daring, imaginative programming. Director Mark Hindley is best-known in Scotland for his work as chorus master of the Scottish Chamber Orchestra. www.wordsworthsingers.org.uk.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Razing Eddie
Description: Eddie's a bad lad. He wants to be good. Can he change his destiny and find true love? Award-winning Horizon Arts (Heroin(e) for Breakfast) present an explosive and heart-breaking drama, exploring casual violence, family feuds and restless ghosts.
Artist: Horizon Arts with Richard Jordan Productions Ltd
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Doug Allan
Subtitle: BRUSHES WITH POLAR BEARS
Description: The cameraman behind the lens of some of the BBC’s finest wildlife documentaries has produced an astonishing book about his experiences in the Arctic and Antarctica. Doug Allan has been described by David Attenborough as ‘the toughest in the business’ and he has had plenty of close encounters, including a polar bear at the door of his tent. Today he talks to Conor Woodman, an international bestselling author, TV presenter and adventurer himself, to recount his experiences and present his breathtaking photographs.

Title: Ship of Fools: Children of Twelchford
Description: Straight from the imaginary streets of Twelchford comes a show featuring squid, Shakespearean job centres, speed-dating hoovers and snotty hotties. Sea state: moderate to sexy. Come and see us do a thing why not.
Artist: Ship of Fools / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description:
Bannermans is one of Edinburgh's premier live music venues, located in the heart of the historic Old Town. With live music six nights a week, and a host of other events constantly on the go, it's proved a firm favourite with locals and tourists for many years now.
\nOpen 12pm till 1am every day, apart from Sunday when we open at 12.30pm.

Title: Liam Grahame Olsen: Half Pint - Live
Description: A mix of observational stand-up comedy and acoustic comedy music, Liam Grahame Olsen brings his cheeky chappy comedy to his first Edinburgh Fringe in 2012.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Hangman
Description: The legendary Russian Do-Theatre returns with the must see Fringe First Winner from 2007. It's a game and the personage in one, a dance macabre of crime and punishment where the roles of victim and executioner are constantly swapped.
Venue description: The Roxy, a beautifully converted former chapel, is the latest addition to Assembly's growing list of venues.  Built in 1809 and located just north-east of our George Square hub, the Roxy houses three performances spaces; the 400 seat former nave Roxy Central, the 168 seat Roxy Upstairs and our 60 seat studio Roxy Downstairs.  The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: As Ye Sow
Description: As an old man's mind fragments, a fear he thought long buried drags itself from the earth. Hitchcockian psychodrama meets the supernatural tradition of MR James in a terrifying modern haunting from the masters of theatrical horror.
Artist: Theatre of the Damned and Bare Bawds Theatre
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Kemble's Riot
Description: Winner, Best Theatre, Brighton Festival 2011. Ever been to a riot? In a theatre? Re-live 1809’s audience rebellion. 'We stamped, we bellowed, we sang. It's marvellously liberating. Masterful' ***** (FringeGuru.com). 'A massive slice of fun' ***** (Latest7). www.kemblesriot.com.
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Michael Downey - Standing Up Again
Description: Michael Downey took an odd route to get here. Comedy Award Finalist alongside Alan Carr and John Bishop. Then a car crash, hospital and the supermarket. He is back, but he took the bus.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Strawberry Sauce
Description: Languishing in a police cell for murder by plastic gun, Joe McBride awaits a trial in which the 'victim' will stand witness. With morals lost in farcical black comedy, the audience decide whether Joe lives or dies. www.freshbloodtheatre.com.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: David O'Doherty Presents 403 Second Masterworks
Description: David introduces very short presentations delivered by top comedy talent on specialised subjects they have chosen. Each one may be informative. It may be eye opening. It will definitely be over after 403 seconds.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Sexytime!
Description: A very physical comedy exploring what it means to be sexy. Hosts Woman and Man 'will have the audience in fits’ (Chortle.co.uk) as they combine characters, dance, clown and outrageous costumes. 'Funny as Hell' ****1/2 (Age).
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Lost in the 80s
Description: Witty, jazzed-up renditions of classic 80s hits. Michael Jackson, Bon Jovi, George Michael, AC/DC, Culture Club and more get a gypsy swing makeover from this platinum-selling Canadian trio. Awe-inspiring musicianship delivered with thoroughly charming humour.
Venue description: The Famous Spiegeltent. The original, beloved, iconic festival venue returns to the faithful! The grandest dame of all is back in town, out of the gardens and onto George Street: sexy, funny, dangerous – a living legend!
Venue accessibility:
2459
\nWheelchair access, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC.

Title: Luke Harding
Subtitle: FROM RUSSIA WITHOUT LOVE
Description: Is Putin’s Russia under the thumb of a despot with as much power as Stalin, or is it a chaotic state with corruption so rife that Putin has hardly any control at all? Luke Harding was foreign correspondent for the Guardian until 2011, and last year he was turned away at Domodedovo Airport, informed that his presence was no longer welcome. In his new book, Mafia State, Harding offers a fascinating perspective.

Title: Piaf - the Songs
Description: Eve Loiseau sings the songs of Edith Piaf, with Fiona Barrow (violin) and Edward Jay (accordion). Featured on Radio 3's In Tune. Credits include Kneehigh Theatre. 'World-class' (Gilbert Biberian). ‘Virtuoso musicianship’ **** (Venue). ‘Sublime’ (Daily Nation, Barbados).
Venue description: The Edinburgh Academy is centrally located in the New Town, with ample off-street parking and an on-site cafe for festival patrons. The venue is centered on its amazing oval Hall, built in 1824 and designed by William Burn.

Title: The Edinburgh International Circus Festival
Description: World-class circus artistes gather in Edinburgh to compete in a star-studded circus spectacular, to thrill family audiences. Aerialists, acrobats, illusionists and of course clowns, in a once in a lifetime circus extravaganza!
Venue description: State-of-the-art Big Top, central performance area, tiered seating and foyer. Parking available on site. A new and exciting venue on the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
29
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible.
\n
\n

Title: Karen McCombie
Description: Karen McCombie is the bestselling author of many fantastic series including Ally’s World and Indie Kidd. Her latest is You, Me and Thing following the adventures of Ruby and Jackson, who get the surprise of their lives when they discover a Thing at the bottom of the garden. It’s cute, it’s funny and it’s very, very mischievous which makes life awfully tricky! Delve into these delightful new stories and find out exactly what is a Thing.

Title: Icarus: a Story of Flight
Description: Incredible aerial circus and breathtaking feats tell the story of Icarus as never seen before, discovering what happens after the fall. Poetic, beautiful, visually spectacular. 'Such stuff as dreams are made on' ***** (EdinburghSpotlight.com). www.backhandtheatre.com.
Artist: Backhand Theatre with South Hill Park Arts Centre and C theatre
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Hitler's Li'l Abomination
Description: Her father is a Jewish Holocaust survivor. Her mother was in the Hitler Youth. What the devil is she...? An irreverent true story of one legacy of war. You are cordially invited to tea and swastikas...
Venue description: Managed by theSpaceUK, this intimate space hosts an array of new and established theatre. Located seconds from the Royal Mile with bar and cafe facilities. For show information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Tumble Circus: This Is What We Do For a Living
Description: Adelaide 2012 Best Circus winners’ Edinburgh debut. No fanfare or sequins, just extraordinary skill from two acrobats on a lifelong adventure. 'Very impressive' **** (Adelaide Advertiser). 'Ingenious' (Sunday Times, Australia).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Into the Fog
Description: A small community reunites once every millennium for a story. They don’t know what the story will be. They will illuminate the words on the page as best they know how.
Venue description: Venue 13 promotes new writing. Run by the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama in collaboration with the California Institute of the Arts, the 2012 season will feature the best new theatre from Wales and the United States.

Title: Cheese-Badger presents... Midge (a Two-Man Musical) - Free
Description: Cheese-Badger returns with the dark tale of orphaned 13-year-old Midge and his mad uncle Clive... Spaceships, explosions and ferocious bears, brought to life by a guitar, a balalaika, and two bespectacled men.
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, the Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11am-2am. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.

Title: Duncan Campbell-Smith
Subtitle: THE SOLID STAMP OF AUTHORITY
Description: Former financial journalist and all-round money man Duncan Campbell-Smith introduces us to the origins of the Post Office in Masters Of The Post: The Authorized History Of The Royal Mail. In charting an extraordinary story from the Tudors to today, he recounts a series of tales, including the Bletchley Park code-breakers, the Great Train Robbery and the influence of trade unionism during the 1970s.

Title: Mitch Benn: Reduced Circumstances
Description: The world is shrinking, the economy's shrinking and last year Mitch Benn, ‘The country's leading musical satirist’ (Times), shrank by 10 stone. So what will he (and we) do now? Music. Mirth. Morbid obesity.
Warnings: 14+ must be accompanied by an adult
Artist: Mitch Benn / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue: The Stand Comedy Club III & IV
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue, Stand III is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand IV an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: 50 Acts
Description: Wendy Houstoun launches a spirited one-woman retaliation against ageism and other modern rubbish. This intimate and affecting solo involves manifestos, apologies and errors, random acts, small dances and big ideas, ghostly appearances, serious stupidity and more.
Venue: Dance Base - National Centre for Dance
Venue description: Centrally located in the Old Town, Dance Base is a beautiful and inspiring setting for dance. We present performances by the best British and international dance companies and also offer classes and workshops from breakdance to ballet - for all ages.

Title: Quantum Battlestar Deep-Space Voyager Tardis Wars: The Million-Dollar Space Epic
Description: Join Starship Nebula's adventure beyond scientific integrity, plot plausibility and character continuity! With equal awesomeness to ridiculosity, this is the biggest reboot since Windows 95. Geeks get priority seating. www.twoshadesofblue.org.uk.
Venue description: Paradise Green brings you theatre at the heart of the Fringe, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, enjoy our coffee bar and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Emylia Hall & Karl Ove Knausgaard
Subtitle: FAMILY DRAMAS EXPOSED
Description: In Emylia Hall’s debut The Book of Summers, Beth Lowe receives a letter informing her that her long-estranged mother has died, and a memento-stuffed scrapbook. Her past then vividly and painfully tumbles back into the present. Karl Ove Knausgaard’s A Death in the Family is a Proustian exploration of his own past, in which the author creates a universal story of the struggles that we all face.

Title: Choral Celebration
Description: St Giles’ Choir, directed by Michael Harris, with Peter Backhouse, organ, in a concert including Handel's coronation anthems and music by Walton and Parry. Vibrant music and the spectacular Rieger organ fill the ancient splendour of St Giles’.
Venue description: Founded in the 1120s, St Giles' was the church of John Knox during the Reformation and is renowned for its stained glass, Rieger organ and beautiful Thistle Chapel. Open daily. Free guided tours, concerts, Cathedral shop and restaurant. Donations welcome.
Venue accessibility:
24
\nWheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.
\n
\n

Title: Rod is God
Description: Rod and Jack made a mistake. They created a cult to make some quick cash. They weren't expecting people to join. Now the cult’s getting too big for them. Everyone now really does believe Rod is God...
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Phill Jupitus is Porky the Poet in 27 Years On
Description: In 1985 Phill Jupitus left the white-hot cauldron of the civil service for life as a performance poet. He has finally managed to get an hour together. Just about. www.offthekerb.co.uk.
Artist: Off The Kerb Productions / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: The Jam House is a live music venue, conceived by Jools Holland. It offers live performances, fine food and has a vibrant atmosphere. A broad range of musical styles is available for all age groups. We are situated on Queen Street, and have a beautiful venue which includes our historical Chapel Bar.

Title: Mio Shapley
Description: Mio Shapley is a skillful storyteller who loves to tell stories which celebrate the wonder, mystery, wisdom and magic of the natural world in all its many colours and shapes, enriched by her playing of the clàrsach.

Title: Rose
Description: Hiding alone in her farmhouse, Rose (Agata Kulesza) is a widowed Polish Masurian, attempting to survive in the aftermath of brutal attacks by Soviet soldiers and subject to systematic abuse by desperate Polish locals.  Having returned her husband’s photograph and wedding ring, former soldier Tadeusz (Marcin Dorocinski) decides to stay and assist Rose in replanting her mine-infested potato field. Gradually a tender and fiercely loyal relationship develops between the two in this magnificently acted, captivating drama.

Sophie is joined by Dr Alistair Elfick, Director of the Centre for Biomedical Engineering at Edinburgh University and Dr David Kirby, Senior Lecturer in Science Communication at the University of Manchester, to explore why so often in fiction the creative scientist is portrayed as an evil genius.

Title: Virgin Money Fringe on the Royal Mile

Artist: Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society / Virgin Money Street Events
Venue: High Street, Cockburn Street to George IV Bridge
Venue description: The High Street is transformed into a huge performance space for all to enjoy. World-class street performers, buskers, an arts and craft market, the Fringe box office and millions of flyers make this the centre of the Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: JOURNALISTS ON THE FRONTLINE

Our series of events today focuses on the journalists who risk their lives to expose human rights violations in situations of war and conflict. Reading today: William Brodrick, Will Wiles, Donovan Hohn and Peter Stamm.

Title: Alexander McCall Smith
Subtitle: MEET ONE OF THE WORLD'S MOST POPULAR AUTHORS

In a joyful, rambunctious hour, McCall Smith introduces a cast of his loveable characters including Precious Ramotswe, Bertie and his mother Irene, and Edinburgh's own amateur sleuth, Isabel Dalhousie. Surprises await!

Title: Santa's Dead and We Have Killed Him

Title: Ghillie Gigs
Description: Get a taste of local Scottish talent with house bands playing live on the Ghillie Dhu stage! Enjoy a delicious two course dinner followed by traditional favourites, upbeat classics and a bit of rock and roll. www.ghillie-dhu.co.uk.
Venue description:
Ghillie Dhu is a traditional Scottish pub and live entertainment venue serving the finest local produce, ales and premium spirits as well as showcasing the best local, national and International acts.

\n
\nThe breathtaking auditorium is the perfect space for events and performances of all styles whilst the ambient main bar provides a platform for musicians.

Description: BBC Radio 1 DJ and award-winning stand-up comedian Tom Deacon (Rob Brydon Show, Dave's One Night Stand) returns to Edinburgh. Tom talks gap ‘yahs’ and stag dos, bank robbery and potentially causing Greece's economic crash (oops).
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Max Benitz & Sandy Gall with James Fergusson
Subtitle: AFGHANISTAN: IS THERE A SOLUTION?
Description: The veteran ITV newscaster Sandy Gall has been passionate about Afghanistan for many years. His new book on the current conflict oozes with wisdom and clear thinking. Also with first-hand experience is the journalist Max Benitz, who spent several months with the Scots Guards in Helmand. Gall and Benitz discuss their experiences with Edinburgh-based journalist James Fergusson, a leading voice on the Afghan people.

Title: Simon Donald’s School of Swearing
Description: Pass your 'coarse' with flying colourful language. An investigative journey to the four corners of the four-letter word. Featuring Celebrity Swears with all your favourite stars of film, television and the international drug trade! www.simondonald.com.

Title: Constant Craving - Free
Description: Are you satisfied? Do you want to be more than just another noodle in a big bowl of pasta? Join the club! ‘Insightful jagged barbs’ (List). ‘A surreal edge, terrific original ideas’ (Scotsgay). www.saraharcher.co.uk.

Title: Daniel Sloss - Extra Shows!
Description: Later and probably ruder shows from comedy’s half-man-half-Xbox star of Michael McIntyre’s Roadshow, 8/10 Cats and his own BBC show. ‘Meteoric’ (Scotsman). ‘Genuinely funny’ (Time Out). ‘Nothing short of hysterical … stunning!’ (Sunday Express). Sold-out 2008-2011!
Artist: MZA and Get Slossed Productions Ltd

Title: Men Are From Mars, Women Are From Venus
Description: Men and women live on different planets! Everyone’s been irritated by incomprehensible behaviour from the opposite sex. Why? The answer lies in this witty one-man show based on John Gray's best-selling book.
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Party Time

Title: London 2012 Festival Films
Description: London 2012 Festival, Film 4 and BBC Films co-commissioned four of the UK’s finest directors, Mike Leigh, Lynne Ramsey, Asif Kapadia, and Max Giwa and Dania Pasquini, to come up with short films to celebrate the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The films will be shown as part of the London 2012 Festival on cinema screens during the Olympic Summer, and subsequently broadcast on Channel Four and the BBC.

Title: Drama Workshops for 5 - 12s

Title: The Many Mishaps of Mr. Vinegar
Description: Ever had a day where everything goes wrong? Join the hilariously unlucky Mr. Vinegar on his fun-filled adventures, full of infectiously catchy songs and comical puppets. An enchanting re-working of a British folktale. www.2baap.co.uk.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: The Best of Irish Comedy
Description: Ireland’s finest under one roof. Excellent value celtic showcase featuring three top comics for the price of one. Fringe institution since 1999. ‘Wonderful line-up truly justifies show’s title’ (Evening News). Great craic, different line-up nightly. www.thestand.co.uk.

Title: Joe Simpson
Subtitle: STARING DEATH IN THE FACE
Description: The author of Touching the Void last joined us in 1997 to discuss his bestselling account of his extraordinary survival in the Andes. Now he brings us his gripping novel, The Sound of Gravity. Patrick and his wife are trapped on a stormbound mountain: he loses his grip on her hand and she falls... Patrick survives, but his life is shattered and he can't resist going back.

Title: The Rabbit and the Rose

Title: The History Girls Present: A Summary of Things So Far
Description: Best Show Award nominees at Dave's Leicester Comedy Festival 2012, The History Girls stick a wig on history and laugh at its bits. 'A sort of Bronté Python... ' (Chortle.co.uk).

Title: Joan Lingard

Join her to hear about her new novels, The Stolen Sister and What Holly Did.

Title: Rock N Roll Politics presented by Steve Richards
Description: Award-winning columnist and broadcaster, Steve Richards, takes you behind the scenes of politics, bringing characters and great dramas to life. Laugh, ask questions, take part in this topical show when politics is all shook up.

Title: Walk Like a Black Man
Description: We've all wanted to be black, haven't we? Rafiq is no exception - he's 50% black, 50% Indian and 100% confused! 'I recommend you see this' (OnTheFringePaper.co.uk). 'Brilliant' (FringeReview.co.uk).

Title: Chapiteau Show
Description: A prize winner at last year’s Moscow International Film Festival that went on to become a surprise hit in cinemas across Russia. At a Crimean resort, various characters cross paths with one another across an intricate multi-story narrative. Among them are a mismatched couple who meet on the Internet, a group of deaf people, an estranged father and son, and a young promoter trying to make a star of a lookalike of the late Russian rock legend Viktor Tsoi. An amazing film for its inventiveness and style.

Title: Mickey and Judy
Description: This hilarious musical memoir, chronicling Hughes’ childhood obsession with Judy Garland and his journey from psychiatric ward to off-Broadway, ‘will inspire you to be yourself and follow your dreams’ (Theatromania.ca). Best of Fringe! ***** (NOW Magazine). www.mickeyandjudy.ca.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: CHINA: ECONOMIC GROWTH AND HUMAN RIGHTS
Description: China continues to face domestic discontent about economic and social inequalities, corruption in the judicial system, police abuses and suppression of human rights. As we build our relationship with China we must take care not to trade away universal human rights for profit. Our daily series today features extracts from writers such as Ai Weiwei, the renowned artist and political activist. Reading today: Krys Lee, Kerry Hudson, Lisa O’Donnell and Benjamin Wood.

Title: Al Pitcher – Tiny Triumphs
Description: Now living in Sweden, the Kiwi returns. With awards from Australia, the UK and Sweden, this 'hysterical comedy force' (Time Out) and 'freewheeling genius' (Sydney Morning Herald) brings his tall tales of tiny triumphs.

How many people will suffer in order that the wife of the colonial boss can secure her seventh house back in France? Almost everyone, according to Atxaga in his powerful story.

Title: Lust in Translation
Description: Boy decides to meet girl. Boy fails miserably. Boy eventually meets girl. Sh*t meets fan. Tom’s sexual (mis)adventures come to an end when he befriends Sarah, but is there any benefit to friends with benefits?
Venue description: One of the festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross genre performance makes this central venue a must for all.  Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Hear a Pin Drop Here
Description: Holly Rumble doesn’t like crowds. In retrospect, visiting Edinburgh in August wasn’t such a good idea. To remedy this, she has spent a week GPS-tagging the quietest Edinburgh locations. Daily updates online 3rd-9th August. www.hearapindrophere.com.
Artist: Holly Rumble / Escalator East To Edinburgh
Venue description: Lauriston Halls (both modernised) are situated between the Grassmarket and Tollcross, 10 minutes walk from Princes St. The Large Hall has air-conditioning which makes it ideal for dancing. It is a regular ceilidh venue, popular with locals and visitors.

Title: Steve Shanyaski’s Life-Survival Bible
Description: Everyone’s life better than yours on Twitter? Accidentally said, ‘amazeballs’ in’t pub? What’s TOWIE? Surviving modern life requires assistance… Steve Shanyaski’s Life-Survival Bible is here to help. As seen on ITV1’s Comedy Rocks. ‘Uproariously funny’ (Chortle.co.uk).
Artist: Lee Martin for Gag Reflex Management
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: How to Work with Agents
Description: This no-nonsense session will ask fundamental questions: What does an agent do? Do you really need one? What can you expect from them and what will they expect from you? We'll explain how to approach an agent and look at the legal and financial aspects of getting represented.
Artist: The Stage Events with Jennifer Resichel
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Le Nozze di Figaro by Mozart, Youth Performance
Description: Youth adaptation - a fantastic introduction to opera and a tale of ruthlessness which ultimately loses out to love! Our production is set in 1930s Italy. Bargain ticket prices!
Venue description: Over the past 18 years, Greyfriars Kirk has become an acclaimed city centre venue with a relaxed atmosphere and magnificent acoustics. The Kirk is open every day throughout the festival. Perfect venue for choral and orchestral performances.

Title: Undateable
Description: Yvonne Lake has been running an experiment via online dating websites.
Venue description: Located on George Street, Whynot? is the number one late night venue in Edinburgh. During the Fringe, our doors are open Monday to Friday, 12.30 to 9.30pm, for free comedy shows, and the club opens late as usual for those who wish to party the night away.

Title: 4.48 Psychosis
Description: ***** ’Definitely people to watch’ (FringeReview.co.uk). ***** ‘Tour de force on the Fringe’ (RemoteGoat.co.uk). **** ‘A hit’ (List). Fourth Monkey return to the Fringe with their Off-West End nominated version of Sarah Kane's iconic and poetic contemporary classic.
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.

Title: Fishy Tails with Liz Kessler
Description: Emily Windsnap lives on a boat, but her mum doesn’t want her to go swimming. She soon learns why: as soon as she gets into water, she grows a tail! Join Liz Kessler as she divulges all about her Emily Windsnap stories – magical adventures, centred around mermaids, friendship and family.

Title: Colours of Tango
Description: Travel back to the Buenos Aires of a century ago... Experience the passion of Tango, its music and dance, with singer Oscar Ovejero and an international group of artistes honoured by the Argentinian National Academy of Tango.
Venue description: Situated in the heart of the New Town, The Royal Scots Club offers a distinctive combination of cosy charm and elegance.
Venue accessibility:
34
\nAssistance dogs welcome. Lift for access

Title: Superbard Starts to Save the World
Description: Join fantastical storyteller Superbard (BBC Radio 4, Newsnight) in an uplifting, multimedia adventure through time, love, beauty and spreadsheets. Kafka meets YouTube. Douglas Adams meets Sigur Ros. ‘Funny, intelligent, clever and inspiring. Highly recommended’ (FringeReview.co.uk).
Venue description: 40 metres from the centre of Princes Street, just up from the National Gallery, this beautiful venue has a reputation for quality ***** and **** sell-outs! Outstanding, international companies: interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, classics, cutting-edge plays, dance, quirky comedy and musicals...

Title: Gavin Webster: Bill Hicks Wasn't Very Good
Description: Bill Hicks? He didn't do proper jokes, never mind funny walks or witty monologues about stuff and that. An hour of non award-winning comic Gavin Webster not celebrating this celebrated dead comic.
Artist: Gavin Webster / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Round the corner, our little sister club is in its thirteenth year. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: That Old Noir Magic - A Film Noir Jazz Journey Into Night, in Story and Song
Description: Your hard-boiled private eye sings you spellbound in a nostalgic jazz trip through iconic classic film noir, eg, Laura, Double Indemnity, Casablanca etc.
Venue description: At Greenside we believe we encapsulate the true spirit of the fringe! With our three fantastic spaces, gorgeous gardens, shows that won’t cost the earth matched with every conceivable performance genre all only a minute walk from the Edinburgh Playhouse!

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning events for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. Appearing today: Sue Heap.

Title: Phil Mann's Full Mind
Description: Incredible acts of short-order investigation, new improvised show daily. ‘A brilliantly comedic creation’ (Scotsman) ‘Enviable flair for comic timing’ (Fest). ‘Hilarious ... Quite endearing’ (Stage). ‘Very funny, delivered with delight and scruffy charm’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘Eccentric. Breathtaking’ (FringeReview.co.uk).
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.

Title: A Little Night Music
Description: Broadway's neglected masterpiece - Sondheim's achingly beautiful A Little Night Music - deals with love in all its wondrous, humorous and ironic permutations. Performed by senior cast and orchestra of the multi-award winning Norfolk YMT.
Venue address: St Columba's by the Castle,Johnston Terrace
Venue description: C's original offshoot with alfresco chillout barbecue-bar. C4kids - the top children's shows. Showstopping musicals. Shakespeare played backwards, forwards, any way at all. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: People Show 121: The Detective Show
Description: Someone's been murdered. But there's no body, no weapon and no motive. People Show delve into the world of all things Agatha Christie - funny, frightening ferocious. 'Madly experimental, visually stunning theatre' (Sunday Times).
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
