024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Gotcha!
Description: This new one-man play presents Ernie, a prickly Glaswegian traffic warden, and seven other intertwined characters. Tragedy strikes, but Ernie's indomitable Scottish spirit triumphs over adversity with humour and courage. Laugh, cry, and be enriched by this experience!
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Lady Sings it Better
Description: Smashing expectations one soaring harmony at a time, these women reinvent tunes from the greatest male musicians. Soulful, sassy and surprising, the ladies romp through popular culture, with stellar vocals and a little ridiculous dancing.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Ian McEwan
Subtitle: THE SPY WHO LOVED ME
Description:
The most gifted British novelist of his generation unveils his new book at the Book Festival. Sweet Tooth tells the story of a woman drawn into intelligence activities, who then falls in love and faces a challenge to maintain the fiction of her undercover life. Ian McEwan’s previous bestselling novels include Saturday, On Chesil Beach and the Man Booker Prize-winning Amsterdam.

	If you didn't manage to get tickets to see Ian McEwan at the Book Festival he will also take part in a Q&A session following the screening of The Cement Garden on Thursday 23 August at 6pm at the at the Filmhouse in Lothian Road, Edinburgh. Tickets are available from the Filmhouse website or call their box office on 0131 228 2689.

Title: The Fringe Comedy Academy: Class of 2012
Description: Join the graduated of the Fringe Comedy Academy, a unique project supporting the development of emerging comedy talent. Hosted by Susan Morrison with a special headline guest. One night only.
Artist: Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society / Virgin Money supported by Mike Westcott Fund
Venue: The Stand Comedy Club III & IV
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue, Stand III is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand IV an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Angus Roxburgh
Subtitle: A SHOW OF RUSSIAN STRENGTH
Description: When the Kremlin decided it needed a more user-friendly image, it hired Angus Roxburgh and his New York-based PR firm. Now that he has left the employment of Vladimir Putin, Roxburgh’s insider perspective has given him a wealth of fascinating material on the man. In his insightful and balanced book, The Strongman, Roxburgh describes the Putin administration and its PR disasters, and explores what the future holds for the recently re-elected President.

Title: Simon Mawer & Michèle Roberts
Subtitle: SECRETS THAT SHAPED THE SECOND WORLD WAR
Description: This event brings together two brilliant authors whose novels offer tremendous insight into the effects of the Second World War on the women who experienced it. Simon Mawer and Michèle Roberts, each previously shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize, discuss their new novels. In both stories, women in very different situations are driven to behave in courageous, sometimes shocking ways.

Title: Amok
Description: “Fajardo's technical exercise is a showcase of his talent for skewering disparate lives momentarily trapped in an urban labyrinth through a random act of violence” (Khavn de la Cruz, filmmaker).

Title: Spaghetti Junction
Description: Andi needs a new route. She's stuck in a one-way system. Can she navigate through the chaos ahead? Featuring song, movement and storytelling. ‘A beautiful reflection on growing up and the absurdities of life’ ***** (WhatsOnStage.com, for Vertigo).
Venue description: Bedlam Theatre plays host to an eclectic mix of theatre, dance and comedy at the heart of the Fringe. Enjoy the unique atmosphere of our famous cafe and discover some of the most innovative shows the festival has to offer.

Title: Sue Hendra
Description: Sue Hendra is the creator of Barry The Fish With Fingers a delightful, inspiring and very funny story with bold, bright illustrations. Come and meet Sue’s latest character, Keith The Cat with the Magic Hat and join in with stories, drawings and Barry-related crafts.

Title: Foreigner Go Home (With Me)
Description: Join Stephanie Chan in a strange, phenomenal, poetical journey called Moving to London from the Far East, exploring why the hell everyone from everywhere feels the need to go away to find themselves.
Venue description: The Royal Oak is Edinburgh's premiere traditional music and folksinging howff. Rub shoulders with the top names in folk music, join in or just sit and listen; sample a cask ale or a fine malt and enjoy the convivial atmosphere.

Title: Alex Gray & Mons Kallentoft
Subtitle: A LIFE OF GRIME
Description: Mons Kallentoft has had Scandic crime fans lapping up his words since his 2000 debut, Pesetas. Single mum Malin Fors is his chosen crime-fighter and in Summertime Death, she tries to piece together the clues when a grisly discovery is made. Closer to home, Alex Gray's new thriller A Pound Of Flesh has DCI Lorimer investigating not one but two gruesome serial killers loose in Glasgow.

Title: Sophie Bancroft and Tom Lyne
Description: Dynamic and intimate interpretations of jazz songs with a wonderful telepathy between voice/guitar and double bass. ‘Hip, cool and simply beautiful’ (Big Issue). ‘Their performance, imbued with warmth and humour, was delightful’ (Herald). www.sophiebancroft.co.uk.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Michael Sandel
Subtitle: THE MORAL LIMITS OF THE MARKET
Description: In What Money Can't Buy, Michael Sandel examines one of the biggest ethical questions of our time: What is the proper role of markets, and how can we protect the moral and civic goods that markets do not honour and money cannot buy? Sandel is a professor at Harvard, delivering a massively popular course on justice. In 2010, China Newsweek named him the 'most influential foreign figure of the year' in China.

Title: China Red
Description: Edinburgh debut for an award-winning young Chinese company. A packed and spectacularly varied programme combining the finest traditional Chinese dance with a diverse array of international styles, delivered with passion and exuberance by Beijing's rising dance talents.
Artist: Beijing Students Golden Sail Art Troupe
Venue description: An award-winning extravaganza of the best performances from across the Fringe spectrum. The majestic Main House is packed with outstanding dance and physical theatre from around the world while the Cabaret Bar and Studio host thrilling drama, comedy and music.

Title: The Kids We Used To Be - Free
Description: Come and join four rising stars of the Scottish circuit for an hour of carefree laughter as they say goodbye to their childhood and dread their inevitable transition to adulthood.
Venue description: A daily selection of Free shows, comedy, theatre and cabaret, running as part of the Free Festival, with performances running all day from midday until midnight in this friendly venue, offering a wide range of drinks and food

Title: This Audio Tour Belongs to Lionel Richie
Description: Download this audio walking tour - any day, any time - and become intimate with Fringe history, even perform yourself if you choose. Tour begins at Hunter Square. Go to www.thisbelongstolionelrichie.co.uk to download.
Venue description: Half-way between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood palace on the Royal Mile is the Tron Kirk, the departure point for Auld Reekie's Tours in Edinburgh. Meet at the black sign by the Tron Kirk and learn about the dark side of Edinburgh.
Venue accessibility: \nWalking tours. Not accessible to wheelchair users.

Title: Fringe Film Festival
Description: Returning for its eighth season, critically acclaimed curated programme showcases silver screen shorts and contemporary filmmakers all day, every day. Features work from UK, Europe, Americas, Asia, worldwide. The destination for discerning film folk. 'Spectacular' (Scotsman). www.CtheFilm.com.
Venue description: Brand new city-centre hub venue. Fantastic found spaces spanning seven storeys. The most thrilling theatre and exhilarating events you'll find on the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Theresa Breslin & Elizabeth Laird
Description: This is a fantastic opportunity to meet two award-winning writers and hear about their latest books. Theresa Breslin’s new novel, Spy for the Queen of Scots, is a tale of mystery, plotting and intrigue; Elizabeth Laird’s, The Prince who Walked with Lions, is the true-life tale of a young Ethiopian prince adopted by Queen Victoria. Together they discuss historical characters and share the secrets of how they go about researching and creating a story from the original germ of an idea.

Title: Jennifer Thomson Exhibition
Description: Exhibition of limited edition prints and cards. Jennifer paints detailed and humorous pictures of the places she visits and the people she sees there. Colourful scenes of Edinburgh including the Castle, Grassmarket and Royal Mile.
Venue accessibility: \nNo disabled access.

Title: Hilary Mantel
Subtitle: WHERE FACT AND FICTION OVERLAP
Description: Wolf Hall was one of the most remarkable novels of recent years and it became the bestselling Man Booker Prize winner to date. Now Hilary Mantel joins us to discuss its much anticipated sequel, Bring up the Bodies, which imagines Anne Boleyn's downfall at the hands of Henry VIII and Thomas Cromwell. She discusses her work with James Runcie, director of a stunning BBC2 documentary about Mantel.

Title: Surprise Movie
Description: Back after a three-year hiatus, The Surprise Movie is back! It could be literally anything, in any format, any language, any genre. As you may have seen from this year's programme, our taste is varied and unpredictable. The most tightly guarded secret at EIFF - even if you think you know what the Surprise Movie is, you're wrong. What we guarantee is that it’s something that we're excited about and we think you will be too. Do not miss it.

Title: Midnight Sun Event featuring Insomnia
Description: “Print courtesy of the Norwegian Film Institute.”  [JR]]]

Title: Card Ninja: ReDeal
Description: Following the success of last year's Festival Javier Jarquin returns with an all-new show for 2012. Combining killer wit and cards as weapons, Card Ninja: ReDeal brings more comedy, more Ninja and many more cards.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Presidential Suite: a Modern Fairy Tale
Description: Remember the French VIP who allegedly raped the black chambermaid in the Manhattan hotel? A darkly humorous play from acclaimed US screenwriter reveals the story behind the headlines - in both bedroom and courtroom.
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: The  Australian Voices in Concert
Description: Come and experience the sublime sounds of The Australian Voices Six singing beautiful choral classics from Mozart and Bach to Bruckner and Rachmaninov, plus Australian works. This is what cathedral acoustics were made for!
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Practical Poetry
Description: Join the Scottish Poetry Library to discover how we can inspire young people to write poetry and find the spark for new writing. Liz Niven shares some successful poetry projects where new text has been created and installed around schools and towns. From placemats to ebooks and poets’ chairs to stone dykes, words can appear anywhere. Be refreshed and ready to rock with new ideas.

Title: Julia Donaldson
Description: Due to popular demand, Children’s Laureate Julia Donaldson will be presenting a further fantastic event. Come and join her for the opportunity to experience some of her award-winning picture books such as The Highway Rat, The Singing Mermaid and perhaps even The Gruffalo. There will be songs, performance and plenty of moments to join in and take part in being one of her great characters. And as an extra special treat acclaimed Scottish author James Robertson will be joining in the fun with a Scots rendition of The Gruffalo. This is a brand new event that’s just been added to the programme and therefore it does not appear in the printed brochure. Grab this opportunity to get tickets for one of the Book Festival’s most popular authors.

Title: Flying Blind
Description: A stylish mix of erotic love story and political thriller. Helen McCrory stars as a brilliant aerospace engineer who is drawn into a passionate affair with a younger male student while working on a government contract for an aircraft destined for military use. As the contract deadline nears, her doubts about her new lover mount, and she comes to understand the shadowy sides of her professional career and her personal life.

Title: Twonkeys Kingdom - Free
Description: ‘Mr Twonkey is a true comic original’ **** (Scotsman). Melodrama with known loon and likeable surrealist comedian/musician, Paul Vickers. Nothing less than the Walt Disney Mark E Smith. ‘The hit of the Fringe’ **** (Scotland on Sunday).
Artist: Paul Vickers / Heroes of Alternative Comedy
Venue description: Genuine Comedy Legends, alongside the most exciting non-conformists of today. Centrally located. Shows all day. Nightclub until 5am. An alternative to expensive tickets. Recreating the spirit of adventure that existed before Alternative went Mainstream. No Rules, No Limits, No refunds!

Title: Paterson Arran Ten at Ten
Description: A delicious morning reading from one of our Festival authors to set you up for the day. Check the screen in the Entrance Tent to see who’s reading each day.

Title: Bungo Menebla!
Description: Idiocy, sketches and silliness from the combined talents of top stand-up Kevin Dewsbury, 'a real treat' (ThreeWeeks), ‘sheer talent’ (TimeOut), and comedy actor Mark Sparkler (star of recent film Surprise and one time writer for Steve Coogan). www.bungomenebla.com.
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: Liza Klaussmann & David Rain
Subtitle: LOVE AND WAR IN AMERICA
Description: This year’s Book Festival kicks off with a simmering novel of passion, betrayal and violence in America at the end of the Second World War. Liza Klaussmann’s debut Tigers in Red Weather features cousins whose children are destined to uncover some dark secrets. David Rain also zones in on fractured relationships in the States during that pivotal historical period with The Heat of the Sun, as depression, brutality and upheaval take hold.

Title: Sound of Seventeen
Description: The Sound of Seventeen is an Edinburgh-based big band, which will be playing a selection of music from the big band era. This year we will be celebrating our 10th anniversary with a wide range of music.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Jigsaw: Gettin' Jiggy
Description: ‘A super group' (Fest) - Dan Antopolski, Tom Craine and Nat Luurtsema, meteoric stars of BBC3's Live At The Electric and Radio 4's Sketchorama, return after last year's sell-out debut smash. 'Makes the Fast Show look languid' (Guardian).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Tom Bullough & Jane Sullivan
Subtitle: 19TH CENTURY TALES OF WONDERMENT
Description: Set in 1867 Central Russia, Tom Bullough’s Konstantin follows a carefree 10 year old who is left deaf after an illness. Only his fascination with space and the stars gives him the drive to continue. In Little People, Jane Sullivan transports us to 1870s Australia where a governess rescues a child from drowning. Except the ‘child’ turns out to be the star of a celebrated troupe of midgets.

Title: Just So Stories
Description: Kipling’s best-loved tales told with magic, music and rambunctious storytelling. ‘An exceptional group who consistently produce terrific work’ (Scotsman). ‘Exciting and dynamic young company’ ***** (Herald). Critics’ Choice Independent 2010. ***** (ThreeWeeks, Editor’s Choice 2009).
Venue description: Just off the Lawnmarket our friendly venue is centrally placed on the terrace above Victoria Street . We provide a 65 seating rake and a black box theatre, our own box office and reception area. Our venue profits go to charity.

Title: Carol Ann Duffy
Description: Carol Ann Duffy has been acclaimed as the first Poet Laureate for the whole family with her brilliant poems for children as well as adults. Join her with musician John Sampson for an hour of beautiful words, accompanied by masterfully performed melodies from an array of exotic wind instruments such as a crumhorn and hilusi.

Title: Lynne Rickards
Description: Lewis is a puffin who wants to be something completely different and so decides to join the circus. Come and hear more from author Lynne Rickards about Lewis and all the exciting circus characters he encounters. Great fun for little ones. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: Piano and Flute Recital
Description: Maya, a Belarusian pianist, has delighted Edinburgh audiences on previous occasions. Joined by Kristina, an Australian flautist, these much-lauded recent graduates of RNCM will present solo and duo works by Schubert, Schumann, Stravinsky and Piazzolla.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Daniel-Ryan Spaulding: How Dare You!
Description: Provocative, intelligent, with the right amount of sass, internationally touring Canadian stand-up comic Daniel-Ryan Spaulding welcomes you to the world of a fearless, lovable, young gay man, who doesn't take sh*t from anyone! **** (Scotsgay.co.uk).
Venue description:
The Hudson Hotel is ideally located at the west end of Princes Street. With an extensive wine and cocktail list, live music on Friday and Saturday nights from 9pm, and Bacaro nightclub hosting free comedy from 1:30pm until 10pm daily. Open from 8am. Food served throughout the day until 10pm Sunday to Thursday and 9pm Friday and Saturday.
\n
Venue accessibility:
01234569
\nAccessible parking, level access, wheelchair access, lift, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC

Title: Eric's Tales of the Sea - A Submariner's Yarn
Description: Award-winning Fringe favourite (5th consecutive year) insider's view of life on a nuclear submarine. Unique, riveting, funny and poignant. 'Mesmerising' (Guardian). 'Quietly wonderful show' (Times) 'One in a million show' ***** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: The Wheelchair on My Face
Description: Little Miss Sunshine meets My Left Foot. Part memoir, part theatre, part stand-up comedy - a delightful story of a myopic seven-year-old by Sonya Kelly (Savage Eye). Fishamble - Fringe First, Herald Angel, 2011.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Charles Allen
Subtitle: ASHOKA: A GREAT NAME IN WORLD HISTORY
Description: Two centuries before the birth of Christ, one man was known and revered across the Asian continent. Ashoka is the subject of Charles Allen's impressively wide-ranging and entertaining study, and he re-introduces a major historical figure who deserves to be better known. Ashoka was the only ruler to preside over the entire Asian subcontinent; he also preached non-violence and introduced a welfare state.

Title: Sinful - Free
Description: ‘Forget whatever else you have planned - go and see this brilliant show!' ***** (WhatsOnStage.com). Seven wickedly surprising shorts for seven deadly sins. ‘Outstanding ... outrageously rude ... all-round excellent show ... a writer and performer to watch out for’ (UKTheatre.net). www.eyeofthestormproductions.co.uk.
Warnings: Some very strong language Some very strong language
Artist: Carly Tarett /  Eye of the Storm Productions / Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Helen Dunmore
Subtitle: THE PAST COMES BACK TO HAUNT US
Description: She won the Orange Prize for her novel A Spell of Winter, and was Man Booker longlisted for The Betrayal. Now, this most versatile of writers has produced a deliciously chilling novella set in East Yorkshire. The Greatcoat tells the story of a woman who discovers an RAF officer's coat in her new flat. Later, in her dreams, she hears a knocking on the window...

Title: Firebird
Description: Lost, alone and afraid, a solitary firebird searches for companionship. ikou!’s imaginative storytelling uses beautiful puppets and original music in an intimate tale with an interactive twist, as the audience’s choices determine his journey across this mysterious landscape.
Venue description: Managed by theSpaceUK, this intimate space hosts an array of new and established theatre. Located seconds from the Royal Mile with bar and cafe facilities. For show information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Sparkleshark
Description: Fourteen-year-old Jake takes refuge from bullies by writing and telling stories on a rooftop. Soon some of his classmates become enmeshed in the story, enacting a fantastic tale that mirrors their own friendships and enmities. www.ept.org.uk.
Venue description: Conveniently situated in the south side of Edinburgh, off South Clerk Street and near to Queen's Hall. On main bus routes.
Venue accessibility:
01459

Title: Clinton the Musical
Description: It's hard enough being the president by yourself. Bill Clinton's problem is that there are two of him. A musical comedy about Bill Clinton and Bill Clinton on their quest to save their presidency and change America.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Wild Allegations
Description: Join Matthew John Curtis, a thriving actor, as he becomes tangled in a farcical web of lies and deceit. As we delve into our hidden depths and vulnerabilities, who is really at fault and who can we trust?
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Clive Stafford Smith
Subtitle: COURTING THE FAVOUR OF NO ONE
Description: The bane of Western tyranny and advocates of capital punishment everywhere, Clive Stafford Smith returns with Injustice: Life And Death In The Courtrooms Of America. When a man is wrongly condemned to death for murder, a crusading lawyer is determined to free him and his investigation reveals corruption at every turn. It may sound like a page-turning crime noir fiction, but it’s all horribly true.

Title: Ian Rankin
Subtitle: DEAD GOOD FICTION
Description: On the 25th anniversary of the first Rebus mystery, Ian Rankin’s new crime fighter DI Malcolm Fox is busy making his own mark. In The Impossible Dead, he is looking into a case of police corruption in Kirkcaldy and uncovers a whole lot of other trouble. In this special event, Ian Rankin discusses his latest bestseller as well as his forthcoming novel – published in November – whose contents are currently a closely guarded secret.

Title: Harriet Dyer (Plus the Odd Pal) - What a Palaver!
Description: Recently rejiggled tales of palaversome girth! Come along for fun and frolics with at least one special comedy guest each night! 'She’s got funny bones!' (Kevin Bridges).
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: A Vintage Evening of Song
Description: From the turn-of-the-century elegance of the Edwardian era, covering the advent of recorded music, the strife of the Suffragettes, the tragedy of the Titanic and life-changing events of The Great War.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Owen Hatherley & Rowan Moore
Subtitle: WHY ARCHITECTURE MATTERS
Description: Rowan Moore is the most lucid, outspoken and entertaining writer on architecture in Britain today. His new book, Why We Build, examines what inspires us to make great architecture. He is joined by Owen Hatherley whose A New Kind of Bleak argues that an era of public sector cuts will leave Britain’s landscape to rot. Here are two writers whose views on British architecture will provoke, entertain and enlighten.

Title: Fiona McLaren
Subtitle: AN ART LOVER'S DA VINCI CODE
Description: It’s billed as one of the most sensational detective stories in the history of art. Fiona McLaren tells her story of a painting that belonged to the family for years until they began to realise it may be rather special. Could it have been by a pupil of Leonardo da Vinci, or even by the master himself? McLaren’s spellbinding account includes some astonishing insights into the Roman Catholic Church. Chaired by Jackie McGlone.

Title: Michael Frayn
Subtitle: ALL THE FUN OF THE FARCE
Description: The Man Booker-shortlisted and Whitbread-winning author of Headlong and Spies joins us to discuss his latest novel, Skios. Michael Frayn is one of Britain’s most respected playwrights and he brings his mastery of the stage farce to this new comedy. As the Fred Toppler Foundation prepares for its annual lecture, it turns out there’s a case of stolen identity that threatens to get the organiser into hot water…

Title: From Mozart to Muse
Description: By wiring a violin and a clarinet up to shiny laptops and stomping on chunky pedals, this duo loops together a thousand unexpected sounds from a breathtakingly eclectic range of genres for audiences of all ages.
Venue description: Edinburgh's all-year-round multi-arts venue. We offer a gourmet selection of theatre, cabaret, live music, visual arts and clubbing. Our cafe adds delicious homemade food, free internet and great coffee to the mix. All brought to you by the friendliest staff in town.

Have you been making short films as a hobby and do you want to develop this into a full time job? Are you considering a film course? Our expert practitioner will explain how to make it in this intensely competitive industry.

Title: James Geary & Sam Leith
Subtitle: UNLEASHING THE PERSUADERS
Description: In an age of abundant spin and rampant PR, the art of persuasion has never been more important. Sam Leith’s You Talkin’ to Me?: Rhetoric from Aristotle to Obama is a witty and stylish exposé of the persuaders. James Geary’s I is an Other suggests that metaphor is present in everything these days, from ordinary conversation and commercial messaging to news reports and political speeches.

Title: Ted & Co The Dinner Show

Title: Lone Frank
Subtitle: LETTING THE GENOME OUT OF THE BOTTLE
Description: The internationally acclaimed science writer Lone Frank goes on a fantastic voyage with My Beautiful Genome to provide an intimate and, at times, personal account into the new science of consumer-led genomics. The Dane ponders the consequences of biological fortune-telling, and explores the psychologists who hope to uncover just how much our environment will matter in a new genetic driven era.

Title: Debate: Rethinking Democracy
Subtitle: HAVE WE LOST OUR FAITH IN GOVERNMENT BY THE PEOPLE?
Description: It has a near-sacred status in the West, and yet democracy is far from perfect. Why has democracy signally failed to eradicate inequality at a global level? And in democracies, why does it appear that the range and imagination of political ideas is shrinking, and our faith in politicians evaporating? Something is going badly wrong. Radical ideas are welcome in this discussion with the former leader of the Liberal Democrats, Menzies Campbell and Matthew Flinders, author of Defending Politics.

Title: Ruth Padel
Subtitle: WE'RE ALL FROM SOMEWHERE ELSE
Description: 'All human life, all countries began with migration from Africa,' says Ruth Padel. In a stunning new book looking at the ebb and flow of migration, the renowned poet and writer has created a book of wonders – a glorious collection of poetry and prose that is a brave and often brilliant achievement. Padel joins us today to discuss what led her to embark on this remarkable project. Chaired by James Naughtie.

Title: Michelle Wormleighton - Bewildered
Description: Failed playwright and actress Michelle Wormleighton portrays discarded characters from her ill-fated gangster epic, Crimefellows. Burritos available. ‘Michelle Wormleighton was great’ (Hairline.org.uk).

Title: Dating George Orwell - Free

Subtitle: THE COMPLEX CHARACTER THAT WAS CHARLES DICKENS

Carol Ann Duffy is joined on stage by her friend, the virtuoso musician John Sampson, and a variety of his favourite woodwind instruments. Duffy and Sampson are a perennial highlight of the Book Festival.

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: THE COLOUR ORANGE
Description:
A colourful collaboration of music, spoken word, literature and poetry. Working with the Dutch Foundation for Literature we have brought together artists for readings and performances reflecting the historical and cultural influences that combine to create Dutch culture. From the historical legacy of its empire in South Africa and Indonesia, to the influence of American culture in the 20th century, and the impact of multicultural Europe in the 21st century. Join novelist, Karin Amatmoekrim, acclaimed hip-hop artist, Blaxtar, and Christine Otten, poet and author of the fictional biography of The Ghost Poets, De Laatste Dichters / The Last Poets, the legendary group of Afro-American poets and performers.

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Description: Comedy half of Men That Will Not Be Blamed For Nothing present a right gruesome steampunk knees-up, with songs. **** (Independent). ‘Genius ... side-splitting’ ***** (Big Cheese).
Artist: Blamed For Nothing / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: At the heart of Canongate on the Royal Mile, the Canon's Gait is an historic, recently redecorated bar serving lunches, real ale and an extensive selection of malt whiskies. Comfortable seating and relaxed, friendly atmosphere to enjoy a drink between shows.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Mess
Description: Josephine is putting on a play - Boris and Sistahl help. It's about anorexia. But don't let that put you off. A new play with songs from 2010 Stage Best Solo Performer Award winner Caroline Horton.
Venue description: Scotland's new writing theatre 'is the festival's most prestigious home of serious drama' (New York Times) and a multiple Fringe First and Herald Angel award winner. 'The main hub of festival-focussed action during August' (List).

Title: Michael Grant
Description: Michael Grant is the author of the Gone series, the sci-fi thrillers where every adult disappears leaving only children behind. Some want anarchy and others want control but no one knew what would follow: man-eating worms, starvation and plague. These are brutal stories, dark and yet utterly compelling. Michael has said that all he wants is to ‘scare the reader, surprise the reader and make that reader fall in love.’ He has most definitely succeeded, these are books that once read are never forgotten. Come and meet their creator.

Title: Munfred Bernstein's Cabinet of Wonder
Description: Witness a cabaret of wild stories collected from around the globe in this hilarious musical misadventure from a man unhinged. Step inside the Cabinet of Wonder! You've nothing to lose, except your wallet and keys.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Loud and Proud
Description: Loud and Proud, Scotland's LGBT a cappella singing sensation, combines Scottish songs, international repertoire, stirring anthems and pop classics. A Fringe hot ticket - book early! Supporting Waverley Care.
Venue description: Fine Georgian building designed by architect James Milne and built 1823. The Church is a superb concert venue with a Steinway baby grand piano and has excellent acoustics.
Venue accessibility:
2489
\nAccessible WC, Wheelchair accessible, hearing loop in performance space, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Niño
Description: A witty and incisive portrait of an aristocratic Philippine family in decline. The elderly family patriarch is ill, and his daughter wants to sell the house, to the alarm of his sister, Celia, a former opera star, who had been looking forward to spending her last years peacefully among her memories of the past. Celia pins her hopes for a miracle on her young grandson, whom she dresses up as the Santo Niño (holy child).

Title: Daniel Franklin
Subtitle: IS THIS PROGRESS?
Description: In 2050 there will be 9.3 billion people alive. The over 65s will have more than doubled and the number of cars on India’s roads will have increased by 3880%. Economist executive editor Daniel Franklin’s Megachange explores the trends that will shape the coming decades. Predicting the future may be risky, Franklin argues, but he firmly believes not all will be bleak. Join him today to find out why.

Title: Forever Young
Description: An uplifting collection of heart-warming and nostalgic tales exploring love and happiness against the backdrop of the 60s brought to you through the mediums of theatre, live music and dance.
Venue description: the SpaceUK present another high calibre venue. This wonderfully-located space between Bristo Square and the Pleasance offers a high brow alternative to the traditional fringe venues. Ideal for Stand-Up, Chat, Music (bands), A Capella, Improv, Sketch and Cabaret.

Title: Introduction to Forum Theatre
Description: An introduction to forum theatre using skills and techniques to help devise and question issues of conflict and oppression. These workshops aim to provide a broad understanding of forum theatre and its application across theatre.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Dustbowl Blues with a Glasgow Kick
Description: A soul-grasping musical road trip from this Glasgow roots and blues man. Tales of lonesome desert highways to the Mississippi Delta, calling in at Glasgow shipyards and Scottish hills along the way. www.johnalexander.info.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: John Robertson - The Dark Room - Free
Description: Trapped in a dark room, you must escape. An unscripted, unhinged and live ‘choose your own adventure’, as seen on YouTube, in Variety magazine and all your best nightmares. ‘A revelation!’ (Scotsman).
Artist: John Robertson / PIAS / It's The Comedy You Deserve
Venue description: Genuine Comedy Legends, alongside the most exciting non-conformists of today. Centrally located. Shows all day. Nightclub until 5am. An alternative to expensive tickets. Recreating the spirit of adventure that existed before Alternative went Mainstream. No Rules, No Limits, No refunds!

Title: Style vs Content
Subtitle: How should authors approach the task of writing a novel today?
Description:
What is more important: the content of a novel or the style in which it is written? Ali Smith’s novels successfully marry ambitious themes with a variety of confident linguistic styles – from the deliciously playful to the crashingly simple. Smith addresses today’s Conference session about approaches to the construction of the novel today, in an event chaired by Nathan Englander – whose short pieces have been described by Michael Chabon as ‘masterpieces of short-story art’.

	Visit the Edinburgh World Writers’ Conference website - www.edinburghworldwritersconference.org - to watch a live broadcast of this and other conference events and to join in the conversation online. Follow the conference twitter feed: #WorldWritersConf.

	Supported by the Scottish Government's Edinburgh Festivals Expo Fund, Creative Scotland, the City of Edinburgh Council and Event Scotland.

Title: A Compas Flamenco
Description: Flamenco for all! Join the fiesta for an exciting experience exploring the origins and stories of this Andalucian art. Try out the rhythms, the clapping, some steps! Meet the artists! Critics'/audience choice! Five stars worldwide! Ace! www.flamencoflow.com.
Venue description: the SpaceUK present another high calibre venue. This wonderfully-located space between Bristo Square and the Pleasance offers a high brow alternative to the traditional fringe venues. Ideal for Stand-Up, Chat, Music (bands), A Capella, Improv, Sketch and Cabaret.

Title: CRYPT with Andrew Hammond
Description: Andrew Hammond made his first foray into fiction last year with The Gallows Curse, the smart, fast-paced first book in his new teen horror series CRYPT, which we launched at last year's Book Festival. Join him for a roller-coaster ride through the grim and gruesome history of the world's most famous cities with Traitor's Revenge, the much-anticipated second in the series. Ghosts and ghouls guaranteed!

Title: Festival Club
Description: We bring you the best Polish alternative culture. During August the Adam Mickiewicz Institute invites to the Festival Club in Summerhall - each evening there will be meetings, discussions, workshops, live music and movies. www.culture.pl.
Warnings: Supported by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute www.culture.pl
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: The Very Scariesome Lollipop Lady
Description: A tale told in rhyme. A story of bravery, busy roads, friendship, a magical lollipop stick, and a really, really, really scary road crossing patrol officer. ‘Unbelievably brilliant’ (Scotsman).
Venue description:
Ryan's is situated in the heart of Edinburgh's chic west-end and comprises of three departments: Main Bar, Coffee Shop and Cellar Restaurant. 
\nRyan’s hidden gem is bursting with character and this is where the comedy acts will be on. As well as the main area where the performances take place the restaurant features seven private alcoves for dining. The venue boasts a piano bar and live Jazz every Sunday night.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Hand Over Fist
Description: Hannah Eidinow directs Dave Florez's dark, redemptive monologue about lost love and Alzheimer's. Praise for the prequel, Fringe First 2011 winner Somewhere Beneath: Critic's Choice (List), 'Hard- hitting drama burns bright. '**** (Metro). 'Engaging, unpredictable' **** (Fest).
Artist: Festival Highlights and the Comedians Theatre Company
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Best in the World
Description: One man, three darts, no second chances. Join our quest discovering what being best really means. Featuring champions’ insights, live darts and emergency bananas. Are you the best audience in the world? ‘Thrillingly talented people’ (Guardian).
Artist: Unfolding Theatre in association with Northern Stage
Venue description: Northern Stage at St Stephen’s is a creative home for the most exciting and unusual theatre made in the Greater North of England. Original stories, new performances and spirited special events that will delight, provoke and entertain you.

Title: Miss Marchbanks
Description: The year is 1865, Victoria is on the throne and Miss Marchbanks has finished school. She returns home determined to conquer society and parlour politics, but will attentions from three eligible gentlemen prove too much of a distraction?
Venue description: Paradise Green's purpose-built venue in the vaulted basements of Augustine United Church hosts an exciting programme of theatre and comedy for all tastes, from classics to new and experimental work. Soak up the true spirit of the Fringe.

Title: Jonathan Emmett
Description: One birthday, Callum receives a special present – a construction kit. The possibilities are endless and Callum finds himself building all sorts of fantastic things. But what happens if you build so many things your house falls down? If you like making things more than you like reading then Callum’s Incredible Construction Kit is the book for you. So, come and join author Jonathan Emmett to learn more and find out how the story ends.

Title: Allan Burnett: Bringing History to Life
Description: Allan Burnett is a historian and author and his And All That series takes you back through hundreds and thousands of years to distant places – some familiar – where you can join in some exciting real-life adventures. Along the way you get to learn fascinating facts, exercise your imagination, get splattered in a bit of gore and experience being a part of something so much bigger than yourself.

Title: Arguments and Nosebleeds - Free
Description: Warning: excessive side-splitting may lead to blood loss. A craic squad of performance poets tackle life's major issues (scary schoolteachers, body hair, missing teapots etc) pausing only for laughter and medical emergencies. www.argumentsandnosebleeds.com.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: How a Man Crumbled
Description: Babushkas fall from windows smashing like porcelain, internal organs spill outwards and a cucumber can kill a man. Lecoq-trained company combine expressionist silent film with grotesque buffoonery in this tragicomedy inspired by Daniil Kharms.
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Curtains Up with Julia Donaldson, Vivian French & Simon Puttock
Description: There are many different ways to tell a story and one is to dramatise your favourite book. This event offers a unique opportunity to work with three leading picture book writers. Working in a group, you help devise a short play from a picture book. At the end, your parents and friends get the chance to watch the final performance. Break a leg! Tickets admit 1 participating child and 2 spectators. The final performance will commence at 11.30am.

Title: The Happy Prince
Description: Sue Casson's enchanting adaptation of Oscar Wilde's classic tale features a cast of four and a piano. Original score, witty lyrics and soaring melodies. Both children and adults will be entranced by this show. www.englishcabaret.co.uk.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Alain de Botton
Subtitle: WHAT NON-BELIEVERS COULD LEARN FROM FAITH
Description: The accessible philosophies of Alain De Botton are given fresh impetus with Religion For Atheists in which he argues that non-believers should quit mocking those with faith and start stealing some of their good ideas. That way, agnostics and atheists can build a stronger sense of community, make relationships last, get more out of art and overcome feelings of envy and inadequacy. De Botton discusses his ideas with BBC News arts editor Will Gompertz.

Title: Graveyard, Murder and Mystery Tour
Description: Join us as we journey through the darker side of Edinburgh's most haunted and historical graveyards and venture through the Old Town. Stories told in a humorous and entertaining way. Storytelling at its best.
Venue description: To find Greyfriars Bobby Bar from the Royal Mile, turn left onto George IV Bridge, continuing until you reach a railing and the Greyfriars Bobby statue on the right-hand side. The bar is just behind the statue (Candlemakers Row).
Venue accessibility: \nNot accessible to wheelchair users.

Title: Meet the Producers
Description: Want to know how to build and develop a successful show? A panel of experienced producers will explain the secrets of their trade and answer your questions.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: Educating Ronnie
Description: 'Brother, I need £20 to stay in school. Help?' Compelling true story of Joe meeting Ronnie in Uganda and a decade of giving. A provocative exploration of charity, friendship and how good intentions can become guilty burdens. www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Alan Anderson: Whisky For Dafties
Description: Six malt whiskies to be tasted, many laughs to be had. 'Inventive, fun, light-hearted way to learn about whisky' (Scotsman). 'Warm and hilarious' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Very humorous ... good night out for anyone' **** (Adelaide Advertiser).
Warnings: 'ID REQUIRED. If you look under 25, you will be asked for Proof of ID
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Tron
Venue description:
A close up room, perfect for comedy. Intimate, laid back, uptight. Low ceiling, up close, underground. Perfect!
\n

Title: Obsession - A Life With Magic
Description: What happens when you show an Asperger’s kid something cool? Ian's 21st Fringe year is an update of last year's five-star complete sell-out show. Get inside the head of a world-class magician.
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: Eleanor Tiernan - Rogue
Description: Stand-up comic / ex-civil servant talking on stage. A humorous hybrid of Sinead O’Connor and Carol Vorderman. Expect gags, diagrams and blistering logic. May contain useless information. 'A touch of whimsy grounded in astute observation' (Chortle.co.uk).
Warnings: 14+. Must be accompanied by an adult
Artist: Eleanor Tiernan / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue: The Stand Comedy Club III & IV
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue, Stand III is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand IV an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Wild Turkey
Description: A gritty, dark yet humorous look into the world of a late night burger bar. Wild Turkey centres on four men and their acrimonious relationships with each other and their struggle for status. Written by Joe Penhall.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Humour and Heart! - Free
Description: New York musical theatre entertainer and comedian Jonathan Prager presents a warm and humorous evening of American Songbook favourites along with exciting, unusual material and Jonathan’s original songs. Prepare to be moved and inspired. www.TheSeriousComic.com. www.FreeFestival.co.uk.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Edinburgh City Football Club
Venue description: A friendly and relaxed bar, with two theatres, based in a large Georgian building at the top of Leith Walk, with a programme of free comedy and theatre shows throughout the day, and one of the cheapest bars in Edinburgh.

Title: Berberian Sound Studio
Description: In the 1970s, a British sound technician (Toby Jones) is brought to Italy to work on the sound effects for a gruesome horror film. His nightmarish task slowly takes over his psyche, driving him to confront his own past. Berberian Sound Studio is many things: an anti-horror film, a stylistic tour de force, and a dream of cinema. As such, it offers a kind of pleasure that is rare in films, while recreating in a highly original way the pleasures of Italian horror cinema.

Title: Shostakovich Late
Description: Shostakovich's searing String Quartet No 11, plus Webern's lush late romantic Langsamer Satz performed by the Castalian Quartet. Perfect musical nightcap for Fringe diehards. Includes a complimentary glass of wine beforehand. www.roslarts.org.uk.
Venue description: Edinburgh's most central venue, with stunning castle views, has an intimate chamber music room, plus gallery. Restaurant and bar with food. An oasis of calm in the heart of the festival hustle and bustle.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Poe's Last Night - Free
Description: Enter the fascinating mind of Edgar Allan Poe. Share the horror of his last hours. Hear his most revealing works come to life. David Crawford (of Dawn of the Dead) portrays Poe’s haunting story.
Artist: David Crawford / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue address: 4 India Buildings, Victoria Street (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from midday-5am every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 11pm-5am.

Title: Nick Page: My Glorious Hypothetical Life As a Eunuch
Description: Some people grab life by the balls, some would have achieved more without them. 'Tales about life, love, and brushes with the law' (Guardian Pick of the Week).
Warnings: Not suitable for really really stupid people Some adult themes and (clever) strong language
Venue description: A year round comedy space in Edinburgh's city centre.
Venue accessibility: \nThis venue is in a basement and as such is not accessible for wheelchair users.

Title: Peatbog Faeries
Description: Nominated for Best Live Act, BBC Folk Awards 2012. This legendary Isle of Skye band have been described as the future of Celtic dance music as their jigs and reels blend with jazz, hip hop, reggae and more!
Venue description: Edinburgh's leading live music venue offers classical, jazz, blues, pop, rock, world, folk and comedy in the intimate surroundings of a converted Georgian church. www.thequeenshall.net

Title: Late Night Widor
Description: The great French composer Widor composed 10 symphonies for organ. The final two (Gothique and Romane) are rarely performed but represent his most personal utterances. Hear these beautiful works in the late-night splendour of St Peter's.
Venue description: Conveniently situated in the south side of Edinburgh, off South Clerk Street and near to Queen's Hall. On main bus routes.
Venue accessibility:
01459
\nAccessible WC, Wheel chair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Robert Douglas & Cynthia Rogerson
Subtitle: TWO BRILLIANT VOICES IN SCOTTISH FICTION
Description: Robert Douglas only started writing after he’d retired, but now he’s a bestselling author. He discusses the third book in his fictional trilogy set in Glasgow’s Maryhill, Last Dance at the Wreckers’ Ball. An American writer living in Scotland, Cynthia Rogerson unveils a short story collection Stepping Out and a new novel If I Touched the Earth, each exploring moments when everything is thrown into disarray.

Title: Absolutely Agitated Acupuncturist Returns to Find It - Free
Description: Olivia the singing acupuncturist returns to find It. What is It? Join her journey to find out. With storytelling and songs, Olivia will explore and reveal the matters of the heart. www.freefestival.co.uk.
Artist: Diamond Wave Productions / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Refurbished in 2011, The Meadow Bar offers two stylish bars with distinctive service and an extensive selection of beers, spirits, shooters, cocktails and drink offers. Also an internet cafe. Free performances of stand-up comedy run here from midday to 3am

Title: What's He Building in There?
Description: A wonderfully absurd dark comedy about a carpenter who is having an affair... with a chair. This Lynchian nightmare is accompanied by a live, original score. For STaG 2011 - **** (Scotsman), **** (Herald). www.whats-he-building-in-there.com.
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: Cheer Up! It’s Not the End of the World…
Description: Images of apocalypse, 2012, the end of the world? Including original prints by Jake and Dinos Chapman, Gordon Cheung, Damien Hirst and Andy Warhol.
Venue description: Edinburgh Printmakers promotes contemporary, innovative printmaking through an open-access studio, shop and gallery. The public can view and purchase limited edition prints, artist books and multiples by a wide range of artists. Open Tue-Sat, 10:00-18:00 in July and Open Tue-Sun, 10:00-18:00 in August. Closed Mondays.

Title: Ahdaf Soueif
Subtitle: THE WRITER AND THE EGYPTIAN REVOLUTION
Description: Can a people's revolution that's democratic, inclusive and peaceable succeed? That's the question asked by the eminent Egyptian writer Ahdaf Soueif in her profoundly affecting memoir, Cairo: My City, Our Revolution. In it, she charts the uprising as it unfolded in Cairo last year. 'This book is not a record of an event that's over', she explains. Here, she discusses a revolution that Egypt is still living through. Chaired by Kate Allen, Director of Amnesty International UK.

Title: The Ash Girl
Description: Sin. Passion. Fire. Can a young girl’s rage ignite the flame that will lift her from despair? PULSE presents this shockingly dark and visceral twist on the Cinderella fable – not to be missed.
Venue description: One of the festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross genre performance makes this central venue a must for all.  Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Just
Description: Ali Smith, prize-winning Scottish writer, creates dazzling and bizarre fictions, and Just fits this bill: a surreal exploration of the perversion of justice in a twisted society. A Magritte umbrella pierces a body at the bus stop - whodunnit?
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: The Two Most Perfect Things
Description: Five performers present a new show celebrating the lives and careers of Noel Coward and Ivor Novello, the biggest stars of the interwar years, through their unforgettable words and music.
Venue description: The Roxy, a beautifully converted former chapel, is the latest addition to Assembly's growing list of venues.  Built in 1809 and located just north-east of our George Square hub, the Roxy houses three performances spaces; the 400 seat former nave Roxy Central, the 168 seat Roxy Upstairs and our 60 seat studio Roxy Downstairs.  The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Out of the Blue
Description: Oxford's all-male, all-vocal sensation and stars of Britain's Got Talent return with their incredible blend of stunning singing, comical choreography and boyish charm. 'True, simple entertainment' (WhatsOnStage.com). 'An absolutely unforgettable musical experience' (ThreeWeeks). @ootboxford. www.ootb.org.uk.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Ewan Morrison
Subtitle: SHOPPING CHANNELED
Description: He caused a stir last August with his ‘end of books’ chat, but what will Ewan Morrison have up his sleeve this year? Tales from the Mall is a mash-up of fact, fiction, essays and multi-format media that tells of the rise of the shopping mall, an iconic symbol of our age. These stories feature some true-life tales of those who work, shop and sometimes even make love within those walls. Chaired by the Guardian’s Literary Editor, Claire Armitstead.

Title: Cooperative Learning for the 21st Century
Description: Canadian educationalist Christine Ward is an internationally renowned trainer in Cooperative Learning. In this event she explains how we can help youngsters develop the qualities they will need for life in a fast-changing world. Ward focuses on learning and teaching strategies which stress positive independence, individual accountability and social skills, whilst promoting academic achievement.

Title: Peter Popham
Subtitle: BEHIND THE SCENES WITH AUNG SAN SUU KYI
Description: Little more than a year after her release from house arrest in Burma, the progress of Aung San Suu Kyi is remarkable, with the pro-democracy campaigner having won a seat in the Burmese parliament. Peter Popham's timely biography of Suu Kyi draws on the journalist's several meetings with the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize. Join him for a vivid, up-to-date account of a singular woman.

Title: Boris & Sergey's Vaudevillian Adventure EXTRA SHOW
Description: 'Hilariously filthy but strangely full of pathos. Unadulterated genius' (WeLikeThisToo.Blogspot.com). Join Puppetry's Balkan bad boys, the greatest double act ever conceived for the small stage. Expect riotous exploits, malarkey, molestation and mirth!
Warnings: adult themes and strong language explicit language
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Booking Dance Festival - Split Bill
Description: Exquisite, extraordinary, captivating dance from two top USA companies. Hammerstep taps out an extravaganza of monumental proportions, accompanied by live music while Dallas Black Dance Theatre portrays Nina Simone in an engaging narrative. www.bookingdance.com.
Venue description: Venue150 @ EICC just gets better and better! This year, take in some big names, world-class comedy, internationally renowned dance and jaw-dropping acts from across the globe. All in the capital's comfiest venue! www.venue150.com

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: LITERARY DEATH MATCH
Description:
In 2011 literary pugilists Chris Brookmyre and Billy Letford were embroiled in a numerical battle royal. In 2012, the Literary Death Match returns to these shores from its international travels to see who can win the most sought after title in literature! Four writers must compete to win the hearts and minds of the fickle all-star judging panel, including Greg Proops, Rory Skovel and you, the noble audience with only their words as their weapons. The two authors who succeed in deftly dazzling all involved go onto a death-defying final round where survival is down to wits alone. Readers will include Nikesh Shukla and Tupelo Hassman. Join your host and LDM founder, Todd Zuniga, for a ringside seat.

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Title: The Tim Vine Chat Show
Description: The audience are the stars of the show! Tim Vine brings his 2011 sell-out show back to the Fringe. With new guests, new jokes and new nonsense, expect the pun-expected. ***** (Scotsman).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Killing Time
Description: Friendship. Futility. Foreskins. Two teenage boys find something to laugh about - and in case you’ve forgotten, there’s an impending Armageddon. It’s not all bad at the end of the world. A new comedy from the EUTC.
Warnings: Some reference to adult themes, some strong language
Venue description: Bedlam Theatre plays host to an eclectic mix of theatre, dance and comedy at the heart of the Fringe. Enjoy the unique atmosphere of our famous cafe and discover some of the most innovative shows the festival has to offer.

Title: The Shape of Things by Neil LaBute
Description: (First performed: Almeida Theatre Company). How far would you go for love? What would you change or risk? Labute addresses these painful questions as he explores the nature of love and art.
Venue description: Situated right in the middle of it all, located on the Royal Mile, theSpaceUK presents an international programme of collective performance art, from theatre to improv, from sketch to monologues. All show information at www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Mervyn Stutter's Pick of the Fringe
Description: See live extracts from eight top shows and then go and see the ones you like. Simple! Brilliant! Comedy, music, theatre, dance, the lot. 'A stimulating showcase of talent' (Scotsman). Copied but never equalled.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Colin Steele / Brian Kellock
Description: Intricate interplay, melodic dynamism and harmonic surprises from two of Scotland’s top jazz gurus! Sparks fly as trumpeter Steele, famed for his Chet Baker/Miles Davis shows, teams with the Oscar Peterson/Cecil Taylor range of pianist Kellock.
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Berlie Doherty’s latest, Treason, follows the fortunes of Will Gaveston from page boy to little Prince Edward, son of King Henry VIII. Title: The Suburban Trilogy
Description: Veteran found footage filmmaker Abigail Child is well known for her radical reworking of established cinematic and cultural codes through an idiosyncratic use of montage and disjunctions of sound and image. This feature-length project renews these concerns with three distinctive films that move between home movie, found footage and documentary material – a fascinating anthropological collage that examines myths of gender and national identity, as well as themes of family, memory, class and history.

Title: Keith Lowe
Subtitle: AFTER THE WAR, THE VENGEANCE
Description: At the end of the Second World War, more than 35 million people had been killed and many cities flattened. Yet, according to Savage Continent, a remarkable and painstakingly researched new book by Keith Lowe, the killing didn't end there. Much of Europe was on the brink of starvation and some battles continued. In this event Lowe explains how Europe finally got to grips with the new world order.

Title: Pat Barker
Subtitle: A CELEBRATED NOVELIST AT THE HEIGHT OF HER POWERS
Description: The winner of the 1995 Man Booker Prize joins us to unveil Toby's Room, the sequel to her acclaimed novel Life Class. Toby is 'missing, believed killed' on the battlefields of France, but his sister begins to question how he died – and why. Pat Barker's unforgettable stories highlight the emotional traumas of the First World War and Toby's Room might just be her most powerful yet.

Title: Festen

Starring Kieran Hodgson, of Fringe favourites Kieran and The Joes. ‘Relentlessly hilarious’ ***** (Daily Telegraph). ‘Intelligently written and skilfully acted’ **** (Chortle.co.uk). ‘Hilarity … delightfully misguided’ **** (Metro).
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.
Venue accessibility: \nNo access for wheelchair users - venue up flight of stairs.

Title: Wonderland
Description: Down the rabbit hole and through a pool of tears exists a world so strange, Alice thinks it can't be real. But is it? Follow her through Wonderland, a thrilling alternate reality and a show that promises to delight.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: Damien Crow: The World According to Damien Crow
Description: Ever wondered what is going on inside the mind of a Goth? Join Damien Crow as he lays bare his soul with devastating, unexpected and hilarious consequences. ‘Gloriously miserable’ (List).
Warnings: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult
Venue description: The famous Assembly Rooms is at the heart of the New Town. Following an extensive restoration, this beautiful venue offers the highest standards throughout. Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the best in theatre, comedy and music on offer on the Fringe.

02459
