Title: Unbound
Subtitle: HOMEWORK
Description:
Homework, a night of literary cabaret based in East London, relocates to Edinburgh for a night of obsessions. The four Homework residents, and a secret guest, will explore their compulsive sides: Joe Dunthorne writes a letter to the first girl at school he loved (and still loves); Tim Clare raps his favourite niche magazine, Tree News; John Osborne tries to fall in love with every seaside town; Ross Sutherland revisits, again and again, The Crystal Maze.

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: HIGH INFIDELITY
Description:
Bringing a different vice to the Unbound canon, Glasgow-based newcomer Kohl Publishing presents High Infidelity – an evening celebrating adultery in literary fiction. Featuring new writing, scarlet literature from the past, live music with a sensual twist and wayward trivia, the Kohl girls promise to turn The Guardian Spiegeltent into a den of deviance. Kohl will also unveil an enticing digital peepshow – a new reading experience of tantalising downloads, showcasing Elizabeth Reeder’s Fremont, their brilliant debut novel. Watch out for the scarlet letter for giveaways.

	Our Unbound series of events offer a literary experience like no other. Free and on every night in the Guardian Spiegeltent in Charlotte Square Gardens, anything goes: storytelling, music, performance, poetry, stand-up – it’s a raw, surprising, sometimes emotional ride. Come with an open mind!

Title: David Whitney - Struggling to Evolve
Description: Taking his first steps out of the primordial soup, Whitney provides a guide to sex, drink and violence, and not getting away with it. 'Genuine spirit of fun' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Huge laughs ... silver-tongued warrior' (Spectator).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Future Tales (Sierakowski)
Description: A fictitious future biography of S?awomir Sierakowski, the influential Polish left-wing intellectualist and activist. A debate about the attitude of the New Left’s leaders, their methods of activity and choices of presenting ideology in art. www.culture.pl/edinburgh.
Warnings: Supported by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute www.culture.pl
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Sex Ed: The Musical!
Description: It's coming! Ever wondered what a prostatic utricle was? A urethral sponge? A scrotum? Forging paths through a jungle of sexual ignorance, this team of titillating teachers explain everything you never wanted to know about sex.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Code: Rosalinda + Everybody Says Long Live Bobby Holly
Title: Rosalinda + Everybody Says Long Live Bobby Holly
Description: These two short films highlight the richness of recent South American cinema. From one of Argentina’s most important new directors, Rosalinda is not only an original meditation on Shakespeare’s As You Like It, but a rich and enjoyable work that sustains a brisk comic tempo within a mellow, sunlit atmosphere. Everybody Says Long Live Bobby Holly is an ingenious and farcical fake rockumentary chronicling the achievements of an unknown giant of Uruguayan music.

Title: Jason Byrne: People's Puppeteer
Description: Jason Byrne is back with a brand new show where he effortlessly conjures up a night of hilarity. Featuring new stories, props and of course, the star of every show, The Audience. ‘A Comedy God’ (Mirror.co.uk).
Artist: Phil McIntyre Entertainments by arrangement with Lisa Thomas Management
Venue description: Venue150 @ EICC just gets better and better! This year, take in some big names, world-class comedy, internationally renowned dance and jaw-dropping acts from across the globe. All in the capital's comfiest venue! www.venue150.com

Title: After Hours Comedy
Description: Legendary and unmissable, After Hours celebrates its 10th birthday! Showcasing this year's biggest stand-ups, some so hot we mightn't be allowed to mention them beforehand. 'The best late night show on the Fringe, brilliant' (Jason Byrne).
Artist: Pleasance Theatre Trust and Amused Moose Comedy
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Dean Friedman - In Concert
Description: This legendary songwriter performs hits Ariel, Lucky Stars, Lydia and more. ‘Utterly Brilliant’ ***** (ThreeWeeks). 'Troubadour of Choice!' (Scotsman). 'Every Song a Classic!' (London Theatre Guide). Powerful, poignant, hilarious songs from a master songsmith.
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.
Venue accessibility: \nNo access for wheelchair users - venue up flight of stairs.

Title: Him and Me: Sketch Circus - Free
Description: Sketches, music, videos, wigs, moobs, boobs, ladies’ clothing, inflatable genitalia, a guitar and a tambourine. Performed by the hit YouTube duo! ‘A more accessible Reeves and Mortimer…' **** (Large Manchester).
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink. With a section of free Fringe shows in the downstairs room throughout the day.

Title: Philip Hughes & Kathleen Jamie
Subtitle: WILD AND WONDERFUL
Description: In Sightlines, Kathleen Jamie describes landscapes as varied as a gannetry in Shetland; and the lining of a stomach. She achieves what one reviewer described as ‘an exact transcription of the deep unsettling weirdness of the wild.’ Philip Hughes’ Tracks describes his many walks through British landscapes, featuring exquisite drawings of places such as Assynt, Islay and Orkney. Both ask powerful questions about what we mean by the ‘natural’ world. Chaired by the Guardian’s Online Books Editor, Sarah Crown.

Title: The Wrigley Sisters
Description: '...play from the heart about their Orkney Islands homeland' (Canberra Times). '...put their own spin on traditional jigs and reels' (Denver Post). '...bending traditional tunes to jazzy, tonal surprises, keeping crowds guessing' (Santa Cruz Metro). www.wrigleysisters.com.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Steven Butler
Description: Join Steven Butler for the fourth book in his hilarious, disgusting, Roald Dahl Funny Prize-shortlisted series, The Wrong Pong. Come along for truly troll-tastic fun, hear about the latest books and about Steven’s love of trolls, including their yucky habits and gruesome food. And, if you’re brave enough, you can compete in the famous Wrong Pong Troll-Off.

Title: Tibetan Book of the Dead: The Musical - Free
Description: An exploration of the meaning of The Tibetan Book of the Dead, a book that prepares the listener for, and guides him through, the experience of death.
Venue address: 50 Blackfriars Street within Smart City Hostels,(entrances on Blackfriars Street and Cowgate),Edinburgh
Venue description: Located within the five-star Smart City Hostel, Bar 50 is a bar and restaurant offering free shows, drinks and tasty, locally-sourced pub grub in laid-back, modern and stylish surroundings – and a rooftop terrace.

Title: Scott's Songs
Description: Deeply rooted in tradition, yet with a profound sense of... Och, enough of this rubbish. I'll be singing my own songs - there'll be some pathos, some humour and there's a story behind each song.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Cathy Cassidy & Fiona Foden
Description: Authors Cathy Cassidy and Fiona Foden have been friends since they worked together at Jackie magazine. Now they come together to talk about their writing: Cathy to discuss her latest Chocolate Box story, Summer’s Dream and Fiona with her debut novel, Cassie’s Crush. Join them as they chat about friendship, first crushes, daydreaming and writing for teen mags.

Title: Hanks and Conran - Pigs in Blankets
Description: Mix two comedians, a classic double-act dilemma and a touch of variety. Add laughter, to taste. Serve with tongue firmly placed in cheek. 'These two make me honk with laughter' (Sarah Millican).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Here's to the Heroes
Description: This massed voice choir sings from the heart, with songs conveying the power of heroism and the Olympic spirit. Including Wherever You Are, made famous by the Military Wives Choir, their concerts support Help for Heroes.
Venue description: St Mary's is ideally placed in the city centre, with its stunning new pipe organ, concerts Mon-Sat and the traditional service of Choral Vespers during the Fringe. The neighbouring Cafe Camino is the perfect place for refreshment and relaxation.

Title: Le Nozze di Figaro
Description: Aria Alba are back with a fantastic production set against the rising fascism and looming war of 1930s Italy. Our 2011 audiences said, 'enchanting ... seriously good singing!' Unmissable!
Venue description: Easily accessible by bus or by parking on Bruntsfield Place, this is our second year in the Fringe. On the ground floor the church has traditional fixed pew seating facing the stage, with some restricted view seats.
Venue accessibility:
0289
\nOn street parking for a blue badge holder, accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space).

Title: Asher Treleaven: Troubadour
Description: An autobiographical show that ponders the question, 'is my life actually interesting enough to talk about for a whole hour?’ Edinburgh Comedy Awards, Best Newcomer Nominee 2010, *****, (Mirror), (Age), (ThreeWeeks).
Artist: Mick Perrin for Just For Laughs Live
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Gilbert and Sullivan in Brief(s)
Description: A madcap race through all 14 operettas. Prepare for pirates, sailors, major generals and gondoliers in this topsy-turvy musical romp! Direct from New York. 'The very model of a modern major hit!' (Washington Post).
Artist: Ingenious Paradox / Nick Brooke Productions / Queens Theatre
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Comedy Brass - Free
Description: No brass or knicker? Putcha purse away and come watch stand-up from Scott Adams and Anthea Neagle, plus a surprise act daily from the London circuit. You'll leave like you're made of funny. Kaboom. www.laughinghorsecomedy.co.uk.
Warnings: over 18 - some swearing and sexual content
Artist: Adams & Neagle / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Refurbished in 2011, The Meadow Bar offers two stylish bars with distinctive service and an extensive selection of beers, spirits, shooters, cocktails and drink offers. Also an internet cafe. Free performances of stand-up comedy run here from midday to 3am

Title: 10 Films With My Dad
Description: How do fathers and sons communicate? Sports? Cars? Tattoos? From John Wayne to 3D, see how two men found each other through cinema. 'Charmingly funny' (Scotsman). ‘Heart-warming' **** (ThreeWeeks). 'Delightful' **** (Latest7).
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.
Venue accessibility: \nNo access for wheelchair users - venue up flight of stairs.

Title: Tom Cottle's These Twisted Folk
Description: Michael Twist was born with baby girl's hands. Sad! Has this affected his life? Yes! Come to Iron Belly as Tom Cottle 'Comedy Gold' ***** (WhatsOnStage.com) hosts an evening of macabre tales with funny goings-on.
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars 'til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: The  Magical Adventures of Pete Heat
Description: Surreal, irreverent and downright amazing hour of comedy magic from lanky charmer Pete Heat. May contain eloquence, delight and posh weasels. 'Pete scares me. And then there's his magic...' (Rich Fulcher, The Mighty Boosh).
Venue description: Gilded Balloon at Third Door is an exciting new space, just moments from Teviot Row House. Bringing you the very best in theatre, comedy and magic, reflecting the diverse and innovative programming that the Gilded Balloon is world renowned for.

Title: Anything But (A One-Woman Play)
Description: Agnes is always trying to help, but never herself. A funny, wistful story about the messiness of living. Winner of the prestigious Harry Porter comedy prize, judged by Tim Key. 'Hilarious and moving' ***** (Varsity).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: The Edinburgh Fringe Survival Guide: Live!
Description: Top performers share secrets about staging a successful Edinburgh Fringe show with the author of Methuen Drama's celebrated guide. 'A wonderfully practical but also inspirational book full of good advice' (Guardian). www.edinburghfringesurvivalguide.com.
Artist: Mark Fisher in association with Pleasance
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: The Red Bus Puppet Shows
Description: Charming entertainment for children under six aboard our 1962 red double-decker Routemaster bus in the Meadows. Puppet shows on the top deck from Celeste's Circus and Free Range. Rides for all ages every day. www.theredbus.co.uk.
Venue description: Charming entertainment for children under six aboard our 1962 red double-decker Routemaster bus in the Meadows. Puppet shows on the top deck from Celeste's Circus and Free Range Puppeteers. Rides for all ages every day. www.theredbus.co.uk.
Venue accessibility: \nThis is a vintage vehicle in original condition and as such the venue is not accessible to wheelchair users.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: FREEDOM FROM TORTURE
Description: All over the world people are imprisoned for writing critically about their government or country. Each day we pay tribute to writers who have been persecuted for their words, thoughts and opinions. Today we hear the work of the writers group from Freedom from Torture. Reading today: Michèle Roberts, Gerbrand Bakker, Anna Raverat and Peter Popham.

Title: The Charlatans
Description: For more than two decades now, The Charlatans have been an inspirational force in British rock.
Venue description:
The HMV Picture House is Edinburgh's best venue in which to experience live music and clubs. 
\nThe lovingly restored Caledonian cinema on Lothian Road - you may remember it as the Caley Palais - is perfect for performers and audience alike.

Title: Gained in Translation
Description: Join Sarah Ardizzone and Daniel Hahn to hear about what makes a good translator, why being a good linguist isn’t enough and how the best are creative writers themselves. Ardizzone is an award-winning translator of works for adults and children; Hahn is a writer, editor and translator of fiction and non-fiction working on texts as diverse as those by José Saramago and Brazilian footballer Pelé.

Title: Ruchir Sharma
Subtitle: IN SEARCH OF THE NEXT ECONOMIC MIRACLE
Description: The head of emerging markets at Morgan Stanley, Ruchir Sharma has first hand experience of economies across the world. In his provocative new book, Breakout Nations, Sharma argues that the time-honoured method of watching 'global trends' to forecast growth will no longer work. In this event he offers some surprising tips about which countries are the rising stars, and which will be economic flops.

Title: Brake
Description: Stephen Dorff is a man who awakes to his incarceration in the trunk of a moving car and a deadly demand.  Either he gives his captors the information they want or he and his loved ones will be executed.  It’s a white-knuckle ninety-minute ride as Dorff, encased in the trunk, is put through every manner of mental and physical torture in an attempt to extract the all-important secret.  But will he crack?

With live music, multimedia projections, and pulsating physicality, we enter oppressive Oceania in this new adaptation of 1984. Winston spins between hopes of love and threats of torture, as his every movement is tracked. www.1984fringe.tumblr.com. ‘Arresting’ ***** (RemoteGoat.co.uk).
Warnings: Strong language and strobe lighting Strong language and strobe lighting
Artist: EmpathEyes Theatre in Association With UCLU Runaground
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: Norman Davies & Tom Pow
Subtitle: WHAT WAS LOST
Description: Kingdoms come and go: Sparta, Rome, Byzantium, the Soviet Eastern Bloc – all are vanished, and the eminent historian Norman Davies describes some of these lost empires in his epic new book. Meanwhile there is a different kind of shift taking place: Scottish poet and writer Tom Pow's elegiac book In Another World takes him to dying villages across Europe as he chronicles the effects of an era of rural depopulation. Chaired by Scottish author Alistair Moffat.

Title: Billy Kirkwood’s - Show Me Your Tattoo 2012
Description: Last year’s Smash hit returns to this years Edinburgh festival and takes gleeful run down the hilarious Highway of Human Graffiti in the blistering funny worlds first Stand up/Improv/Chat Tattoo Comedy show! ***** Fest Mag
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: A smart bar, located right in the centre of the Grassmarket with a large open bar space, free shows upstairs and a secluded beer garden and terrace - with food and drink available all day a great place to hang out during the Fringe. 18+

Title: Conversations With Love
Description: This award-winning show is Ann Akin's debut as a writer/director/choreographer. It's a monologue piece about the many different kinds of conversations that one can have with love, incorporating music, movement and sign language.
Warnings: Occasional strong language Occasional strong language
Venue description: Whitespace is a central venue at the top of Leith Walk with many restaurants and bars close by.  An intimate space with good acoustics that stays cool in hot weather with good ventilation and good access from the street.
Venue accessibility: \n

Title: Bach Cello Suites
Description: The accomplished cellist Anne-Isabel Meyer returns to the Fringe with Bach's great masterworks for solo violoncello. Take this rare opportunity to hear the whole cycle over three days.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: The Three Faces of Doctor Crippen
Description: A marvellously twisted tale of love, death, and a bathtub full of body parts. Based on the true story of the notorious murderer Doctor Crippen. Terrible vaudeville, daring escapes, and rather lovely hats. www.freerangeproductions.co.uk.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Vitamin
Description: These are my friends - we used to ring doorbells and wait for the door to open in the pose of garden gnome statues, the first to move would lose. One day... A hilarious physical play. 'Beautifully executed silliness' (Prague.tv).
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: Formby
Description: Written and performed by Ewan Wardrop. Directed by Ed Hughes. George Formby's rise from awkward stable boy to one of Britain's biggest stars. A funny, touching look at the life of an essentially ordinary man with an extraordinary talent.
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility:
024579
\nWheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: And No More Shall We Part
Description: Tom Holloway’s beautiful new play is an uplifting testament to the power of love and the indomitability of the human spirit. Directed by James Macdonald with Dearbhla Molloy and Bill Paterson.
Venue description: Scotland's new writing theatre 'is the festival's most prestigious home of serious drama' (New York Times) and a multiple Fringe First and Herald Angel award winner. 'The main hub of festival-focussed action during August' (List).

Title: Sam Bourne
Subtitle: THE THRILLING TALE OF A PLOT TO CREATE A MASTER RACE
Description: What did Nazi Germans and left-leaning thinkers such as Bertrand Russell and George Bernard Shaw have in common? One answer is eugenics – selective breeding for the supposed betterment of the human race. In his latest thriller, Sam Bourne (aka Guardian columnist Jonathan Freedland) spins a propulsive story and a true-life secret project involving the British and US intelligentsia. Chaired by Allan Little.

Title: The GO-GO (Club Night)
Description: The legendary Sixties club goes fortnightly with two of Scotland's most authentic retro-bands; French garage-rockers Les BOF! and beat-stompers The New Piccadillys. One band each night. Fab 60s sounds from DJs Tall Paul and Big Gus.

Title: Fables Here and Then
Description: A versatile company of young actors and musicians presents a collection of stories from around the world, ranging from the comic to the tragic, told through movement, music and the spoken word.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: The Knowledge Emporium
Description: A sweetshop inside a 1960s airstream caravan, The Emporium doesn't accept money - you trade stuff you know for sweets. Then we'll perform a reading at the end of the week from all the knowledge you've given us.
Venue description: Northern Stage at St Stephen’s is a creative home for the most exciting and unusual theatre made in the Greater North of England. Original stories, new performances and spirited special events that will delight, provoke and entertain you.

Title: The  Wau Wau Sisters Are Naked as the Day They Were Born Again
Description: Stripped of their beloved props, homemade costumes, high heels, wigs and travel-sized booze bottles – they show us what they are made of, quite literally, setting out to make a show out of nothing at all!
Warnings: Under 18's must be accompanied by an adult may contain adult themes and nudity
Artist: The  Wau Wau Sisters/ The Famous Spiegeltent
Venue description: The Famous Spiegeltent. The original, beloved, iconic festival venue returns to the faithful! The grandest dame of all is back in town, out of the gardens and onto George Street: sexy, funny, dangerous – a living legend!
Venue accessibility:
2459
\nWheelchair access, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC.

Title: Nell Freudenberger & Krys Lee
Subtitle: RISING STARS OF AMERICAN LITERATURE
Description: Nell Freudenberger is an American literary sensation and her new novel, The Newlyweds, has been one of the most breathlessly anticipated books of the year in the States. Krys Lee was born in South Korea and raised in the USA, and her new book of short stories shines a light on the experience of Korean families struggling to live the American Dream. Chaired by the Guardian’s Literary Editor, Claire Armitstead.

Title: Noo Saro-Wiwa & Binyavanga Wainaina (*Binyavanga Wainaina has cancelled*)
Subtitle: HOW TO WRITE ABOUT AFRICA
Description:
A new generation of writers is changing perceptions of post-colonial Africa. In this event, journalist Noo Saro-Wiwa describes her return to Nigeria, the sleeping superpower where her father was executed for campaigning against devastation of the environment by oil companies. Binyavanga Wainaina's brilliant memoir takes the reader through Kenya, Uganda and South Africa. Both reveal an exuberant continent of complexity and contradiction.

	
	Please note: Binyavanga Wainaina has cancelled and this event will go ahead with Noo Saro-Wiwa.

Title: Mark Cooper-Jones: Geography Teacher - Free
Description: The tall one from WitTank performs stand-up whilst emphatically reinforcing geography teacher stereotypes. No chewing. Chortle Best Newcomer nominee 2012. Runner-up, Loaded Laftas 2011. Star of BBC3’s Live at the Electric with WitTank. ***** (List).
Venue accessibility: \n

Title: B*tch Boxer
Description: London. 2012. The Olympics. For the first time in history women can compete in the sport of boxing. But in a man’s world, can one woman prove she’s worth the title? Winner - Old Vic New Voices Edinburgh Season.
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)

Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.

Title: Bernard the Ferret (Happy to be Himself!)
Description: This funny and magical storytelling with puppets, launches a new book by playwright Eve Stebbing. Performances are followed by a workshop. See www.spinofftheatre.co.uk for more information.

Title: The Boy and the Bunnet
Description: 'Scotland's Peter and the Wolf' (Sunday Herald). Big Sky presents Gerda Stevenson and seven of Scotland's finest traditional musicians in a captivating musical adventure written by James Robertson. Brilliant all ages - four upwards. **** (Scotsman). www.theboyandthebunnet.com.

Title: Nick Hayman: Middle Aged, Useless and Talented! - Free
Description: One-man comedy show bringing together stand-up comedy, satirical songs, comic instrumental performance, musical slapstick and clowning. A surreal combination in the tradition of Norman Wisdom, Les Dawson, and Tommy Cooper.
Artist: Nick Hayman / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Writing Workshop
Subtitle: THE ART OF PERFORMANCE
Description: The relationship between the written and spoken word is changing for authors, with performance and public reading becoming an integral part of a writer’s career. In this workshop, performance poet Tim Turnbull explores how performance and public reading can inform and improve your writing. Using your own work, the workshop will look at voice, structure, rhythm and timing.

Title: The Improvised Musical
Description: Six actors. A live band. Your suggestions. Unique theatrical experience, improvised before your eyes. Anything can happen, and everything will, in this high-energy show you can enjoy again and again. 'Something special' **** (ThreeWeeks). www.noshoestheatre.co.uk.
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performance. Twenty-one performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 21st year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Heaven's Gate

Title: Debate: Rethinking the Internet
Subtitle: IS THE WEB CHANGING SOCIETY FOR THE WORSE?
Description:
We have embraced the online revolution with open arms and nearly 20% of all retail purchases are now made via the internet. More than that, the internet appears to be empowering citizens in ways that challenge the traditional relationship between individual and state. Is the net effect positive or negative? Writer Nick Harkaway, novelist Naomi Alderman and James Gleick, author of The Information, lead the discussion. Chaired by Ian Katz, Deputy Editor of the Guardian.

	Please note: Naomi Alderman will no longer be appearing in this event.

Title: Free Daily Walks Down the Royal Mile

Places are limited and you’ll be asked to submit material in advance so your specialist can give you the best possible support. Part of the Edinburgh City of Literature New Writing Programme. Each ticket admits one person to a 15 min discussion with one of four experts. Please contact the Box Office to book your time slot. (Tickets cannot be purchased online.)

Two masters of historical fiction discuss their new novels in this unmissable event.

The trio conspire to murder Chris’s mum for the insurance money and hire policeman/hit man Joe (Matthew McConaughey) to carry out the deed. Description: Germany's best-selling, smash-hit stand-up makes his hilarious Edinburgh debut. A colossal excursion into the home of the wild and the wilderness of the home. 'Very very very funny' (Bono, U2).
Artist: Mick Perrin for Just For Laughs Live and Eddie Izzard
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Peter Burke
Subtitle: KNOWLEDGE IS STILL POWER
Description: Peter Burke’s new volume of A Social History of Knowledge picks up where the first left off, around 1750, at the publication of the French Encyclopédie, and follows the story all the way through to Wikipedia. Focussing on groups, institutions, collective practices and general trends rather than individuals, he delivers an impressive range of scholarship through entertainingly accessible prose.

Title: So You Want Your Own Blog
Description: Stage blogger (and theatre journalist) Mark Shenton hosts a session on setting up and managing a successful theatre blog. Learn the power of using blogs as a marketing tool and be effective in driving traffic to your site.
Artist: The Stage Events with Mark Shenton
Venue description: A resource exclusively for particpants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe & bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.

Title: McLaren Animation 3: For the Family
Description: The final presentation showcasing the extraordinary talent the UK has to offer the world of animation. Norman McLaren, the great Scots pioneer who experimented with a range of innovative animation techniques and whom our award for the Best British Animation is named after, endeavoured to communicate to all through his work regardless of borders, class or age; and it is in this spirit that we present a programme of films which can be enjoyed by all the family.

Title: Don Quixote! Don Quixote!
Description: A surreal journey through the restless mind of Don Quixote de la Mancha. An unconventional physical theatre piece where the grotesque becomes poetic and the boundaries between fantasy and reality blur...
Artist: Panta Rei Theatre Collective, Pleasance Theatre Trust
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Fusion Shorts
Description: This year our short fiction, documentary, experimental and animation programmers have put their heads together to create a truly eclectic programme of international short films that defy categorization. Fusing different cinematic techniques and moving through a variety of themes from marginal characters, imagined worlds and contemplative journeys to existential angst, fraught relationships and the poetry of the everyday, these hybrid films celebrate the diversity of short filmmaking.

Title: In Musical Company
Description: Lose those recession blues and be uplifted by songs from this dynamic company’s catalogue of smash-hit musicals including Sweeney Todd, West Side Story, A Chorus Line and Rent. If you love musicals you’ll love this! www.edinburghtheatre.co.uk.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Our Soldier
Description: A war correspondent's unbelievable story of violence and corruption in an absurd world. A dynamic blend of comedy and movement, tragicomic clowns tells the tragic tale of a soldier named Macbeth. Awarded Redbridge Drama Centre's Apprentice Company 2012.
Venue description: Zoo's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, classic drama, rising comedy talent and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: About Comedy - Stand-up Comedy Courses
Description: Learn the skill and art of stand-up comedy performance on this two-day intensive comedy training course. Our tutors are comedians and writers. Course includes a performance in a Fringe show. Further information at www.aboutcomedy.co.uk.
Warnings: Ticket is for two days. 4.5 hours a day.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Edinburgh City Football Club
Venue description: A friendly and relaxed bar, with two theatres, based in a large Georgian building at the top of Leith Walk, with a programme of free comedy and theatre shows throughout the day, and one of the cheapest bars in Edinburgh.

Title: Lucy Ayrton: Lullabies to Make Your Children Cry
Description: Women in fairy tales are rubbish. But they never used to be. What happened? Poet/songstress Lucy Ayrton unravels the dark, beautiful fairy tales of our past, and spins some of her own.
Venue description: Two comfortable and spacious performance spaces set in Scotland's most haunted pub.
Venue accessibility:
49
\nAccessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.
\n

Title: Cracking Yolks - Free Range Comedy
Description: Free range comedy from three spring chickens - Ruth Bruce, Nena Edwards and Jo Ogden. You'll be cracking up as they scramble together disaster stories of love, life and breakfast foods.
Artist: Jo Ogden / Nena Edwards / Ruth Bruce / Free Festival
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Frenemies
Description: Young timid playwright meets with neurotic, Hamlet-obsessed national theatre manager to discuss production of his breakthrough play. A quick-paced new comedy with a brilliant, unexpected plot twist. From acclaimed Israeli Fringe duo making their international debut.
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items ... Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning events for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs and rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. A great way to set you up for your Book Festival day. On today: Stories with Edinburgh For Under Fives.

Title: Samba Sene and Diwan: African Dreams
Description: Diverse international collection of musicians, led by charismatic Senegalese singer Samba Sene. Exuberant fusion of Afrobeat/mbalax grooves, with undercurrents of ska and Senegalese soul. ***** (EdinburghSpotlight.com). **** (Scotsman). **** (List).
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Code: And If We All Lived Together?
Title: And If We All Lived Together?
Description: Several screen icons star in a comedy-drama that treats delicate issues with tact, humour and intelligence. Five long-time friends (Jane Fonda, Geraldine Chaplin, Claude Rich, Pierre Richard, Guy Bedos), now past retirement age, decide to move in together. Under the watchful eyes of their younger caretaker (Daniel Bruhl), an anthropology student, the new housemates confront some hidden issues from their shared past while struggling to cope with the problems of ageing.

Title: Chris Ramsey: Feeling Lucky
Description: Following two consecutive sell-out Edinburgh shows and a sell-out UK tour, Foster’s Award nominee and panel show regular, Chris Ramsey, returns to the Fringe with his new stand-up show. ‘A brilliantly engaging natural storyteller’ (Evening Standard).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: People Like Us
Description: Just out of a bad relationship, Stacey wasn't looking to date, let alone fall in love. Then she met Simon. He promised never to hurt her, but even sincere promises are sometimes hard to keep.
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Pool of Blood
Description: A cabaret of blood where plots twist, corpses laugh and all are dancing on the edge of the abyss. But these dark machinations of a dying 1911 Liverpool Music Hall suspiciously shadow worlds we know too well...
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: The Look of an Angel on the Devil Himself
Description: The Look of an Angel on the Devil Himself. Ireland's comedic pied piper speaks about life’s fork in the road when change comes knocking on your door.
Warnings: Strong language which some may find offensive
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air conditioning.

Title: Manu Joseph & David Park
Subtitle: LOVE AND HUMANITY IN THE CITY
Description: Two brilliant novelists from different countries and cultures share astute observations about the nature of human relationships. Manu Joseph, shortlisted for last year's Man Asian Literary Prize, returns to launch Illicit Happiness of Other People, a darkly comic novel set in 1990s Madras, while Belfast-based writer David Park discusses his powerful and tender novel The Light of Amsterdam.

Title: Terror On Presley Beach
Description: One doomed planet. One missing scientist. Two surfing aliens. Four crazy kids. A rampaging gorilla. A hunky bodybuilding academic. Elvis Presley! A brace of boppin' tunes. This summer, everyone should dance on Presley Beach!
Venue description: Paradise Green's purpose-built venue in the vaulted basements of Augustine United Church hosts an exciting programme of theatre and comedy for all tastes, from classics to new and experimental work. Soak up the true spirit of the Fringe.

Title: Someone, Somewhere
Description: Second (Hackney Empire) NATYS 2012, second Leicester Square New Comedian 2011, second Laughing Horse New Act 2011, Chortle Best Newcomer nominee 2012 has the best show on the Fringe and is fit. 'True to his boastful word' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: Open from 9am at the heart of the Festival on the Royal Mile, free comedy shows starting from 10am every day and free live music from 9:30pm to 3am every night. Food is served all day with outside seating available.
Venue accessibility:
49
\nAccessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Flanders and Swann
Description: The most important anniversary of 2012 must not go unmarked! Not the Diamond Jubilee but the 90th anniversary of the birth of Michael Flanders! 'Muddy marvellous' (Evening Standard). ‘Outstanding show’ (FringeReview.co.uk). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Artist: Tim FitzHigham and Pleasance in association with Jeremy Meadow
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Vikki Stone: Hot Mess
Description: Award-winning musical comedy and stand-up from 'hilarious and brilliant' (Heat) Vikki Stone (MTV's Flashprank, BBC3's Britain in Bed). Top 5 Edinburgh Acts 2011 (Observer). 'Bette Midler for the Adele generation' (Sunday Herald). 'Terrific’ (Scotsman).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Failure and How to Achieve It
Description: In this fast-paced comedy from Max Fletcher and Nick Davies of the Oxford Revue, two pastry chefs search for the perfect marriage of cake and frosting. ‘Pastry chefs ... nowhere to be found’ (Oxford Student).
Artist: Max Fletcher and Nick Davies / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860s interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy suite and ballroom will be used during the festival.
Venue accessibility: \nNo access for wheelchair users - venue up flight of stairs.

Title: Waiting for Stanley
Description: This moving physical comedy takes us back to a railway station in 1945 where a wife anxiously awaits her husband's return from the war. ‘Inventive, witty and pacy ... a real pleasure’ (TimeOut Critics’ Choice).
Venue description: The Roxy, a beautifully converted former chapel, is the latest addition to Assembly's growing list of venues.  Built in 1809 and located just north-east of our George Square hub, the Roxy houses three performances spaces; the 400 seat former nave Roxy Central, the 168 seat Roxy Upstairs and our 60 seat studio Roxy Downstairs.  The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: Fred Cooke: Standing, tilted
Description: ‘The Edinburgh Fringe creates many comedians in the same sea. If Jimmy Carr has a cruise ship, Fred Cooke has a canoe with a hole in it’ (Fred Cooke). ‘Stupidly enjoyable’ (Scotsman).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24 hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Overexposed: A Slightly Awkward Peep Show
Description: Straight from a sold-out run in the City of Brotherly Love, three performers standing at a crossroads of sexuality come together to perform extremely funny and remarkably revealing storytelling. More info, www.slightlyawkwardpeepshow.com.
Artist: Jamison Foreman, Jennifer MacMillan and Daniel Student / PBH’s Free Fringe
Venue description: Finger's piano bar is an institution established in the early 80s. During the Free Fringe shows Finger's turns into one of the best cosmopolitan venues in Edinburgh. An experience not to be missed! Opening hours 2pm till 5am. No disabled access.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Short Films 3: Strange Geometry
Description: This selection salutes both eccentric characters as well as the incredible reach of the human imagination. Zig- zagging though tales that chart the vivid manifestations of childhood fear, the memorabilia arising from a life spent collecting artefacts, a love letter recorded on a reel to reel tape recorder and the dehumanising effects of industrial capitalism.

Title: Short Films 1: Identity and Revolution
Description: The core focus of this programme investigates how the individual orients and defines itself in reaction to collective, shared history and the fragments of the past half remembered, invented or fabricated by themselves and others. How does this refracted burden define how we conceive ourselves in the present? Fragments of family Super 8 films, found photographs and unusual parallels serve as tools to interrogate, question and explore stories of self and history.

Title: Pleasance Bytes
Description: Pleasance's hit series of live audience recordings where journalist Mark Fisher asks leading actors what makes a great performance. Available on iTunes. 'Fisher ... the perfect host' **** (ThreeWeeks). 'Unique insight to life behind the Fringe' (EdFestMag.co.uk).
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: My Journey Throughout China
Description: This classical zheng performer, the most celebrated international soloist of any Chinese national musical instrument of her generation, makes her annual return to Edinburgh to take us on a journey through the spirit of China.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hilton), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Leo and Stephen Go Down On You!
Description: Enjoy the sharp tongues of Leo Kearse, ‘Very funny, very shocking!’ **** (List, ThreeWeeks) and Stephen Bailey, ‘Very funny!’ (Matthew Wright), for a hilarious romp from monkey sex to masturbation!
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: Brides of Comedy
Description: Williamson and Jones learnt some valuable lessons touring with Paddy McGuinness in 2011 - but failed to grasp 'everything in moderation'! Sketch show with a difference! 'They make me piss my sides, very very funny!' (Paddy McGuinness). www.bridesofcomedy.com.
Venue description: Historic original Fringe venue in an unrivalled location. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: The Good Person of Szechwan
Description: Drama students from Hong Kong present a brilliant interpretation of Brecht’s famous modern parable. The company’s South-East Asian cultural heritage is central to this story in the Epic Theatre tradition combining music, politics and comedy.
Venue description: the SpaceUK present another high calibre venue. This wonderfully-located space between Bristo Square and the Pleasance offers a high brow alternative to the traditional fringe venues. Ideal for Stand-Up, Chat, Music (bands), A Capella, Improv, Sketch and Cabaret.

Title: An Evening with Richard Demarco, CBE
Description: Enjoy an evening with Richard Demarco, CBE - involved with every Fringe since its inception in 1947, co-founded the Traverse Theatre in 1963 and was associated with artists such as Joseph Beuys and Tadeusz Kantor.
Artist: Fringe University and Demarco European Art Foundation
Venue description: Summerhall is a new venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former ‘Dick Vet’ building of Edinburgh University.

Title: My City Saturday
Description: A normal Saturday in Edinburgh, or at least it should be. Somebody didn’t come home last night and now everybody’s implicated. Tension mounts as we hurtle through the lives of a group of troubled teenagers.
Venue: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel
Venue description: Gryphon Venues at the Point Hotel offers two performance spaces ideal for intimate, experimental, and engaging theatre. We present a programme of theatrical performance, especially innovative works, original works, devised theatre, movement, puppetry, immersive theatre and music.

Title: Nish Kumar - Who Is Nish Kumar?
Description: Stand-up comedian? British Asian? Idiot? The answer is all three. A show about being proud of your roots and ashamed about everything else. ***** (Scotsman). 'A comic force not to be ignored' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: Garth Nix
Description: The hugely successful, award-winning writer Garth Nix travels to Edinburgh from Australia to draw you into his world of fantasy and science fiction. His many books are popular worldwide and include the Sabriel trilogy, The Keys to the Kingdom series and his latest novel, A Confusion of Princes. Find out what it takes to make a fantasy novel really work (or not!) and pick up some expert tips on how to write a compelling book of your own.

Title: Insights
Description: Insights is a choreographic platform which supports graduates as they embark on their journey into the professional dance world. Jai Hutchison created Insights with an aim of providing performance opportunities for recent graduates within dance, choreography and physical theatre.
Artist: Five emerging choreographers from across the U.K.
Venue description: One of the festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross genre performance makes this central venue a must for all.  Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Povs and Hefter Uncensored
Description: Povs and Hefter Uncensored is about two misunderstood misfit comedians from opposite sides of the pond who have joined forces to have their voices heard and understood through the power of stand-up comedy.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through the day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard. Huge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of new surprises in 2012!

Title: The Company of Wolves
Description: An extraordinary twist on the beloved fairytale, Little Red Riding Hood. Exploring temptation and forbidden sexuality, this interactive performance employs stunning use of mask, live music and physical theatre. 'Beautifully crafted' (ThreeWeeks).
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Rock
Description: In this musical show, presented at Avignon Festival, actor Pierre Baux and cellist Vincent Courtois give life to New York's 70s rock scene through dialogues, memories and digressions collected by Legs McNeil and Gillian McCain in Please Kill Me.
Venue description: Just minutes from Princes Street, the Institut français offers an intimate theatre space, presenting a fantastic programme of theatre and children’s shows. The Bistro offers a cosy French atmosphere to enjoy some food and drinks throughout the day.
Venue accessibility:
4
\nAssistance dogs welcome.

Title: Black Box Shorts 4: Particles
Description: Three films that explore, with almost obsessive precision, the minutiae of phenomena in flux, including Paul Clipson’s series of intimate Super-8 studies of plant and animal life, Rose Lowder’s ethereal observations of the crystallization of sea water, and Telcosystems’ take on particle theory through the unstable fluctuation of digital data. Moving from the poetic to the hypnotic, from the figurative to the abstract, and from calm to chaos, this programme promises an intense audiovisual experience!

Title: Denise Scott - Regrets
Description: This is multi award-winning Australian comedian Denise Scott's Fringe debut. Scotty is Australian comedy's next big thing and she's been around for a while. 'A fresh, funny and exquisitely delivered masterclass of frill-free stand-up' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound presents the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces The Hall, Rainy and the Baillie.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nWheelchair accessible except for Baillie Room, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Once Upon A...
Description: Enter a world where books come to life at the turn of every page. Once Upon A... is an interactive, storytelling children’s show which gives its audience the opportunity to get involved.
Artist: Pipe Up Productions and New Celts Productions
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Flea Circus Open Slam
Description: Top talent from across the Edinburgh Festival Fringe meet to compete in battle. The prize? Glory, and a chance to make a video with Tea Fuelled. Past acts include Penny Dreadfuls, Mark Grist, Tom Rosenthal and Pappy's.
Venue description: Two comfortable and spacious performance spaces set in Scotland's most haunted pub.
Venue accessibility:
49
\nAccessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.
\n

Title: Fèis Rois and Cèol Mòr
Description: Currently on their Year of Creative Scotland Trad Trail tour, this exceptional group of Fèis Rois musicians collaborate with young musicians from the Aberdeen International Youth Festival. Scottish traditional music at its very best! www.tradtrails.org.uk.
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.

Title: Lady M
Description: Shakespeare didn't tell you everything that happened in Macbeth's castle. Now the lady-in-waiting takes the stage and divulges all the gruesome details he neglected to mention. Critically acclaimed solo show from The Netherlands. www.lady-m.nl.
Artist: Het Vijfde Bedrijf - The Fifth Act (The Netherlands)
Venue address: Edinburgh College of Art,Lauriston Place and Lady Lawson Street
Venue description: Theatre, comedy, spectacle. The brightest and biggest musicals, dance, drama, circus, cabaret and children's shows. Courtyard with outdoor performances, food and bar. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Loretta Maine: Bipolar
Description: Country's grungiest singer returns to explore the two sides of her personality: angry and really f*cking angry. 'The finest female character comic around' (Time Out). 'Brilliantly observed' (Guardian). 'Murderously funny' (Evening Standard). www.lorettamaine.com.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the fringe!

Title: Minotaur
Description: ***** ’Spellbinding physical theatre (FringeReview.co.uk). ***** ‘A tour de force’ (RemoteGoat.co.uk). Adapted from the Greek myth, a story of the creation of the beast known as Minotaur. Is there a way out of this labyrinth of lust and blood?
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: When I Grow Up I Want to Be...
Description: An energetic family-friendly piece, exploring the wonders of the imagination and where it takes an audience. Primarily a physical theatre performance that includes feel-good toe-tapping musical numbers.
Artist: Springboard Theatre Company - University of Gloucestershire
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.

Title: Piano Duo
Description: Enjoy an evening of scintillating masterworks for piano (four hands) including Schubert's Lebenssturme Allegro, Onslow Sonata Op 22, Szelenyi Colorit and Barber Souvenirs performed in the beautiful acoustic of centrally located St Mark's.
Venue description: The artSpace programme of music and drama, in our acoustically excellent auditorium within St Mark's Unitarian Church, is performed by virtuosos, both well-known and newcomers. The church welcomes you at 11:00 Sundays for Church Service including a short recital.

Title: MNL 143
Description: On a commuter's trip from Manila's business district to the suburbs, the director finds a myriad of possibilities, ranging from miniature ironic situations to a love story that is finally finding its unexpected closing. An emotional rollercoaster ride of despair, dreams and desire, MNL 143 is also a black comedy about limited private spaces in conflict with sprawling public realms.

Title: Mark Watson's Edinborolympics
Description: International teams of comedians (including David O'Doherty, Adam Hills and Mark Watson) compete in a variety of disciplines not recognised by the so called 'real' Olympics. Different, mostly stupid events each night. Full schedule at www.markwatsonthecomedian.com.
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Frankie from the Valley - Free
Description: Stand up comedy from Frankie Williams, Geraint Evans and guests. The Welsh comedians have managed to escape Swansea and will be bringing their tales of life’s little struggles to Edinburgh with hilarious consequences.
Artist: Frankie Williams, Geraint Evans and Guests
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items ... Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: Rocks and Fossils with Alan McKirdy & Moira McKirdy
Description: Scotland’s landscape has evolved over the last 3 billion years and by looking at rock formations, minerals, fossils, volcanoes and more, we can find out the whole story. Alan and Moira McKirdy take you on an exciting journey back through time to discover the secrets of the landscape, animals and ice-flows which have shaped the nation. Grab the opportunity to handle the rocks and fossils of all types and ages which tell its story.

Title: Wild West End
Description: The company behind national sell-out success Fresher the Musical, present this deliciously dark comedy revue. Witness the West End's greatest hits stripped bare by our scandalous parodies. This is musical theatre alchemy, no song is safe.
Venue description: The transformed and newly refurbished Pleasance Dome offers five venues presenting the best in comedy, theatre and live music all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late into the night.

Title: Romeo and Juliet
Description: An all-teen cast surpass expectation in an intimate and intense adaptation of the one true love story, faithfully portraying the tempestuous insanity of adolescent life and love that has helped define the genre. **** (ThreeWeeks, 2011).
Venue description: One of the festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross genre performance makes this central venue a must for all.  Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: 12th Night: Serenade
Description: Love triangles, mistaken identity, disguises, pranks and... pop songs? Combining classical language and contemporary music, 12th Night: Serenade is an enchanting, mix tape tribute to Shakespeare's most musical comedy.
Venue description: Church Hill Theatre was originally built as a church in 1892.  Purchased in 1960 by the Council, it has served as a theatre for community and Fringe performers since 1965. It has been home to the AHSTF shows for twelve years.

Title: Noël Coward's Tonight at 8:30
Description: An evening's entertainment to make your morning! In their award-winning production, Oxford's Trinity College present two hilarious half-hour comedies from Noël Coward's collection of plays, Tonight at 8:30. 'Hugely entertaining' **** (OxfordTheatreReview.com).
Venue description: With an unrivaled location right in the middle of it all and part of our Royal Mile hub, the venue offers a fantastic high calibre platform to showcase some of Edinburgh's best large scale shows.
Venue accessibility:
249
\nAccessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Fruitful Ties and Bone Dust
Description: Their first encounter was in the 1980s. Now Palsson and Hawkins reunite, conjuring an elegance that feels just ripe. Billed with Lucy Suggate's Danse Macabre, a surprising exploration of what happens beyond bodily decay.

Title: Conversations: Hebrides Ensemble and Synergy Vocals
Callum Innes: The Regent Bridge
Description:
Celebrated internationally for his abstract paintings, Edinburgh based artist Callum Innes works for the very first time with light, in a simple intervention which floods a dark tunnel on Calton Road with colour to reveal the magnificent architecture of the Regent Bridge above. 
 
The bridge was designed in 1814 by Archibald Elliot to create an entrance to Edinburgh where the London Road entered the New Town. It was constructed under the direction of Robert Stevenson and completed in 1819, thus solving the long-standing problem of entering the city through narrow and inconvenient medieval streets. Although still a major thoroughfare between the Old and New Towns, centuries of dirt and a lack of light make the bridge feel more of a dark tunnel than a celebratory arch.
 
Working with architect and lighting artist Gavin Fraser, of FOTO-MA Lighting Architects, Innes has evolved a scheme that transforms the flat sides of the lower arch at street level into an illuminated plinth of floating colour. The work follows a series of set rules to create a structured and yet deliberately random order of coloured light, revealing and lifting the giant curve of the arch above. The Regent Bridge is commissioned by Edinburgh Art Festival and Ingleby Gallery.
 
Installed at the base of the Regent Bridge on Calton Road, under Waterloo Place

Title: We are all U.F.O.-nauts
Description:
Taking as its starting point the photographic series Self-portraits as a U.F.O.-naut by Slovakian artist Július Koller (1939-2007), this group show explores the ongoing potency of Koller’s works and related actions. 

Assuming a playful strategy of resistance to the failings of ‘reality’ by pairing them with the ‘other-worldly’, the works in this show question methods of navigation unrestrained by logic and also the connection between imagination, optimism and agency in contemporary art. The exhibition will feature a series of Koller’s photographs from the 1980s and new works by artists including Gintaras Didžiapetris and Catherine Payton.

Code: Melvin Moti: One Thousand Points of Light
Title: Melvin Moti: One Thousand Points of Light
Description:
One Thousand Points of Light is Dutch artist Melvin Moti’s first UK solo show. 

Working with UV light emitting rocks from the mineralogy collections at National Museums Scotland, Moti has made a stunning film that induces feelings of either flying through space or looking down a microscope, immersing the viewer in the uncanny beauty of these luminous objects by removing any sense of their physical scale. 

Moti considers that rocks are in some way communicating directly by absorbing UV light, changing it and emitting visible light in vivid colours. Alongside his film, Moti has brought together an extremely diverse range of other objects from the museum’s collection, all of which communicate through their material qualities - including scent bottles made with Uranium glass, dried scorpions, millions of years old fossils and jellyfish suspended in spirit.

The exhibition is supported by Creative Scotland with additional support from the Mondriaan Fund.

Description: Taking cues from soul greats such as Otis Redding and Sam Cooke mixed with fiery blues, pop sensibilities and slick guitar playing. Debut album in 2012. www.freefestival.co.uk.

Code: Ailie Cohen Puppet Maker (SCOTLAND) Cloud Man
Title: Ailie Cohen Puppet Maker (SCOTLAND) Cloud Man
Description:
A highly visual, gentle story with few words and an original soundtrack of atmospheric music. 

Cloudia has always had her head in the clouds. She is a cloud expert and all of her life she has dreamt of seeing a Cloud Man - an extremely rare creature who lives a quiet life high up in the sky.  
 
Follow the clues to the very top of Cloud Mountain where the view is always surprising. If you are lucky, you may see something very special indeed.  
 
‘a deceptively simple story that will melt even the flintiest of hearts.’ The List
Artist: Ailie Cohen Puppet Maker (SCOTLAND) Cloud Man

Title: Ask-I Trio
Description:
A rare opportunity to experience the music of neyzen Ilhan Barutcu. Highly acclaimed in his native Turkey, his virtuoso mastery of this ancient flute - the Nay - is awe inspiring. Renowned for his stunning improvisations - his sensitive interpretation of classical mystical pieces and of his own compositions.  Accompanied by the beautiful sound of Peter Strandberg on Flamenco guitar and the incredible talent of Adam Reid on Darbuka.
Ask-i Trio's music is classical sufi , with Nay improvisations, uniquely  married with Flamenco - mystical and full of emotion. The sound of the Nay is said to be close to the sound of the human voice and combined with the passion of Flamenco and the  heady rhythms of the darbouka makes the music of the Ask-I Trio utterly compelling .

Title: Grimm's Sheesha with Peter Chand
Description: South Asia holds up a mirror to our favourite Grimm stories. Did they begin in the East told by travellers, migrants and gypsies or are they universal? It’s all in the entertaining, magic hands of our own British-Punjabi Genie, Peter Chand.

Code: Inspired by Van Gogh to Kandinsky: Symbolist Landscape in Europe - A Two-Day Practical Course (Day One)
Title: Inspired by Van Gogh to Kandinsky: Symbolist Landscape in Europe - A Two-Day Practical Course (Day One)
Description: Led by artist Campbell Sandilands. Inspired by the exhibition Van Gogh to Kandinsky: Symbolist Landscape in Europe 1880-1910, learn how to combine woodblock, painting and collage to make your own creative landscapes and colourful compositions.
